proposals.behaviour: Triage among competing applications. With the owner gone, the remaining preparer can only work on a limited number of grant applications at once and ranks them. The ranking favours high-return or expansion projects and labor-recovering projects over small maintenance-like APS retrofits. APS gets worked on only if it ranks inside the capacity, even when its own BCR clears 5.0.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus hiring freeze while another capital application deadline overlaps an HSIP/APS window (several grant calls land in the same quarter). Capacity K_app is below the number of open deadlines.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a cross-application queue ahead of the PREPARING state. An APS task moves IDLE -> PREPARING only if its rank is within K_app. Otherwise it is held and counted as MISSED at the deadline, with no deflection event and no owner-tier change. This lowers p_start on top of the owner drop, because it depends on what else is competing rather than on APS pressure.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. D3.1 gives each field-window task its own independent p_start with an owner/strain term. F-h and F-i only lower owner tier or K_crew (construction). There is no shared preparation-capacity constraint across A2's other applications, so this is not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: grant rule 'prioritize expansion over maintenance; the most flexible money goes to match' (CIPpol p.11, line 149). 01 s2.2 line 154: CIP rule 'fund urgent needs in phases by project/grant readiness'. 01 s2.1 line 113: grants pay Signal Shop labor, so projects that recover staff cost rank higher. No document directly shows A2 triaging deadlines. That part has no document support.
proposals.parameter: K_app (concurrent applications the preparer can carry) and rho_aps (APS rank percentile among competing applications, 0 = top). Triage switch sw_triage = 0/1.
proposals.range: K_app in {1, 2, 3} (baseline 3 = no constraint). rho_aps ~ U(0.3, 0.9) from the 'maintenance ranks low' reading. Applies only while the post is vacant (t_vac) or strain > 0.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 IDLE -> PREPARING transition: adds an admission test 'rank <= K_app' before the p_start draw. Failure goes to MISSED, not DEFLECTED.

proposals.behaviour: Carry-forward of the previous cycle's package. To save effort, the preparer resubmits or lightly edits the earlier HSIP APS package (the same C-type intersections, the same carriers) instead of re-scoring crashes or re-pricing. Preparation is fast, but inputs are stale: old crash window, old unit price, a stale LRSP or flag status.
proposals.trigger: The vacancy removes the person who knew how to rebuild a package, while a window opens with the earlier package or the already-programmed placeholder lines (SG142/SG143 'EST') still on file.
proposals.effect_in_model: Shortens D_prep by a factor, so more windows are made. But it applies a stale penalty to the BCR (old Y_win, unit price below the current $40k+) and raises the chance of a flag or eligibility failure. This trades fewer MISSED outcomes for more F-a/F-b/F-c failures. It also skips the repack step in D3.3 step 5, so no new package forms from newly freed intersections.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. D3.3 step 1-5 regenerates the package from scratch each round, and D_prep is a single draw. F-b allows a repack only after a rejection. No carry-forward mode exists.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 line 140: CIP rows SG142 ($488,144, C13 EST) and SG143 ($1,588,144, C14 EST) already programmed, which is the natural template. 01 s2.1 line 119: unit price rising 9-10% a year, which is what makes stale numbers fail. No document shows reuse of an old package. That part has no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_carry (0/1), D_prep multiplier m_carry, BCR stale discount d_stale.
proposals.range: m_carry ~ U(0.3, 0.7). d_stale ~ U(0.85, 1.0) applied to BCR. Extra q_flag_stale ~ U(0, 0.2) added to the rho_flag eligibility draw. Active only when the post is vacant.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING duration (D_prep + (m-1)*delta_split) and the D3.3 BCR/eligibility checks. Replaces the full repack in D3.3 step 5 with the previous package.

proposals.behaviour: Hiring a grant consultant or a short-term acting preparer to write the application, instead of waiting for a replacement. This is outsourcing of preparation, not of construction. It costs money and procurement time, and the written package may be less accurate about local engineering details.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus a hiring freeze, while the unit still has some capital or operating money for consultants (including cost recovery through the grant itself) and a window is about to open.
proposals.effect_in_model: Provides a way around the strain on p_start. It changes preparation capacity from in-house-only to purchasable, after a lag t_proc. The purchased route has its own quality factor and a cost that comes out of the unit's local match or an 'extra budget' line. This runs against the model's assumption that the vacancy makes owner and strain fall until t_vac ends.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-e/F-i outsourcing refers to the CON phase (tendering, t_contract) and does not touch application preparation. F-h only has recovery by hiring back (t_vac).
proposals.evidence: No document support for consultant use in application preparation. Related: 01 s2.1 line 106 (one associate engineer scores all applications, so there is a single point of failure) and 01 s2.2 line 152 ('no new headcount' in the budget), which make a purchased substitute the only option when the freeze holds.
proposals.parameter: sw_consult (0/1), t_proc (procurement lag, months), q_qual (acceptance quality factor), c_consult (extra cost, counted in cost_by_actor).
proposals.range: t_proc ~ U(3, 9) months. q_qual ~ U(0.7, 1.0) multiplying BCR-based acceptance or the eligibility draw. c_consult ~ U($30k, $120k) per package, not included in the HSIP BCR denominator.
proposals.rule_modified: F-h/F-i. The vacancy penalty on owner and strain ends t_proc months after the vacancy starts, instead of at t_vac. D3.1 p_start recovers by a partial amount equal to q_qual.

proposals.behaviour: Silent window miss from lost tacit calendar knowledge. The informal owner held the deadlines and relationships in his head. After departure nobody opens the window. This is not reluctance (a low p_start); the task simply never triggers. A second effect is that the shared-state hand-off to Public Works or SFCTA contacts is also lost.
proposals.trigger: Informal ownership with no written duty. The first HSIP/CTC call after the departure, before a successor or written handover exists.
proposals.effect_in_model: A pre-gate before the p_start draw: with probability p_unaware the window is not noticed at all, so the task never leaves IDLE and no deflection or MISSED is logged to outsiders. The gate decays as a successor learns the calendar or a documented checklist is created. Output shows more 'never started' windows than the current model produces.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-h lowers owner a tier and aborts PREPARING with q_drop. But the owner term is inside the logistic for willingness. No separate awareness gate exists, and p_start in D3.1 is always strictly in (0, 1) with no floor for a window never being seen. Kept as a distinct switch.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 line 106: one associate engineer scores all applications ('unique' is inferred). 01 s2.1 line 115: the policy does not require applying for funds, so there is no automatic trigger. 01 s2.2 line 161: no board item on HSIP or grants, so nothing external prompts the unit. No direct document on missed calendars. That part has no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_unaware (probability the first post-departure window is not noticed) and tau_learn (months until the awareness gate decays to zero).
proposals.range: p_unaware ~ U(0.1, 0.6) for the first window after departure, decaying linearly over tau_learn ~ U(6, 24) months. Set to 0 under M-B/M-C when the owner is retained.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 IDLE gate: p_start_eff = (1 - p_unaware(t)) * p_start. Reset to 0 when t_vac ends or when the PW3 'named owner' pathway puts a written duty in place.

proposals.behaviour: Paper-funding placeholder. When the APS-only line cannot be applied for, staff leave SG142 in the capital plan with its estimated HSIP C13 source unchanged (or roll it to C14 by re-labelling) instead of declaring it unfunded. The line then acts as a visible 'funded in plan' signal to oversight and advocates, which lowers outside pressure and removes the trigger to restart.
proposals.trigger: The deadline passes (or is about to pass) with no eligible APS instance prepared, and the plan line still shows an estimated external source. Changing the line costs staff little. Leaving it costs nothing.
proposals.effect_in_model: Suppresses pressure(t) and oversight after a MISSED or REJECTED outcome. p_start in the next window is lower, because the 'no money' narrative looks resolved. This lengthens the 'no one applies, no one is blamed' loop.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. D3.1 DEFLECTED only reduces pressure after a pressure event. D3.5 F-a to F-m have no failure where a plan line masks a missed application. Closest: the M-A silence loop, and F-m (advocacy goes quiet exogenously).
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 line 140: SG142 $488,144 is listed as 'HSIP C13 – EST', yet the application is ineligible as written (01 line 420). 01 line 224: the earlier SG136 'APS FY25' $1.0M was planned from HSIP C12, and no SF APS application appears in the C12 list. 01 line 83 gives the 'no money / not applied' loop, but the plan-line-as-signal link is inference with no direct document support.
proposals.parameter: p_placeholder
proposals.range: 0 to 0.8 per missed or rejected cycle. If the placeholder is held, pressure(t) is multiplied by (1 - ρ_ph) with ρ_ph in U(0, 0.5), for t_ph months with t_ph in U(12, 36).
proposals.rule_modified: Post-MISSED/REJECTED step of D3.1 and the pressure(t) decay in D3.1. Adds a switch to the M-A and M-D columns of D3.2.

proposals.behaviour: Pre-deadline scope enlargement of the carrier project. Staff widen the SG015 visibility upgrade's corridor list or its work items (more 8-inch to 12-inch heads, backplates) so that more pending C-type APS intersections sit inside the same HSIP application. This lets the APS ride on a BCR-eligible carrier.
proposals.trigger: The pure-APS line is known to be ineligible. A carrier already exists in the same cycle and its scope is set by staff, not by a board.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the number of intersections in the PW1/C13 bundle above about 1. The cost is more prep time (δ_split-like) and some BCR dilution. Changes whether PW1 'covers fewer than 2 intersections' fires and so whether the model switches to C14.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.3 and PW1 fix the SG015 scope to five named corridors, giving about 1 intersection. They add other corridors only after a C13 failure, in C14. Expanding the carrier within C13 is not allowed.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 444: SG015 corridors are limited to five named ones, and the project description says 'selected corridors' (inference: about 1 extra intersection). 01 line 432 lists corridor candidates that 'join at corridor design (candidate)'. No document shows staff widening the scope before a deadline, so this is a plausible behaviour with no document support.
proposals.parameter: n_carrier_expand
proposals.range: Integer 0 to 8 extra pending C intersections added to the SG015 scope at C13 application time. Each costs δ_split extra prep months and raises the carrier cost by c_12in or c_bp. Applied only if the prep time fits before the deadline.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 packing algorithm step 1 (the PW1 candidate set limited to SG015 corridors) and D3.6 PW1 trigger.

proposals.behaviour: Strategic abstention to wait for a rule change. Staff deliberately do not prepare a restructured APS-with-carrier application because the state advisory committee said it would 'study' funding APS-only projects. They expect a later cycle to accept pure APS.
proposals.trigger: A public statement that eligibility will be reviewed, combined with an ineligible plan line and heavy workload close to the deadline.
proposals.effect_in_model: Sets p_start to 0 in the window, not just lowers it. It adds a timed 'wait' state that ends when a rule signal appears or after a number of cycles. This differs from a random MISSED outcome because it lasts across cycles and breaks the 'restart in the next window' assumption.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. D3.3 states that no 'rule relaxation' switch is modelled and deletes it because no landable rule exists. D3.1 has only IDLE → PREPARING at p_start, MISSED or DEFLECTED. A staff decision to wait is not any of them.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.4 line 207: the committee answered a letter that 'HSIP does not fund APS-only projects' and that it 'will study it again'. That is the only line. That staff wait because of it has no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_wait_rule and n_wait_cycles
proposals.range: Switch 0/1. If on, p_start for the HSIP field is forced to 0 for 1 to 2 cycles (n_wait_cycles in {1, 2}) from a start date. It is reset by a rule-change event with rate λ_rule in U(0, 0.15) per cycle, or at the end of the waiting period.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 IDLE → PREPARING transition for the HSIP field. D3.6: adds an exit to PW0.

proposals.behaviour: Triage of one preparer's capacity in the final week. Staff prepare the application with the highest sure-win value (the SG015 safety upgrade, already in the plan with a BCR story) first. The APS-bundle application is built only if time remains, or is submitted unfinished or not at all.
proposals.trigger: A deadline within about one week, with two or more instances competing for the same few preparers. One instance has a clean eligibility record, the other has risk (dilution below BCR 5.0, an unclear carrier).
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes instance preparation order-dependent. The APS-bearing instance is more likely to be MISSED even when the field task starts. Currently instances are prepared in sequence only through the additive δ_split. Nothing makes the APS one the first to be dropped.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1: prep time = D_prep + (m - 1)·δ_split, and unprepared instances are MISSED. The ordering by value or risk is not modelled. The prepared set is always filled in a fixed order, not by priority.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1 and §2.2 on staffing strain (the Signal Shop hiring freeze, line 549, P1) support limited preparation capacity. The CIP lists SG015 and SG142 on separate rows in the same year (line 442). No document shows triage ordering, so it is a plausible behaviour with no direct support.
proposals.parameter: prep_priority_aps_last
proposals.range: Probability 0 to 1 that, when instances are limited, the APS-bearing instance is the first to be dropped. Combined with a prep capacity parameter C_prep in {1, 2} instances per window.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 deadline step ('instances prepared are submitted one by one; unprepared are MISSED') and D3.3 step 5 (C pack and N pack each run once).

proposals.behaviour: Informal pre-clearance with Caltrans Local Assistance before committing prep time. The preparer phones or emails the district liaison to ask whether an APS element on a signal-hardware carrier (SI02/SI07/SI18PB) will be treated as eligible. They proceed, reshape the bundle, or drop APS from the application based on the answer.
proposals.trigger: Deadline is within weeks (here, next week), the written rule says APS-only is ineligible, and the carrier-eligibility question is unresolved. Triggered when the task is about to enter PREPARING and the expected cost of a rejected submission exceeds the cost of asking.
proposals.effect_in_model: Turns the global, unresolved SI02_carrier switch into a per-actor information event. With probability p_precheck A2 learns the realised eligibility before D_prep is spent. If the answer is 'unavailable', A2 skips PREPARING and goes straight to route B, a local fund, or the next window. If the answer is 'available', the eligibility draw at review is conditioned on it. This cuts wasted prep and F-a/F-c style rejections. It also makes it possible for APS to be left out of C13 while SG015 still goes in.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. Eligibility is drawn once per intersection at review (D3.3 table, column 'resource'). SI02_carrier is a single shared uncertainty switch kept in parallel (end of D3.6). The text assumes no agent acts on it before submitting. F-a only covers BCR < 5.0 after packing.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 3.1, hard-facts list: SI02 as an APS carrier rests on 'author interview (primary), no public Caltrans determination'. That shows eligibility is settled through informal channels. 01 section 3.1 also says the C10-to-C13 rule change has 'no written rule' before the 2025-12 minutes. Only indirect support for A2 asking. No document shows an SFMTA staffer doing so (no document support for the behaviour itself).
proposals.parameter: p_precheck: probability that A2 obtains an eligibility answer before starting PREPARING, plus accuracy a_precheck (probability the answer matches the later review outcome).
proposals.range: p_precheck U(0, 0.8); a_precheck U(0.6, 1.0). 0 reproduces the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 start rule (p_start branch) and D3.3 eligibility draw / SI02_carrier switch. Adds a conditional branch before the PREPARING transition.

proposals.behaviour: Post-award scope add. A2 submits a clean carrier-only application (the SG015 visibility upgrade) and then adds APS to the funded project afterwards. It uses a scope change at design, a local-match line, or the planned SG142 local money, instead of putting APS into the HSIP application.
proposals.trigger: Eligibility risk makes putting APS in the application unattractive, but the carrier is already planned for the same cycle. The trigger is SG015 being approved, followed by the design-complete node.
proposals.effect_in_model: Gives a delivery path that skips the HSIP APS eligibility and BCR gate. APS cost is no longer in the HSIP BCR denominator and carries no HSIP rule risk. Installs ride on the SG015 timeline (t_partner / CON E-76). Cost is paid locally, outside the 10% match arithmetic. Adds a conversion probability and a budget-availability check. Failure falls back to F-j/F-k style local-funding fights.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly, so check overlap. PW4 'corridor candidate (added at design time)' and D3.4 'merged into existing project' cover adding APS to a parent project, but only for intersections already classified. PW1 puts APS in the same application up front. A decision after approval that adds APS to the awarded project, with local money paying the APS share, is not written as a rule.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.1 decision rule: 'all new signals and major signal upgrades install APS; installing with existing work is cheapest' (MDC23 p.6; MDC26 p.7). 01 section 2.1 resources: SG142 is $488,144, about 22 intersections, no excavation, built by the Signal Shop. 01 section 3.1: same-round listing of SG015 and SG142 in the CIP.
proposals.parameter: p_postadd: probability, per approved carrier project, that A2 converts a clean carrier award into an APS add at design-complete, subject to local money b_post being available.
proposals.range: p_postadd U(0, 0.6); b_post tied to the existing local-fund variables (general fund / Prop L), 0 to $0.5M per year.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 HSIP delivery row: new event after design-complete. Also the D3.3 packing step, which would stop forcing APS into the HSIP bundle when this switch is on.

proposals.behaviour: Paper funding: keep the nominal 'HSIP – EST' capital-plan line (SG142) alive as evidence that APS is funded. Use it to answer advocacy and oversight pressure ('it is in the capital plan'), even though the line cannot be funded as written.
proposals.trigger: Pressure event (advocate or oversight body asks about APS funding) while a placeholder line exists that has not yet failed eligibility review. Strongest in the period between the application deadline and the approval list (about 5 months).
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a second deflection response. Pressure is absorbed for longer without any application being submitted. The task goes to DEFLECTED with a longer hold time r_plan, and the placeholder resolves only at the C13 result, when pressure releases at once. This delays the realised cost-pressure signal and can lengthen time to first funded install.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 DEFLECTED covers answering with 'cost / no money' and pointing to SFCTA, budget or Caltrans (and 'planned, awaiting a window' is a form of pointing elsewhere). It has no rule that a placeholder line changes the deflection content or duration, and no cliff when the placeholder fails.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.1: the response pattern is 'respond to advocacy with cost and no funding' (MDC26 p.4-6, p.8). Also 'oversight does not work in practice, parties pass responsibility', labelled human-sourced fact. 01 section 2.1 also records SG136 'APS FY25' with no money row. 01 section 7 and the review notes treat the SG142 date as EST and a progress risk. Support for the exact behaviour (using the line as a shield) is an inference only; no direct document.
proposals.parameter: p_deflect_plan: extra deflection probability while a plan line exists, with hold time r_plan.
proposals.range: p_deflect_plan U(0, 0.5) added to p_deflect; r_plan U(3, 12) months (versus base r). 0 recovers the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 deflection branch (p_deflect, r). Conditioned on a state variable 'placeholder_line_active' that ends at the C13 decision.

proposals.behaviour: Risk-hedged split under a deadline. A2 prioritises a clean carrier-only SG015 package that is certain to be eligible and reaches BCR 5.0 without APS. It prepares an APS-containing package second, or not at all. The APS-containing package is not made by default to share an application with the carrier, because an eligibility rejection would sink the carrier too.
proposals.trigger: Prep time is nearly exhausted (days to deadline, D_prep + (m-1)*delta_split greater than remaining time) and APS-attached eligibility is uncertain.
proposals.effect_in_model: When time is short the order of preparation is chosen by eligibility risk, not by how the packing algorithm happens to order C and N groups. The clean carrier instance is protected from rejection; APS-bearing instances are the ones that become MISSED. In the model today this gives the same MISSED outcome but a different instance mix and a different correlation between instance outcomes.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 already splits into m instances by measure union and marks late ones MISSED. D3.3 treats C and N as separate independent groups. It does not choose which instance to finish first by rejection correlation, and a rejection in a mixed instance is not assumed to cost a clean carrier.
proposals.evidence: No document support for the ordering behaviour. Context only: 01 section 3.1 shows INS13 p.4 (APS-only ineligible) and the 'progress risk' note that the SG142 schedule conflicts with the C13 timing. 02 D3.3 says each instance is judged independently, so any hedge would need a new rule.
proposals.parameter: sw_hedge_order: switch (0 or 1) plus p_taint, the probability that an ineligible APS element makes the whole mixed instance fail instead of just the APS part.
proposals.range: sw_hedge_order in {0,1}; p_taint U(0, 0.5).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 preparation ordering at the deadline and D3.3 eligibility review (instance-level REJECTED rule).

proposals.behaviour: Shared preparer bandwidth and triage: with the owner gone, the remaining capital-application preparer(s) have one pool of prep hours for ALL fields (HSIP, Prop L, general fund, other SFMTA signal and safety projects). APS is a low-scoring, low-visibility, 'optional' item (policy does not require applying), so it is crowded out by deadline-bound or Board-visible applications. The preparer triages by deadline, fund certainty and BCR.
proposals.trigger: Owner vacancy plus hiring freeze while an HSIP deadline (C13 closes 2026-11-02; C14 next) or the CIP/budget cycle is open and competing applications demand the same person-weeks.
proposals.effect_in_model: Cross-field coupling of the task state machine. Today each field has an independent task (D3.1 'every field one task'), so PREPARING in HSIP does not delay PREPARING elsewhere. With a shared pool, p_start for the APS task falls when other fields' tasks are PREPARING, and the instance count m is capped at 1 during the vacancy. Outcome: more MISSED at deadline, fewer split bundles, APS dropped first.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-h only lowers owner one tier and aborts in-progress PREPARING with q_drop. strain(t) lowers p_start and K_crew (Signal Shop construction), but not preparer time shared across fields. R_other (D10) shares only the $10M funding cap with other SF HSIP applications, not preparer capacity. Partial overlap with M-B 'strain', but strain is not cross-field.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1: 'one associate engineer scores all applications' (MDC26t), a single point of failure (the 'only one' reading is marked inference). 01 s2.1: policy 'does not require applying for funds' (POL10 p.2), so APS is the optional item to drop. 01 s2.2: CIPpol p.6 funds 'urgent needs by phase', no accessibility category (CIP25 p.4). No document directly shows the triage behaviour, so it is an inference.
proposals.parameter: w_crowd (crowd-out weight) in [0, 3] logit units, plus m_cap_vac in {1, unlimited}
proposals.range: w_crowd ~ U(0, 3); subtract w_crowd * (number of other fields in PREPARING within the same quarter) from the p_start logit; m_cap_vac applies for t_vac months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start formula (add the term) and the PREPARING instance count m; active during F-h vacancy; independent of the M-A to M-D switches

proposals.behaviour: Tacit-knowledge loss and template re-use: the departed owner held the scoring tool, the candidate list, the BCR carrier tricks (for example SI02 as the carrier), and the contacts at SFCTA and Caltrans. The successor or caretaker either re-files the last package unchanged (rolling over the previous year's instance, no APS add-on) or needs far longer to prepare a new one. Alternatively they ask for outside consultant help.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy begins and an application window opens before a replacement is hired (the model's own t_vac U(3, 18) months against a 6-9 month hiring time and a 2-year HSIP cycle).
proposals.effect_in_model: Prep time D_prep is inflated and the BCR package quality is degraded for the duration of the vacancy: in the HSIP route, the carrier set is limited to the previously used measures (SI02/SI18PB without the APS add-on), and the SI02 carrier switch (sw_si02) is effectively off for any package prepared during the vacancy. Also lowers the probability that the 'APS rider' is added at all.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-h gives only an owner tier drop plus q_drop; D_prep is a constant U(1, 6) independent of staffing; delta_split is independent of who prepares. The sw_si02 carrier switch rests on an author interview with no public Caltrans ruling (01 s3.1), and the model treats it as a global switch, not as person-dependent knowledge.
proposals.evidence: 01 s3.1 hard facts: SI02 as APS carrier rests on 'author interview (first-hand), no public Caltrans recognition', which means the know-how is oral and person-held. 01 s2.1: one engineer scores everything; 'easy intersections already installed, harder and costlier since'. No direct document on handover or knowledge loss, so 'no document support' for the loss rate itself.
proposals.parameter: kappa_know (multiplier on D_prep) and q_template (probability the instance is a plain re-file without APS/carrier add-on)
proposals.range: kappa_know ~ U(1, 2.5) applied for t_vac months; q_template ~ U(0, 0.6)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 preparation duration D_prep + (m-1)*delta_split, and D3.3 carrier selection (sw_si02 / s_12in_C availability) for packages prepared during F-h vacancy

proposals.behaviour: Vacancy as a stated reason (a new deflection reason and a longer wait): staff answer APS pressure with 'we have no staff and the post is frozen', then wait for the freeze to end or for a new hire before touching the request. This is a stall tactic with a visible end date, not just a cost excuse.
proposals.trigger: Pressure event (advocate request, MDC question, demand letter) arrives while the post is vacant and the freeze is in force.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises p_deflect and lengthens r (recovery from DEFLECTED to IDLE) during the vacancy, and may shift the deflection target to 'wait until strain_end' so that the task cannot restart before the freeze lifts; also lowers the future pressure effect, because an excuse that cites a visible constraint is harder to counter. Outcome: fewer starts at the very time pressure may be highest.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 DEFLECTED with p_deflect and r exists, but the reason is cost or 'no funds'. In D3.2, p_deflect is 0 in M-B (staff strain) and is on only in M-A/M-D, so the model forbids staff-shortage deflection from co-occurring with the strain mechanism. Hence the vacancy-reason deflection is not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 'decision rule (response pattern)': the responses to advocates are 'cost' and 'no funds' (MDC26 p.4-6, p.8: 'selected based on funding'), and the author's first-hand 'buck-passing'. 01 s2.2: hiring freeze context (sfmta-media-41700). No document shows staff shortage as the stated reason: no document support for that specific reason.
proposals.parameter: d_vac (additive logit increment on p_deflect) and r_wait (switch: r = max(r, remaining freeze months))
proposals.range: d_vac ~ U(0, 2); r_wait in {0, 1}
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch; D3.2 matrix row 'p_deflect > 0' (decouple from the M-B on/off setting for the vacancy period); uses strain_end (D10)

proposals.behaviour: Labor-cost reclassification to capital: since the frozen post cannot be filled and Signal Shop time is partly funded from operating money, staff re-tag work orders so that APS-adjacent hardware or electrician time is booked to a capital project (SG000 reserve, an existing signal capital line or a project-support fund). That keeps some installs moving without a new application or a new hire.
proposals.trigger: Hiring freeze plus operating deficit, with the capital line (project support fund) able to absorb labor (8 of 21 electrician posts already charged to project support).
proposals.effect_in_model: A quiet partial restoration of K_crew and of funding for some Fi intersections without passing through the A2 application state machine (no SUBMITTED, no HSIP). It bypasses the 'design complete and funding secured' gate for a small number of intersections, or lowers strain/phi for the freeze period. It also creates a risk branch: a later audit or board reaction cancels it.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. PW5 (design standard) adds APS to a maintenance work order within the b_hw budget and PW6 uses SG017; but reclassifying Signal Shop labor to a capital code (a funding-source substitution rather than a new line) is not a rule. q_dir covers the commissioner's 10% / SG000 as a binary, not as work-order reclassification. Overlap with PW5 is partial and must be checked.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 'decision rule': the 2025-02 budget options include 'move 25% of paint and sign shop staff to capital priorities' and 'restructure work orders so they count as capital projects' ($2.5M, T/staffing/sfmta-media-41700.txt p.9, p.17), not naming Signal Shop; 01 s2.1: 8 of 21 electrician posts on project support fund (38%, ASO27 p.123). 01 s2.2: CIPpol p.10 intends to 'widen the capital definition'. Support is indirect.
proposals.parameter: sw_reclass (switch) with q_reclass (probability per year per vacancy that a reclassification covers APS work) and a_reclass (dollars per year)
proposals.range: sw_reclass in {0, 1}; q_reclass ~ U(0, 0.3); a_reclass ~ U($0, $150k) per year; expires when strain_end passes or with probability q_audit ~ U(0, 0.3) per year
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 internal route (adds a funding source into the Fi design/construction queue without a batch award) and the K_crew computation under strain (D3.2 M-B row)

proposals.behaviour: Cost-line carving: A2 keeps APS hardware cost out of the HSIP application (or lists only the carrier, e.g. SG015 visibility upgrade or SI02 or a new countdown head). APS is then installed with local SG142 money, or added later as a construction change or scope add-on under the same contract. APS reaches the intersections but is not part of the funded scope.
proposals.trigger: Deadline is within days, APS-only is ineligible, and the full-cost BCR with APS is thin or the 10% match is tight. A2 wants the cleanest possible 'safety project' on paper.
proposals.effect_in_model: The BCR denominator and the 'extra budget' ledger change. With carving on, the application cost excludes the APS part, so BCR rises and more packs clear 5.0 (F-a fires less). The APS cost shifts to the local line (A_local / SG142) or to a post-award add event, and it is delivered by Signal Shop only if local money and K_crew allow. A new failure branch appears: the add-on is refused at construction (q_addon_fail), so the intersection returns to the backlog pool. The cost_by_actor split between HSIP and local also changes.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.3 fixes the BCR denominator at full project cost (carrier + APS + eligible incidentals) regardless of where the money sits. PW1 bundles APS with SG015 inside the application. No rule lets A2 choose not to put APS in the application. This is not captured.
proposals.evidence: No direct document support for the carving itself. Indirect support: 01 §2.1 'riding on existing works is cheapest' and 'all new signals and major upgrades install APS' (MDC23 p.6, MDC26 p.7). 01 §2.4 / QA13 Q1-Q2 allow APS to ride with new SI18PB heads. 01 §2.2 shows SG142 ($488,144) already sits in the CIP as an HSIP C13 'EST' line. The rule that non-safety items are capped at 10% of construction cost (LAPG ch.9 p.4) is the constraint that may or may not bite.
proposals.parameter: aps_in_app
proposals.range: Discrete {0 = APS cost in application (current rule), 1 = APS carved out to local funds, 2 = APS added post-award}. Prior: equal weights. With 2, q_addon_fail U(0.2, 0.8) and t_addon U(3, 12) months.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 route A, 'BCR denominator uses full project cost', plus the cost_by_actor accounting in D4. Add one branch in D3.4 delivery for post-award add.

proposals.behaviour: Strategic parameter selection to clear the BCR threshold. A2 picks the crash window (3 or 5 years), the service-life rule, the affected-zone fraction, the carrier mix, and which intersections to include so the pack just passes 5.0. Examples: take whichever window gives more pedestrian crashes, treat f_aff near its upper end, drop a weak intersection at the last step.
proposals.trigger: A pack lands just below 5.0 close to the deadline, with no time to find a new high-crash site. Caltrans has said it wants to fund all qualifying BCR applications, so the effective cut-off may be the 5.0 floor itself.
proposals.effect_in_model: A2 chooses the Y_win / L_rule / f_aff combination per instance instead of drawing it randomly. BCR becomes upward-biased near the line. More instances are submitted with a BCR just above 5.0. If c_final is higher than that, they are rejected more often (F-b). This sorts out whether the main failure is 'cannot reach 5.0' or 'reaches 5.0 only by optimistic choices and then fails the final cut-off'.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D10 treats Y_win and L_rule as equal-probability random draws, and f_aff as a random U(0.5, 1.0). The packing algorithm drops a junction when the pack BCR falls below 5.0, but it does not tune the evaluation assumptions. The all-f_aff = 1 case is called only an upper bound, not an actor choice.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.4: 'Caltrans said it wants to fund all qualifying BCR applications, so the threshold may be 5.0' (QA13 l.555, Q65). Threshold history 3.5 / 7.5 / 12 / 18 / 7 (QA13 Q69; SL13 slide 22). No document support that real staff tune assumptions.
proposals.parameter: bcr_tuning
proposals.range: 0 to 1: probability that A2 takes the max-BCR option among the admissible Y_win / L_rule / f_aff combinations. 0 gives the current random draw. Default prior U(0, 1). Cap f_aff at 1 only as the upper bound.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 route A: the draw of Y_win, L_rule and f_aff, and the pack step ③ in the packing algorithm.

proposals.behaviour: Belief-driven carrier choice with pre-submission asking. A2 acts on its belief about whether SI02 (12-inch heads, backplates) is accepted as an APS carrier, not on the true state. A2 may ask Caltrans Local Assistance or the district ahead of the deadline. Where the answer is unclear, A2 avoids the doubtful carrier and uses only the safe one (new countdown heads, SI18PB, or an LPI).
proposals.trigger: The SI02 carrier rests only on the author's interview with no public Caltrans ruling, the deadline is next week, and a wrong guess means rejection at the eligibility check.
proposals.effect_in_model: Splits the SI02 switch into a world state and an A2 belief. If the belief is 'unusable', C-type packs shrink to SI18PB / SI22PB carriers even when SI02 is truly allowed. This lowers the number of packable intersections and the BCR. If the belief is 'usable' and the truth is 'not', packs with SI02 are submitted and rejected at the eligibility check. A query event may update the belief, with a delay that can cost the window.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.6 says sw_si02 only decides whether SI02 is usable, and it is a world parameter. A2 has no belief variable and no query step. The rule 'always report the unusable branch in parallel' is a scenario split, not actor behaviour.
proposals.evidence: 01 §3.1 hard facts: SI02 as carrier comes only from the author's interview, with 'no public Caltrans ruling'. 01 §2.4: the 2025-12 advisory committee said 'HSIP does not fund APS-only projects' and 'will study again'. The C12 result for pure APS was 0/3.
proposals.parameter: p_belief_si02
proposals.range: A2's prior that SI02 is usable, U(0, 1). With a query event: q_ask U(0, 1) probability of asking before the deadline, t_reply U(0.5, 4) months, and the reply equals the true state with probability 0.8 to 1.0.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 route A carrier choice (the 'highest BCR combination' selection) and the sw_si02 handling in D3.6. Add an A2-belief variable in O2.

proposals.behaviour: Waiting for a rule change. A2 does not file an APS-bearing application this cycle (or files only the safe carrier). It holds the APS line for the next window because it expects Caltrans to relax or clarify the APS-only rule, with the advisory committee having said it would study it again.
proposals.trigger: Deadline pressure plus an open-ended 'we will look at it' signal from Caltrans. Delay is cheap for A2 because no policy requires it to apply for money (POL10 p.2).
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers p_start for the HSIP field in the current window and shifts the start to C14 (2028-07), producing MISSED / IDLE without any pressure or deflection. Adds a decay: if no rule change shows up, the wait belief drops after each window.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly, and not in this form. DEFLECTED covers answering pressure with 'no money'. D11 explicitly lists 'relaxing the APS-only rule' as not modelled, and D3.3 deleted a rule-relaxation switch because no rule can be put on the ground. That excludes the rule change itself, not A2's act of waiting on the hope of one. The p_start logistic has no 'waiting for a signal' term.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.4: 2025-12 advisory committee minutes, 'HSIP does not fund APS-only projects; will study again' (T/peers/caltrans-hsip-meeting-minutes-20251211.txt p.3). 01 §2.1: no policy duty to apply for funds. No direct document support that SFMTA staff do this.
proposals.parameter: w_wait
proposals.range: Subtracted from the p_start logit in the HSIP field only: U(0, 1.5) logit units. Decays each window by a factor U(0.3, 0.9) when no relaxation occurs. Set to 0 for control.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start formula (add the term −w_wait·wait(t) for HSIP) and the DEFLECTED / IDLE reset.

proposals.behaviour: Scope-stretch of the carrier line: the preparer widens SG015's corridor list or its 'selected corridors' wording so that more unfunded C-type intersections count as carrier sites in the C13 package. This is done by a CIP or application wording change, not by waiting for C14.
proposals.trigger: Deadline is one week away and the five named SG015 corridors cover only about 1 unfunded C-type intersection, so the combined package would fail the 'fewer than 2 intersections' signpost. The only fast fix is to redefine the carrier scope.
proposals.effect_in_model: At C13 the PW1 candidate pool is no longer limited to the five SG015 corridors. With probability p_scope_amend it also includes other C-type intersections (drawn via s_12in_C). The cost is a scope-amendment delay t_amend added to prep time and an extra rejection risk q_scope for 'scope not matching the programmed project'.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.6 PW1 widens to other corridors only at C14, after the C13 signpost fails. Nothing lets A2 widen SG015's scope inside C13, and nothing models the amendment as a bureaucratic act with its own delay and risk. Not dropped, because the C13-time widening is absent.
proposals.evidence: 01 CIP27m l.2441-2446 (via 01 l.444): SG015 corridors are Alemany, Outer Mission, 25th, Brotherhood, Sunset; priority is multi-lane arterials where visibility could be improved using existing signal poles. 01 l.444 [inference]: SG015 and APS share only about 1 unfunded C intersection. No document shows the amendment practice itself, so no document support for the behaviour.
proposals.parameter: p_scope_amend (probability), with companion t_amend U(0,3) months and q_scope U(0,0.3)
proposals.range: p_scope_amend 0-0.5
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 packing algorithm step 1 (candidate set) and the D3.6 PW1 start condition at C13; adds a delay to the D3.1 PREPARING duration.

proposals.behaviour: Non-participating cost carve-out: the preparer moves the APS hardware cost out of the federal application. The application then holds only the carrier measures. The APS is paid fully from local money (the SG142 local line or the general fund) as non-participating work. That raises the application's BCR above 5.0 while the APS still gets installed.
proposals.trigger: The combined BCR of carrier plus APS (full cost in the denominator) falls below 5.0, so F-a blocks submission. Separately, SG142 is already programmed as a line with a fixed dollar amount.
proposals.effect_in_model: With the switch on, APS cost is removed from the BCR denominator and from the federal cost. It is added to a local cost counter and a local-funding dependency (q_local_ok). BCR rises, so more packages pass the 5.0 gate. In exchange the APS install depends on a local approval event, and with probability 1-q_local_ok the APS part falls back to the waiting pool.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.3 freezes 'BCR denominator uses full project cost (carrier + APS + eligible incidental), regardless of whether carrier money is in other plan lines'. APS is reported as 'additional budget' only and never leaves the BCR cost.
proposals.evidence: 01 l.637 (C4): 'eligible portion local pays only 10%, ineligible portion fully self-paid' shows the source recognises cost that is paid locally outside the federal share. Whether APS hardware can be carved out of the BCR cost is not confirmed, so this is weak support.
proposals.parameter: sw_aps_carveout (switch), plus local approval probability q_local_ok
proposals.range: sw_aps_carveout in {0,1}; q_local_ok U(0.3,0.9). Run as a sensitivity branch.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 route A 'BCR denominator' rule and the F-a gate; the 'additional budget' accounting.

proposals.behaviour: Rushed or thin submission: with the deadline close, the preparer submits an incomplete or lightly checked application instead of missing the window. It goes in on time but carries more defects (crash matching, missing eligibility documents, an open LRSP or flag question).
proposals.trigger: Remaining preparation time is less than the remaining work while the window closes in under a month. Missing the window means a two-year wait.
proposals.effect_in_model: At the deadline, an instance that is not ready is no longer always MISSED. With probability p_rush it is SUBMITTED anyway, with a higher eligibility-review rejection probability (+q_rush_rej) and a BCR error multiplier on the submitted value. Some MISSED outcomes become REJECTED outcomes, which differ in recovery path (F-c) and in how the failure is read.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 says that at the deadline unprepared instances are MISSED and ready ones are SUBMITTED. There is no partial or low-quality submission. F-c covers a red-flag rejection but not a quality penalty caused by time pressure.
proposals.evidence: No document support. 01 l.587 notes the LRSP can be revised or reconfirmed 'without having to be finalised by the submission date', so some paperwork can run in parallel, but that is not about thin applications.
proposals.parameter: p_rush with q_rush_rej
proposals.range: p_rush U(0,0.6); q_rush_rej U(0.1,0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 deadline transition (MISSED branch) and the section O3 eligibility review event.

proposals.behaviour: Decoupled fallback: when the combined carrier-plus-APS package looks risky, the preparer submits the carrier line (SG015 visibility) alone in C13 so the safer part is not lost. The APS part waits for C14 or goes local.
proposals.trigger: Estimated combined BCR is near the 5.0 line, or the 'fewer than 2 intersections' signpost is already visible, while SG015 is itself programmed in C13 at about $1.1M.
proposals.effect_in_model: A new branch in the PW1 package step. With probability p_decouple the carrier instance is submitted without the APS package, and the APS intersections go back to the waiting pool. This yields a carrier approval with 0 APS delivered in C13, instead of the whole package being dropped.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.3 splits packages by measure union (C pack, N pack) and F-g covers partner delay or cancellation. But a carrier-alone submission with deliberate APS deferral is not an actor choice. D3.3 step 3 stops adding intersections when package BCR falls below 5.0, which is a mechanical drop.
proposals.evidence: 01 l.442: SG015 ($1.1M) and SG142 ($488,144) are listed as two separate rows in the same plan and cycle, both funded 'CaltransFHWAHSIPCycle13(2027) - EST'. That makes decoupling a plausible administrative choice. No document describes an actual decoupling decision.
proposals.parameter: p_decouple, applied when package BCR is within a margin theta_bcr_margin of 5.0
proposals.range: p_decouple U(0,1); theta_bcr_margin 0.5-2.0 BCR points
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW1 start and D3.3 packing step 4 (package to instance).

proposals.behaviour: Portfolio triage across fields. With one fewer person, A2 stops treating each field's task as independent and ranks all open application windows by expected funding per preparation-month. The APS task is dropped (not started, not aborted mid-way) in a window that collides with higher-priority non-APS capital work, e.g. the HSIP deadline falling in the same weeks as CIP/budget cycle work, while the cheap local request is kept.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy of the informal owner plus hiring freeze, with two or more windows whose preparation periods overlap (e.g. HSIP C13 close on 2026-11-02 vs the annual CIP request), and APS has no mandated owner or deadline.
proposals.effect_in_model: p_start for the APS task in field X is reduced when a rival task is in PREPARING or about to open. Changes which windows get skipped (MISSED/IDLE), so the pathway signals (PW1 trigger 'C13 list has no SF APS') fire for a different reason: not-submitted rather than rejected.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 has one independent task per field and p_start has strain(t) (m_B) and costpress(t) terms; F-h cuts owner and aborts PREPARING with q_drop. None of these makes the start probability depend on competing tasks in other fields, so cross-field crowding-out is not modelled. Kept because the dependency is absent, not because it is stated.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.1 (decision rules): scoring has 'no cost or feasibility item' and policy has no duty to apply for funds ('无义务' inferred); 01 section 2.2: CIP draft rule funds 'urgent needs in phases (raising project/grant readiness)' and priority categories are SGR and street safety with no accessibility category; 2.2 also notes 89 vacant positions deleted and no new positions. No document directly shows APS being triaged against another application: no document support for the mechanism itself.
proposals.parameter: w_triage (crowd-out weight)
proposals.range: 0 to 1.5, default 0 (off); 0.5 to 1.5 in sensitivity
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 logistic p_start: add term -w_triage * n_rival_PREPARING(t), where n_rival counts non-APS tasks in PREPARING within the same D_prep horizon; active only while owner==0 (vacancy).

proposals.behaviour: Recycle-and-resubmit. Instead of rebuilding a package, the remaining staff re-file the previous cycle's package (same intersections, same measures) with little revision. Preparation is quick but the package is not re-optimised for BCR, ignores new crash data and newly eligible intersections, and does not re-split by measure union.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus deadline pressure when a prior-cycle package exists (e.g. C13 package available when C14 opens, or a prior N/C package that was rejected for BCR).
proposals.effect_in_model: D_prep and delta_split shrink sharply, so more instances are SUBMITTED rather than MISSED, but the D3.3 packaging algorithm (BCR-sorted greedy repack, re-split) is replaced by 'carry forward last set'. BCR and eligibility are therefore drawn from the old composition, raising F-a/F-b rejection risk and keeping the same intersections locked in a rejected alternative group.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.3 step 4 says a package under BCR 5.0 'is not submitted' (F-a) and repack mode re-optimises each round; F-b says 'resubmit next round, may change package' only as an option, with no cheap-copy variant or quality penalty.
proposals.evidence: No document support. Closest: 01 section 2.1 says easy intersections are already done and the rest are 'harder and costlier' (cost drift $20k to $40k floor), which is why an unrevised old package would drift; 02 D3.3 packaging algorithm is deterministic.
proposals.parameter: sw_recycle (switch) with recycle_prep_factor
proposals.range: sw_recycle 0/1, default 0; recycle_prep_factor U(0.3, 0.7) multiplies D_prep; recycled package skips repack and BCR is evaluated on old composition with current-year costs.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 preparation time (D_prep + (m-1)*delta_split) and D3.3 packaging algorithm steps 1-5, active only when owner==0 and a prior-cycle package exists.

proposals.behaviour: Stop-gap staffing through an acting designee or a contractor/on-call consultant for application writing, which a headcount freeze does not necessarily prevent, plus the loss of the departed engineer's tacit knowledge. The workaround restores part of the capacity after an onboarding lag but with a steeper learning curve in the first cycle.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy with freeze in force, and application work tied to project-support-fund or grant-funded labour (that is, non-headcount money).
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes the F-h recovery: instead of waiting for the whole t_vac, owner rises from 0 to an intermediate level after t_onboard, but D_prep is inflated by (1+nu) for the first cycle (lost knowledge or learning) before returning to baseline. Splits the single 'owner drops one tier until refilled' state into acting and no-cover branches.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-h models vacancy with owner dropping one tier and q_drop abort, then full recovery at t_vac; F-e models outsourcing but only for construction after a failed PIF, and sw_consult covers design consultants (CON 42 months), not application preparation. An acting/consultant substitute for the owner role and a knowledge-loss penalty on D_prep are not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.1: sub-grants pay Signal Shop labour, so SFMTA has an incentive to apply (inferred); one associate engineer scores all requests and 'only one person' is inferred, which supports knowledge concentration (MDC26t); 01 section 2.2: 89 vacancies deleted and 'no new positions'. No document directly shows consultants writing applications or an acting designee: no document support for the workaround itself.
proposals.parameter: q_cover (probability a cover arrangement is found during vacancy) with t_onboard and nu
proposals.range: q_cover U(0, 0.7), default 0; t_onboard U(2, 8) months; nu U(0.2, 1.0) multiplier on D_prep for first cycle after cover starts
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-h (owner restoration path and q_drop), D3.1 D_prep.

proposals.behaviour: Reframing the request into a funded category. With APS having no category of its own in the capital plan, the remaining staff relabel the request as signal state-of-good-repair or street/Vision Zero safety so that it fits a priority bucket, and fold the APS into a larger signal-replacement or safety line. Fund eligibility improves but the APS content is diluted: the line can be approved without APS being delivered, or APS is cut first when the budget is rebalanced.
proposals.trigger: A local general-fund or CIP request window opens while accessibility has no category and the budget is under pressure (capital moved to operating).
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises approval odds of the general-fund/CIP request (PW2 end, PW6) but adds a leakage term: a fraction of the funded line is spent on non-APS scope or the APS portion is reduced at rebalancing, so installs per dollar fall. Changes the PW2/PW6 outcome and the cost_by_actor accounting.
proposals.already_in_model: No. PW5 attaches APS to hardware replacement work orders and PW6 adds APS to the SG017 replacement grant text, but both are delivery-rule or grant-wording changes; no rule lets A2 relabel the request category for approval or models dilution, and the general-fund approval chance is not tied to how the request is labelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2: FY25-29 CIP priority categories are SGR, street safety, zero emission, etc., 'no accessibility category' (CIP25 p.4); FY27-31 CIP plans to broaden the definition of capital investment to cover life extension of maintenance; 2025 budget option 'restructure work orders so they count as capital projects' (T/staffing/sfmta-media-41700.txt p.9, p.17); also 2.2 shows FY27/28 street-safety emphasis names no APS (BB27 p.6-7).
proposals.parameter: q_reframe with d_dilute
proposals.range: q_reframe U(0, 0.8) (share of local requests relabelled), default 0; approval multiplier +0 to +0.3 absolute probability; d_dilute U(0, 0.5) share of the funded line not spent on APS
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2 'general fund annual request' approval step, PW6, and D3.4 delivery capacity for lines funded this way.

proposals.behaviour: Stale carry-forward packaging. With the post empty, A2 does not re-optimise the HSIP package. It recycles the previous cycle's package, or the existing CIP line as written (a pure-APS line, an un-split C+N bundle, the old intersection list), and submits it with minimal edits. Preparation time falls, but the package is not re-sorted by BCR, not split by measure-union, and not checked against current eligibility.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy is active (F-h / F-i state) and a window with a deadline opens (HSIP biennial deadline, or the local window of Jan to Jun).
proposals.effect_in_model: Replaces D3.3 packing steps 2 to 5 (BCR sort, measure-union split, 5.0 gate) with a copy of the last submitted instance set. Effects: D_prep is multiplied down, so more PREPARING tasks finish before the deadline. The instance is more often ineligible or below the cut line, giving more F-a / F-b / F-c outcomes and fewer APPROVED. The 3-measure cap and the pure-APS ineligibility are no longer silently repaired. This turns 'vacancy = fewer starts' into 'vacancy = more starts of lower quality'.
proposals.already_in_model: Not covered. F-h only lowers owner and aborts PREPARING with q_drop. D3.3 always runs the frozen greedy optimiser at submit time. D3.1 has no quality dimension for an instance.
proposals.evidence: 01 s3.1 hard facts: SFMTA's own SG142 (pure APS, $488,144) 'is ineligible in C13 as currently written' and exceeds the $360k cap, so a CIP line was carried as written without being repackaged. 01 s2.1 row 'Accessibility: SG136 planned HSIP C12 money was not applied for' (line 549, P1). Not direct evidence of vacancy behaviour, but it shows the low-effort path exists. Otherwise: no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_stale
proposals.range: Bernoulli per submission while vacant, p = U(0, 0.8). On a hit: D_prep x U(0.3, 0.7); package = previous instance set unchanged, with no repack and no split. Passes the 5.0 gate only by its old BCR recomputed on current costs (u0 / g_cost drift).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 packing algorithm (steps 2-5) and D3.1 PREPARING duration. Active only when F-h vacancy is on.

proposals.behaviour: Vacancy lets the administrative obligations lapse. The same person handles the back-office duties that keep SF eligible and projects alive: LRSP renewal, red-flag remediation, E-76 / PIF paperwork, the 5-year extension request. With the post empty these tasks are late or dropped, even when no new application is started.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy is active and any in-flight obligation exists (LRSP expiry month, a red flag, a PIF or CON E-76 milestone, a 5-year check).
proposals.effect_in_model: Stretches durations (t_lrsp, t_fix, t_pif, t_dsg, t_con) by a multiplier while vacant. Raises the chance that LRSP lapses before the review date, so the whole agency is ineligible, which is a collateral loss for other SF applicants too. Raises the chance that a milestone is missed and flagged, which feeds back into later eligibility reviews. It adds a second route from vacancy to lost funding that does not go through p_start, and it hurts projects already funded.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-h touches only owner and PREPARING. t_lrsp, t_fix, t_pif and t_dsg are fixed draws that do not depend on staffing. strain only lowers K_crew and p_start.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1: one associate engineer scores all applications and a senior engineer manages the signal group ('only one person' is an inference), line 106. 01 s5 table: hiring an approved vacancy takes 6 to 9 months (citywide average 8 months), line 583. No direct document of lapsed paperwork: no document support.
proposals.parameter: nu_vac
proposals.range: Multiplier on t_lrsp, t_fix, t_pif, t_dsg while vacant: U(1.0, 2.5). Plus a per-milestone drop probability q_miss_admin U(0, 0.3), after which the milestone becomes a red flag.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 eligibility review (LRSP continuous-state rule) and D3.4 HSIP milestone nodes. Switch tied to F-h / F-i.

proposals.behaviour: Funded-position workaround to the freeze. A2 argues the vacancy is cost-recovered from capital or grant funds and so is not 'non-essential hiring'. The post is refilled as a limited-term or project-funded position, or a consultant or other division covers it. This is only possible if some APS money already exists. So vacancy length depends on funding state: no money means no hire means no application.
proposals.trigger: A funded APS line or approved project exists, or a project-support fund line is available. Competes with the freeze (F-i).
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes t_vac endogenous. With funding, vacancy ends early after t_short. Without funding, it runs the full t_vac plus any freeze remainder. This creates a lock-in loop: after SG105 ran out, no hire, so no application, so no money. It lengthens the P1 cliff (zero internal installs for four cycles) in M-A and M-D, and it makes the PW1 / PW2 first funding awards matter more than their dollar size, because they unlock staffing.
proposals.already_in_model: Not covered. F-h has an exogenous t_vac U(3, 18). F-i's recovery is 'freeze ends; or outsource (as F-e)', and the outsourcing in F-e is for construction only, not for grant preparation.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1: 8 of 21 electrician posts sit on the project-support fund, 'expected to be recovered from capital projects' (38%), line 107. 01 s2.2: the 2025-02 budget options 'move 25% of paint and sign shop staff to capital priorities' and 'restructure work orders so they count to capital projects' (T/staffing/sfmta-media-41700.txt p.9, p.17). 01 s2.1 incentive row: grants pay Signal Shop labour and ease the operating deficit. The 9145 eligible list grew to 41 during the freeze (2025-05), so hiring exceptions do occur. Direct evidence for a grant-writer post: no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_exempt
proposals.range: Probability U(0, 0.7) per quarter that the vacancy is converted to a capital-funded limited-term post, conditional on APS funding in the system (A_local > 0 or any APPROVED instance). On success the vacancy ends after t_short U(2, 6) months and D_prep x kappa_learn U(1.0, 2.0) for t_learn U(3, 12) months. Without funding q_exempt = 0.
proposals.rule_modified: F-h (t_vac becomes state-dependent) and F-i (freeze recovery), plus the D10 rows for t_vac and strain_end.

proposals.behaviour: Competing-queue triage. A2's grant-preparation capacity is shared with every other SFMTA capital application. With one fewer person, APS is the first item cut, because APS is not a named category in the capital priorities and the scoring tool has no cost or feasibility term. The task does not simply 'fail to start': it is bumped by a higher-priority application that falls in the same window.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus overlap of the HSIP deadline (2 November in a cycle year) with other agency application deadlines or the CIP / budget season.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a shared prep-capacity pool across fields X. At each window, tasks are served in priority order and APS is ranked behind the exogenous competing workload. Tasks that do not get capacity go straight to MISSED. This makes p_start correlated across fields in the same month. It also makes the HSIP window and the local window interact, which the model's per-field independent state machines do not allow. It reduces effective starts in exactly the months when pressure(t) is high.
proposals.already_in_model: Not covered. D3.1 runs an independent state machine per field. strain(t) lowers p_start globally but there is no capacity budget or ordering, and non-APS workload is not an entity.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: FY25-29 CIP priority categories are SGR, street safety, zero emission, Metro modernisation, Building Progress, cable cars, with no accessibility category (CIP25 p.4); grant rules 'prefer expansion over maintenance' (CIPpol p.11); budget options 'phase funding by readiness' (CIPpol p.6). 01 s2.1: scoring has no cost or feasibility term (TOOL p.2-5). The supporting inference that A2's capacity is shared is not documented: no direct document support.
proposals.parameter: L_comp
proposals.range: Exogenous competing prep workload, in person-months per window: U(0, 1.5) x capacity. Capacity = 1 - vacancy_share (U(0.3, 1) while vacant). APS priority rank w_aps U(0, 1). If L_comp x (1 - w_aps) exceeds free capacity, the task is set to MISSED.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 IDLE to PREPARING transition (replaces independent p_start by a capacity-gated draw during windows). Interacts with m_B / strain.

proposals.behaviour: Cost-narrative padding. Under pressure, A2 does not only say 'costly' in the meeting (the model's DEFLECTED state). It also carries the high-end cost framing into the application itself: more contingency, higher assumed per-site price, 'worst-case' pipe and ramp scope. That pushes BCR toward or below the 5.0 gate and makes 'too costly' come true on paper.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event hits the A2 task while the window is open, and the A2 task is in PREPARING or about to start.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises c_full, u0 and the pipe/ramp add-ons (and effectively kappa_cont) for packages built while pressure(t) is high. Lowers package BCR. This raises the rate of F-a (BCR<5, cannot submit) and F-b, and shrinks the packages that clear the threshold. It differs from p_deflect, which only skips the task. This one yields a submitted-but-weak or non-submitted application.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly adjacent but not covered. D3.1 has p_deflect (a verbal reply, task goes to IDLE) and D3.5 F-f has an exogenous kappa_cont U(5%,15%) and overrun noise. Neither ties cost estimates to pressure or to the speaker's incentive. Not in D3.2 switch matrix. Kept as a new endogenous cost-framing link.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 row 'Adjustable parameters' (line 127): the senior engineer says unit cost 'can easily exceed 500' (thousand). Row 'Decision rule (response pattern)' (line 130): the 2026-07 MDC briefing spent 3 pages on 'Technical Challenges & Cost' and quoted the $1.5M upper end. No document shows padding inside actual applications, so the application-side half is 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: psi_pad (cost-framing inflation), applied as multiplier (1+psi_pad*1[pressure(t)>theta_p]) on c_full, c_cd and the pipe/ramp add-ons in the packing step
proposals.range: 0 to 0.4 (0 = control, 0.2 = baseline guess); sweep as a sensitivity, never pooled with the base
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 route A packing algorithm (step 2 single-intersection BCR) and the two BCR gates; links to D3.5 F-a and F-b.

proposals.behaviour: Soft pledge / timeline promise. In reply to pressure, A2 does not say 'no money' flatly. It says it will 'look at the next HSIP cycle', 'prioritize as funding allows', or 'most will be installed in the coming years'. This sets advocates' expectations and cools their pressure, but it creates no task, no PREPARING state, and no commitment to start.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event when A2 has no open window or no ready package, so a real start is impossible.
proposals.effect_in_model: On the 1-p_deflect branch, a fraction q_pledge of events decay pressure(t) faster (shorter k) and raise the advocates' tolerance, which lowers their escalation hazard (lambda_press) for a lag t_pledge. Task state is unchanged. Result: pressure disappears without any p_start increase. Later, if nothing happens, trust drops and escalation jumps (a one-time larger enforce step). This produces the pledge-then-silence pattern.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 has only two outcomes for a pressure event: DEFLECTED (r months, 'no lasting effect') or pressure kept in pressure(t) with k-month decay. F-m lets advocates go quiet at random but not because of A2 words. D3.6 PW3 escalation uses theta_idle but not a broken pledge.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 row 'Decision rule' (line 125): reports to MDC moved from '20 of 71 under way' (2018) to 'most will be installed in coming years' (2023, ~70) to 'about 1/3' (2026). That is a shifting public promise against falling funded share. Line 124: the rest are 'selected based on available funds'. No evidence of the effect on advocate behaviour, so that half is 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: q_pledge (probability a non-deflected pressure event is answered with a soft pledge) and k_pledge (months of accelerated pressure decay)
proposals.range: q_pledge 0 to 0.6; k_pledge 3 to 12 months; plus esc_jump U(1,2) on the later enforce step if no start within t_pledge
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 task state machine, the 'pressure event' branch; feeds pressure(t), enforce(t) and the lambda_press logic in F-m / PW3.

proposals.behaviour: Reclassifying Signal Shop work to capital. Because operating deficits are large and 8 of 21 electrician slots sit on the project-support fund, A2 favours work that can be booked to capital grants, and may relabel APS installs or hardware-swap work orders as capital-eligible maintenance. APS then gets done where labor is recoverable, not where need or score is highest.
proposals.trigger: Operating gap pressure (budget balancing) plus a CIP rule that widens the definition of capital investment; active in each budget cycle.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a funding path for C-type intersections that is not HSIP, not local dedicated, and not the b_hw hardware-swap rider. Intersections in a reclass-eligible set go to the internal queue, bounded by K_crew and a reclass budget. Also biases which intersections are chosen (those whose labor can be booked to capital), so it changes the sort order away from BCR.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW5 (D3.6) lets APS ride on button/hardware replacement through a maintenance allowance b_hw U($0,$300k). PW6 uses existing SG017 grants. Neither models relabeling of work orders or capital-definition expansion as an A2 choice. So only the reclass/labor-recovery selection bias is new; I drop the plain maintenance rider.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 'Decision rule' (line 158): 2025-02 budget options include 'restructure work orders so they count to capital projects'; line 159: FY27-31 CIP proposes to widen the definition of capital investment to maintenance extending life 5+ years. s2.1 line 104: 8/21 electrician slots on project-support fund, expected to be recovered by capital projects; line 113 (inference): SFMTA has a motive to apply for grants that pay Signal Shop labor. The documents do not name APS as a target of this, so APS use is 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: sw_reclass (0/1) with b_reclass (annual dollars of APS work booked to capital) and w_labor (weight on labor-recoverability in the choice of the next intersections)
proposals.range: b_reclass $0 to $400k/year; w_labor 0 to 1 (0 = BCR order only); sw_reclass off in M-A, M-B, M-C and on in a new M-E only
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 packing step 2 (sort order), D3.4 internal queue, and D3.6 PW5 as an alternate source of the b_hw allowance.

proposals.behaviour: List triage by re-scoring and re-labeling. To shrink the unfunded count that advocates cite, A2 moves requested intersections between categories (C, N, Fs, merged-into-project) or marks them 'covered by planned work', so the visible backlog falls without installs. The 'about 1/3 covered by projects' figure is the public face of this.
proposals.trigger: A disability council meeting or other review where the unfunded share is quoted; also when the 'merged into project' status is cheap to assert (parent project still unbuilt).
proposals.effect_in_model: The pool of 'pending' intersections that advocates and the monitor see shrinks at a rate rho_relabel per review, moving intersections to the Fs state with the parent-project delay (t_parent, pi), while the real chance of installation does not rise. Output metrics (share served, never_served) can look better than true delivery. Tests whether the model's outputs are sensitive to who classifies.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.4 already has 'merged into existing project' with probabilities pi for 'likely/unverified' parents, and the C/N/Fs categories exist as initial attributes. But categories are fixed at initialization (D1) and do not change as an A2 choice. So endogenous relabeling is new; a fixed pi is not.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 line 124: in 2026 the list was said to be about 75, 'about one third' covered by engineering; line 125: the covered share changed from 20/71 (2018) to 'most' (2023) to ~1/3 (2026), which is consistent with changing counts and categories. Line 122 notes score does not decide funding. No document shows relabeling itself, so the mechanism is 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: rho_relabel (per-review fraction of pending C/N intersections reclassified to Fs/merged status)
proposals.range: 0 to 0.15 per annual review; paired with pi_audit U(0.3,1) = share of relabels that later prove false and revert to the pending pool after an audit
proposals.rule_modified: D1 initialization (category fixed) and D3.4 'merged into existing project' row; changes the denominator used in D4 outputs.

proposals.behaviour: Post-overrun descoping and substitution inside the batch. After design shows conduit and curb-ramp needs, the A2 planner does not wait for a top-up decision. They re-cut the batch: swap the expensive sites for cheaper, no-excavation sites from the pending list, or convert a site to a hardware-only APS (no touching the existing ramp). The over-cost sites go back to the pool with no TERMINATED penalty.
proposals.trigger: Design-complete node (F-f discovery) where actual cost exceeds planned cost x (1 + kappa_cont) and the gap is large relative to the batch budget.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes the F-f branch. Today the gap is covered by contingency, then a top-up request (q_topup), then TERMINATED. With descoping, a share of overrun sites is silently swapped out before any top-up request. The batch installs more sites at lower unit cost and the swapped-out sites wait in the pool. This raises throughput and shifts which sites get served (cheap first, hard last), which the model's 'never_served' output would show.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.5 F-f only has 'use contingency, then top-up, else TERMINATED'. 02 D3.3 selects no-excavation sites at packing time (SG142 'about 22 sites, no excavation') and D3.4 says in-house sites must be design-complete, but nothing lets A2 re-select sites after the overrun is discovered. Not a duplicate.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1: senior engineer says not touching the existing ramp is 'five times faster' (MDC26t, stated, untested); 'easy sites already done, getting harder and costlier' (NA24 s1.4); SG142 written as 'no excavation, all built by Signal Shop' (01 s2.2, CIP27m l.292-294).
proposals.parameter: p_descope
proposals.range: U(0, 0.8) per overrun site; a second knob f_swap_cap in {0, 0.25, 0.5} caps the share of the batch that can be swapped (0 reproduces the current model).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f. Insert a step between 'overrun beyond contingency' and 'top-up request (q_topup)'. With probability p_descope the site is returned to the pool and replaced by the next cheapest candidate in the same batch. Otherwise the existing path runs.

proposals.behaviour: Cost-shifting the excavation part to another program (Public Works curb-ramp budget or a parent project), keeping only the APS hardware on the SFMTA line. The applicant argues that the ramp and conduit work belong to the ramp program or to the signal state-of-good-repair line, and asks the ramp program to build that part first.
proposals.trigger: Overrun is dominated by the ramp/conduit components, which have identifiable owners (the ramp program is funded separately and growing).
proposals.effect_in_model: Cuts the funding gap by a share rho_shift of the ramp/conduit cost. In return it adds a dependency delay on the other program (like t_partner), so the site waits for the ramp contract. It converts a funding failure into a timing failure.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW4 and D3.4 'folded into an existing project' attach sites to parent projects chosen at listing time, and F-g handles partner delay. Nothing allows A2 to move cost to another program after an overrun at design completion. Not a duplicate, but close to F-g in structure, so it could reuse t_partner.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.11: Public Works designs ramps with 'reservation for future APS' but ramp construction does not trigger APS; APS 'is MTA's business' (MDC26t); ramp budget growing $4.0M to $8.1M (FY27); Contract 35 delayed about 8 years by ramp design. 01 s2.1: pipe and ramp each about $200k.
proposals.parameter: rho_shift
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6) share of ramp/conduit cost moved; paired with t_shift U(6, 36) months added delay, drawn from the same distribution family as t_partner.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f gap calculation (gap = actual cost - plan x (1 + kappa_cont) - rho_shift x ramp_conduit_cost) and D3.4 timing (CON start = max(..., ramp program completion)).

proposals.behaviour: Holding the top-up request for a better window (timing and framing). A2 does not file the supplemental request immediately. They wait for the annual capital budget cycle or the next 5YPP window, or fold the request into a broader 'signal asset condition' ask. They may also request phased funding: fund remaining design and pause construction, rather than fund the whole gap.
proposals.trigger: Gap exceeds contingency while the request would compete with an operating deficit and a CIP described as 'not enough to fund all approved projects'; filing off-cycle looks likely to fail.
proposals.effect_in_model: Replaces the one-shot q_topup by a request that can only be decided at a cycle date. The project idles for t_wait months (it counts against the 60-month clock and against CON/PE red-flag limits), and q_topup is higher when filed at-cycle than off-cycle. This creates a trade-off between faster rejection and slower approval, and feeds F-d red flags.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 F-e uses t_pause (3 to 12 months) after a failed top-up, only for the outsourcing branch, and F-f has one q_topup draw with no timing. No cycle-gated request exists.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: CIP policy 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project/grant readiness)' (CIPpol p.6); capital revenue $246M lower, 'not enough to fund all approved projects' (CIPpol p.5, p.20); board wants diversions 'one-off' (CIPpol p.18, p.21); SFCTA precedent of a top-up request for another project (01 s2.11 / 2.3, as cited in F-f).
proposals.parameter: t_wait and q_topup_cycle
proposals.range: t_wait = months to the next cycle date (calendar-gated; in the model, cycle dates set by an input: annual in month 3 and an optional 5YPP date); q_topup_cycle = q_topup + delta with delta U(0, 0.3); off-cycle requests use q_topup - delta. Switch sw_cycle_gate in {0, 1}; 0 is the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f top-up request: event date moves to the next cycle date, success probability depends on whether it is at-cycle, and idle months accrue against the 5-year check in F-d.

proposals.behaviour: Re-labelling the overrun cost into a fundable category. The applicant records conduit, pole or ramp work as state-of-good-repair or 'extended-life asset' work, or as a part of a controller/hardware replacement work order, to draw on SGR or hardware replacement money rather than the (empty) APS-specific line.
