proposals.effect_in_model: Makes the SG017 block probability a state-dependent function of a failure-backlog shock instead of a constant, so PW6 fails more often in the months after a shock. It also adds correlation: a shock hits PW6 and the strain/cost mechanisms in the same period.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 and D10 have q_sg017_block (U(0.2,0.9)) for 'funds used by controller/failure-priority projects', but it is exogenous, constant and sits at SFCTA. No shock process or A2-side withholding exists (02 D3.6 PW6 row, D10 line 375). Kept because the decision is endogenous to A2 and time-varying, not covered by the constant.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 176: 'visible-failure-driven: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' [inference]; 01 §2.1 line 126 and §3 lines 446-447: FY25-26 $1M went to ~98 controllers with firewall flaws, even though the 2023 PIF listed APS replacement as eligible; FY27-28 use unknown.
proposals.parameter: lambda_out and blk_boost. lambda_out = outage/vulnerability shock rate, U(0, 0.5)/yr. blk_boost = additive logit shift on q_sg017_block for t_shock months after a shock, U(0, 2) in logit units, t_shock U(6, 24) months.
proposals.range: lambda_out U(0, 0.5)/yr; blk_boost U(0, 2) logit; t_shock U(6, 24) months. Setting blk_boost = 0 gives the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 signpost q_sg017_block, and D10 row q_sg017_block (made time-varying).

proposals.behaviour: Permissive scope wording versus explicit APS line item. The writer can put a named APS line with a dollar amount in the SG017 request, or leave APS only in the broad scope text ('where poles and conduit are satisfactory') and decide at spend time. An explicit line is easy for SFCTA to cut; vague wording keeps flexibility but gives no commitment and no accountable owner.
proposals.trigger: Preparing the FY27/FY28 SG017 allocation request when past allocations were all controllers, so an explicit APS line risks a scope challenge.
proposals.effect_in_model: Splits PW6 into two sub-modes. Explicit mode raises SFCTA scope-challenge probability and sets a binding, countable amount of money (higher owner/specified, lower flexibility). Vague mode lowers block probability but spends the money on controllers by default (leakage) and gives APS no protected funds.
proposals.already_in_model: No. PW6 treats the request as a single event where APS is 'written into' the allocation request; the only filter is the exogenous q_sg017_block. A2 has no choice about how the APS scope is expressed.
proposals.evidence: 01 §3 line 446: CIP scope text allows new APS 'where it is determined that existing conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition' (a conditional clause), while the 5YPP says only 'replace'. 01 §2.1 line 115: policy does not require seeking funds. No document support for how the request is actually worded.
proposals.parameter: sw_explicit (0/1) with p_explicit. If 1: block probability multiplied by m_chal and a_sg017 earmarked and protected. If 0: block probability multiplied by 0.5 but the realised APS share of SG017 drawn as U(0, a_sg017) and flows first to controllers when a failure shock is active.
proposals.range: sw_explicit Bernoulli, p_explicit U(0, 1); m_chal U(1, 2); leakage fraction U(0, 1).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 start; D10 q_sg017_block and a_sg017.

proposals.behaviour: Labor-recovery shaping: SFMTA writers size and select requests to fund Signal Shop electricians already booked to the project-support fund. This favors small no-excavation in-house C-class jobs (like the SG142 pattern of ~22 intersections) and disfavors N-class jobs or contractor work that does not pay for in-house labor.
proposals.trigger: A budget deficit combined with a hiring freeze and a share of electrician posts charged to project funds, so any grant that pays Signal Shop labor relieves operating pressure.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises p_start and the priority of in-house-installable requests when the deficit is high, and biases pack composition toward C-class. Increases throughput of the Fi queue but pushes N-class intersections to never_served.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in the rules. D3.1 p_start uses owner/specified/oversight/pressure/enforce/strain/costpress only; the labor-recovery motive appears in 01 as inference but has no parameter or term in 02. M-B strain only runs one way, as a brake.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1 line 104 (8 of 21 electricians on the project-support fund, expected to be recovered from capital projects); line 113 (grant pays Signal Shop labor, relieves operating deficit; marked inference); §2.2 line 158 (work orders restructured to count as capital); line 141 (SG142: ~22 intersections, no excavation, all Signal Shop).
proposals.parameter: w_labor, with an in-house bias b_in.
proposals.range: w_labor U(0, 2) logit, added to p_start only for requests where all intersections are in-house-installable; b_in U(0, 1) multiplier on the share of C-class in the pack; scaled by operating-deficit index (0-1).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start (add term + w_labor * labor_recovery_flag), D3.3 packing step (candidate ordering).

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS as a street-safety/Vision Zero crossing improvement to compete for money in categories that exist in the capital plan (street safety, the 25% baseline set-aside), instead of presenting it as accessibility compliance for which no CIP category exists.
proposals.trigger: Capital plan priorities list street safety but no accessibility category, and the writer needs a funded category to attach the request to.
proposals.effect_in_model: Opens a second local funding route for the APS request (general-fund baseline) with different selection: scored by crash exposure, not by APS list order. Moves money to high-injury intersections, away from the oldest requests, and removes the APS-specific accountability.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. A_local carries a general fund baseline ($0-0.57M), and Route B (crossing-only HSIP) scores by KSI crashes. But no reframing choice exists on the A2 side and no use of the 25% street-safety baseline pool.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 line 155 (priority categories include street safety; no accessibility category [inference]); line 147 (FY27/28 street safety focus does not name APS); line 142 (baseline general fund $65M/yr, 25% for street safety ≈ $16M [derived]).
proposals.parameter: p_reframe (A2 relabels the request) and a_ss (share of the street-safety baseline reachable).
proposals.range: p_reframe U(0, 1); a_ss U(0, 0.05) of $16M/yr; priority order changes to descending KSI instead of APS score when sw_reframe = 1.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.2 funding source and A_local (add a_ss), plus D3.3 ordering.

proposals.behaviour: Local-match substitution (supplanting): once an APS/SG015 HSIP application is submitted or awarded, finance treats the federal 90% as a reason to withdraw or defer the local flexible APS money (SG143 $570k general-fund baseline line, any APS use of SG000/director discretion) and redeploys it to the operating gap or to a higher-priority match. The 10% local share is paid in staff-hours (soft match), so the cash line is cut.
proposals.trigger: An APS-containing HSIP application is submitted or approved while the capital plan shows operating deficits and the rule that the most flexible money goes to match other grants. The deadline-week choice to book SG142 as 'HSIP-funded' triggers it.
proposals.effect_in_model: Local APS money available for later rounds, fallback paths (PW2 general fund, F-j/F-k recovery) and F-e/F-f top-ups falls after an HSIP submission. This makes HSIP success reduce fallback funding, so a later HSIP rejection (F-a, F-b) lands on a thinner local safety net. It also lowers q_topup for overruns.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k covers director 10%/SG000 'not used for APS' as an independent coin flip q_dir. Nothing links it to the HSIP submission or award, and costpress is a unit-cost term, not a diversion of money. No rule withdraws local money after a federal award.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'the most flexible money goes to match'; 'capital moved to operations, up to $40M per round'; 'board: diversion should be one-time ... dispersed, not leave a project without funds'; local flexible money for APS $0-0.57M/yr; 10% local match can be staff-hours soft match (01 s2.4 line 203, 'staff hours may count as soft match'). No document shows this being done to APS specifically: partial support only.
proposals.parameter: sw_supplant (0/1) with rate rho_supplant U(0, 1): the share of the SG143 general-fund APS line and of the q_dir-eligible reserve withdrawn within the same fiscal year as an APS-containing HSIP award or submission.
proposals.range: rho_supplant in [0, 1]; sw_supplant in {0, 1}; tested only in M-A, M-C and M-D mechanisms where local money matters
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-k (q_dir becomes conditional on HSIP state), PW2 and PW6 fallback availability, F-e/F-f q_topup

proposals.behaviour: Budget-line relabeling instead of application re-packaging: finance merges or renames the APS-only line SG142 into the SG015 visibility line (or records the APS cost as an incidental item inside the carrier) in the capital plan, so the plan row passes as an eligible carrier project. The package then carries APS cost with no separate budget row. The APS scope can then be trimmed quietly if the carrier is cut.
proposals.trigger: The application deadline is close, SG142 is APS-only and ineligible, and the manager needs the capital plan and application to match. Re-packaging takes the signal engineers' time, but renaming a plan line is a finance-only action.
proposals.effect_in_model: The APS 'added budget' becomes zero or hidden, the 22-intersection SG142 scope shrinks to the SG015 corridor intersections (about 1), and APS loses its own visible line. This raises approval odds in the current round but lowers the later accountability signal (oversight/specified drop) and raises F-g sensitivity (partner cancellation removes APS with no line to fall back to).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW1 bundles APS with SG015 on corridors (about 1 intersection) and the 'added budget' bookkeeping separates APS cost from the carrier. The model has no step where the plan-line identity itself changes, and no loss of the separate APS line or its oversight visibility.
proposals.evidence: 01 s3 (lines 442-444): SG015 $1.1M and SG142 $488,144 sit in the same CIP, same year, same HSIP C13 EST source; SG142 is APS-only and ineligible; SG015 scope is limited to five named corridors. 01 s2.2: CIP draft plans to 'expand the definition of capital investment' and a budget option to 'restructure work orders so they count as capital'. No document shows a line merge.
proposals.parameter: sw_line_merge (0/1) with p_merge U(0, 1): when SG142 is ineligible at deadline, the share of its scope folded into the SG015 carrier line; sets APS visibility oversight_drop = delta_vis in [0, 1] and removes the separate APS budget row when set.
proposals.range: p_merge in [0, 1]; delta_vis in [0, 1]
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 route A packaging step (candidate set, added-budget accounting), D3.6 PW1, and the oversight term in p_start

proposals.behaviour: Hold-and-defer at the window edge: the manager does not fund the extra preparation work for an APS-containing package (split/repack, cost estimates, carrier BCR) this cycle and instead holds the money and the staff estimate for the next cycle, saying 'we need better readiness'. The reason is readiness, not rejection.
proposals.trigger: One week to the C13 deadline, SG142 ineligible, and the draft rules fund urgent needs 'by stage (raise project/grant readiness)'; preparing a competitive BCR package costs staff time that is already scarce (hiring freeze, 89 positions cut).
proposals.effect_in_model: Produces a scheduled MISSED/skip decision by finance before the engineering task starts, so a window closes without the task state machine ever seeing it. The prep time D_prep and delta_split are not the cause: the funding gate is. Pushes APS to C14 (two years later) and shifts the whole delivery chain by one cycle.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 treats start as p_start logistic(owner, specified, strain, costpress); MISSED arises from not finishing prep. No finance-side gate before PREPARING exists; F-k is about reserves, not prep funding.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 decision rule: 'fund urgent needs by stage (raise project/grant readiness)'; 'no new positions'; 'delete 89 vacant positions'. No document says a project was deferred for this reason: no document support for the behaviour itself, only the rule.
proposals.parameter: p_gate U(0, 1): probability that finance releases prep funding for an APS-containing application in a given window; if it fails, task goes IDLE with a window skipped (new state SKIPPED_FIN) and a re-test at the next window.
proposals.range: p_gate in [0.2, 1.0]; reset each window
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 state machine: adds a guard before IDLE -> PREPARING; p_start = p_gate * logistic(...)

proposals.behaviour: Placeholder-awarding with swap: the capital plan keeps APS lines as 'EST' HSIP placeholders (SG142, SG143) and the manager re-uses the same federal-looking line for another project if the HSIP award is lost, with the APS row moving to a 'future cycle' label. The line is never zeroed, so it looks funded to outsiders (the board, advocates, MDC) while the money has gone.
proposals.trigger: HSIP result (F-a/F-b rejection) or a late-year need elsewhere, with the CIP rows labeled EST that need no board vote.
proposals.effect_in_model: The observable 'APS funded' signal (a plan row) diverges from the real funded state, so signposts and MDC/advocate pressure (pressure(t), oversight) react to a row that has no money. Delays the signpost used in PW1 (no SF APS in the C13 list) and PW2/PW6.
proposals.already_in_model: No. Signposts use C13 approved lists and board decisions, and no rule makes plan rows lie about funding.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: CIP rows 'EST'; board agendas Aug-Oct 2026 contain no HSIP or APS item; applications need no board vote (so the plan row is the only public trace). Support for the mechanism is indirect only; no document shows a swap.
proposals.parameter: p_stale U(0, 0.5): probability that after a rejection or de-prioritization the APS plan row stays on as a funded-looking row for t_stale months (U(6, 24)); during t_stale the pressure(t) decay on advocates' complaints is slowed by factor (1 - p_stale).
proposals.range: p_stale in [0, 0.5]; t_stale in [6, 24] months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW signposts (detect time of failure), pressure(t) update, F-b/F-c recovery timing

proposals.behaviour: Controller-first narrative drafting (scope laundering by precedent): the SG017 request text is written in the same 'controller / cabinet / detector / RRFB' vocabulary as past allocations, with APS listed only as an eligible-but-optional 'where conditions allow' item, so the request is easy for SFCTA to approve but APS can be dropped without anyone deciding to drop it. The staff member, not SFCTA, pre-empts APS at drafting time.
proposals.trigger: Past three SG017 allocations contain no APS; SFCTA staff are known to fund visible-failure items; the preparer wants approval certainty and a fast turnaround on a small $500k line.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a pre-submission filter inside the SG017/PW6 request: the share of the request that is explicitly earmarked for APS (a_sg017 as written in the request) is cut by a factor before SFCTA ever sees it. Currently q_sg017_block is applied only on the SFCTA side (scope limited to replace, or money used up by controllers); this adds an independent A2-side channel, so the model would otherwise put the whole blocking on SFCTA and misattribute it.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: PW6 and q_sg017_block (02 D3.6, D10 row q_sg017_block/a_sg017) model SFCTA limiting the scope or controllers consuming the money. NOT covered: the applicant itself under-specifying APS in the request text. Kept because the A2 side of the block is absent from D3.1 (A2 only has p_start, p_deflect, m splitting).
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.x SG017 facts (lines ~446-447): CIP scope text allows new APS 'where ... conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition', but FY24 allocation covered cabinets, detectors, RRFB and FY25-26 $1M went to ~98 controllers; 01 line 176: 'result is failure-driven: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (inference). No document directly shows how the request text itself was worded, so the A2-side effect is no document support.
proposals.parameter: phi_draft (APS earmark fraction retained in the A2-written SG017 request)
proposals.range: U(0.2, 1.0); 1.0 = APS written at full a_sg017; multiplies a_sg017 before q_sg017_block is drawn
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 request content / D10 a_sg017 (new multiplier applied at SUBMIT in D3.1)

proposals.behaviour: Condition-gated APS scope with a pole-and-conduit survey that is never funded: the CIP wording makes APS available only 'where it is determined that existing conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition'. The preparer can leave that determination undone (no survey, no list of qualifying intersections), which converts an eligible scope into a standing option nobody can draw on, with the justification that scope cannot be programmed without an engineering determination.
proposals.trigger: The request must name where APS goes, but surveys cost staff time and the same engineers are the Signal Shop strain bottleneck; naming sites would also commit SFMTA to deliver them.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a precondition to PW6: only intersections with a completed 'poles OK' determination can be written into the SG017 request. Without it, eligible C-type sites are zero regardless of a_sg017. Creates a time lag and a staffing cost before PW6 can start, and makes the first usable window later.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 treats 'existing poles OK' as a static type attribute (C class, s_12in_C etc. in D3.3 table) and PW6 uses it as given. No step in D3.1 to D3.6 requires a determination action by A2 before eligibility.
proposals.evidence: 01 lines ~446: CIP wording 'where it is determined that...' (quoted). No document support that SFMTA has or lacks such determinations; 01 line ~441 notes SID may not match the field and 38 of 76 are unsampled, which suggests the survey gap is real but is inference only.
proposals.parameter: sw_survey (0/1) and t_survey (months)
proposals.range: sw_survey in {0,1}; t_survey U(3, 18) months, with a survey capacity of n_survey sites per year U(2, 15)
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 trigger and D3.1 PREPARING duration (adds a prerequisite stage before D_prep)

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS as state-of-good-repair: because signals are described as one of SFMTA's most degraded assets and SGR money is 'extremely limited', the preparer labels APS replacement as end-of-life hardware (the first half of the CIP wording: 'Replace ... APS nearing end of useful life') rather than as new accessibility installs, so it competes under the SGR priority rather than under a category that does not exist for accessibility.
proposals.trigger: The CIP priority categories lack an accessibility category; SGR and street safety are listed; the request is competing inside a small SGR line.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes which sites qualify: replacement framing only works for intersections that already have an APS (useful-life replacement), which are not on the backlog of 76 sites lacking APS; so it shifts money to existing APS without adding backlog sites. In the model this is a leak: an APS share of the SG017 money is spent that does not reduce the list.
proposals.already_in_model: No. PW6 only covers new installs at C-type backlog intersections; D3.4 delivery counts installs only for backlog intersections. No leakage of APS money into replacements that do not move the backlog.
proposals.evidence: 01 line ~153: signals 'one of the most degraded assets, SGR funding extremely limited'; line ~155: FY25-29 CIP priority categories SGR, street safety, ... no accessibility category (the absence is itself inference); line ~446: scope text includes 'replace ... APS nearing end of useful life'. No document shows that SFMTA staff actually do this reframing.
proposals.parameter: leak_replace (share of APS-labelled SG017 money spent on replacement of existing APS)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6); reduces a_sg017 available to backlog installs by that share
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 internal delivery and PW6 funding (a_sg017 effective = a_sg017 x (1 - leak_replace))

proposals.behaviour: Hold-and-bundle for a later, better window (strategic waiting): rather than spending the SG017 $500k per year on APS, the preparer carries the APS candidates forward and waits to attach them to a partner project (such as a signal visibility corridor upgrade) or to the next 5YPP (2027 autumn to 2028) because a single bigger package has better BCR and a lower chance of controllers displacing it.
proposals.trigger: FY27 SG017 request deadline comes before the corridor/HSIP package or 5YPP window is ready; staff judge that a small APS line is more exposed to being re-prioritised than a joint package.
proposals.effect_in_model: Delays the PW6 SUBMIT by a number of cycles with a probability, and moves candidates from PW6 into PW1 or PW2. Models the 'wait for window' behaviour that D3.1 does not have: currently p_start with an open window starts PREPARING, and a failed or deflected task only returns to IDLE.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: PW1/PW2 sequences are triggered by failure signposts only (D3.6), and D3.1 has no voluntary skip while a window is open. Voluntary waiting with an open window is not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 line ~154: CIP rule 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project readiness)'; line ~68: SFMTA 'first meets obligations, protects SGR, raises application readiness by stage'. These suggest readiness-before-asking, but no document shows a skipped SG017 cycle.
proposals.parameter: p_wait (probability of skipping an open SG017 cycle for APS)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.5) per window; skip lasts 1 cycle (12 months), then tested again
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 IDLE to PREPARING transition (adds a skip branch with return to IDLE after r months, or direct hand-off into the PW1 start)

proposals.behaviour: Vehicle-sponsor swap: the finance manager keeps the APS-only line (SG142) as a placeholder but re-labels or merges it under an eligible host (e.g. the SG015 visibility upgrade) before the deadline, so the HSIP application can name a carrier. A budget-line move, not a project change; the line stays as the local-match source if the bundle wins.
proposals.trigger: Deadline within about a month, APS-only ineligible, and a funded eligible host (SG015) exists in the same cycle. Relabelling is cheap, reversible, and within the finance manager's control of CIP line structure.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lets PW1 start even when A2's task state machine has not prepared the bundle: the budget actor creates the carrier precondition. Removes F-g 'carrier missing' risk but ties the APS line to SG015 delay. Raises the chance a C13 instance contains APS; SG142 funding date tracks SG015's E-76.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW1 (D3.6) and F-g (D3.5) model the bundle and partner delay, but the bundle is generated only by the A2 task state machine (D3.1) and packing algorithm (D3.3 step 1). No rule lets the budget actor relabel a plan line to create the carrier link. Kept: the actor-initiated relabel is not in 02.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: SG142 'HSIP C13 - EST, FY28', about 22 intersections, no excavation, Signal Shop (CIP27m l.292-294, l.2511); SG015 HSIP C13 $1.1M (CIP27m l.1184-1186). No document shows an actual relabel (inference). Capability support only: 'reorganize work orders so they count as capital projects' (staffing p.9, p.17).
proposals.parameter: p_relabel (probability the budget actor relabels/merges the APS line under an eligible host before the deadline) plus switch sw_host_relabel in {0,1}
proposals.range: p_relabel U(0, 0.6); sw_host_relabel 0/1
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 route A step 1 (candidate selection) and D3.1 PREPARING: when sw_host_relabel=1 and the SG015 host is funded, the bundle instance is created by the budget actor independent of p_start, and its APS line inherits the host's t_partner delay (F-g).

proposals.behaviour: Reserve-for-match priority: ahead of the deadline the manager earmarks SG000 reserve or the 10% director margin as the HSIP local match backstop for the SG015 bundle and other federal bids, so flexible money goes where it leverages 90% federal funds and is unavailable for standalone APS spend.
proposals.trigger: Application needs 10% local match; CIP policy says the most flexible money goes to match and capital is short by about $246M; the deadline forces a visible commitment of match money.
proposals.effect_in_model: Turns q_dir (F-k) from an exogenous probability into a competition for the same pool. When many HSIP bids need match, less margin remains for APS; if the APS bundle wins, the margin is spent with federal leverage.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k has a flat q_dir U(0, 0.8) and D3.3 sets 10% local match, but neither models competition for the pool or match-first priority. Kept: the competition/earmark part is not in 02.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'most flexible money used for match' (CIPpol p.11); director may adjust capital budget up to 10% (RES l.22, l.82); staff hours count as soft match (QA13 Q14, Q59); SG000 $1.6M FY27 + $0.5M FY28 (CIP27m). Whether the pool is contested by other match claims is inference.
proposals.parameter: m_match_claim = share of the discretionary pool already claimed by other match needs; optional switch soft_match in {0,1}
proposals.range: m_match_claim U(0.3, 0.9); APS-available pool = (1 - m_match_claim) x pool
proposals.rule_modified: F-k and D3.3 (10% local match): replace the flat q_dir draw by a pool-capacity check of (pool - claimed) against the APS match need.

proposals.behaviour: Wait-for-result hold: the manager defers committing local money to APS until the C13 result is known, to avoid supplanting a pending federal bid, and releases the local line only after rejection.
proposals.trigger: A pending HSIP bid for the same scope; risk of double counting or federal ineligibility if local money is spent on the same intersections; low-visibility delay no committee reviews.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a lag between a failure signal (F-a/F-b rejection) and release of local money, delaying PW1 to F-k/PW2 transitions by t_hold months and avoiding double routing of the same intersection.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.6 transitions fire at signposts and move to the next available window, but no rule holds money after the signal. F-j has t_defer only for the Prop L amendment. Kept.
proposals.evidence: No document support for the hold itself. Related: 'fund urgent needs in stages (raise readiness)' (CIPpol p.6); 'one-time diversions' (CIPpol p.18, p.21); C13 results 2027-03/04 (02 D3.6 PW1).
proposals.parameter: t_hold: months between a failed bid and release of local flexible money; switch sw_escrow in {0,1}
proposals.range: t_hold U(0, 12) months; sw_escrow 0/1
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW1 signpost-to-local step and F-k: the local-money event is scheduled at signal time + t_hold when sw_escrow=1.

proposals.behaviour: Operating-to-capital reclassification of APS labour: the manager reclassifies Signal Shop labour on APS installs as capital (asset-life extension, or attached to a capital work order) so installs draw on capital or grant money, easing the operating deficit instead of using dedicated APS money.
proposals.trigger: A $307M operating gap and a CIP draft that proposes to expand the definition of capital investment; grants pay Signal Shop labour, which relieves the operating deficit.
proposals.effect_in_model: Creates a funding route needing neither HSIP nor a dedicated line: part of internal installs is funded by reclassified labour, bounded by an audit/eligibility ceiling, and queue priority tilts toward capital-eligible jobs, competing for K_crew.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW5 (D3.6) has a maintenance add-on budget b_hw U($0, $300k) per hardware event, which is a work-order add-on, not an actor decision to reclassify labour. No reclass share or crew-steering parameter. Kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'reorganize work orders so they count as capital projects' and 25% of paint/sign shop staff moved to capital ($2.5M; staffing p.9, p.17; Signal Shop not named); 'expand capital investment definition to cover maintenance extending life 5+ years' (CIPpol p.10); grants pay Signal Shop labour (01 s2.1, inference).
proposals.parameter: rho_reclass: share of APS-related Signal Shop labour cost charged to capital; switch sw_reclass in {0,1}
proposals.range: rho_reclass U(0, 0.5); sw_reclass 0/1
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 internal delivery funding check and PW5 budget b_hw: when sw_reclass=1, b_hw is augmented by rho_reclass x labour cost and queue priority favours capital-eligible installs.

proposals.behaviour: Capitalizing labour: the finance manager books the vacant engineer's remaining APS design/management hours, or the Signal Shop crew's APS installs, as capital-eligible work (reclassifying work orders as capital, or extending the capital definition to life-extending maintenance). This relieves the crew-capacity limit and the local-match burden without any new cash. Tactic is about changing the accounting category of existing labour, not allocating new money.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus hiring freeze plus operating gap (strain high, K_crew down) while a pending HSIP match or the internal APS queue needs staff time; strongest when an operating-to-capital shift is already on the balance list.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises effective K_crew or lowers the local cost of internal installs for APS (labour counted as capital or as soft match against the HSIP 10% share). Reduces strain-driven install stall in M-B/M-D and lowers cost_by_actor on the operating side. Cannot create a new application, so it only helps delivery and match, not p_start.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. D3.4 treats K_crew as fixed by strain(t) only; F-i only lists 'contract out (same as F-e)'. D3.3 says 10% match but has no labour-as-match switch. Closest: strain(t) and K_crew in D3.2, but no accounting reclassification rule.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2 rows 'FY27-31 CIP to expand the definition of capital investment to cover maintenance extending life 5+ years' (CIPpol p.10, l.159) and '2025-02 budget options: reclassify work orders so they count toward capital projects' (sfmta-media-41700 p.9, p.17, l.158). Also section 2.x HSIP row: 'staff hours may count as soft match' (QA13 Q14, Q59, l.203).
proposals.parameter: sw_capitalize_labor (0/1) with share rho_cap in U(0, 0.5): fraction of K_crew effort for APS installs charged to capital/soft-match instead of operating.
proposals.range: rho_cap U(0, 0.5); switch default 0 in M-A, on in M-B/M-D sensitivity.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 internal delivery (K_crew workload account) and D3.3 local match cost; adds a term in F-i recovery path.

proposals.behaviour: Dollar-neutral hold-and-wait: with no named owner to put forward a ready application, the finance manager does not reserve money but also refuses to release it. The unallocated signal reserve (SG000) is left as an uncommitted line and counted as a shared buffer that can be swept into higher-priority obligations (controller failures, contract obligations, operating transfers) at the next budget cycle, so the money disappears quietly instead of being rejected for APS.
proposals.trigger: Reserve exists and no ready APS application is on the table at the time of the biennial budget; operating gap and rule 'fund by phase, raise readiness first' make 'not ready' a sufficient reason to hold.
proposals.effect_in_model: Turns F-k from a one-shot Bernoulli (q_dir) into a state: the discretionary pool for APS drains over time while the post is vacant, so an application that arrives after hiring faces less slack. Raises the cost of vacancy duration t_vac beyond owner downgrade.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k has q_dir (director 10% / SG000 not used for APS), but it is a one-time Bernoulli draw with no time dependence and no link to vacancy or to other claimants. Not modelled: sweep depletion that depends on how long the post is vacant.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2: SG000 $1.6M (FY27) + $0.5M (FY28) unspecified signal reserve (l.139); rule 'fund urgent needs by phase (raise project/grant readiness)' (CIPpol p.6, l.154); board wants reallocations 'spread out so no project loses funding' (l.157); and section 2.3 row that SG017 FY25-26 money went to replacing about 98 controllers (l.447). No document directly shows a sweep when a post was vacant.
proposals.parameter: lambda_sweep: monthly hazard that uncommitted reserve is claimed by other priorities, multiplied by a vacancy factor (1 + v_vac when owner is vacant).
proposals.range: lambda_sweep U(0.01, 0.10) per month; v_vac U(0, 2).
proposals.rule_modified: F-k and the SG000/director-10% pool in D10; links to F-h t_vac.

proposals.behaviour: Ready-made match pre-commitment as a gatekeeping signal: the finance manager offers to fund only what arrives with a named champion and a completed scope (the 'readiness' rule), and also asks external advocates or another agency to bring the project to the budget office. Without an internal owner, the finance manager redirects the request to the sibling program that already has a delivery lead (e.g. corridor or signal-upgrade projects), meaning APS gets bundled as a rider in those instead of being treated as its own request.
proposals.trigger: A request for APS funding reaches the budget office while the informal owner's post is vacant; the budget office can say 'no sponsor, no money' without being seen to refuse.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a rule where the budget office's response depends on whether a sponsor exists; with no sponsor, funds are conditionally redirected to rider-on-corridor projects (PW4 corridor route), raising the share of intersections served by embed-in-parent but making them depend on parent delays.
proposals.already_in_model: Mostly not. F-h only lowers owner tier and drops PREPARING tasks; p_deflect sends pressure to SFCTA/budget/Caltrans but the model has no rule where the budget actor re-routes funding to rider projects as a function of sponsor presence. PW4 and 'embedded' route exist for delivery (D3.4), but are not triggered by a budget decision.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2 'fund by phase: raise project/grant readiness' (CIPpol p.6, l.154) and 'priority to growth over maintenance; most flexible money used for match' (CIPpol p.11, l.149); section 2.11 / CP-T p.11 that accessibility capital 'usually reflected in other departments' budgets including traffic and signals (APS)' (l.265). No document shows an actual re-routing in response to a vacancy.
proposals.parameter: sw_sponsor_gate (0/1) and p_redirect U(0, 0.6): probability that, with owner at the weak tier, an APS request is turned into a rider on a corridor/signal project instead of denied.
proposals.range: p_redirect U(0, 0.6)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (p_deflect splits into pure deflect vs redirect-to-rider) and D3.6 PW4.

proposals.behaviour: Soft-match and work-order recapitalisation. The finance manager covers the 10% local match for the APS/SG015 package with Signal Shop staff hours or by re-coding existing work orders as capital, not with new cash. This makes the package cheap to approve internally. It also pushes labour onto a crew that is already the binding constraint.
proposals.trigger: Deadline is next week, an unbudgeted APS add-on appears in the package, and the operating deficit makes any new local cash hard to release.
proposals.effect_in_model: The local-match cost to the budget actor falls to near zero for the APS portion, so internal approval becomes easier. The cost moves into crew workload, so strain(t) goes up and K_crew goes down after award. Net effect: a higher chance the package is filed, and a higher chance of later delivery delay or an F-f/F-e style funding gap.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D10 treats the match as a 10% cash share (section 5, 'HSIP local match', QA13 Q14/Q59). F-k covers the director 10% as a cash backstop. Nothing in 02 D3.3, D3.4 or D3.5 lets in-kind labour count as match or lets work-order recoding move cost into strain. The cash-versus-labour trade is not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2, decision-rule row: the 2025-02 budget options 'reorganise work orders so they count as capital projects' and 'move 25% of paint-and-sign shop staff to capital priorities' (T/staffing/sfmta-media-41700 p.9, p.17). 01 section 5 / QA13 Q14: 'staff hours can serve as soft match'. 01 section 2.2: the FY27-31 CIP proposes to 'expand the definition of capital investment'. The documents do not say this was applied to APS or to the Signal Shop.
proposals.parameter: softmatch_share
proposals.range: U(0, 1). 0 = match is all cash (current model). 1 = the whole 10% is covered by crew hours. Each unit of softmatch_share adds a crew-month load to strain(t) and lowers K_crew.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 local match and 'appended budget' accounting. D3.2 strain(t) (m_B channel). D3.4 internal construction queue (K_crew).

proposals.behaviour: Strategic withholding of the local backstop, plus a sweep of unobligated placeholder lines. The finance manager does not pre-commit local money to SG142 as a fallback, and at the next budget cycle sweeps the unobligated EST dollars to higher-pressure uses such as SGR or the operating gap. The reasons are to keep leverage so the application team has to file, and to protect the discretionary margin.
proposals.trigger: The HSIP outcome is not yet known and SG142 is not eligible as written. The operating gap is $307M or more, and the capital-to-operating transfer is already on the balancing list.
proposals.effect_in_model: After an HSIP miss, or after an application that was never filed, the chance that director discretion or other local money is available for APS drops over time. The failure paths F-b/F-c/PW1 that fall back to 'local' therefore end in dead ends more often. The model gets a decay in fallback availability instead of a fixed chance.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k (D3.5) and q_dir (D10) give a one-shot chance that the director's 10% or SG000 is not used. That is a static Bernoulli draw. The model has no time-dependent sweep, no link to the operating-deficit signal, and no 'withhold the backstop so the applicant must file' effect on p_start.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2: balancing list includes 'capital funds moved to operations' (BB27 p.2-3). CIP draft rules allow up to $40M diverted to operations, reduced to $20M, 'one-time' and 'spread out so no one project loses funding' (CIPpol p.6, p.18, p.21). 'The most flexible money goes to match' (CIPpol p.11). The rule that a placeholder is swept or kept in force is no document support.
proposals.parameter: sweep_rate
proposals.range: annual hazard U(0, 0.5) applied to any unobligated APS/SG142/SG000 placeholder dollars once an HSIP application fails or lapses. Optional switch backstop_commit in {0,1}. At 0, q_dir is also multiplied by exp(-sweep_rate*years since miss) and costpress/p_start for the applicant side gets a small positive term (pressure to file).
proposals.rule_modified: F-k and q_dir in D3.5/D10. Fallback branch of PW1 ('director 10%'). p_start in D3.1.

proposals.behaviour: Bundle veto or de-coupling of SG015 from APS. The budget manager keeps the SG015 visibility upgrade as a stand-alone HSIP application to protect its BCR and its schedule, and refuses to tie it to APS, even though that is the only way APS becomes eligible. The motive is to protect the larger, already-eligible dollars from partner-delay risk (F-g), PIF risk, and the 5-year clock.
proposals.trigger: One week to the deadline, the two lines are listed separately in the same CIP and cycle, and bundling adds an unfinished scope to a funded line.
proposals.effect_in_model: PW1 ('same package in C13') is no longer an automatic result of the applicant's BCR calculation. It becomes a stochastic gate set by the budget actor. If the veto fires, APS is left to later cycles or to local sources. SG015 files alone, and the APS path loses its main C13 carrier.
proposals.already_in_model: No for the veto. D3.3 packing is driven by BCR (>=5.0) and the instrument union (<=3 measures). F-g covers partner delay or cancellation after the bundle exists. Nothing lets a finance actor block a bundle for risk reasons before filing.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 3 (bundling paths), the 'same plan, same round, listed separately' fact: SG015 $1.1M and SG142 $488,144 both 'HSIP Cycle 13 - EST' in FY28 (CIP27m l.1184-1188, l.1218-1220). 01 section 3 also notes SG015 corridors cover only about 1 unfunded C intersection. 01 flags schedule risk: SG142 starts 2027-07 while C13 approval is 2027-03/04, and CON takes 15-28 months after award. No document says the finance side has vetoed a bundle.
proposals.parameter: p_bundle_veto
proposals.range: Bernoulli, U(0, 0.6). Higher when the partner's q_partner_cancel or t_partner is high. Applied once per application window, before the packing step.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 packing algorithm, step 1 (candidate set) and PW1 start condition. Interacts with F-g.

proposals.behaviour: Internal rationing of the $10M agency cap and local match across SF's own HSIP applications. The finance manager allocates match and cap room by agency priorities such as SGR signals or the mayor's street-safety items, which squeezes the APS-carrying package even when its BCR passes.
proposals.trigger: Several SFMTA applications (the other signal projects, SG015, SG143) compete for the same $10M cap per cycle and for scarce local match. The approval deadline is fixed.
proposals.effect_in_model: R_other changes from an exogenous number to partly endogenous. Part of the cap is reserved by the finance actor before the APS package is sized, so the APS package can be cut or dropped even when it clears BCR >= 5.0. The result is a lower approval probability for marginal packages, and a possible split into several smaller bids.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.3 treats $10M as a hard constraint shared with outside SF applications through R_other (exogenous U(0, 10M), D10). There is no actor deciding the split, and no link between the operating deficit and how much match the actor will release.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2: 'The most flexible money goes to match' (CIPpol p.11); capital revenue is $246M below the last CIP, 'not enough to fund all approved projects' (CIPpol p.5, p.20); phased funding of urgent needs by 'improving readiness' (CIPpol p.6). 01 section 5: $10M per agency, C12 $3.97M. The finance manager's actual ranking among HSIP bids is no document support.
proposals.parameter: cap_reserve_other
proposals.range: fraction of the $10M cap reserved for non-APS bids before packing, U(0, 0.8). R_other = max(R_other_exog, cap_reserve_other * 10M). A second parameter is match_release_budget in $0-X, U($0, $1M) per cycle.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 multi-application selection ($10M constraint, R_other) and the package size limit in the packing algorithm.

proposals.behaviour: Scope-only listing: A2 keeps the CIP wording that allows new APS, but allocates no dollars to it in the SG017 request. APS can be bought only from whatever is left after controller and failure-driven hardware needs. This is symbolic compliance with the scope text, and it follows how past SG017 allocations were spent.
proposals.trigger: SG017 request drafting for FY27/FY28. Past grants all went to controllers (FY24 cabinets, detectors, RRFB; FY25-26 $1M for about 98 firewall-vulnerable controllers). Controller risk is the visible, defensible priority, and the capital-budget rules say to protect state-of-good-repair first.
proposals.effect_in_model: Splits the SG017 APS money into two parts. A committed part is a ring-fenced a_sg017 that PW6 spends. A residual part is max(0, 500k - controller_spend) and exists only in years when controller failures are few. This makes PW6 funding lumpy and delayed. It also lowers PW6's chance of passing its signpost, so more runs fall through to Prop L amendment, general fund and HSIP.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 and D10 have q_sg017_block (money used up by controller-type projects) and a_sg017 (APS dollars from SG017, U(0, 250k)). These treat the shortfall as a draw from a distribution or as SFCTA behaviour. They do not model A2's own choice to leave APS unfunded in its own request, or the 'residual only' timing. This is a modification, not a duplicate.
proposals.evidence: 01 §3.2, lines 446-447: the SG017 CIP scope text allows new APS, and no past allocation was used for APS (FY24 controllers/RRFB, FY25-26 $1M for about 98 controllers). 01 §2.2: CIPpol p.6 rules (fulfil contract obligations, protect SGR, fund 'urgent need by stage'). 01 §2.1: the EP17 $1M went to controllers although APS replacement was an eligible use in 2023.
proposals.parameter: phi_scope_only (switch/probability). Effective APS money = (1 - phi_scope_only) * a_sg017 + phi_scope_only * max(0, 500k - controller_spend_t). controller_spend_t is a yearly draw from the controller-need distribution.
proposals.range: phi_scope_only U(0, 1), base about 0.5 (inferred). Sweep {0, 0.5, 1}. At 0 the model reduces to the current PW6.
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 starting action in D3.6 and the a_sg017 / q_sg017_block definitions in D10 (the 'money available' step before the task state machine).

proposals.behaviour: Field-verification first: before committing SG017 money to named APS sites, A2 funds or schedules a pole-and-conduit adequacy survey. The scope condition is 'where the existing conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition', so A2 must be able to defend each site. Some C-labelled sites are found inadequate and reclassified to N. The sites that remain have lower cost uncertainty.
proposals.trigger: The SG017 scope language is conditional on pole and conduit state. A2 wants the request to survive SFCTA review and avoid later overruns that need top-up. CIP policy language favours funding 'readiness' stages first.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a pre-step to the SG017/PW6 route: delay t_survey, then a fraction rho_demote of C sites move to N. Verified sites get a smaller sigma_over in F-f and a lower pipe/ramp surprise. Net effect is a slower start, a smaller eligible pool, and fewer later TERMINATED projects. It also changes the C/N pool seen by PW1/C14 repacking.
proposals.already_in_model: No. C vs N is a fixed label from the SFMTA list. F-f draws pipe and ramp needs once at list entry as known work, and overrun is drawn only at the design-complete node. No rule lets A2 re-check C status before spending.
proposals.evidence: 01 §3.2, line 446: the CIP text conditions new APS on conduits and poles being satisfactory. 01 §2.2: CIPpol p.6 says to fund urgent needs by stage, 'raising readiness'. 01 §2.1: pipe and ramp are each about $200k, and a senior engineer says leaving the ramp alone is about five times faster. The 01 §3.2 passage on SG142 says 'about 22 sites, no excavation'. No document shows SFMTA doing a pre-survey, so support for the behaviour itself is indirect.
proposals.parameter: sw_prever (0/1), with t_survey U(3, 9) months and rho_demote U(0.1, 0.5). If sw_prever = 1: delay the PW6 start by t_survey, move a fraction rho_demote of C sites to N, and set sigma_over to 0.5 * sigma_over for the remaining sites.
proposals.range: sw_prever in {0, 1}; t_survey U(3, 9) months; rho_demote U(0.1, 0.5); sigma_over multiplier U(0.3, 0.8). All inferred.
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 pre-step in D3.6; the C/N pool definition in D1/O2; the overrun rule F-f in D3.5.

proposals.behaviour: Waiting for C13: A2 defers the APS share of the FY28 SG017 request until the HSIP C13 result (expected 2027-03/04) is known. If SF's APS-bundled application is approved, FY28 SG017 stays with controllers and APS is dropped from it. If it is not approved, A2 moves a share of FY28 SG017 to APS as a fallback. A related option is to keep part of SG017 as a reserve for HSIP overruns or top-up.
proposals.trigger: The C13 decision falls inside the SG017 FY28 drafting window. Both sources are staff-level actions that need no board vote. Avoiding double-funding the same sites, and retaining a reserve against F-e/F-f gaps, look rational to a preparer.
proposals.effect_in_model: Couples the PW1 and PW6 funds. The yes/no outcome of C13 becomes an input to the FY28 SG017 APS amount (a_sg017_FY28 = a_sg017 if C13 fails, else 0). Part of the amount may be moved to the q_topup source for HSIP projects. This changes sequencing: PW6 would trigger only after the C13 outcome, not in parallel, and it raises q_topup in runs where a HSIP APS project overruns.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.6 describes switching only after a signpost, 'to the next available window'. PW1 failing leads to C14, Prop L amendment, then general fund. PW6 is its own path with a signpost from the SFCTA side. The model has no rule where A2 decides the FY28 SG017 share in light of the C13 result. q_topup is a flat probability and does not link to which fund covers it.
proposals.evidence: 01 §3.2 / 'Open question 1': C13 approval is expected 2027-03/04 and SG142 starts 2027-07. 01 §3.2, line 446: SG017 is shown with FY27 and FY28 $500k each. 01 §2.2: the 10% director adjustment and SG000 reserve exist, showing that staff manage reserves informally. 01 §6 C3 notes the schedule risk for SG142. No document shows SG017 used as a top-up source, so this part has no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_cond_fy28 (0/1) plus psi_backstop. If sw_cond_fy28 = 1: a_sg017_FY28 = 0 when the C13 outcome is positive for SF APS, else a_sg017. psi_backstop is the share of SG017 FY28 reserved as a top-up source; it multiplies q_topup (q_topup_eff = q_topup + psi_backstop * (1 - q_topup)) for HSIP projects.
proposals.range: sw_cond_fy28 in {0, 1}; psi_backstop U(0, 0.5).
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 timing in D3.6 (add a trigger order after C13); q_topup in F-e/F-f in D3.5; link between PW1 and PW6 in D10.

proposals.behaviour: Symbolic submission: A2 submits an SG017 request that mentions APS, or a thin APS request, mainly so it can report 'funding requested and status' to the settlement-style oversight and advocates. It puts little preparation effort and almost no real money into it. The submission reduces pressure, but does not raise delivery.
proposals.trigger: Advocacy pressure or a semi-annual report to plaintiffs asks what funding SFMTA has sought. The report format counts requests and status, not installations. A2's usual response in the evidence is cost and 'no funds' (the deflect response), so a token request is a cheaper middle option.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a third branch to the pressure-event response besides DEFLECTED and 'pressure stays'. With probability p_symbolic, a pressure event produces a token SG017 or HSIP submission (D_prep short, a_sg017 near 0, BCR/eligibility not checked), and pressure(t) is cut by a factor kappa_sym for the next k months. The token submission yields few or no installs. In runs where this is common, more 'submitted' counts but unchanged coverage, which is the paper-compliance pattern.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 has only two responses to a pressure event: DEFLECTED (cite cost, point elsewhere, no effect after r months) or pressure stays in pressure(t) for k months. Submission always means a real application with full preparation time and a BCR/eligibility check.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1, 'decision rule (response pattern)' and the 'oversight' row: costs and 'no funds' are the response, 'real oversight does not work, parties pass blame' (author first-hand, labelled fact-manual). 01 §2.10: the 2007 agreement requires semi-annual meetings and reports with 'funding SFMTA has requested and its status' (SA07 §IV.J.1) and says SFMTA must seek additional funds (§IV.A.1). No document shows a token request, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_symbolic and kappa_sym. Given a pressure event, with prob p_symbolic * (1 - p_deflect) the A2 task goes to a SYMBOLIC state: submit one instance with prep time 0.3 * D_prep, a_sg017 = 0, success probability scaled by 0.1, and pressure(t) multiplied by (1 - kappa_sym) for k months.
proposals.range: p_symbolic U(0, 0.5); kappa_sym U(0.2, 0.8); both inferred. 0 recovers the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: Pressure-event branch in the D3.1 task state machine, and the pressure(t) update rule in O3.

proposals.behaviour: Sponsor-gated discretion. Finance treats the 10% director adjustment and the SG000 signal reserve as 'fund-when-ready' money. It releases it only to a request that has a named sponsor and a staged readiness package. With the owner post vacant, nobody files that request, so the money stays unspent and is later reallocated to projects that do have a sponsor.
proposals.trigger: Owner vacancy (F-h) combined with a CIP shortfall in which flexible money is first claimed for grant match and contractual obligations.
proposals.effect_in_model: F-k currently draws q_dir as a flat probability. This change makes the chance that discretion reaches APS depend on whether a live, ready APS request exists in that month. During a vacancy it is near 0, and unspent reserve can lapse to other uses (reserve decay).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k has q_dir U(0,0.8) for 'discretion/SG000 not used for APS'. It is an unconditional coin flip with no link to sponsor presence or readiness, so the vacancy-to-no-ask-to-no-money chain is not captured. Kept as a modification of F-k, not a duplicate.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 decision rules (CIPpol p.6): 'fund urgent needs in stages (raise project/grant readiness)'; CIPpol p.11: 'most flexible money goes to match'; SG000 $1.6M FY27 + $0.5M FY28 unassigned (01 §2.2 resources). No document directly says discretion is refused when no sponsor exists, so that link is an inference.
proposals.parameter: sw_dir_sponsor_gate (0/1). If 1, q_dir_eff = q_dir * 1[live ready APS request this month] * (1 - owner_vacant). Also reserve_lapse_rate U(0, 0.5) per year: the share of unspent SG000 reallocated.
proposals.range: switch 0/1; reserve_lapse_rate U(0,0.5)/yr
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-k (and the F-h to PREPARING link in D3.1)

proposals.behaviour: Vacancy-savings sweep. Finance sees the frozen post's salary and project-support funding as free money. It sweeps it to the operating deficit or relabels it to capital, and it stops treating the post as a fundable APS cost line. Even after the freeze ends, the position's funding is lost, so refilling it needs a new justification.
proposals.trigger: Operating gap of about $307M, a hiring freeze, and the 2025 budget options of moving shop labor to capital and restructuring work orders so they count as capital (01 §2.2 line 158).
proposals.effect_in_model: Vacancy duration t_vac in F-h stops being an independent draw. It becomes longer, or the funded crew ceiling K_crew is permanently cut by a fraction after the vacancy, so F-i 'freeze ends' does not restore the original strain level.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-h gives the vacancy length t_vac and F-i lets strain persist and K_crew fall until the freeze ends, then fully recover. A permanent loss of funded capacity (ratchet) is not written anywhere.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1: 8 of 21 electrician posts sit on the project-support fund (38%), expected to be recovered from capital; 9145 headcount flat for six fiscal years; 01 §2.2 line 158: 'relabel work orders as capital'. The sweep itself has no direct document support. It is an inference from deficit-driven behaviour.
proposals.parameter: q_sweep (probability the funding line is swept during the vacancy) and K_loss (fraction of K_crew permanently lost if swept).
proposals.range: q_sweep U(0,0.6); K_loss U(0,0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-h/F-i recovery path; K_crew in D3.4 internal delivery

proposals.behaviour: Funded-post backfill exemption, and its absence. Finance decides which positions get a freeze exemption. It approves a refill if the post is grant-reimbursable, for example when it is tied to an awarded HSIP or Prop L grant. APS has no such grant, so the owner post is not exempted. The result is a chicken-and-egg loop: no owner means no grant request, and no grant means no exemption.
proposals.trigger: Hiring freeze in force, post vacant, and a finance rule that exemptions follow secured outside money.
proposals.effect_in_model: t_vac in F-h depends on the state: if an APS-related grant or dedicated line is live, t_vac is short; otherwise it extends to the end of the freeze (strain_end). This makes the vacancy self-reinforcing, and the PW3 accountability pathway or a dedicated SG-line acts as the exit.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. F-h t_vac U(3,18) and F-i strain_end are independent exogenous draws with no link to funding status.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1: the 9145 list grew to 41 people in 2025-05 'during the freeze', so some hiring did pass; this suggests exemptions exist for some posts. 01 §2.1: the internal line installed 23 intersections in 2023-01 to 2024-08, then 0 for four periods after the SG105 money ended. No document says what the exemption rule is, so it is an inference.
proposals.parameter: sw_exempt_by_funding (0/1) and t_vac_unfunded: vacancy length when no live APS-linked line exists.
proposals.range: switch 0/1; t_vac_unfunded = strain_end - now, or U(12,36) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-h (t_vac) and F-i (strain_end)

proposals.behaviour: Match-letter gate. Finance will not pre-commit the 10% local match, or the local funds for the extra cost of a bundle, until an award exists. Submitters need a match commitment before they can file. With no owner to chase finance, no commitment is requested, and the HSIP submission is blocked even when the BCR threshold would be met.
proposals.trigger: Preparing an HSIP application when the most flexible money is reserved first for grant match (CIPpol p.11), and no sponsor is asking.
proposals.effect_in_model: SUBMIT of an HSIP instance requires a binary 'match-committed' state. The probability of getting it rises with owner strength and pressure(t) and falls with the CIP shortfall. If it is absent at the deadline the instance becomes MISSED, which is a new cause alongside D_prep running out.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. D3.3 mentions a 10% local match and 'staff hours can count as soft match', but no rule makes the finance commitment a gate on submission. D3.1 MISSED arises only from preparation time.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.4: reimbursement 90%, local match 10%, staff hours count as soft match; 01 §2.2 CIPpol p.11: the most flexible money is used for match. Whether finance actually issues a match letter before the award is undocumented.
proposals.parameter: q_match_commit = logistic(a0 + a_own*owner + a_pr*pressure(t) - a_gap*costpress(t)); soft_match_share U(0,1) (the fraction of the match met by staff hours, bypassing the gate).
proposals.range: a0 U(-1,2); soft_match_share U(0,1)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING to SUBMIT transition (new MISSED cause); D3.3 route A submission

proposals.behaviour: Carrier-protection veto at packing time. The finance manager keeps APS out of the SG015 HSIP application (or strips it back out) when adding it would thin SG015's BCR margin, use up part of the shared $10M per-agency cap, or add a non-safety cost line. The goal is to protect the higher-value visibility project. APS is then pushed to C14 or to local money.
proposals.trigger: Deadline is a week away. SG015 ($1.1M, SI02 carrier) is the clean bid. SG142 ($488k, pure APS) is ineligible alone. Merging them risks the package BCR falling toward c_final (U(3.5,18), unknown until award). Finance prefers the sure bid.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a finance veto between the packing algorithm (D3.3 steps 3-4) and SUBMIT. Even when the mechanical package BCR is >= 5.0, the APS-carrying instance is withheld if its margin is too small. PW1 then fails by choice, not by F-a. It lowers P(APS submitted in C13) and raises P(SG015 funded).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.3 packing stops only on a mechanical BCR < 5.0 (F-a) and applies the cap against R_other. PW1 bundles APS with SG015. Nothing lets a budget actor drop APS from a package that passes the BCR gate. So this is not a duplicate.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 decision rules: 'fulfil contract obligations first, protect SGR, fund by stage (raise grant readiness)', and 'prioritise expansion over maintenance'. 01 s3 (about l.442) lists SG015 and SG142 as separate rows in the same cycle. 01 l.420-421 flags schedule risk for SG142. No document records a finance veto, so this is an inference.
proposals.parameter: p_dilute_veto with delta_margin: veto if (BCR_package - max(5.0, c_final_expected)) < delta_margin
proposals.range: delta_margin U(0, 2.0) BCR points; p_veto 0-1; 0 reproduces the current model
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.3 packing algorithm step 4 and the submit decision in D3.1: add a finance gate after the BCR >= 5.0 test

proposals.behaviour: Reimbursement cash-flow gating. HSIP pays 90% after the fact, so finance must front cash and commit the 10% match. Under an operating deficit, finance slows or sequences the release of that front-money or ties it to fiscal-year boundaries. A funded, approved project starts late.
proposals.trigger: FY27 operating gap of $307M rising to $434M; the balancing list includes moving capital to operations; capital revenue is $246M below the last CIP. An award would need front money and match in FY28.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a finance-controlled delay between APPROVED and CON E-76 or construction start, separate from the t_con lognormal. Extends delivery time and can push projects toward the 5-year no-CON check (F-d).
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-d, F-e, F-f, F-i cover delays from design, PIF, overruns and hiring freeze. F-k covers only whether director discretion is used for APS. D3.4 gives t_con as an empirical lognormal and the match as a fixed 10%, with no release delay.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 incentives: operating deficit and 'capital funds moved to operations'. 01 s2.4: reimbursement 90%, staff hours allowed as soft match. 01 s5 l.604: local match fixed at 10%. No document supports finance delaying match release, so this is an inference.
proposals.parameter: t_fin_hold, delay added to CON start, applied with probability p_hold (scaled by costpress(t))
proposals.range: t_fin_hold U(0, 12) months; p_hold U(0, 0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.4 HSIP delivery row: CON E-76 = max(design complete, PIF conclusion, cycle start + t_con, finance release date); also feeds costpress(t) in D3.2 (M-C)

proposals.behaviour: Placeholder-line sweep. The 'EST' HSIP-funded lines (SG142 FY28, SG143) are treated as parkable placeholders. If the APS-only line is ineligible or unlikely, finance reassigns or draws down its share toward grant-ready projects, or re-scopes it so it stays alive without extra local money.
proposals.trigger: SG142 is APS-only and ineligible for C13, but is carried as 'EST' in the CIP. Finance must show a balanced plan with $246M less capital revenue.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a transition on the budget line itself, APS line -> SWEPT, removing a funding source the model assumes exists. This lowers local APS money for the fallback steps in PW1, PW2 and PW6 and leaves APS dependent on being bundled.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-k covers only the director 10% and SG000 reserve not being used for APS. 01 has 'capital moved to operations $20-40M per round' but 02 does not use it as a sweep on a named APS line. SG142 and SG143 amounts are fixed resource inputs.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'capital moved to operations $20-40M', 2025-02 budget options 'reorganise work orders so they count as capital', board view that transfers be one-off and 'spread out so no project is cut off'. The SG142/SG143 rows are both labelled 'EST'. No document says an APS line was swept, so this is an inference.
proposals.parameter: q_sweep, annual probability that an unfunded EST line is cut or reassigned, with sweep fraction f_sweep; active only when the line has no award and the HSIP application is ineligible or failed
proposals.range: q_sweep U(0, 0.4) per year; f_sweep U(0.25, 1)
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D2/D10 resource inputs and F-k in D3.5: add an F-n failure path, APS budget line cut; interacts with local fallbacks of PW1, PW2, PW6

proposals.behaviour: Deliberate window-skipping. With a week to the C13 deadline, finance may decline to start new bundled work and submit only shovel-ready items. It reasons that C14 offers more preparation time and a possible Prop L amendment, so APS should wait. This is a choice, not a miss.
proposals.trigger: Deadline in about one week, which is less than D_prep plus delta_split for an extra instance. SG142 construction is planned for 2027-07, only months after the 2027-03/04 award, which finance may already see as unrealistic.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers p_start for the APS task at that window by a finance term. APS skips C13 on purpose and the task goes to the next window; the cap is kept for SG015. This is weaker than the first proposal and overlaps with it.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 has p_start, D_prep and MISSED, and D3.6 says to turn to the next window. These cover missing a window through slow preparation, not an actor who declines to start because of schedule outlook. Kept as a separate switch because it is a budget-owner choice.
proposals.evidence: 01 l.420-421 and s6 C3: SG142 plans a 2027-07 start, while award to construction authorisation has taken 15-28 months in SF. No document shows finance deferring on purpose, so this is an inference.
proposals.parameter: p_defer_window, probability finance vetoes starting APS preparation at a window whose remaining prep time is under T_min; enters p_start as a multiplier (1 - p_defer_window)
proposals.range: T_min U(1, 6) months; p_defer_window U(0, 0.6)
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 p_start (add a finance term) and the window logic in O3

proposals.behaviour: Match-letter gating. The finance manager will not issue the local 10% match / soft-match commitment (staff hours) for an HSIP application until a named project owner exists. With the engineer gone and a freeze on, the match letter is held, so a PREPARING instance that is otherwise ready misses the deadline or goes in without a funded match.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy of the informal APS owner (F-h) plus hiring freeze (F-i) while an HSIP window (C13 deadline 2026-11-02, or C14) is open. Finance has no named counterpart and also has to protect scarce flexible money.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a finance-side gate between PREPARING and SUBMIT: each instance needs a match commitment, issued after delay t_match. If it is not issued by the deadline, the instance becomes MISSED (or is submitted late and fails the F-c eligibility check). The gate drops once an owner exists or once a partner project already carries the match.
proposals.already_in_model: Not present. F-h only lowers owner and applies q_drop to PREPARING; the 10% local match is a fixed cost share inside D3.3 (cost minus 90% funding). No rule makes the match commitment a separate decision with its own timing. F-k covers only the director 10% not being used, and is a different decision.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 line 149: 'the most flexible money is taken to be used as match'. 01 line 203: 90% reimbursement, staff hours can serve as soft match (QA13 Q14, Q59). 01 line 154: phased funding to 'raise readiness'. 02 F-h and F-i. No document describes a match letter being withheld, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_match_hold (probability that finance holds the match commitment while there is no named owner), with delay t_match
proposals.range: q_match_hold U(0, 0.7); t_match U(1, 6) months. 0 reproduces the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 task state machine (adds a gate before SUBMIT), D3.3 eligibility step, F-h recovery path (match released once the post is filled).

proposals.behaviour: Labour recoding to capital. Under the operating deficit, finance relabels Signal Shop hours as capital work orders, so APS installs are booked to capital. It also uses any frozen position's salary savings for this. It does not create new money for APS. It changes which installs look affordable, and it competes with the capital rules for Shop hours.
proposals.trigger: Operating gap ($307M FY27) combined with a hiring freeze, where the Signal Shop keeps its remaining crew busy on work that is chargeable to capital.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a share f_recode of Fi internal-install labour cost that is paid from capital lines instead of the APS budget. This lowers costpress(t) and the size of the top-up needed. But it pulls Shop hours toward capital-chargeable jobs: K_crew available for APS is cut by a factor, and APS work-orders that are not chargeable are queued behind.
proposals.already_in_model: Not present. PW5 b_hw is a maintenance-budget allowance for APS add-ons on a hardware swap, which is a different mechanism. M-B strain and K_crew are exogenous to finance decisions. F-i only covers the freeze itself.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 line 158: 2025-02 budget options 'move 25% of paint and sign shop staff to capital priorities' and 'restructure work orders so they count as capital projects' (Signal Shop not named). 01 line 159: FY27-31 CIP widens the capital definition to maintenance extending life 5+ years. 01 line 113: grants pay Signal Shop labour, reducing the operating deficit.
proposals.parameter: f_recode (share of internal APS install labour booked to capital) and k_crew_shift (fraction of K_crew diverted to chargeable work)
proposals.range: f_recode U(0, 0.8); k_crew_shift U(0, 0.4). Both 0 reproduces the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 internal delivery (Fi to I): K_crew and cost accounting; M-B/M-C switches in D3.2 (costpress and strain).

proposals.behaviour: Discretion pool as defensive reserve. The finance manager treats the 10% director adjustment as one shared pool, and uses it first to top up already committed projects (cost overruns, partner shortfalls, projects at risk of 'breaking funding') and to avoid a visible gap on committed work. APS is last in line, because it has no champion and no named owner.
proposals.trigger: Several top-up requests in the same fiscal year (F-f overruns, F-e outsourcing premium, F-g partner delays), plus a vacancy that leaves no one to argue for APS.
proposals.effect_in_model: The chance that discretion or the SG000 reserve is available for APS is no longer a fixed q_dir. It shrinks as the pool is drained: q_dir_eff = q_dir × max(0, 1 − drain), where drain grows with the count of unmet top-ups across all projects in the same year. The 10% pool also stays a per-year budget, so unused room does not accumulate.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k has a fixed q_dir, 'not used for APS', and q_topup in F-f/F-e is a separate approval chance. But the two never draw from one pool, so there is no rival claim. Keep the proposal only as the coupling.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 line 156: director may adjust up to 10% cumulatively (~$65M). Line 157: board wants diversions 'one-time' and spread 'so no project loses funding'. Line 139: SG000 reserve $1.6M FY27 + $0.5M FY28. Line 154: rule order starts with 'fulfil contract obligations'. No document shows how the pool is divided between claimants.
proposals.parameter: w_drain (weight of other projects' top-up requests on the shared discretion pool)
proposals.range: w_drain U(0, 1) per unit of pool use; 0 reproduces the current independent q_dir.
proposals.rule_modified: F-k (q_dir becomes state-dependent), F-f and F-e (q_topup requests draw from the same pool), D3.4 termination rule.

proposals.behaviour: Match-first funding sequencing: with no engineer to file, finance releases local flexible money to APS only as the 10% match to an application that already exists. 'No application' then automatically means 'no local money'. Money is parked for higher-priority grant matches instead of being offered first.
proposals.trigger: Vacant owner post plus hiring freeze plus operating deficit; CIP rule that the most flexible money is used as grant match; no APS application in the pipeline.
proposals.effect_in_model: Local APS money (SG000, general-fund baseline line, F-k director discretion) is conditional on a live SUBMITTED/APPROVED instance. Sequence is 'application then money'. This blocks PW2/PW6 local-first paths as self-starting sources during vacancy.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: F-k has q_dir as a one-off draw independent of vacancy or whether an application exists. F-h only lowers owner tier. Neither makes funding conditional on a filed application.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'subsidy rules prefer expansion over maintenance; the most flexible money goes to match' (CIPpol p.11); 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project/grant readiness)' (CIPpol p.6); local APS money only $0-0.57M/yr. Conditional-on-application behaviour: no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_dir_vac: multiplier on q_dir while F-h vacancy is active, or switch sw_match_first (0/1)
proposals.range: q_dir_vac 0.2-1.0; sw_match_first 0/1
proposals.rule_modified: F-k (q_dir draw) and D3.2 local-line opening in M-A/M-D; PW2 and PW6 entry conditions.

proposals.behaviour: Crew-hour reallocation by reimbursability: under the freeze, finance recodes Signal Shop work orders as capital and steers existing crew hours to externally funded, capitalizable work, away from unfunded APS installs; staff hours also count as soft match for grants.
proposals.trigger: Operating deficit plus hiring freeze: no new headcount, so existing crew hours are the scarce resource finance allocates.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers K_crew available to unfunded Fi/C installs; optionally reduces the cash local match for an HSIP application.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.2 strain(t) lowers K_crew exogenously and uniformly; D3.4 queues by funded status only; no rule has finance steering crew hours.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: budget options 'move 25% of paint-and-sign shop staff to capital priorities' and 'restructure work orders so they count as capital' ($2.5M, sfmta-media-41700 p.9, p.17, Signal Shop not named); s2.12 HSIP staff hours as soft match (QA13 Q14, Q59).
proposals.parameter: phi_fund: share of K_crew reserved for externally funded work during strain; optional m_soft: staff-hour credit against the 10% local match
proposals.range: phi_fund 0.5-1.0; m_soft 0-0.5
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 internal construction queue (K_crew allocation); D3.3 HSIP local-match cost; M-B strain mechanism.

proposals.behaviour: Window-waiting with readiness funding: finance holds the request until the next programming window (5YPP autumn 2027-2028 or CIP revision), then funds only a readiness step (application prep/design) that partly substitutes for the vacant owner, instead of a full install or an immediate 10% adjustment.
proposals.trigger: Pressure or 'no funds' complaint arrives while the owner post is vacant and the next CIP/5YPP window is still distant.
proposals.effect_in_model: Two-stage local funding: a small readiness grant released at the next window restores part of the owner tier without hiring, shortening later D_prep, but delaying money by the window gap.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: F-j/PW2 wait for 5YPP only as a failure path of the Prop L amendment. Finance funding a 'readiness' step to substitute for the vacant owner is absent; F-h recovers only by hiring (t_vac).
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project/grant readiness)' (CIPpol p.6); next 5YPP window 2027 autumn-2028 (01 s2.3 table). Substitution for a vacant owner: no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_ready (probability readiness grant released at next window) and ready_gain (share of the F-h owner drop restored)
proposals.range: q_ready U(0,0.5); ready_gain U(0,0.7)
proposals.rule_modified: F-h recovery path (owner restored without hiring), p_start via beta_own; interacts with F-k.

proposals.behaviour: Responsibility parking from the capital side: asked about APS money, finance says it is a program/design matter for the engineering unit, which has no head, so nothing can be allocated until an owner and an application exist. Delay without a decision.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy: no named engineer, so each side can point at the other.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure reaching finance is absorbed instead of added to pressure(t), and the DEFLECTED duration r is longer because no counterpart can accept the task.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: D3.1 DEFLECTED covers A2 deflecting to SFCTA/budget/Caltrans. The reverse leg (finance pointing back at a vacant engineering post) and longer r under vacancy are not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 82: the gap step between list and application has no deadline, no board vote, no named person; line 83: 'no funds' to 'no application' loop. Finance-side version: no document support.
proposals.parameter: r_vac_mult: multiplier on DEFLECTED duration r during F-h vacancy; p_deflect_vac: add-on to p_deflect
proposals.range: r_vac_mult 1-3; p_deflect_vac 0-0.3
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (r and p_deflect) made conditional on F-h state.

proposals.behaviour: Pre-emptive sweep of discretionary capital (SG000 signal reserve, 10% director adjustment room) into the operating deficit or into higher-ranked, grant-matching projects BEFORE any APS request exists, so the pot is gone when a disability-council push arrives.
proposals.trigger: Operating-gap pressure (the $307M FY27 gap; board wording on one-time capital-to-operations transfers) rises while no APS line has a named owner or pending grant. Fires on the budget calendar, not on advocate pressure.
proposals.effect_in_model: F-k today is a one-off draw (q_dir: pot unused for APS). This adds a time-dependent erosion of the pot: each budget cycle the available discretionary balance shrinks by a fraction, so q_dir rises over time and PW1's last step (director 10% / general fund) loses value the longer earlier steps take. It also makes the late fallback in PW1 worse than the early one, which changes path ranking.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k (02 D3.5) and q_dir (02 D10, l.382) cover 'not used for APS' as a static probability. The time-erosion/sweep dynamic is NOT written. It is a modification of F-k, not a drop; I keep it only because the time dependence is new.
