proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: l.146 'capital moved to operations' is on the balancing list; l.154 CIP draft rule allows up to $40M operating diversion; l.157 board says diversions should be 'one-time' and cut to $20M; l.163 'capital-to-operations each round $20-40M'; l.139 SG000 $1.6M FY27 + $0.5M FY28. No document shows a diversion that specifically hit APS (no document support for the APS-specific link).
proposals.parameter: sweep_rate (annual fractional erosion of the discretionary/SG000 balance available to APS)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.5) per year; 0 = current static q_dir behaviour
proposals.rule_modified: F-k and the PW1 final step; q_dir becomes q_dir(t) = 1 - (1 - q_dir0)*(1 - sweep_rate)^years

proposals.behaviour: Cost-framing as a refusal tool: when pressed, finance cites the high per-intersection cost (the number used is the upper end, e.g. full-upgrade cost) rather than the cheap internal-install cost, and holds the figure unrevised until pressure fades. This makes costpress look larger than the true C-type cost.
proposals.trigger: A direct public question 'why are most of the ~76 unfunded' at a disability council meeting, combined with a gap between the stated unit cost ($40k+ in MDC26) and internal cost (SG142 about $22k).
proposals.effect_in_model: Separates 'real cost' from 'stated cost'. The stated cost feeds the DEFLECTED response and the advocates' belief about what is fundable, but not the real delivery cost. If advocates or the council accept the stated cost, pressure(t) is damped for k months; if they can check it (oversight high), the reply becomes a credibility loss and enforce(t) rises.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. Deflection to 'cost / no money' is in D3.1 (p_deflect, r months). costpress(t) in M-C is a REAL cost effect. A gap between stated and real cost, and its effect on advocate credibility, is not written.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 and s6 C4 (l.637): 'SG142 about $22k vs MDC26 minimum $40k, unresolved'. 01 s0/l.83: 'saying no money and not applying form a loop'. No document shows intentional over-statement; it is a plausible reading of an unresolved conflict, so label it a hypothesis.
proposals.parameter: cost_overstate (ratio of stated to real C-type unit cost used in the deflection reply)
proposals.range: U(1.0, 2.0); 1.0 = no overstatement. Used in D3.1 deflection: pressure damping = f(cost_overstate) if oversight low, penalty if oversight high.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 deflection branch (pressure(t) damping) plus an oversight-conditioned credibility penalty to enforce(t)

proposals.behaviour: Re-labelling APS work as state-of-good-repair or 'extended capital definition' (work orders restructured so labour counts as capital), so APS rides on the signal asset-renewal budget instead of needing a standalone new-install line. Finance allows this only if the item fits the board's capital-definition expansion.
proposals.trigger: Draft rule to widen the capital definition (5-year life-extension maintenance counts) coincides with signal assets listed as 'among the most degraded' and SGR 'extremely limited'; advocates ask for a line item.
proposals.effect_in_model: Opens a finance-controlled channel where APS is bundled into SGR hardware replacement at no new line item. It gives APS a cheap route but only for existing-pole C-type intersections, tied to how often replacements happen. It also lets finance claim 'APS is funded' while the volume stays small.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW5 (02 D3.6 l.246) has b_hw, the maintenance-budget quota for adding APS to hardware replacements. It treats this as an advocate-demanded design rule, not as a finance-initiated reclassification. The new element is the FINANCE actor choosing to use it, and the count-as-funded effect. If judged redundant with PW5, drop.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: l.159 CIP expands capital investment definition to cover maintenance extending life 5+ years; l.158 2025 option 'restructure work orders so they count as capital' ($2.5M); l.153 signals 'among most degraded assets', SGR funding 'extremely limited'. None names APS (no document support for APS use).
proposals.parameter: p_reclass (probability finance, when asked, routes a C-type request to the SGR/work-order channel)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6); 0 = PW5 only as advocate-driven
proposals.rule_modified: PW5 trigger: b_hw is activated by finance with probability p_reclass even when PW5 is not the chosen pathway; also adds a flag 'counted_as_funded' used in D4 outputs

proposals.behaviour: Staging by readiness: finance funds a project only after the grant/design is 'ready', so it tells advocates to come back when a design or grant exists, and then does not budget any pre-design money. This creates a wait-for-readiness step that blocks local money until another actor produces a ready application.
proposals.trigger: CIP funding rule 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project/grant readiness)' meets an APS request with no design and no named owner.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a precondition on local money: a local dedicated batch is released only after readiness (a design stage or a pending grant match). Where the model lets local money go straight to 'designing' (t_des), this inserts a pre-design funding gap and lengthens the loop 'no application -> no money -> no application'.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.4 starts design only once 'funding is secured', and nothing requires a readiness stage before funding. Closest: D3.1 DEFLECTED sends the task elsewhere with no waiting rule.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 l.154: 'phase funding of urgent needs (raise project/grant readiness)'. 01 l.83 loop narrative. Support for the rule is documentary; support that it is applied to APS is none.
proposals.parameter: readiness_gate (binary switch plus delay t_ready months of unfunded pre-design work)
proposals.range: switch {0,1}; t_ready U(3, 18) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 internal path (Fi): local batch funds designing only after t_ready elapses; prepares entry into D3.1 PREPARING with a pre-design step

proposals.behaviour: Capitalising Signal Shop labour. Finance reclassifies work orders or staff time as capital, or widens the 'capital investment' definition to cover life-extension work. Internal APS installs then draw on an existing capital line and need no new local money. The 'no money' reply is true only for cash, not for labour.
proposals.trigger: Operating deficit pressure plus advocates pressing on the ~76 unfunded intersections. Triggered when a C-candidate (in-house install) intersection is stuck only because of 'no cash'.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a funded path for C-type intersections that skips HSIP, Prop L and the General Fund. It lowers costpress(t) and strain(t) for those intersections. It also lets the 'no money' answer hold for N-type intersections while C-type ones get installed. This changes how M-C (cost) and M-B (staffing) are told apart.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. 02 D3.2 and D3.5 have no labour-reclassification rule. q_dir (D3.5 F-k, D10) is a flat chance that the 10% / SG000 money reaches APS. It does not cover moving labour cost between operating and capital.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'reorganise work orders so they count toward capital projects' and '25% of paint and sign shop staff moved to capital priorities' (sfmta-media-41700 p.9, p.17); 'expand the definition of capital investment to cover maintenance extending life 5+ years' (CIPpol p.10). 01 s2.1: grants pay Signal Shop labour and so relieve the operating deficit. The sources do not name the Signal Shop.
proposals.parameter: p_capitalize
proposals.range: U(0, 0.5), inferred. Share of C-type intersections whose install labour is booked to capital. Also q_cap_year, the month it starts, with sweep points 2026-07, 2027-07 and never.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 delivery (the internal-install funding condition) and costpress(t) in D3.2 M-C. Adds a funding path to D3.1 for C-type intersections.

proposals.behaviour: Discretion diverted to the operating deficit. The 10% director adjustment and the SG000 reserve are the same flexible cash that the capital-to-operating transfer draws on. In a deficit year it goes to operations or to match for large grants, not to a small APS batch. The finance manager never says no to APS; the money is simply gone first.
proposals.trigger: The operating gap is large (FY27 $307M) and a transfer round is being sized. Also triggered when a bigger grant needs flexible match money.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes the chance that q_dir is usable fall as operating pressure rises and as competing match demands appear. It also makes PW1 (HSIP first) and PW6 collide with other claims on the same cash. The fallback paths in F-k then open more often.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. q_dir (D3.5 F-k, D10) is a fixed probability U(0, 0.8) with no link to the deficit or to other claims. The transfer itself is not a state variable. Keep this as a state-dependent q_dir, not a new rule.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: operating gap $307M / $344M / $434M; balancing list includes 'capital money moved to operations'; transfer $20-40M per round (CIPpol p.6, p.21); 'the most flexible money is used as match' (CIPpol p.11); unrestricted funds gave $0 to the FY25-29 CIP (CIP25 p.5); board wants transfers 'one-time' and spread out (CIPpol p.18, p.21).
proposals.parameter: k_dir_deficit
proposals.range: U(0, 1), inferred. q_dir_eff(t) = q_dir * (1 - k_dir_deficit * deficit_share(t)), where deficit_share is the operating gap divided by its FY27 level, taken from a series.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-k and the D10 parameter q_dir. Becomes a time-varying probability that also feeds the PW1 fallback.

proposals.behaviour: Readiness-only funding. To answer the public meeting, finance funds a small piece, such as scoping, design or the BCR work for a batch. It does not fund construction. Advocates read it as progress. The money buys a faster later application, not an install.
proposals.trigger: Public pressure at the council meeting while construction cash is not available. Finance needs a visible answer that is cheaper than a build budget.
proposals.effect_in_model: Cuts D_prep for the next window and so raises p_start. It also lowers pressure(t) at once, since part of the pressure is absorbed. That removes some of the push toward an application. Net effect on the funded share can be either sign, so it is worth testing.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. D3.1 treats pressure as either deflected (p_deflect) or kept in pressure(t). There is no 'partial response that reduces prep time and absorbs pressure' branch. D_prep is fixed per run.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: draft CIP rule 'phase-fund urgent needs (raise project / grant readiness)' (CIPpol p.6). 01 s2.1: only unit costs and 'selected based on funding' were given to the Committee (MDC26 p.4-6, p.8). No document shows this done for APS, so no direct support for APS use.
proposals.parameter: p_ready
proposals.range: U(0, 0.4), inferred. Chance that a pressure event gets readiness funding. Side parameters: D_prep reduced by 1-3 months; the share of the event's pressure removed, U(0.3, 0.8).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1: adds a third branch at the pressure event. It changes D_prep (preparation time) and pressure(t) decay.

proposals.behaviour: Refusing to commit the 10% local match. Finance will not promise match for a grant application unless the match can be paid by staff-hour soft credit, or from a reserve it controls. Without that commitment the application is not started.
proposals.trigger: Time to prepare an HSIP or SS4A application. Match must be named for a batch of intersections, and the cash-flexible funds are already claimed.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a gate on p_start, or on SUBMIT, for grant applications. It is separate from workload (strain) and from unit cost (costpress), so it gives M-A / M-B / M-C a fourth rival cause. If the soft-credit route works it also explains why batches that use Signal Shop labour get applied for more often.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. 02 has HSIP eligibility and a benefit-cost threshold (D3.3), but I found no local-match commitment step. Searching 02 for the 90/10 split found nothing.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.4 (HSIP): reimbursement 90%, local match 10%, staff hours may count as soft match (QA13 Q14, Q59). 01 s2.2: 'the most flexible money is used as match' (CIPpol p.11). SS4A Tenderloin match $1.4M Prop L on a $5.6M federal share (20%).
proposals.parameter: p_match_gate
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6), inferred. Chance a grant-type task is blocked at start by lack of a match commitment. Switch match_soft = 0/1: staff-hour credit allowed (gate halves when on).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start for grant fields (HSIP, SS4A) and the F-series failure paths in D3.5, adding a failure type before SUBMIT.

proposals.behaviour: Paper commitment: finance answers pressure by listing an unfunded, estimated-source APS row in the CIP or a future-year line (a placeholder, in the style of the old APS FY25 line that named HSIP Cycle 12 money but never had an application). The row relieves advocate pressure and lets the agency say 'it is programmed', but no cash or application follows, and the row is reprogrammed away at the next CIP rollover.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event (disability council meeting, advocate letter) arrives while no real funding source is available and a flat 'no money' reply would look too weak. Also at CIP preparation when a row has to be dropped for the capital revenue shortfall.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a third outcome to a pressure event besides DEFLECTED and 'pressure kept'. The placeholder cuts pressure(t) (a longer or faster decay than k) and blocks a new pressure-driven p_start for the lifetime of the row, but creates no PREPARING task and no money. At rollover the row lapses silently and pressure returns. So advocates are appeased for a while with no installs.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 DEFLECTED sends the request to SFCTA, budget or Caltrans and leaves no lasting effect. F-k covers a reserve that goes unused. Neither covers a visible, time-limited commitment that suppresses later pressure. Not found in 02 as a mechanism. Close but different from M-A deflection.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 table line 140 (CIP27m: SG142/SG143 APS rows are 'EST'); line 224 (CIP25 SG136 APS FY25 $1.0M from HSIP Cycle 12, but C12 has no SF APS application); line 109 (SG136 has no funding row in FY27-31). Together these show a listed row with no money behind it exists in the documents. That it is used as a response to pressure is no document support (inference).
proposals.parameter: p_placeholder (probability a pressure event is answered with a placeholder row instead of deflection) U(0, 0.6); T_row (months until the row lapses at the next CIP rollover) U(12, 30); pressure damping factor d_row U(0.3, 0.8) applied to pressure(t) while the row is live
proposals.range: p_placeholder 0-0.6; T_row 12-30 months; d_row 0.3-0.8
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure-event branch: adds a third branch beside p_deflect and 1-p_deflect, and a row-lifetime timer that multiplies pressure(t) in p_start.

proposals.behaviour: Discretion pool drained by competing claims. The 10% director discretion and the SG000 reserve are not a standing pot for APS. The same flexible money is used to move capital to the operating deficit and to cover other projects' local match. By the time APS is considered there is little left, and the decision is made against whatever other claims exist that year.
proposals.trigger: A structural operating gap (about $307M in FY27, rising to $434M) and a CIP draft that already authorises capital-to-operating shifts of $20-40M. Each fiscal year starts a new round of claims on the same discretion.
proposals.effect_in_model: Turns q_dir from a fixed probability into a state-dependent one. A pool D(t) of discretion is replenished each fiscal year and drained first by operating-deficit swaps and other matches (rate rho_raid). APS can draw from D(t) only if the remainder exceeds the unit price of a small batch. In deficit-heavy years q_dir falls to near 0, in lighter years it rises. This produces a year-to-year pattern of 'sometimes there is a little, usually none'.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k has a constant q_dir U(0, 0.8) and no link to the deficit or to claims. costpress and strain (M-B, M-C) cover cost and staffing, not competition for flexible money. Not found as a dynamic pool.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 line 156 (director may adjust capital up to a cumulative 10%, about $65M); line 157 (board wants swaps one-off, cut from $40M to $20M); line 163 (capital moved to operating $20-40M per round); line 145 (operating gap $307-434M); line 149 (the most flexible money goes to match). The deficit-versus-APS competition inside the pool is inference.
proposals.parameter: rho_raid, the fraction of the annual discretion pool taken by deficit swaps and other matches before APS is seen; with q_dir replaced by q_dir = 1[ D(t)*(1-rho_raid) >= c_batch ] * q_base
proposals.range: rho_raid U(0.5, 1.0); pool size 0-10% of capital budget, base about $65M; q_base U(0.3, 0.9)
proposals.rule_modified: F-k and the PW1 end step (director 10% / SG000): replaces the constant q_dir with a yearly draw against a depleting pool; also the PW1 -> F-k transition.

proposals.behaviour: Wait-for-window deferral. Finance says 'we will consider it in the next CIP or next 5YPP cycle' and holds all local money decisions until the formal calendar point, instead of treating the reply as a short stall. The request then rolls from one cycle to the next; the board agenda for the cycle may not include accessible-signal items at all.
proposals.trigger: The council meeting falls between budget milestones. The next CIP adoption or 5YPP window is more than a few months away, and no formal item exists for the board to act on.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes the DEFLECTED return time r depend on the calendar rather than a fixed number. If a pressure event comes after the CIP is locked, the earliest restart is the next CIP adoption or the 2027-autumn 5YPP window. A repeat deferral can occur at each point with some probability. This lengthens idle time, and may push the next PREPARING start after a window closes, so a deadline is missed (MISSED).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 DEFLECTED returns to IDLE after r months, with r a plain parameter. D3.6 PW2/PW6 refer to the next 5YPP window and 'next usable window'. The finance office's own act of deferring to its own CIP calendar, and repeated rolling, is not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 line 160 (8 budget meetings Nov 2025 to Apr 2026, none on accessibility or signals); line 154 (CIP rule: fund urgent needs in stages); s2.3 line 69 (next 5YPP window 2027 autumn to 2028); line 187 (TNC programmed one year at a time). The use of the calendar as a delay tactic is inference.
proposals.parameter: sw_calendar_defer (0/1) with p_redefer: replace constant r by r = months until the next budget milestone m*, and re-defer at that milestone with probability p_redefer
proposals.range: sw_calendar_defer in {0,1}; p_redefer U(0, 0.6); milestones: CIP adoption (yearly), 5YPP window (2027-09 to 2028)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED -> IDLE transition (the r parameter) and, through it, the PREPARING start timing.

proposals.behaviour: Design-only or readiness funding. Finance funds only planning and design (PE) for a subset of intersections from local money, citing the 'stage funding, raise readiness' rule, and holds construction until an outside grant (HSIP) is won. It looks like a response and costs little, but produces no installs for years.
proposals.trigger: Advocates demand a visible commitment while the CIP draft says to fund urgent needs by phase and put flexible money into match for external grants.
proposals.effect_in_model: A new branch for the local line: n_pe intersections get design money only. They become 'design done' (shortening t_dsg and the PE step for a later HSIP package, and supporting the BCR-ready inventory) but remain outside the installation queue. If HSIP is not won within a horizon, they stay as stranded design with no install, and the design may go out of date after a time.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in 02. D3.4 has the local special batch going 'under design' then to construction after t_des; HSIP has t_dsg, but a design-only local grant with a conditional construction is not a rule. F-f ties overrun discovery to design completion, which would then be paid for with no construction.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 line 154 (CIP draft rule: stage funding of urgent needs, 'raise project/grant readiness'); line 149 (flexible money to match); line 113 (incentive to apply for grants that pay Signal Shop labour). The use of design-only funding as a stalling response is inference, no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_design_only (0/1) and n_pe (number of intersections given design-only money per cycle); design validity t_stale
proposals.range: sw_design_only in {0,1}; n_pe U(5, 25); t_stale U(36, 72) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 local special batch (Fi -> I) rule and the HSIP design node t_dsg for the intersections chosen.

proposals.behaviour: Operating-deficit sweep of the small local APS line. When the capital budget is rebalanced against the operating gap, the finance manager quietly pulls back unspent, non-contractual local flexible money (the general-fund population-baseline APS row and unassigned signal reserve) toward higher-priority needs before it is ever granted to an APS batch. The line shrinks without any decision against APS.
proposals.trigger: Operating deficit year (FY27 gap about $307M, rising), board asks that capital-to-operating transfers be spread so no project loses all funding, and APS has no contractual claim on the row.
proposals.effect_in_model: A_local (annual local money available to APS) is multiplied by a stochastic haircut each year. This lowers money for the local batch (PW2, PW6, PW5 top-up) and for the local fallback after HSIP failure. It also makes the local fallback in the PW1 and PW2 chains less reliable.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D10 has A_local as a static U(0, 0.57M) and F-k for the director 10 percent / SG000 not being used for APS. Neither lets an existing APS-labelled row be taken away over time. 02 has no capital-to-operating transfer rule (grep for sweep/transfer found nothing). The 01 'adjustable parameter' of $20-40M per round is not used in 02.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2: operating gap $307-434M per year (l.145); 'transfer capital to operating $20-40M per round' (l.163); board wants one-time transfers and wording 'spread out, so no project loses funding' (l.157); CIP draft rule 'protect SGR, phase funding' (l.154). The only local APS general-fund rows are estimates (l.162). No document says an APS row was actually swept, so the sweep itself has no direct support.
proposals.parameter: sweep_local: annual probability U(0, 0.5), and fraction taken U(0.2, 1.0) (or a single scalar haircut h_sweep in U(0, 0.8)).
proposals.range: p_sweep U(0, 0.5) per year; fraction U(0.2, 1.0). Applies in M-A, M-C and M-D; zero in a control run.
proposals.rule_modified: D10 A_local: A_local(t) = A_local0 x (1 - Bernoulli(p_sweep) x fraction), applied at each fiscal year start. Also alters the F-k recovery branch in D3.5.

proposals.behaviour: Grant-contingent placeholder rows. Finance keeps an APS row in the CIP that is labelled as funded by a future grant (an 'EST' row tied to a grant cycle). The row signals to advocates that APS is funded or on track, but no local money is committed and no one holds a duty to backfill if the grant is not won or never applied for.
proposals.trigger: A disability council meeting or pressure event arrives while no application has been submitted. The cheapest response is to point to the CIP row, and the row costs nothing in local funds.
proposals.effect_in_model: While a placeholder is live and the grant has not been awarded, pressure(t) from advocates is discounted. When the grant window passes with no application or an award fails, no backfill is triggered, and F-d 'local money tops up the refunded part' does not fire. The row is then silently dropped or rolled to the next cycle.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 treats the SG015 C13 row as an EST only for the BCR denominator (D3.3 l.191). F-j, F-k and the DEFLECTED state handle verbal deflection, not an on-paper funding row that damps pressure. No rule makes pressure react to the presence of a placeholder.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2: CIP27m rows SG142 $488,144 'HSIP C13 - EST' and SG143 $1,588,144 'HSIP C14 - EST' (l.140). 01 3 (HSIP section) l.224: FY25-29 CIP planned SG136 'APS FY25' $1.0M from 'HSIP Cycle 12' while the full C12 application list has no SF APS application. 01 section 2.1 l.109: SG136 has no funding row in FY27-31 (inferred). So the pattern 'row exists without application' is documented. The effect on advocates' pressure is not documented (inference).
proposals.parameter: q_placeholder: probability that, at a pressure event with no active application, a grant-contingent row exists. Companion: pressure discount factor delta_ph U(0, 1) on pressure(t) while the row is live; backfill probability on failure q_backfill U(0, 0.3).
proposals.range: q_placeholder U(0, 1); delta_ph U(0, 1); q_backfill U(0, 0.3); row lifetime tied to the next HSIP window.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED/pressure update (adds a third branch: 'absorbed by placeholder'), and D3.5 F-d recovery path (backfill).

proposals.behaviour: Local-match triage. Finance withholds or declines to certify the 10 percent local match for an APS-bearing HSIP package, because the most flexible local money is already earmarked as match for larger-leverage grants (large safe-streets or signal grant awards that need 20 percent match). APS-sized asks lose the internal competition for scarce match dollars.
proposals.trigger: An APS package is ready for HSIP submission while large grant awards with match obligations are on the books and the capital budget is short by about $246M versus the previous plan.
proposals.effect_in_model: A submission step that currently passes on BCR alone gains a second gate. A package with BCR at or above 5.0 is held (delayed one cycle) or shrunk (only the C-group package goes) with probability q_match. This reduces SUBMITTED counts and shifts submissions to later windows. It adds a failure mode separate from F-a (BCR below 5) and F-c.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.3 treats the 10 percent local match as a cost line in the project cost only. D3.3 'additional budget' (APS part) is reported in cost_by_actor but not used as a gate. F-a to F-m contain no match-denial path. M-C is about unit cost pressing on start probability, not about match competition.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2: 'most flexible money must be used as match' (l.149); capital revenue about $246M below last CIP, 'not enough to fund all approved projects' (l.148); 01 section 3: HSIP reimburses 90 percent, local match 10 percent, staff hours can count as soft match (l.203); SS4A Tenderloin match $5.6M federal plus $1.4M Prop L (l.240) shows large match claims on the same pool; CIP27 SG106/SG115 sums $8.0M and $15.97M (l.237). No line says APS was denied match.
proposals.parameter: q_match: probability a ready package is denied or deferred for lack of match, applied at the submission step. Companion hold time t_match U(6, 24) months.
proposals.range: q_match U(0, 0.5); t_match U(6, 24); soft-match credit (staff-hour share) s_soft U(0, 1) reduces q_match multiplicatively.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 'Route A' submission gate (before the BCR at or above 5.0 test) and D3.1 SUBMIT transition.

proposals.behaviour: Reclassifying Signal Shop labor and APS work as capital or as an existing eligible category (street safety, SGR extension, ADA curb-ramp program) so APS can use otherwise-restricted capital or relieve operating cost, instead of asking for new money. This is the reverse of the 'no money' answer. Finance sometimes finds funding by relabeling, which also lets staff cost be charged to capital.
proposals.trigger: Operating deficit pressure plus a board proposal to widen the capital definition (maintenance extending asset life five years or more counts as capital), at the same time as advocates ask for visible movement.
proposals.effect_in_model: Creates a new money source for the internal route. Signal Shop hours on C-class installs get charged to a capital line, raising effective K_crew budget headroom and A_local without a new grant. Costs: it uses up the same relabel headroom that other maintenance competes for, and may bring a scope fight (replace versus new install, as in the PW6 SG017 chain).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW5 (maintenance budget add-on b_hw) and PW6 (writing new APS into existing SG017 replacement scope) are reclassification-like but are specific lines. No general parameter covers 'work-order relabel to capital' or 'broaden the capital definition'. Drop-risk: if the team judges PW5/PW6 to cover it, merge into b_hw.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2 l.158: 2025-02 budget options 'move 25 percent of paint and sign shop staff to capital priorities' and 'restructure work orders so they count as capital projects' ($2.5M; Signal Shop not named); l.159: FY27-31 CIP proposes to 'expand the capital investment definition' to cover maintenance extending life 5+ years. 01 section 2.1 l.113: grants paying Signal Shop labor can ease the operating deficit (inferred incentive). No document says the idea was applied to APS.
proposals.parameter: q_relabel: probability per year that finance adopts relabeling for Signal Shop APS installs; effect size b_relabel (dollars per year, U(0, 250k)) added to A_local-like pool.
proposals.range: q_relabel U(0, 0.6); b_relabel U(0, 250k) per year; scope-fight blocking probability q_scope U(0, 0.5) as in q_sg017_block.
proposals.rule_modified: D10 A_local and D3.4 internal route (K_crew funding) plus PW5/PW6 chain when active.

proposals.behaviour: Cost-shifting of curb-ramp and conduit work to another budget line or agency. The finance manager re-codes the ramp and excavation share of an over-budget batch to the Public Works curb-ramp program, the ADA right-of-way general-fund earmark, or the host project's budget, so the APS line only carries hardware. The overrun is moved, not paid.
proposals.trigger: Design finishes (t_des) and the discovered overrun exceeds contingency (kappa_cont), with ramp or conduit being the largest part of the excess.
proposals.effect_in_model: Reduces the funding gap that F-f sends to q_topup or TERMINATED. It also adds a lag for the ramp share (wait for the PW program), and raises cost_by_actor for PW and ODA-related lines. Fewer sites are terminated, but ramp-dependent sites install later.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-f allows only three gap sources: contingency, a q_topup request, or TERMINATED. D3.4 says pipe and ramp needs are fixed into planned cost at list-entry. PW curb-ramp money appears in 01 but is not a source in the 02 rules. Nearest items are F-f top-up and F-k director 10%, which are different mechanisms.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 (and the budget memo line near 258/265): mayor's budget lists priority curb ramps and obstacle removal as a citywide capital priority. 01 s2.10 or the nearby row (~line 373): curb ramps FY26 $4.0M, FY27/28 requests $8.1M/$12.2M. 01 around line 265: CP-T says accessibility capital 'usually appears in other departments' budgets, including traffic and signals (APS)'. Row ~line 158 of s2.2: 'reorganise work orders so they count as capital projects' (budget-option language, same accounting-reclassification move). No document shows this being done for APS specifically.
proposals.parameter: s_ramp_shift
proposals.range: U(0, 0.8) = share of the ramp-and-conduit excess charged to the PW curb-ramp line instead of the APS batch; companion lag t_shift U(3, 18) months before the shifted part is funded; set to 0 to switch off
proposals.rule_modified: F-f gap-source rule (adds a fourth source before q_topup) and D3.4 internal delivery (ramp-dependent sites wait t_shift)

proposals.behaviour: Scope shedding and phasing of the batch. Rather than topping up or terminating, the manager approves funding only for the sites that stay inside plan+contingency and sends the conduit-heavy sites to a later phase or a later funding window. This is the 'fund in phases' habit applied to a single batch.
proposals.trigger: The batch-level gap after design is positive, and the budget is already tight (costpress high, capital revenue short of approved projects).
proposals.effect_in_model: Splits one local batch into a funded subset and a deferred subset. The deferred sites go back to the pool as new cost-drawn items with a higher unit price, which raises costpress for the remaining pool and may feed M-C1. Replaces the all-or-nothing TERMINATED outcome with partial delivery.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-f terminates the project or the site on a failed top-up, and sends the site back to the pool. It does not let the manager choose a subset at the batch level, and does not apply a rule for which sites to drop (cheapest first, or by a score).
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 decision rule row: CIP draft rule to 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project and grant readiness)' (CIPpol p.6). Board comment row: spread cuts 'so no single project loses its funding' (CIPpol p.21). 01 SG142 row: 'about 22 intersections, no excavation, all built by Signal Shop' shows a no-dig subset already used as a unit. No document shows a mid-batch descope for APS.
proposals.parameter: sw_descope with rule parameter d_cut
proposals.range: sw_descope in {0,1}; d_cut in {cheapest-first, highest-BCR-first, random}; fraction of gap absorbed by dropping sites p_drop U(0.3, 1.0)
proposals.rule_modified: F-f (replaces the project-level TERMINATED branch with a batch-level subset rule) and the local batch sizing step that uses plan cost times (1+kappa_cont)

proposals.behaviour: Competitive, depleting use of the 10% director discretion. The 10% cap is cumulative and shared by every capital overrun in the agency. The manager spends it on higher-visibility needs first (Muni reliability, state-of-good-repair, contractual obligations), so what remains for APS depends on the claims already made that year, and the manager can also hold the room back as a buffer rather than release it.
proposals.trigger: An APS overrun request arrives while other overruns or operating-to-capital transfers are drawing on the same cumulative 10% room.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes the chance of an APS top-up from the director route time-varying and state-dependent, so it falls as the year's claims build up and recovers when the biennial budget resets. It also couples this actor to the operating deficit.
proposals.already_in_model: Only in a static form. F-k has a fixed probability q_dir U(0, 0.8) that the 10% or SG000 reserve is not used for APS. There is no shared stock, no competing claimants, and no reset.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: director may adjust capital budget up to cumulative 10% (about $65M) without the board (RES l.22, l.82); board said diversions should be 'one-time' and cut the diversion from $40M to $20M (CIPpol p.18, p.21); operating gap $307M (FY27) and 'move capital to operating' on the balancing list (BB27 p.2-3); SG000 reserve only $1.6M + $0.5M. The cumulative wording and the competing demands are documented; how the manager ranks APS in that queue has no document support.
proposals.parameter: dir_pool_remaining (state variable) with competing-claim rate lambda_claim and APS priority weight w_aps
proposals.range: lambda_claim U(0.3, 1.5) claims per year, each drawing U(5%, 30%) of the 10% room; w_aps U(0, 1); replaces q_dir by q_dir_t = w_aps * min(1, dir_pool_remaining / gap); pool resets at each biennial budget
proposals.rule_modified: F-k (turns the fixed q_dir into a state-dependent draw) and the PW1/PW2 last-step transition to 'director 10% / general fund'

proposals.behaviour: Delaying the decision to a better window. Instead of approving or refusing a top-up at the design-complete moment, the manager parks the request until the next budget amendment, the mid-cycle budget revision, or the next CIP cycle, expecting more room later or other overruns to resolve first. The site sits designed and unbuilt in the meantime.
proposals.trigger: The gap is beyond contingency and no immediate source exists; the next biennial budget deadline (even-year 5-01) or CIP update is within a known horizon.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a waiting state between design-complete and either funded or TERMINATED. During the wait the site is not in the Signal Shop queue, the designed-but-unfunded stock grows (a visible idle asset), and costs may drift up again while the wait runs.
proposals.already_in_model: Mostly not. F-e has a pause t_pause U(3,12) then one re-request, but only for the PIF-denied outsourcing markup. F-f has an immediate top-up draw with no wait. F-j has t_defer, but for the SFCTA board vote, not for the SFMTA finance decision.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 and 01 line ~412: general-fund requests are two-year and due before 5-01 in even years; 01 line ~187: TNC money is pay-as-you-go and usually programmed one year at a time; 01 row ~190: no EP17 signal request appeared in the 2026 allocation memos. Together these show that windows are discrete and decisions can wait for them. Whether the manager deliberately waits is the model-builder's inference.
proposals.parameter: t_wait_topup and p_wait
proposals.range: p_wait U(0, 0.7) = chance the top-up decision is deferred; t_wait_topup U(3, 24) months (snapped to the next budget window); cost drift during the wait g_wait U(0, 0.1) per year
proposals.rule_modified: F-f (inserts a WAITING state before the q_topup draw) and D3.4 TERMINATED conditions (a site waiting longer than a threshold is terminated or goes to a new window)

proposals.behaviour: Cost-shifting of the ramp/conduit scope to a non-APS line. The finance manager re-books conduit and curb-ramp work to a line that already funds such work (the Public Works curb-ramp program, a paving or signal-modernization project, or a partner project's contingency), so the APS batch only carries the APS hardware and fits its envelope again.
proposals.trigger: Design completion (the F-f overrun-discovery node) shows the overage is mostly the pipe and ramp parts (about $200k each) and exceeds contingency kappa_cont.
proposals.effect_in_model: At the F-f node, a share of the excess (pipe/ramp part) is moved off the APS batch. The gap that must be topped up or terminated shrinks. The cost shows up in cost_by_actor as a different payer, and the shifted ramp work may carry its own delay (like t_parent).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-f only offers top-up (q_topup) or TERMINATED. 'Merged into an existing project' (D3.4, PW4) is decided at intake, not as a reaction to an overrun. No rule moves cost mid-delivery. Close but not the same, so kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 'reorganize work orders so they count as capital projects' (sfmta-media-41700 p.9, p.17) and 'expand the definition of capital investment' (CIPpol p.10). 01 s2.11 and s1.1 row for Public Works: curb ramps have their own funding ($4.0M FY26; $8.1M/$12.2M requested FY27/28) and 'ramp construction does not trigger APS'. 01 s2.1: pipe ~$200k and ramp ~$200k per site.
proposals.parameter: q_shift (probability per overrun event) and f_shift (share of the pipe/ramp excess moved off APS), plus t_shift_delay (months added by the partner line).
proposals.range: q_shift U(0, 0.6); f_shift U(0.3, 1.0); t_shift_delay U(0, 12) months. Setting q_shift = 0 recovers the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: F-f funding-gap handling: add 'cost reassignment' as a third branch before top-up (q_topup) and before TERMINATED.

proposals.behaviour: Triage/descoping inside the batch. The manager keeps the batch money fixed and drops or defers the sites that need new conduit/ramps (the expensive ones). The freed money funds the cheaper APS-only sites, so the batch is cut to fewer, cheaper sites instead of paying the whole overrun or terminating.
proposals.trigger: The post-design site-level cost list shows a few sites far above plan (cost near the $1.0-1.5M upper bound) and the total gap exceeds contingency, with q_topup not granted.
proposals.effect_in_model: The expensive sites go back to the to-do pool (state C), keeping their identity. Cheap sites are installed with the freed money. Installed count in the near term goes up while the hardest sites become 'never served' candidates. This changes the distribution of who gets served, not only whether the batch survives.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-f terminates 'the project / that site' and returns it to the pool, and the batch size is set by planned cost x (1 + kappa_cont) at funding. But there is no rule that swaps in cheaper sites using the money freed by a dropped site, and no rule that chooses which sites to drop by cost rank.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1: unit price $40k minimum to $1.5M maximum; list sites 'selected based on funding'; a senior engineer says not touching existing ramps is '5x faster'. 01 s2.2: board asked that cuts be 'spread so no project loses all funding'. These support selection by cost, but there is no direct document of a descoping practice (no document support for the swap itself).
proposals.parameter: sw_triage (0/1) and rank_rule (drop most expensive first vs. random).
proposals.range: sw_triage in {0, 1}; when 1, the sites dropped are those with the highest realized cost until the gap is within contingency, and freed money buys back cheapest pool sites at u0. rank_rule in {cost_desc, random}.
proposals.rule_modified: F-f and D3.4 internal batch: replace 'batch or site TERMINATED' with 'drop highest-cost sites, then refill from pool'.

proposals.behaviour: Waiting for a budget window before answering the request. The manager does not decide the top-up at design completion; he holds the request until the next mid-cycle budget adjustment or the biennial budget cycle, and meanwhile the sites stay in a paused state.
proposals.trigger: Overrun is above contingency and the needed amount is not small enough to cover quietly from the director's 10% or reserves.
proposals.effect_in_model: q_topup is no longer an immediate coin flip. The top-up can only be granted at fixed calendar dates, so the pause is set by the calendar rather than by t_pause. Construction queue stays empty longer (K_crew idle). It also raises the chance that the cost has moved up again (g_cost) or the owner has left (lambda_quit) before the decision.
proposals.already_in_model: No for this role. t_pause (U(3,12) months) exists only for the F-e outsourcing gap, and F-j's t_defer only for Prop L. The F-f top-up has no timing.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: budget schedule 2025-11 to 2026-04 with 8 board meetings and 'no signal or accessibility agenda'; the 'must treat overruns as one-time' board view; 01 s2.2 the cap of 10% per year. No document says SFMTA actually waits for a budget window on APS overruns (no document support for the delay practice itself).
proposals.parameter: sw_topup_calendar (0/1) and t_topup_wait computed as months to the next budget decision date (or a fixed U range).
proposals.range: sw_topup_calendar in {0,1}; decision dates: April and October each year (two per year); if off, wait = 0. Alternative: t_topup_wait U(0, 9) months.
proposals.rule_modified: F-f 'topup request' step: the request resolves only at calendar dates, not at the design-complete month.

proposals.behaviour: Competition for the director's 10% and reserve pool. When several projects overrun at once, the manager rations the same discretionary pool (cumulative 10% cap, SG000 reserve). A rule that rewards 'readiness' ('fund urgent needs in phases') means a batch that is design-complete and construction-ready gets covered, while an APS batch that is not ready or is politically quiet gets nothing.
proposals.trigger: Several overrun requests in the same year draw on the cumulative 10% director adjustment or SG000 ($1.6M FY27, $0.5M FY28); pool already partly used.
proposals.effect_in_model: q_dir (F-k) and q_topup become state-dependent: a remaining-pool variable that other projects deplete. A decrease in the pool lowers the chance that an APS overrun is covered, and ties the outcome to pressure(t) (the manager responds to visible pressure) and to readiness.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k has q_dir as a fixed probability that the 10% or SG000 is not used for APS, and q_topup is a fixed probability. Neither depends on how much of the 10% has been spent by other projects in the same year or on pressure(t).
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: director may adjust 'up to 10% cumulative' without the board (RES l.22, l.82; about $65M); SG000 $1.6M + $0.5M unallocated signal reserve; draft CIP rule 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project readiness)' (CIPpol p.6); board wants reallocations 'one-time' and 'spread'. The competing-demand part has no direct document support (no document support for other projects' overruns).
proposals.parameter: pool_cap (the discretionary dollars available per fiscal year), load_other (dollars of other overruns drawn from it), and w_press (weight of pressure(t) on the allocation probability).
proposals.range: pool_cap U($0.5M, $6M) per year; load_other U(0, 1.0) x pool_cap; w_press U(0, 1.5) in a logit for q_topup. q_dir / q_topup = logistic(a + w_press x pressure(t) + b x remaining_pool/overrun).
proposals.rule_modified: F-f q_topup and F-k q_dir: replace the fixed probabilities with a function of a yearly pool balance and pressure(t).

proposals.behaviour: Partial descoping instead of whole-project termination: after design shows several sites need new conduit and ramps, the finance manager funds the cheap sites in the batch and strips or defers the expensive ones (re-queued as backlog or N-type), so the batch survives smaller.
proposals.trigger: Overrun found at design-complete (F-f) and actual cost exceeds plan x (1+kappa_cont), and the gap is larger than what top-up can cover.
proposals.effect_in_model: Splits the F-f outcome into two branches. Sites are ranked by overrun per site. Sites are dropped from the most expensive end until batch cost fits the funded envelope. Dropped sites go back to the backlog (becoming N-type if they need a new pole or conduit). The rest enter the Signal Shop queue on time. Changes installed_5y (more early installs, fewer total) and never_served (expensive sites are filtered out).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-f (02 D3.5) only says overrun beyond contingency leads to a top-up request, then 'project / that intersection TERMINATED, back to backlog'. D3.4 'termination' is project-level. There is no rule that selects which sites to cut to keep the rest alive, and no cost-ordered cut.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 decision rules: CIP draft rule 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise readiness)' and board comment on spreading transfers 'so no single project loses funding' (CIPpol p.18, p.21). 01 §2.1: 'easy intersections already installed, now harder and costlier'. No direct document of descoping an APS batch, so the mechanism itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_descope
proposals.range: 0-1 (default 0.5); sensitivity {0, 0.5, 1}. A second knob, descope_rank in {by_overrun, by_BCR}, picks which sites to drop.
proposals.rule_modified: F-f branch after q_topup fails: with prob p_descope, cut sites in order until the cost fits and return only the cut sites to backlog. With 1-p_descope, keep the current whole-project TERMINATED.

proposals.behaviour: Rationed top-up pool tied to the operating-deficit squeeze: overrun requests across all SFMTA capital projects compete for one annual discretionary pool. The manager releases cover only while the pool lasts, and refuses APS more often when the transfer-to-operations pressure is high.
proposals.trigger: Any overrun beyond contingency (F-f) in a fiscal year in which the cumulative 10% director adjustment and/or the capital-to-operations transfer has already been drawn.
proposals.effect_in_model: q_topup (F-e, F-f) and q_dir (F-k) stop being fixed independent draws. They become state-dependent: q_topup(t) = q0 x (1 - deficit_share(t)) x (remaining pool / pool size). Requests arriving later in the year, or many overruns in the same year, face a lower chance. This correlates failures across sites (a clustered overrun year hurts everyone) and links F-e and F-f to the unfunded-signals / SGR competition.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in 02. q_topup and q_dir are fixed U-ranges (D3.5 F-e, F-f, F-k); no pool, no shared annual cap, no link to deficit or transfer-to-operations. strain/costpress in D3.2 act on p_start and crew capacity, not on the funding supply side.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2: 'Operating deficit $307M (FY27), $344M (FY28)'; 'balancing list includes capital moved to operations'; 'Director may adjust capital budget cumulatively up to 10% (about $65M) without the board' (RES l.22, l.82); 'board: transfers should be one-time, cut from $40M to $20M'; 'most flexible money goes to matches' (CIPpol p.11); 'signals are among the worst-degraded assets' (CIPpol p.10).
proposals.parameter: B_disc (annual discretionary pool available for all overrun cover, $M)
proposals.range: U($2M, $65M) as upper bound, with APS share of claims s_aps U(0, 0.05). Plus switch sw_pool in {0,1}: 0 = current independent q_topup/q_dir, 1 = shared pool with first-come drawdown and deficit_share scaling.
proposals.rule_modified: F-e and F-f top-up approval and F-k director discretion: replace fixed q_topup/q_dir with pool-based draw; refuse and move to TERMINATED when the pool is exhausted.

proposals.behaviour: Cost re-attribution of the curb-ramp and conduit portion to another budget line: instead of paying overrun from APS or local flexible money, the finance manager recodes the ramp (and possibly conduit) element to the citywide ADA right-of-way ramp program or to labor reclassified as capital, so the APS batch itself shows a smaller gap.
proposals.trigger: Design-complete overrun in which the excess is mostly ramps/conduit (known +$200k each per site) and an ADA ramp line or a capital-eligible labor-reclassification option exists.
proposals.effect_in_model: Splits the overrun into an APS part (stays with the batch) and a ramp/conduit part. With probability q_shift a share rho_shift of the ramp/conduit excess is moved off the batch to an outside payer (Public Works ramp programme or labor recoded to capital). Reduces the gap that needs top-up. The cost, however, is delay: the shifted ramp work waits for the ramp contractor and ramp-design staff, so the site is held for t_ramp_wait months after design (new Fi-to-Fi wait state before CON/handoff). This trades money for time.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.3 treats ramp cost as a conditional add-on (q_ramp) inside project cost, and PW4 bundles a site with a parent project. There is no shift of the cost to a different payer, and no dependence on the ramp programme's pace.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.12 (curb-ramp lines): 'General fund ADA public right-of-way $55M (FY26-30), $71M (FY31-35)' (CP-I p.4); 'Mayor's budget lists priority curb ramps and barrier removal as a citywide capital priority'; 'ramp design staff shortage slows C35'; 'PW curb ramps FY26 $4.0M; FY27/28 requests $8.1M/$12.2M'. Also 01 §2.2 (2025-02 budget options): 'restructure work orders so they count as capital projects' (T/staffing/sfmta-media-41700 p.9, p.17). The cost-shifting to PW for APS sites is not documented, only the available lines, so partly 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: rho_shift (share of ramp/conduit overrun moved to an outside payer) and t_ramp_wait
proposals.range: rho_shift U(0, 0.8) with switch sw_shift in {0,1}; t_ramp_wait U(3, 24) months (inferred, from 6-9.5 year contract path in 01 §2.12 row 77, only partly)
proposals.rule_modified: F-f gap calculation: gap = overrun - contingency - rho_shift x ramp_excess, with install delayed by t_ramp_wait. Also affects D3.4 internal queue entry time.

proposals.behaviour: Strategic holding: the manager parks the funded-but-overrun batch (no top-up decision) to wait for a better window such as the next CIP/biennial budget cycle, HSIP cycle start, or a 5YPP programming window, rather than approve or refuse now.
proposals.trigger: Overrun gap larger than remaining contingency, no pool money now (see proposal 2), and a known window within about 12 months (CIP Feb-Apr, 5YPP 2027 fall-2028).
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a WAITING state between design-complete and TERMINATED/INSTALL. The request is held until the next calendar window, then decided with the pool and q_topup of that window. Meanwhile the sites sit idle (no Signal Shop work, Fi clock stuck, but the 1.5-year clock from award keeps running). Raises the share of sites whose time to install exceeds 1.5 years (POL10) and may expire the match for HSIP-linked sites. Shifts timing rather than level of success.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-e has t_pause only for the PIF-denied outsourcing case; F-j has t_defer for the Prop L amendment. There is no generic hold-for-window for a locally funded overrun, and no calendar of budget windows for top-up decisions.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2: 'Board budget schedule 2025-11 to 2026-04, 8 sessions' (CIPpol p.23); CIP rule 'phase funding to raise readiness' (CIPpol p.6); 01 §2.3 'next 5YPP window: fall 2027 - 2028'. 01 §2.1: 1.5-year clock runs from award (POL10 p.2). No document of the manager holding an APS request, so the behavior is 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: sw_wait_window, t_wait_max
proposals.range: sw_wait_window in {0,1}; t_wait_max U(3, 18) months, with release only at calendar window months {Feb-Apr, Jul}; also q_expire U(0, 0.3) for the chance that waiting breaks the 1.5-year or match deadline
proposals.rule_modified: F-f unfunded-gap branch: instead of immediate decision, enter WAITING until next window; then draw q_topup(window). Adds one state to D3.4.

proposals.behaviour: Re-scope the batch instead of killing sites. After design finishes and costs exceed contingency, the finance manager keeps the funded count by dropping or deferring only the few conduit-heavy sites, and swaps in cheaper pending sites (C-type, no conduit or ramp work) so the same money buys about the same number of installs. Over-budget sites go back to the pool for a later window.
proposals.trigger: Design-complete event in which batch actual cost > planned x (1 + kappa_cont), and at least one site has a cost far above the batch median.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes who is TERMINATED. Today the overrun is allocated to a project or site and, if no top-up arrives, that site is terminated. With this switch the gap is closed by ranking sites by cost per install, removing the worst ones, and pulling the cheapest unfunded C-type sites from the pool until the funded total fits. Installs are higher and the sites that never get served are different (the expensive N-type tail is pushed back). The pool keeps its hardest sites and so shows a more persistent 'never served' set.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: F-f only has 'top-up or TERMINATE the project/site, return to backlog' and a cost-based batch size at funding time (costpress). It has no post-design substitution of cheaper sites. This is not covered by D3.1 to D3.6.
proposals.evidence: No direct document support for substitution. Indirect support in 01 section 2.1: unit cost rising from $20k to $40k with a $1.5M ceiling, and 'the easy sites are already done'; and in 2.2 the CIP rule of 'phased funding of urgent needs'. MDC26 says remaining sites are 'selected based on funding', which is consistent with funding-driven selection.
proposals.parameter: sw_swap (0/1) and p_swap, the share of the funding gap closed by substitution before any top-up request
proposals.range: p_swap U(0, 1); sw_swap on/off as a mechanism switch
proposals.rule_modified: F-f gap handling: add a step between 'exceeds contingency' and 'top-up request (q_topup)' that applies substitution first and only the remaining gap goes to q_topup.

proposals.behaviour: Cost-shifting by reclassification: the finance manager splits the overrun by cost type and charges the curb-ramp and conduit portion to a different payer or line (the ADA right-of-way or curb-ramp money, or the budget of a concurrent paving/signal project that is already digging), and leaves only the APS hardware on the original line.
proposals.trigger: Overrun is dominated by new conduit and curb-ramp work (the known $200k pipe and $200k ramp components), and another program or project is active at the same site or has a ramp-labelled fund.
proposals.effect_in_model: Reduces the funding gap that reaches q_topup or TERMINATE. It moves part of the cost from 'APS budget need' to another actor's line, so cost_by_actor shifts away from the APS payer and the site finishes sooner. It can also add delay, because the shifted work waits on the other program's schedule.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: 'merged into an existing project' (D3.4) and PW4 route allocation exist, but they are decided at listing time by route, not as a cost split after an overrun. F-f treats the gap as a single block. So the post-overrun cost split is not covered.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2: the General Fund ADA right-of-way earmark of $125M/10 years flows to curb ramps (summary table, line 72); the capital plan says accessibility capital is 'usually reflected in other departments' budgets' (CP-T p.11, line 265); the budget options include 'reorganize work orders so they count as capital projects' (T/staffing/sfmta-media-41700 p.9, p.17, line 158). Section 2.12 notes that curb ramps have a federal transition-plan time obligation while APS does not (line 284). So there is a ramp payer, and a precedent for reclassification.
proposals.parameter: f_shift, the fraction of the ramp/conduit overrun moved to an outside payer, with q_shift as the chance it is accepted
proposals.range: f_shift U(0, 0.6); q_shift U(0, 0.7); t_shift_delay U(0, 12) months added to the delivery of shifted sites
proposals.rule_modified: F-f gap handling: before the contingency check, shift f_shift of the excess to the other payer with probability q_shift; add t_shift_delay to the site's delivery date (D3.4 internal path).

proposals.behaviour: Competing claims on the director's 10% discretion. The manager treats the 10% as a shared pool that is used up across the whole capital programme (other overruns, controller failures, operating shortfalls) so that the amount left for APS in a given month depends on prior use. A partial bridge is made (a loan against a later grant), not an all-or-nothing allowance.
proposals.trigger: An overrun request arrives in a month when the cumulative 10% has already been drawn down by other requests, or when other higher-ranked projects are in trouble in the same budget year.
proposals.effect_in_model: Turns q_dir from a fixed one-off draw into a state-dependent draw. This reduces the odds that a bridge is available exactly when several overruns coincide (the same batch and later batches), and it creates correlation between APS overruns and operating-deficit pressure. It increases the probability of TERMINATED in bad years and leaves more in good years.
proposals.already_in_model: Only partly: F-k has q_dir as an exogenous probability 'director 10% or SG000 not used for APS', and q_topup is exogenous. The cumulative cap and competing claims are not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2: 'the director may adjust the capital budget within a cumulative 10% (about $65M) without going back to the board' (RES l.22, l.82, line 156); the board wants diversions to be 'one-time' and reduced from $40M to $20M 'so no project is cut off' (CIPpol p.18, p.21, line 157); the CIP rule is to 'protect SGR' and fund urgent needs in phases (line 155); the operating deficit is $307M and the balancing list includes shifting capital to operations (lines 143-144); SG000 is an unassigned signal reserve of $1.6M and $0.5M (line 137).
proposals.parameter: B_dir (annual pool in $) and u_dir (average annual use by other claims, as a share of B_dir); q_dir becomes q_dir x (1 − used/B_dir)
proposals.range: B_dir U($5M, $65M); u_dir U(0.3, 1.0); a fixed half of SG000 treated as available
proposals.rule_modified: F-k and the F-f top-up step: replace the constant q_dir with a draw that depends on a running balance of the 10% pool, updated each month.

proposals.behaviour: Hold the request and wait for a better window. The manager does not reject or approve the overrun at once, but parks it until the next budget cycle or CIP update (or until a grant such as C14 or a Prop L amendment is decided), accepting the delay and rising prices in exchange for a funded source.
proposals.trigger: Overrun above contingency, a missing bridge (no director discretion available now) and a known upcoming decision point within the next few months.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a PARKED state for the site or batch between 'design complete' and 'TERMINATED / funded'. Parked sites cost time, and while they wait their price rises with costpress (about 9 to 10 percent a year), which can push a site past the point where top-up is feasible. It also changes the timing of installs, so the 24-month metrics move.
proposals.already_in_model: Only partly: F-e has t_pause for a second request only in the PIF/outsourcing path, and PW paths have 'next available window' for new applications. F-f has no waiting state: the gap is resolved immediately by q_topup or termination.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2 lines 160-161: the board budget schedule runs from 2025-11 to 2026-04 (8 meetings) and none covers accessibility or signals; the CIP is an annual cycle and SG142/SG143 are tied to future years (line 136); 2.1 line 119: prices have risen by about 9 to 10 percent a year. No document shows a finance manager actually parking an overrun, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: t_hold, the months a gap is parked until the next decision window, and p_hold, the share of overruns that are parked instead of decided at once
proposals.range: p_hold U(0, 0.7); t_hold U(2, 12) months, truncated at the next window date; price growth during the wait from the existing costpress parameter
proposals.rule_modified: F-f: add a PARKED state with exit at the next window; on exit, re-draw q_topup using the inflated cost, and terminate if the gap has grown beyond the cap.

proposals.behaviour: Scope-wording hedge: finance drafts the SG017 allocation request so APS is allowed in scope but carries no dedicated line, dollar cap, or deliverable count. The project is justified as 'hardware replacement' and APS is added only 'where feasible'. This lets finance say APS is eligible without committing money, and a later allocation memo can still be spent on controllers.
proposals.trigger: Requests for SG017 to be spent on APS (advocate pressure or an SFMTA APS owner) arrive while controller or firewall failures are visible and SGR money is described as 'extremely limited'. Also triggered by the CIP rule 'fund urgent needs in phases'.
proposals.effect_in_model: Splits PW6 into two outcomes. 'Eligible in scope' no longer implies APS money is reserved. Nominal SG017 scope can be APS-eligible while the allocation request carries a=0 earmark. Drives an extra block probability inside SFMTA's own request, before SFCTA acts.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.6 PW6 and D10 q_sg017_block already cover SFCTA limiting scope to 'replace', or funds used by failure-priority projects. That block is modelled as outcome-side, at the SFCTA or failure-priority stage. The finance manager's own authoring choice in the request is not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 3.2 / l.446: CIP scope text allows 'install new ... APS where it is determined that existing conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition' (the conditional hedge already exists in the text). l.447: FY24 and FY25-26 allocations went to cabinets, detectors, RRFB and ~98 controllers. 01 section 2.2: 'signals among SFMTA's most degraded assets, SGR funding extremely limited' (CIPpol p.10). No document support that finance deliberately omits an APS line.
proposals.parameter: p_scope_hedge
proposals.range: U(0, 0.8); share of SG017 request cycles in which the request text lists APS as eligible but with a_earmark = 0
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 start condition and D10 a_sg017. When the hedge fires, a_sg017 = 0 for that fiscal year regardless of q_sg017_block. APS can still be funded only if a signal-shop or advocate trigger converts it into a named line next cycle.

proposals.behaviour: Earmark-for-leverage: finance carves a small APS tranche (or a pole/conduit survey tranche) out of SG017 or the 10% director discretion, not to install, but to produce 'readiness' (a cost-validated list of C-type intersections with adequate poles and conduit). The aim is to meet CIP 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project/grant readiness)' and to feed an HSIP package or match.
proposals.trigger: A HSIP window is open (C13 deadline 2026-11-02, later C14) and the match pool is thin; the CIP rule says the most flexible money goes to match. Counts as a way to spend discretion on readiness without committing to installation.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a funded readiness step before PW6 or PW1: it reduces the preparation time (t_prep) and the pole/conduit uncertainty for a subset of C-type intersections, and creates an early quasi-commitment that raises the later chance of an HSIP application. Costs a small share of SG017 or discretion, so it competes with controller work.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.2 and D3.3 handle HSIP rules and match, F-k handles discretion as a temporary surplus, but readiness-only spending as a distinct finance action is not in 02 (checked D3.1-D3.6 and D10 q_dir).
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2 CIPpol p.6: 'fund urgent needs in phases (improve project/grant readiness)'; CIPpol p.11: 'flexible money goes to match' (l.149, l.154). 01 section 2.2 row: grant pay for Signal Shop labour reduces operating deficit (incentive, CIPpol p.10). No document support that SFMTA has funded a pole/conduit survey for APS.
proposals.parameter: a_ready (and switch sw_readiness)
proposals.range: a_ready U($0, $100k) per FY drawn from SG017 or q_dir pool; sw_readiness in {0,1}; effect: t_prep reduced by U(0.2, 0.5) for intersections on the surveyed list
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING duration and the eligibility test for C-type (poles/conduit adequate) in D3.6 PW1/PW6; also consumes budget in the F-k pool.

proposals.behaviour: Discretion-as-bridge with a payback expectation: the 10% director adjustment is used for APS only as a loan or bridge against an expected external reimbursement (HSIP 90%, Prop L amendment, SFCTA reallocation), and finance refuses it unless a repayment source is named. Accounted one-off, because the board wants diversions 'one-off'.
proposals.trigger: An APS item has a grant award or a pending Prop L amendment but cash timing is short; or a PW switch lands on 'director discretion' (end of PW1). The board comment 'diversions should be one-off, spread out so no project is cut off' makes a repeatable APS draw hard.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes F-k from a one-draw probability q_dir to a conditional rule: discretion is released only if a named repayment source with status 'approved or pending' exists; the allocation is one-off per APS batch (counter), and it can be clawed back if the source fails. Produces a coupling between F-k and F-b/F-j outcomes.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k has q_dir (U(0,0.8)) and says it is uncertain whether discretion can be used for APS. The conditionality on a named repayment source, one-off counter and clawback are not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.2 l.157: board view that diversions should be 'one-off' and spread 'so no project is cut off' (CIPpol p.18, p.21); l.156: director can adjust up to 10% cumulative (RES l.22, l.82). No document support that discretion was used as a bridge loan.
proposals.parameter: q_dir_cond (and n_dir_max)
proposals.range: q_dir_cond U(0, 0.6) = release probability when no repayment source is approved (else q_dir); n_dir_max in {1,2,3} per five years; clawback when source fails with prob U(0,0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: F-k and the PW1 end node ('director 10% / general fund'). Replaces the single Bernoulli q_dir with a conditional draw.

proposals.behaviour: Post-approval raiding of the restored APS line (reprogramming back to controllers). Finance supports the amendment on paper, then, after the next visible outage or controller failure, quietly shifts the APS line's yearly money to controller/firewall replacement via later allocation requests or a 5YPP reprogramming, so the line exists but does not pay out.
proposals.trigger: A new outage or controller-failure event after the amendment passes, while EP17 stays over-programmed and the remaining margin is $0-0.5M/yr.
proposals.effect_in_model: A_local falls during the year (or the rest of the line's life) after each failure event, so fewer or smaller local APS batches are funded. This makes the dedicated line (PW2) less durable than the current rules assume.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 has q_sg017_block (controllers use up SG017 money), but only for the SG017 hardware line and only at the first allocation request. Nothing lets a line that was already created be taken back (checked D3.2, D3.5 F-j/F-k, D3.6 PW2, D10 A_local). Not a full duplicate, so kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'visible-failure-driven: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (OCT25 p.7, tagged inference). 01 s2.1: EP17 hardware money $1M for ~98 controllers while the 2023 PIF listed APS replacement as eligible (OCT25 p.7; EP17-5YPP p.70). 01 s2.3: EP17 over-programmed ~202%.
proposals.parameter: q_raid (probability that a failure event diverts the line) with outage rate lambda_outage; raid takes fraction f_raid of A_local for that year.
proposals.range: q_raid U(0, 0.8); lambda_outage U(0.1, 0.5)/yr (hypothesis, uncalibrated); f_raid U(0.3, 1.0).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.2 / D10 A_local (new per-year event that reduces it after the dedicated line opens); extends PW6 q_sg017_block to the line created by PW2.

proposals.behaviour: Leverage-only release: finance will give local flexible money to APS only as match for an external award (HSIP 10% match, soft staff-time match), not as a stand-alone cash line. It holds the cash until the HSIP result is known, i.e. waits for a better window and sets the dedicated line up as a contingent match line.
proposals.trigger: The CIP rule 'put the most flexible money into match' plus a $246M capital shortfall and a $307M operating deficit, when the amendment asks for stand-alone APS cash.
proposals.effect_in_model: Local money for APS is released only after an HSIP award (C13 around 2027-03/04, C14 around 2029). Before that, A_local for stand-alone batches is 0, and the money is tied to the HSIP outcome. This delays the local path (PW2) and links it to PW1, so the two are no longer independent.
proposals.already_in_model: No. A_local is a free-standing yearly amount that goes to a batch on approval (s82 local field). HSIP is a separate route, and the 10% match appears only in the HSIP route (checked D3.3, D3.6, D10).
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'subsidy rules prioritize expansion over maintenance; the most flexible money goes to match' (CIPpol p.11); CIP rule 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise readiness)' (CIPpol p.6); Larkin signal example with a 20% local match (s2.5 row). Whether finance would really tie APS money to HSIP is no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_match_only (switch; when 1, stand-alone local APS batches are blocked until an HSIP award exists, then A_local is capped at 10-20% of the award).
proposals.range: 0/1, 50/50 across runs; cap U(0.10, 0.25) of award.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 local field approval rule and D10 A_local; links PW2 and PW1.

proposals.behaviour: Relabelling and cost-shifting: finance counts Signal Shop labour for APS as capital via work-order restructuring and as soft match, so APS looks cheaper in cash terms and the 'over-programmed' line is not charged for labour.
proposals.trigger: Operating deficit pressure that rewards moving labour onto capital or grants, plus an HSIP application that allows staff hours as soft match.
proposals.effect_in_model: Cash cost per site drops by a labour share (so a given A_local funds more sites). But the same Signal Shop hours are committed to the grant, which raises strain(t) and lowers K_crew, so the two effects trade off. It changes cost and crew capacity together.
proposals.already_in_model: No. costpress and strain are exogenous trajectories; no rule ties a finance accounting choice to cost per site or crew load (checked D3.2 and D10).
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 2025-02 budget options 'move 25% of paint-and-sign shop staff to capital priorities' and 'restructure work orders so they count toward capital projects' (staffing-media p.9, p.17; Signal Shop not named). 01 s2.1: 'grant pays Signal Shop labour, easing the operating deficit' (inference). 01 s2.12 / HSIP: staff hours as soft match (QA13 Q14, Q59).
proposals.parameter: f_reclass (share of Signal Shop labour cost moved off the cash budget) with a linked crew commitment that adds f_reclass x delta_strain to strain(t).
proposals.range: f_reclass U(0, 0.5); delta_strain U(0, 0.3) (hypothesis).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 delivery cost per site (u0) and the strain(t)/K_crew rule in D3.2 (M-B rows).

proposals.behaviour: Sponsor-side delay of the amendment request: finance does not bring the amendment to the SFCTA board now but folds it into the 2027-fall to 2028 5YPP window to avoid a mid-cycle fight over an over-programmed line, or packages it with a larger signals request.
proposals.trigger: The over-programmed EP17 and the note that the next five years 'are not expected to have this much front-loading'; a competing controller request that finance ranks first.
proposals.effect_in_model: A new delay between PW2 starting and the amendment reaching the board, before any SFCTA veto or deferral. It raises the chance PW2 falls through to the general-fund request or HSIP.
proposals.already_in_model: Only partly. F-j covers SFCTA vetoing or deferring (q_veto, t_defer), and PW2 switches on theta_defer. The sponsor's own delay before submitting is not modelled (checked F-j, PW2, D10).
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 5YPP revision 'can happen any time (D4 precedent 3-4 months), or wait for 2028' (row in s2 table, line 411); 'only responds to requests from the applicant' (SFCTA, 01 s2.3). Finance's actual choice to hold back is no document support.
proposals.parameter: t_hold (months finance holds the request before submitting) with q_wait (probability it waits for the 2027-fall window).
proposals.range: q_wait U(0, 0.6); t_hold U(0, 18) months, set to the window date when q_wait fires (hypothesis).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2 start rule and F-j (adds a sponsor-side delay before the veto/defer draw).

proposals.behaviour: Displacement (supplanting) of other local money. When a dedicated Prop L APS line is restored, the finance manager lowers the general-fund / SG000 / director-discretion money that would otherwise go to APS, treating the new line as the APS funder. Net new APS money is then less than the restored line.
proposals.trigger: The SFCTA board approves, or is likely to approve, the EP17 amendment. The operating gap ($307M FY27) and the 'capital to operations' balancing list put pressure on every flexible dollar.
proposals.effect_in_model: In PW2 and PW1's end step, local flexible APS money (`a_local`, now a fixed $0-0.57M/yr) becomes reactive. It drops by a fraction of the new Prop L line once that line is live. Net APS dollars flowing = Prop L + a_local*(1-d). Recovery time under PW2 is longer than the model currently shows.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. F-k and q_dir only model whether the director's 10% / SG000 is used for APS at all. They do not model a response to the arrival of another source. D10 treats the local flexible amount as exogenous. DROP check: no match in 02 D3.5 or D3.6.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'CIPpol p.11 补助规则优先扩张而非维护；最灵活的钱要拿去做配套'; 'CIP27m: 本地灵活资金给 APS $0-0.57M/年, only one general-fund APS row'. Displacement itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: `d_displace` (displacement rate)
proposals.range: U(0, 1), with 0 as the model's current behaviour. A 2x2 switch `sw_displace` {off, on} for PW2 and PW6 only.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2 (and the F-k fallback in PW1). Local flexible APS money in D3.3/D10 is reduced by d_displace x the Prop L APS allocation each year.

proposals.behaviour: Post-restoration raid (reprogramming on a visible outage). After the APS line exists, a citywide signal outage or controller failure makes the finance manager move or ask to move the APS line to controllers, using a 5YPP reprogramming or a director adjustment. The line exists on paper but the cash is gone.
proposals.trigger: A visible outage event, which the evidence says drives EP17 hardware money (2022 and 2025 outages). The over-programmed EP17 leaves no other source for the repair.
proposals.effect_in_model: The restored line is no longer a stable stream. After each outage shock, a fraction of the remaining APS balance is moved out and the next allocation request is delayed. This lowers PW2's reach and makes the PW2 vs PW0 gap fragile.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. `q_sg017_block` (D3.6 PW6, D10) covers the existing SG017 line being used up by controllers. Nothing covers the dedicated line after restoration, and no outage shock process is written into D3.5. Keep only the post-restoration part.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 176: 'EP17 结果是可见故障驱动：控制器在 2022、2025 两次停电后拿到 EP17 硬件钱【推断】'; 01 s2.1 line 126: $1M of hardware replacement went to about 98 controllers while APS was an eligible use.
proposals.parameter: `q_raid` (share of the APS line moved per outage) and `λ_outage` (outage rate)
proposals.range: `q_raid` U(0, 0.8) of the remaining balance; `λ_outage` U(0.1, 0.5) per year. Both 0 in the baseline.
proposals.rule_modified: A new event in D3.5 (F-n), acting on the PW2 allocation. It can reuse the F-j path for any resulting amendment.

proposals.behaviour: Sponsor-side timing. The finance manager does not oppose the amendment but asks SFMTA not to submit now. They prefer to fold it into the 2027-28 5YPP update, or to submit it only after controller needs are settled, so the over-programmed plan is repaired once.
proposals.trigger: EP17 is over-programmed (the 5YPP commits about 202% of pay-as-you-go through FY28) and the next 5YPP window is 2027 autumn to 2028. SFMTA is the only applicant, so it controls whether the amendment arrives.
proposals.effect_in_model: PW2 gets a sponsor lag before the amendment reaches the board, separate from board refusal. The extra delay lengthens `recovery_time`. It also changes the order of PW2 versus PW1's C14 window.
