proposals.already_in_model: Not found. F-j (`q_veto`, `t_defer`) is the SFCTA board's decision and delay. `θ_defer` in PW2 is a trigger after submission. No parameter delays the submission itself.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.4 line 411: 'Prop L 恢复 APS 专项, 5YPP 修订随时可走（D4 先例 3-4 个月）；或等 2028'. 01 s2.2 line 180: 'EP17 下一个五年预计不会有这种程度的超前'. No document says the manager has actually chosen to wait.
proposals.parameter: `t_sponsor`, with a binary `s_wait` (fold into the next 5YPP window)
proposals.range: `s_wait` Bernoulli U(0, 0.7); if true, submission moves to the next 5YPP window (2027-10 to 2028-06), else lag `t_sponsor` U(0, 9) months.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2 start: the amendment event time = trigger + t_sponsor, before F-j is drawn.

proposals.behaviour: Labor capitalization. The finance manager prices Signal Shop and design labor into APS capital projects (reclassified work orders, a wider definition of 'capital') to relieve the operating deficit. Each APS capital dollar buys fewer intersections, and the line looks attractive for a reason unrelated to APS.
proposals.trigger: The operating gap ($307-434M/yr). Budget options in the evidence already include reclassifying work orders to count as capital. The FY27-31 CIP widens the capital definition to cover maintenance that extends life by 5+ years.
proposals.effect_in_model: Effective unit cost per intersection rises by a labor-loading factor. Batch size falls. The cost-pressure term enters `p_start` earlier than M-C1's market-driven price rise. It can also push in the other direction by making the line easier to defend.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. M-C's `costpress(t)` (D3.2) is a market unit-cost trend. κ_cont and κ_contract (D3.5 F-f, F-e) are contingency and contracting markups. None is an accounting choice driven by the operating gap.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: '2025-02 预算选项：重组工单以便计入资本项目' (not tied to the Signal Shop); 'FY27-31 CIP 拟扩大资本投资定义，覆盖延寿 5 年以上的维护'; 'BB27 p.2-3 平衡清单含资本资金挪到运营'. The effect on APS has no document support.
proposals.parameter: `κ_cap` (labor-capitalization loading)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.35) added to the planned cost of local-funded APS batches only, with a switch `sw_cap` {off, on}.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 / M-C: planned cost per intersection in local batches. The `costpress(t)` term gets an additive `κ_cap` for local batches when `sw_cap` is on.

proposals.behaviour: Outage-triggered raid on the new line. After the amendment passes, a power outage or controller failure wave makes the finance manager (and SFCTA staff) re-point the freshly restored APS money, plus the SG000 reserve and the cumulative 10% director adjustment, to controller replacement. The line exists on paper but is drained before an APS grant request is filed. Outages are random shocks that deplete a shared pool, not a one-off yes/no.
proposals.trigger: A controller-outage event (rate lambda_outage). The visible-failure rule: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages. EP17 is already over-programmed, so any shock lands on a pool with no slack.
proposals.effect_in_model: Cuts A_local in the same fiscal year and cuts the remaining 10% headroom. Both are then unavailable to F-k and PW2. Raises the chance that the dedicated line (sw_line = 1) pays out zero in a given year. Also makes outages correlated across years.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 has q_sg017_block, but only for the SG017 route and as a static per-grant probability. F-k's q_dir is a single Bernoulli with no depletion. No outage shock process drains A_local or the 10% pool after PW2's line is created. Kept as a narrower, new rule: a stochastic drain on a shared pool, applied to PW2 and F-k.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'outcome is driven by visible failures: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (OCT25 p.7, tagged inference). 01 s2.2: the director can adjust up to 10% without going back to the board. 01 s2.3: EP17 5YPP committed $27.49M against $8.52M pay-as-you-go, about 202% ahead. 02 PW6 mentions faults taking priority only for SG017.
proposals.parameter: lambda_outage (events per year) and f_raid (share of the year's remaining A_local, SG000 reserve and 10% headroom pulled per event)
proposals.range: lambda_outage U(0, 1.0) per year; f_raid U(0, 0.8); first-pass prior, no data
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-k (q_dir becomes state-dependent on the pool), D10 A_local, PW2 line payout, PW6 q_sg017_block

proposals.behaviour: Approve-but-back-load. The finance manager does not oppose the amendment but sequences the APS line into outer fiscal years of the 5-year plan, or limits it to a design or planning phase. This keeps EP17 cash flow inside pay-as-you-go limits. Cash is released only when earlier over-programmed items clear.
proposals.trigger: The amendment is approved while EP17 is over-programmed and finance cannot raise cash-flow capacity. The next 5YPP cycle (2027 autumn to 2028) is a natural 'wait' window.
proposals.effect_in_model: Moves the first year in which A_local is non-zero to after the board vote. This adds a lag between 'line restored' and 'money spendable'. It is neither a veto nor a delay of the vote, and it feeds the PW2 trigger that compares 24-month installs against thresholds.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-j covers veto or deferral of the vote (t_defer). The task start logic gives dedicated_line only on/off. No parameter delays money availability after approval.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'the next five years are not expected to see this degree of over-programming ahead of revenue' (EP17-5YPP p.11), and FY28/29+ pay-as-you-go is about $2.0-2.8M/year (inference). 01 s2.2: CIP revenue is about $246M below the last CIP and 'not enough to fund all approved projects'; the CIP rule is to fund urgent needs 'by phase'.
proposals.parameter: t_backload (months from approval before the line's first spendable year); optional sw_design_only (0/1)
proposals.range: t_backload U(0, 36) months; sw_design_only 0/1 equal probability; inference
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 task start (A_local becomes zero until t_backload has elapsed), F-j, PW2 signpost clock

proposals.behaviour: Hold local money while an outside grant is pending (grant-first crowd-out). The finance manager treats the local APS line as match or backstop and will not release it while an HSIP, SS4A or other grant request for the same intersections is pending. Releasing local money first would waste leverage, so it is held for the grant.
proposals.trigger: A SUBMITTED or APPROVED-but-not-yet-CON HSIP instance exists that covers some of the same intersections. The CIP's leverage scoring rewards this, and the budget rule is to use the most flexible money as match.
proposals.effect_in_model: Sets A_local to zero for those intersections until the HSIP instance is rejected, terminated or reaches CON E-76. If HSIP fails, the local money comes late (a two-year wait). This differs from PW1/PW2 sequencing because the wait happens inside the finance actor's allocation, even when PW2 is the chosen pathway.
proposals.already_in_model: No. PW1 chains HSIP then local, and PW2 chains local then HSIP, as scenario scripts. F-a to F-e send failed projects to local funds. No rule withholds already-available local money because an HSIP instance is pending.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'subsidy rule prioritises expansion over maintenance; the most flexible money goes to match' (CIPpol p.11). CIP rows SG142/SG143 are labelled 'HSIP C13/C14 - EST', so the plan already plans HSIP to carry the cost. 01 s2.3: 5YPP scoring gives leverage 4.
proposals.parameter: sw_grant_first (0/1) and q_hold (probability the hold is applied, per pending instance)
proposals.range: sw_grant_first 0/1 equal probability; q_hold U(0, 1); inference
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 and PW2 local branch: A_local gated on the HSIP instance state; F-k

proposals.behaviour: Reclassify APS work as capital or as part of a hardware job to avoid asking for a dedicated line. The finance manager folds the APS add-on into a controller or signal-hardware replacement work order, or into a capitalised maintenance definition. Cost is charged to a line that already exists, so there is no new competing item for EP17.
proposals.trigger: Pressure to cut operating gaps: the CIP draft proposes to widen the definition of capital investment to cover maintenance extending life by 5 or more years. The 2025-02 budget option moved shop staff to capital and 'restructured work orders to count as capital'.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a route for APS cost with no application: the cost is paid by capital lines, but each reclassified job uses Signal Shop capacity and counts against K_crew. This pairs with strain and is separate from PW5's design standard. Side effect: APS may be installed only where hardware is being replaced, which skews coverage away from the worst intersections.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW5 funds APS from the maintenance budget when hardware is replaced (lambda_hw, b_hw), but it is a design-standard rule triggered by buttons failing. It does not model finance choosing to reclassify costs, nor the matching effect on crew capacity.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2: 'FY27-31 CIP intends to widen the definition of capital investment to cover maintenance that extends life by 5+ years' (CIPpol p.10); 'restructure work orders so they count as capital projects' (sfmta-media-41700 p.17, not naming Signal Shop). No document says finance has done this for APS: 'no document support' for the APS-specific use.
proposals.parameter: p_reclass (probability a hardware job gets an APS add-on via capital reclassification) and eta_crew (extra crew-time share used)
proposals.range: p_reclass U(0, 0.5); eta_crew U(0, 0.3); inference
proposals.rule_modified: PW5 event generation and D3.4 internal delivery (K_crew account); b_hw can be read from the CIP rather than set

proposals.behaviour: Matching-funds hoarding / pre-commitment of local money to grant-leveraged projects. The finance manager keeps the flexible local money (10% director discretion, SG000, general-fund baseline) earmarked as the 10% HSIP/SS4A match for federally funded bundles, and treats a dedicated local APS line as competing with that match pool. A request for a local APS line is answered with 'the flexible money is already committed as match', so the local line is crowded out even when the director's 10% is nominally available.
proposals.trigger: A local-only APS line or amendment is proposed while HSIP/SS4A match obligations are open (C13/C14 awards, SS4A signal projects). Strongest when operating deficit pressure makes flexible money scarce.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes the supply of local money to APS depend on how much match is already committed. This lowers the real value of q_dir (director 10% / SG000) and A_local in PW1/PW2 end-stages, and makes F-k correlate with HSIP wins. Winning HSIP would then reduce the local money that is left over.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k has q_dir and F-j has a local-line veto, but both are independent draws. The 10% HSIP local match appears at D3.3 but is not linked to the pool that F-k draws from. No rule in 02 ties the match pool to F-k.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2: 'the most flexible money is used as match' (CIPpol p.11); limit-free money contributes $0 to the CIP (CIP25 p.5); the Tenderloin SS4A match was $1.4M Prop L (01 §2.x, l.240); the director's 10% is about $65M (RES l.22). No document shows a rejected APS request on these grounds.
proposals.parameter: match_crowd_out (continuous). Each year, A_dir_eff = max(0, A_dir − match_committed(t)), where match_committed = 0.10 × (sum of approved HSIP/SS4A project cost) × share of match taken from flexible money, with that share U(0.3, 1.0).
proposals.range: U(0.3, 1.0) for the flexible-money share. 0 turns the behaviour off.
proposals.rule_modified: F-k and q_dir: the probability of an available temporary buffer. Also the local-funds term in D3.3's 10% local match.

proposals.behaviour: Controller-first triage as a standing, non-random priority rule. When EP17 is over-programmed and outages recur, the finance manager (and SFMTA as the sole applicant) sends the money to controller replacement after each outage, and relabels APS new-install as 'replace in kind' or defers it to the next 5-year plan. Visible failures push out invisible deferred needs. The priority is ratcheted by each outage event.
proposals.trigger: A power-outage or controller-failure event (2022 and 2025 precedents), or a re-programming request inside EP17 that ranks lines.
proposals.effect_in_model: Gives a trigger and a ratchet that only the fault event can turn on. After an outage the diverted amount to controllers rises, SG017's APS-usable share goes to 0 for N months, and the chance a dedicated line survives the board amendment falls. This links the exogenous outage to PW2/PW6 failure.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 has q_sg017_block ('money used by controller failures'). It is a static probability per grant, not an event-driven shock, and 02 has no outage event in O3 that drives it. DROP-risk: the static version exists, so only the event-driven version is proposed.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: 'visible-failure driven: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (OCT25 p.7, tagged inference); §2.1 l.126: EP17 $1M went to about 98 controllers although the 2023 PIF listed APS replacement as eligible.
proposals.parameter: sw_outage_shock plus λ_outage (/yr, U(0.1, 0.6)) and a_divert (share of the SG017/EP17 line diverted for t_div months, U(0.5, 1.0) for U(6, 18) months).
proposals.range: λ_outage U(0.1, 0.6)/yr; a_divert U(0.5, 1.0); t_div U(6, 18) months.
proposals.rule_modified: q_sg017_block in PW6, and q_veto/q_dir. Replaces the static q_sg017_block with an event-triggered value.

proposals.behaviour: Timing / window-waiting by the finance manager. Rather than say no, he or she holds the APS amendment 'for the next 5YPP cycle' or 'until the controller backlog is clear' and quietly pushes it to the 2027-fall to 2028 window. Related tactic: the SFMTA budget cycle (FY27-31 CIP) fixes its asks before the amendment is voted, so the amendment arrives without a matching CIP line and gets read as unfunded.
proposals.trigger: An amendment is on the SFCTA agenda while the SFMTA CIP/budget for the next year is not yet set. Also an over-programmed EP17 and the 'later 5YPP' option being available.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a defer-by-SFMTA (not SFCTA-board) branch before F-j. The amendment can be withdrawn or re-timed by the applicant, with delay t_wait aligned to the next 5YPP window, so it counts as time lost but not as a veto. It also lengthens recovery_time without raising q_veto.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j has t_defer after a SFCTA-board veto or delay, and PW2 switches paths after θ_defer. The applicant's own choice to delay (before a board vote) is not modelled: the actor of the delay is always the SFCTA board.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2: the CIP rule 'fund urgent needs by stage (raise project/grant readiness)' (CIPpol p.6); §2.3: the next 5YPP window is 2027 fall to 2028; D4 precedent of 3-4 months. The applicant-side delay has no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_self_defer (probability that SFMTA asks to hold the amendment) and t_self_defer, aligned to the next 5YPP start.
proposals.range: p_self_defer U(0, 0.5); t_self_defer = months to the next window, U(6, 24).
proposals.rule_modified: F-j: add a pre-vote branch before q_veto; PW2 trigger θ_defer then counts total delay, not only board delay.

proposals.behaviour: Reframing the APS request as 'staff-time money' rather than capital. Under deficit pressure the finance manager prefers funding that pays Signal Shop labor (grant-reimbursed labor, reclassifying work orders as capital) because it relieves the operating budget. APS projects that bring in reimbursed labor are favoured; those that only add unfunded crew load are dropped.
proposals.trigger: Operating deficit rounds ($307M FY27) with a balancing menu that includes moving work into capital, and an APS project that either offsets crew cost (grant-funded) or adds unfunded work (local-only).
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes the finance manager's support depend on the labor-offset share of a project, so a HSIP-funded or SS4A-funded APS item is endorsed and a local-only line is deprioritised. This shifts p_start and q_dir by funding source.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 has strain(t) and m_B on crew capacity but no operating-budget incentive that rewards or penalises sources by labor offset. The incentive appears in 01 but is not in a 02 rule.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1 l.113: 'grants that pay Signal Shop labor relieve the operating deficit, so SFMTA has a motive to apply for APS grants' (staffing sfmta-media-41700 p.9, p.17; CIPpol p.10, tagged inference); §2.2: 2025-02 budget options 'reorganise work orders so they count as capital' (not naming the Signal Shop).
proposals.parameter: w_offset: a multiplier on p_start (and on q_dir) = 1 + w_offset × (labor_offset_share − 0.5) for a project, where labor_offset_share is the fraction of project cost that pays Signal Shop labor and is reimbursed.
proposals.range: w_offset U(0, 1.5); 0 turns it off.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start logit (add a source-dependent term) and q_dir in F-k.

proposals.behaviour: Pre-emptive controller carve-out (earmark-then-reserve): when drafting the SG017 request the finance manager pre-commits most of the FY27/FY28 $500k to a named controller/cabinet replacement list (the visible-failure item), leaving APS only a residual. The model only has a stochastic outcome after the fact (`q_sg017_block`: grant 'limited to replace' or 'consumed by failure-priority projects'); it has no decision by the requester at drafting time to size the APS line.
proposals.trigger: Prior allocations all went to controllers (FY24 cabinets/detectors/RRFB, FY25-26 about 98 controllers); controller failures are visible and tied to blackouts; the 'SGR first, fund urgent needs by phase' CIP rule; no APS line in EP17 5YPP.
proposals.effect_in_model: In PW6, `a_sg017` (money available for APS inside SG017) becomes the residual after a drafting-stage controller share, not a free draw. Higher share lowers APS-eligible dollars and the number of C intersections in the batch, and raises the chance PW6 yields zero, which pushes the pathway on to the Prop L amendment / HSIP fallback sooner.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: F-k, `q_sg017_block` and `a_sg017` (02 section D3.6 PW6 row, D10) capture the outcome that SG017 money goes to controllers. But they treat it as an exogenous probability at SFCTA allocation time. The requester's own pre-emptive choice when writing the request is not modelled. Keep as a narrow extension: it changes who owns the cause, not the outcome class.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.x SFMTA capital budget rows: SG017 FY25-26 $1,000,000 for about 98 firewall-vulnerable controllers (OCT25 p.7); 'results are driven by visible failures' (inference, 01 line 176); CIPpol p.6 'fund urgent needs by phase'. No document shows the finance manager deciding the split; this is inference.
proposals.parameter: `s_ctrl_pre` (controller pre-commit share of SG017 request)
proposals.range: U(0.5, 1.0) of each year's $500k; a_sg017 = (1 - s_ctrl_pre) * 500k, capped at 250k
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 funding amount `a_sg017` and the `q_sg017_block` draw (D3.6 PW6, D10)

proposals.behaviour: Request-language laundering: keep the allocation request text as 'replace' (hardware, SGR framing) and fold new APS into the scope only as a 'where conduit and poles are adequate' option that Signal Shop may use at its discretion, rather than naming APS intersections. This keeps the request approvable at SFCTA while leaving the APS decision to later internal work orders (an informal side deal with Signal Shop).
proposals.trigger: The 5YPP description says only 'replace' while the CIP scope also allows new APS; the manager wants to avoid a scope fight at SFCTA and keep flexibility if controllers fail again.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the chance that the grant is rejected for scope (`q_sg017_block` scope arm) but turns the APS spend into a discretionary, unlisted one: money flows to APS only after a second decision by the delivery side, with a lag and a crew-availability filter. Names no intersections, so no accountability for advocates.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 treats the SG017 request as either including new APS or not (PW6) and then delivery runs through K_crew (D3.4). There is no 'unnamed, discretionary APS option' state or second decision gate.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 446: CIP scope text says 'install new ... APS where it is determined that the existing conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition'; 5YPP says only 'replace' (ledger section 2.3). 'Is determined' implies a later judgment. No document shows what actually happens after allocation; no document support for the side-deal part.
proposals.parameter: `sw_vague_scope` (0/1) with `p_apsrelease` (probability per year that unnamed APS option is actually released into the work queue)
proposals.range: switch 0/1; p_apsrelease U(0.1, 0.6) per year when switch = 1; also reduces scope-rejection prob by factor U(0.3, 0.8)
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 submission/approval step and entry into the internal construction queue (D3.1 SUBMITTED to APPROVED; D3.4 delivery)

proposals.behaviour: Window-waiting with pre-positioned local match: instead of pushing APS into SG017 now, the manager holds the APS ask until the next 5YPP window (2027 autumn to 2028) or until an HSIP award exists, and uses the 10% director discretion / SG000 reserve only as the 10% local match for a federally funded batch (the 'most flexible money goes to match' rule), never as stand-alone APS money. If no HSIP award lands, the discretion money is spent on higher-visibility needs.
proposals.trigger: CIPpol p.11 states the most flexible money is used for match; operating deficit $307M and 'one-time' reallocations; Board wants diversion spread out; C13 award decision (2027-03/04) is a known future date.
proposals.effect_in_model: Introduces conditional, time-contingent release of the discretion money: `q_dir` becomes a function of whether a HSIP C13/C14 award exists, and applies only up to the 10% match of that award. Without award, q_dir collapses toward 0 in the tight budget years. Changes PW1 tail and F-k from a flat probability to a contingent one, producing correlation between HSIP failure and loss of the local fallback (a correlated double failure the current independent draws miss).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: F-k has flat `q_dir` U(0,0.8) as last resort after HSIP fails (PW1 end). PW1 includes 10% local match. The missing part is that the same reserve is committed as match first and so is not available as fallback; the model draws them independently.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 149 'most flexible money goes to match' (CIPpol p.11); line 156 director 10% about $65M (RES l.22, l.82); line 157 Board wants reallocation 'one-time' and spread. Contingent-release logic is inference.
proposals.parameter: `q_dir_match_first` (share of discretion money pre-committed to HSIP match when an HSIP bid is live)
proposals.range: U(0.3, 1.0); effective q_dir_fallback = q_dir * (1 - q_dir_match_first) if any HSIP application is SUBMITTED or APPROVED, else q_dir
proposals.rule_modified: F-k and the PW1 'last resort' step; correlation between F-b/F-a failures and F-k (D3.6 PW1, D10)

proposals.behaviour: Quarter-share sandbagging: the manager gives APS a token 'seed' amount (a few intersections) in SG017 each year to be able to report progress and deflect advocacy pressure, but sizes it below the level that would create a standing line or set a precedent for annual APS funding.
proposals.trigger: Advocacy pressure and ADA litigation threat are rising; CIP has no 'accessibility' priority category; a token item is cheaper than a new 5YPP line.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a funded-but-small outcome class: pressure event leads to a small batch (1-3 sites) rather than DEFLECTED or full batch, with the side effect of resetting `λ_press` effect for a period (pressure relief) while also not changing the backlog trend. Produces long tails where installed_5y rises slightly but coverage_10y does not.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: batch size is set by margin `A_local` and `p_deflect` returns to IDLE with no effect (D3.1). There is no token-batch arm that also relieves pressure.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 155 no accessibility category in CIP25 priorities; 01 line 140 SG143 only $570k general fund in FY31 as the only local row (estimate row). Pressure-relief effect is no document support.
proposals.parameter: `n_token` and `r_press_relief`
proposals.range: n_token in {0,1,2,3} per year; r_press_relief U(0, 0.5) multiplicative cut on `λ_press` for `t_relief` U(6,18) months after a token batch
proposals.rule_modified: Local batch sizing at A_local and the pressure(t) term in p_start (D3.1, D3.2)

proposals.behaviour: Readiness-tranche funding. The finance manager does not fund APS construction from SG017. They release a small staged amount (pole and conduit survey, design, PIF paperwork) for the C-class backlog, citing the draft CIP rule to fund urgent needs in phases that raise project and grant readiness. The money buys eligibility and speed, not installs.
proposals.trigger: The SG017 request has to choose between a controller line and a new APS line while capital revenue is about $246M lower and 'not enough to fund all approved projects'. A readiness-only slice is the cheapest way to say yes without displacing controllers.
proposals.effect_in_model: No installs are produced and a_sg017 is not spent on hardware. For the C-class intersections that are surveyed, the survey removes uncertainty about whether poles and conduit are adequate. It shortens D_prep and t_des for the next HSIP window (C14) and for the SG017 construction call in the following year. It also raises the share of intersections that pass the 'existing conduit and pole satisfactory' test.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in the 02 rules. PW6 (D3.6) treats SG017 as all-or-nothing (new APS inside the grant, or blocked by q_sg017_block). a_sg017 (D10) is a hardware dollar amount. D3.1 has no readiness input that shrinks D_prep.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 decision-rule row (CIPpol p.6): 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project/grant readiness)'. 01 §3.2 line 446 says the SG017 scope applies only 'where it is determined that the existing conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition', but no document says who makes that determination or when.
proposals.parameter: g_ready, the share of the a_sg017 allocation redirected to readiness work
proposals.range: U(0, 0.4). Readiness effect: D_prep and t_des multiplied by (1 − 0.5·g_ready/0.4), and the share of C-class stock confirmed 'poles OK' raised by up to 0.2.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 (D_prep for the next PREPARING) and the PW6 eligibility pool; it also splits a_sg017 in D10.

proposals.behaviour: Conditional hold on SG017 pending the HSIP outcome. The finance manager holds back the APS slice of SG017, or leaves it unprogrammed, until the C13 award result (2027-03/04). They do not want to commit scarce local flexible money that HSIP might replace. If HSIP awards SG142, the local money is kept as the 10% match and the SG017 APS slice goes back to controllers. If HSIP fails, the slice is released late.
proposals.trigger: The C13 submission is in and the result is not yet known. The SG017 allocation request falls in the FY27 window before the award. CIPpol p.11 says the 'most flexible money goes to match'.
proposals.effect_in_model: A time lag t_hold is added to PW6 and a conditional release. APS installs from SG017 start late in the HSIP-fails branch. In the HSIP-succeeds branch the money is moved to match and the controller line. This creates a negative correlation between the local and federal channels that the model currently treats as sequential fallbacks.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW1 and PW6 are separate paths, and the sequential fallback chain (D3.6) runs HSIP → Prop L → general fund. No rule makes the local release wait on the C13 result, and q_sg017_block (D3.6, D10) is drawn independently of the HSIP state.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 constraint row (CIPpol p.11): 'subsidy rules prioritise expansion over maintenance; the most flexible money has to go to match'. 01 line 420 notes that SG142 was scheduled to start 2027-07 while the C13 award comes 2027-03/04. No document describes an explicit hold, so the hold itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_hold (0 or 1) and t_hold. With sw_hold = 1, the SG017 APS slice is released only after the C13 result, plus t_hold months.
proposals.range: sw_hold ∈ {0, 1}; t_hold U(0, 9) months. If HSIP awards, the slice goes to match and controllers with probability 1 − q_rel.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 trigger, F-k and q_sg017_block (D10); it links D3.3 route A to PW6.

proposals.behaviour: Labor capitalisation to stretch scarce capital. The finance manager reclassifies part of the Signal Shop installation labor or the work order as a capital charge, so that the labor cost of APS installs is charged to capital or to a grant. This moves cost off the operating side, which is in deficit.
proposals.trigger: The operating deficit is $307M in FY27 and the balancing list includes shifting capital to operating. The FY27-31 CIP proposes to 'expand the definition of capital investment' to cover maintenance that extends life 5+ years. The 2025 options included 'restructure work orders to count as capital' and moving 25% of the paint-and-sign shop staff to capital.
proposals.effect_in_model: This changes who pays for the internal installs. At the system level the dollars per APS install paid out of SG017 or a grant fall, because the labor part is booked elsewhere. The effective cost per intersection (u0) falls for C-class intersections, and the audit risk, which the model does not carry, rises with it. It also trades against K_crew, since the same crew then has a capital charge target.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in the 02 rules. D10 has u0 as a fixed unit cost, and PW5 (b_hw) funds APS add-ons from a maintenance budget but does not shift labor between operating and capital accounts.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 decision-rule rows: the 2025-02 budget options (T/staffing/sfmta-media-41700.txt p.9, p.17) and the CIPpol p.10 definition. The same file does not name the Signal Shop.
proposals.parameter: f_cap, the fraction of internal-install labor cost moved off the SG017 line to capital or a grant
proposals.range: U(0, 0.5). u0_eff = u0·(1 − f_cap·labor_share), with labor_share U(0.4, 0.7). Switch sw_cap ∈ {0, 1}.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 internal row (cost of Fi → I) and D3.2 M-C costpress (a_sg017 buys more installs); M-B strain is unchanged.

proposals.behaviour: Discretion depleted by operating transfers. The finance manager uses the director's 10% on a deficit-linked basis: the discretion goes first to operating gaps and to visible failures, so it is already used when an APS request arrives. The board has asked that transfers be one-time and spread out so no project loses funding.
proposals.trigger: A deficit year (FY27 $307M, FY28 $344M) and a prior visible failure (for example a power outage that puts many controllers at risk).
proposals.effect_in_model: q_dir becomes state-dependent. It is drawn per year as a function of the operating deficit and of a failure event in the same year, instead of a single U(0, 0.8). In high-deficit years, discretion for APS is close to zero. The 'one-time' board rule means the cumulative draw is capped, so using it for APS early removes it for later years.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k (D3.5) has q_dir as the chance that discretion or SG000 is unavailable for APS, drawn as a static parameter U(0, 0.8). There is no link to the deficit path, to failure events, or to the cumulative 10% cap.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2: 'Director may adjust the capital budget up to 10% cumulatively without the board' (RES l.22, l.82); board view that transfers should be 'one-time' and cut from $40M to $20M (CIPpol p.18, p.21); the deficit rows (BB27 p.2). The failure link is 'inferred' in 01 §2.2 (OCT25 p.7).
proposals.parameter: q_dir_t = clip(q_dir0 + a·deficit_t + b·failure_t, 0, 1), plus a cap cum_10 on how many times the 10% can be used for APS
proposals.range: q_dir0 U(0, 0.8) as now; a U(0, 0.4); b U(0, 0.4); cum_10 ∈ {0, 1, 2} uses over the horizon.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-k and the PW1 end node (D3.6); q_dir in D10.

proposals.behaviour: Fault-shock reprioritisation: when a visible signal failure (blackout, controller firewall vulnerability, cabinet outage) occurs, the finance manager pulls the unspent SG017 tranche back to controllers and cabinets, so the APS share is cancelled or deferred mid-year. The block is event-driven, not a one-off draw.
proposals.trigger: A citywide signal failure event or a new cyber/firewall finding, in the year the APS add-on is scheduled.
proposals.effect_in_model: q_sg017_block stops being a fixed per-cycle draw. It becomes a function of a fault-shock process, so blocks cluster in time and an APS line pushed out one year is more exposed the next. PW6 then shows longer recovery_time tails and a higher chance of falling through to the Prop L amendment.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.6 PW6 and D10 have q_sg017_block (U(0.2,0.9)) as a static probability, and it names 'money used by failure-priority projects'. No fault-event process links to it and there is no carry-over. F-a to F-m contain no controller-failure event.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 176: 'outcomes are visible-failure driven: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 blackouts' [inferred]. 01 line 126: the $1M for about 98 controllers with firewall defects. 01 line 447: past allocations all went to controllers.
proposals.parameter: lambda_fault (annual rate of failure shocks) and kappa_block (the jump in q_sg017_block after a shock, decaying over t_fault months)
proposals.range: lambda_fault U(0.2, 1.0) per year; kappa_block U(0.1, 0.5) added to q_sg017_block, capped at 0.95; t_fault U(6, 24) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 signpost and D10 q_sg017_block: replace the fixed draw with q_block(t) = min(0.95, q_base + kappa_block * shock(t))

proposals.behaviour: Contingent match reservation: the director's 10% discretion and flexible local money are not given to APS outright. They are promised only as the 10% local match, conditional on an HSIP award. The manager holds the money as a contingent reserve and releases it only after the award, which leverages the federal money and spends no local cash if the bid loses.
proposals.trigger: An HSIP cycle (C13 deadline 2026-11-02, award 2027-03/04) with an APS-inclusive package, together with a CIP rule that protects SGR and fulfils contracts first.
proposals.effect_in_model: F-k's q_dir becomes conditional. The 10% discretion is available to APS only for the local-match and ineligible-work share of an already approved HSIP package, and not as stand-alone funding. This raises the chance that a package is accepted and funded after approval, and lowers the chance of stand-alone local APS batches.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-k has a single q_dir (U(0,0.8)) for 'director 10% / SG000 not used for APS'. D3.3 and D10 set the HSIP local match at 10% as a parameter, but with no source for that money and no link to the director's discretion. The conditional, award-triggered use is not written.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.2 line 68: 'the most flexible money goes to match' [fact]; stage-based 'raise application readiness' [fact]. 01 line 156: the director may adjust up to 10% without the Board. 01 line 604: HSIP local match 10%, ineligible work paid by the local side.
proposals.parameter: sw_dir_match (switch) with q_dir_match, the probability that the director's money covers the match given an HSIP award
proposals.range: sw_dir_match in {0,1}; q_dir_match U(0.3, 0.95) when 1; q_dir for stand-alone APS set to 0 when 1
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-k and D3.3 HSIP local match: when sw_dir_match = 1, q_dir applies only at the HSIP award event, covering the 10% match and ineligible costs; otherwise local match funding is assumed available

proposals.behaviour: Token cap and sequencing: the manager keeps APS inside SG017 only as a small capped share, or places it in the second year (FY28) after controllers are served in FY27. The aim is to show compliance with the CIP scope without displacing the SGR backlog, and it serves a few sites rather than the whole list.
proposals.trigger: SGR funding is described as 'extremely limited', and the Board's guidance is to spread diversions out and 'not leave any project without funding'.
proposals.effect_in_model: The APS dollars in PW6 become a share of the allocation with a year phase, not an all-or-nothing outcome. The number of intersections per batch is capped, and the effect on installed_5y and coverage_10y is a small number of sites rather than a path switch.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D10 a_sg017 is U(0,250k) per year, capped at half of SG017, and PW6 covers the basic case of writing APS into the request. Not captured: the choice of year (all APS money in the second year) or a commitment ratchet by which a token amount in FY27 changes the FY28 baseline. A time phase is absent.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 447: FY27 and FY28 use is unknown and SG017 has $500k each year. 01 lines 150-176 (§2.2): SGR priority and 'raise readiness by stage'. 01 line 204 notes the Board wants spreading. No document directly supports year-phasing.
proposals.parameter: phi_aps_year (first year in which APS gets SG017 money) and rho_ratchet (the share of the previous year's APS amount that carries into the next year's base)
proposals.range: phi_aps_year in {FY27, FY28, none}, with probabilities 0.3/0.4/0.3; rho_ratchet U(0, 1)
proposals.rule_modified: D10 a_sg017 and D3.6 PW6: a_sg017(t) = 0 before phi_aps_year, and a_sg017(t+1) = max(base, rho_ratchet * a_sg017(t)) afterwards

proposals.behaviour: Local-match gatekeeping: before the HSIP deadline, SFCTA programming staff decide whether to pre-commit Prop L as the 10% local match (or a leverage letter) for the C13 package, or to withhold it until the award is known. A package with no named match source is held back, submitted late, or submitted with a thinner scope.
proposals.trigger: Deadline is next week. The SG015 + APS package needs a match source. Staff scoring gives 'leverage' weight 4. Staff do not want to program money against an unawarded federal grant.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a pre-submission gate between 'BCR >= 5.0' and SUBMIT in D3.3 / D3.1. With probability 1 - q_match_ok, the instance is not submitted this cycle (it becomes MISSED) or is delayed by t_match months, so the model's F-a to F-c do not cover it. PW1 success then depends on an SFCTA decision, not only on A2 effort.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.3 says 'local match 10%', but the model never names who pays it or whether SFCTA must agree. F-e and F-f use q_topup for overruns, which is a different event. DROP-check: no rule makes the match a precondition of submission.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 and §2.? SS4A example: 'Tenderloin match: federal $5.6M + Prop L $1.4M' (01 l.240) shows Prop Land match is a real practice. 01 l.185: 'grants are made based on a complete application package' (SP p.22). No document support for staff withholding a match commitment before an award.
proposals.parameter: q_match_ok
proposals.range: U(0.5, 1.0); companion t_match U(0, 6) months delay when the gate fails. Switch sw_match_gate in {0,1}, default 0 for backward compatibility.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 SUBMIT transition (add a gate before submission) and D3.3 'two thresholds' (add a third, non-BCR condition).

proposals.behaviour: Sequencing hold: SFCTA staff decline to put a Prop L amendment (the dedicated APS line, PW2) on the board agenda until the HSIP C13 result is known (about 2027-03/04), and advise waiting for the 2027-28 Strategic Plan / 5YPP cycle instead of a mid-cycle amendment.
proposals.trigger: A pending HSIP application for the same scope exists (SG142/SG143 are both labelled HSIP EST). EP17 FY24-28 is already over-programmed (about 202% ahead of pay-go). Staff prefer to see whether federal money lands first.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes PW2 and the F-j delay. The local line opens only after C13 resolves, so t_defer is lengthened to max(t_defer, time until C13 result) when sw_wait_hsip = 1. This makes 'local-first' collapse into 'HSIP-first' when HSIP is live, and also changes the order of PW1 to PW2 fallback timing.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j models a board veto or delay (q_veto, t_defer), and PW2 triggers on a board no or delay. DROP-check: both act at the board. The model has no staff-level agenda control that is conditional on another funding source's pending outcome.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 l.185: 'SFCTA staff evaluate -> CAC -> board' (SP p.22). 01 l.179 'EP17-5YPP: committed $27.49M vs pay-go $8.52M, about 202% ahead' and l.180 'next five years not expected to be so far ahead'. 01 l.177: D4 precedent was 3-4 months with a councillor driving it, so staff speed is not fixed. No document support for a staff 'wait for HSIP' stance.
proposals.parameter: sw_wait_hsip
proposals.range: Bernoulli(p_wait) with p_wait U(0, 0.7). Adds a delay term t_wait = months until the C13 decision when the switch is on and an APS-bearing HSIP instance is pending.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.2 F-j and D3.6 PW2 trigger; the event that opens the local-specialty window.

proposals.behaviour: Reframe through an existing visibility line: staff accept an APS add-on inside the 5YPP 'signal visibility' allocation (about $0.4M/yr in the Prop L EP17 plan) as part of the SG015 scope. They treat it as a scope clarification, not a new programming line, by describing APS as part of making signals visible to all users.
proposals.trigger: The SG015 visibility upgrade is planned for the same cycle. A request needs a funding line that already exists, and no 5YPP amendment is wanted.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a second no-amendment local source parallel to PW6 (SG017). It supplies a_vis dollars per year that can carry new APS at C-type intersections that are SG015 corridor candidates. That reduces the dependence of PW1 on the HSIP BCR outcome.
proposals.already_in_model: No for the visibility line. PW6 and q_sg017_block cover only SG017 (hardware replacement) and its 'replace vs install' wording. The EP17 visibility line (01 l.179) is not a model source. DROP-check passed, since SG015 appears in the model only as a federal HSIP carrier.
proposals.evidence: 01 l.179: 'FY26-28 about $2.80M a year, all to TSP, conduit, signs, hardware replacement ($0.5M/yr), visibility ($0.4M/yr)'. 01 l.442 shows SG015 is also a C13 HSIP line. Whether the Prop L visibility money can carry APS is not documented, so it is an inference.
proposals.parameter: a_vis and q_vis_block
proposals.range: a_vis U($0, $200k)/yr (up to half of the visibility row); q_vis_block U(0.3, 0.9) probability that staff or the board limit it to visibility only. Switch PW6b (copy of PW6 with these two values).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 pattern (add PW6b); D10 next to q_sg017_block and a_sg017.

proposals.behaviour: Bridge or advance: if the HSIP award is expected but the Signal Shop work in SG142 is scheduled for 2027-07 (before the CON E-76 at 15-28 months), staff offer a Prop L cash-flow advance to keep the crew working, to be repaid from the later federal reimbursement.
proposals.trigger: A timing mismatch between the planned start (2027-07) and the real federal time (award 2027-03/04, then PIF and E-76). Idle crew or underspent lines are visible to the board.
proposals.effect_in_model: Shortens the HSIP delivery chain in D3.4 by letting the internal crew start before CON E-76 with local money. This changes t_con for PW1 (effectively max(...) replaced by an early start) and creates a repayment obligation that can fail (project terminated, then local funds stay spent).
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.4 makes CON E-76 a hard precondition for internal construction, and nothing lets local money substitute while waiting. F-g (partner delay) and F-d (milestone delay) only add delay.
proposals.evidence: 01 l.421: SG142 planned start 2027-07 versus C13 approval 2027-03/04; actual award-to-construction authorisation 15-28 months; PIF time has no public data. No document support for SFCTA advancing money against a federal award in this setting.
proposals.parameter: q_bridge
proposals.range: U(0, 0.5) probability of an advance per approved HSIP APS instance; amount cap a_bridge U($0, $500k); repayment-failure probability q_bridge_loss U(0, 0.3).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 HSIP row (CON E-76 precondition for internal install) and F-g partner delay recovery path.

proposals.behaviour: Staff pre-screen / soft gate before the board: with no named SFMTA owner, a programming analyst treats any informal APS inquiry or thin amendment as 'not ready' and tells the contact to come back with a fuller package (cost basis, delivery plan, Signal Shop capacity). The request is never formally filed, so it never reaches the board vote.
proposals.trigger: Vacant owner post plus hiring freeze: the incoming contact is a junior or acting person, the package looks incomplete, and staff cannot get a quick answer on scope or readiness. The rubric gives readiness the highest weight (5).
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the chance that a started A2 task becomes a SUBMITTED instance at the amendment/allocation step. It acts as an extra reduction in p_start, or a stage between PREPARING and SUBMIT where the instance is returned and the task restarts after a delay. This is not the board veto in F-j.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j (02 D3.5) covers a board veto or deferral of an amendment, and D3.1 covers MISSED. Neither models staff-level returns before submission. Kept because the filter sits upstream of F-j.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: allocations are 'based on a qualified applicant's prepared and submitted package; SFCTA staff review -> CAC -> board' (SP p.22); 5YPP scoring puts readiness at 5 of 31 (EP17-5YPP p.12-13). No document support for staff actually returning thin packages in this situation; it is an inference.
proposals.parameter: q_staff_return (per-submission probability of staff return), plus an optional multiplier on it while the owner post is vacant (owner = 0)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.4); multiplier 1.0-2.0 when owner = 0
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 SUBMITTED -> eligibility review step, adding a return-to-IDLE branch with delay r_return U(1, 4) months, before F-j.

proposals.behaviour: Staff default to the cycle: instead of recommending a mid-cycle 5YPP amendment, staff steer APS into the 2027 fall to 2028 5YPP development round, saying the programmed EP17 funds are over-committed and amendments should wait for the cycle.
proposals.trigger: The programmed amount runs about 202% ahead of pay-as-you-go. Without a champion there is no board or sponsor push to justify an exception. Staff also have limited capacity in an agency under a freeze, so a bulk cycle is cheaper than a one-off amendment.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a staff-originated deferral that sets t_defer to the next 5YPP window. The amendment pathway (PW2) is effectively closed until about 2028, and PW6/HSIP take its load.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j allows 'wait for the next 5YPP' only after a board veto. D4's 3-4 month amendment precedent is treated as the base case. A standing staff preference for the cycle over amendments is not modelled. Kept as a state switch on how amendments are processed.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: EP17 5YPP commits $27.49M against $8.52M pay-as-you-go ('about 202% ahead'), and 'the next five years are not expected to be this far ahead' (EP17-5YPP p.11). Precedent for a fast amendment: the D4 Lincoln Way case, 3-4 months (LW p.15-18), which had a sponsoring board member. No document support that staff push the cycle.
proposals.parameter: sw_cycle_only (binary switch) or p_cycle_steer
proposals.range: p_cycle_steer 0-0.8, with the switch forced on if owner = 0 and a vacancy is in force
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j and D3.6 PW2: sets t_defer to months until the next 5YPP window, rather than U(1, 12).

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS as a sub-scope of already-programmed items, so no new line is needed. Staff encourage SFMTA to fold new APS into the SG017 hardware replacement allocation and into EP18 corridor and new-signal allocations. In EP18 SFCTA is itself an eligible applicant, so staff could carry APS in its own corridor work.
proposals.trigger: A cycle-only stance plus a vacancy that leaves no one to write a dedicated APS request. Staff want the least effort and the least visible exposure for the board.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the probability that APS money flows as embedded scope rather than a dedicated request. It also gives an SFCTA-initiated route (SFCTA as applicant) that does not depend on A2's task state machine at all.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 covers SG017 (02 D3.6, with q_sg017_block). Not modelled: staff proposing it, or SFCTA acting as the applicant in EP18. Kept for that narrow gap only.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: EP18 applicants are 'SFMTA, SFPW, SFCTA' (EP p.12); Contract 35 puts Prop L $5.35M into 17 locations that include APS, and C66/C67 new signals mostly include PCS+APS (OCT25 p.3, p.26-27); the SG017 CIP scope text allows new APS (01 around line 446). No document support that SFCTA acts as the applicant for APS in practice.
proposals.parameter: p_sfcta_embed (probability per year that SFCTA or staff steer creates an embedded APS scope in an EP18 or SG017 allocation, independent of A2)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.3) per year; it needs a nonzero pool of C-class locations on EP18 corridors
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 and the D3.1 task trigger: adds a second source of instances that bypasses the A2 task.

proposals.behaviour: Informal 'wait for a champion' signal: staff slow-walk or leave unrecommended an APS request that arrives without a sponsoring board member or CAC voice. In effect the board member's willingness replaces the missing engineer as the owner.
proposals.trigger: The informal owner's absence removes the usual route that brought APS requests to staff with context. Staff then prioritise requests with political backing, such as the D4 Lincoln Way case.
proposals.effect_in_model: Ties approval to a 'sponsor' variable on the SFCTA side. A request without a champion gets a longer review lag or a lower approval chance. A request with one (a board member's NTP-style push) keeps the fast 3-4 month track.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.3 and F-j have q_veto and t_defer as unconditional random draws, and 01 §2.3 notes the board's NTP route. Whether they depend on a sponsor is not modelled. Kept as a conditioning rule.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: D4 board member used NTP $500k for Lincoln Way, with a 3-4 month 5YPP revision (LW p.15-18); NTP5 p.7-8 notes the mayor and council act through board members to move money (01 line 269 area). No document support that staff slow-walk requests with no champion.
proposals.parameter: champion (binary) with q_veto_nochamp and t_defer_nochamp
proposals.range: q_veto_nochamp U(0.1, 0.6) versus q_veto U(0, 0.5); t_defer_nochamp U(3, 18) months
proposals.rule_modified: F-j: makes q_veto and t_defer depend on a champion flag, and adds a champion arrival event.

proposals.behaviour: SFCTA staff act as the sponsor themselves. With the informal APS owner gone and no applicant, staff use the fact that EP18 (Safer and Complete Streets) lists SFCTA as an eligible applicant. They write the APS scope into an SFCTA-led or jointly sponsored corridor or planning item, or into a Prop L amendment SFCTA drafts itself. This goes around the 'only SFMTA applies for EP17' bottleneck.
proposals.trigger: The A2 post is vacant (owner = none) and no SFMTA request has arrived for N months. A visible gap exists (advocate pressure, a Board member's question, an NTP opportunity), and staff have discretion over the scope text of their own items.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a second path to a funded instance that does not need A2's PREPARING state. An SFCTA-originated instance enters the Prop L pipeline directly, bypassing p_start. It still has to pass the 02 D3.5 F-j board step (q_veto) and still faces SFMTA delivery capacity (strain) afterwards. In effect it creates a 'substitute applicant' for the vacant node.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.1 has A2 as the only task owner. 02 D3.1's deflection text says neighbouring nodes do not take over tasks ('推责后的任务不会被相邻节点自动接走（它们没有「接任务」规则）'). PW2 and PW6 are both A2-initiated. SFCTA is only a gatekeeper (F-j, q_sg017_block).
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 says EP18 applicants are 'SFMTA、SFPW、SFCTA' (about line 170). 01 §2.3 line 177 records the D4 Board member's NTP $500k Lincoln Way design with APS, which went through a 5YPP revision in 3-4 months. 01 §2.3 line 185 says grants rest on applications prepared and submitted by 'qualified sponsors'. No document shows SFCTA staff filling a vacant sponsor role, so the substitution itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_sfcta_sponsor
proposals.range: Per-month probability U(0, 0.05) while owner = none and no live instance exists (a 0 setting reproduces the current model). Resulting instance cost is taken from the EP18 / NTP size band (about $0.25-0.5M). Optional lag t_sp U(3, 8) months.
proposals.rule_modified: Adds a new instance source in 02 D3.1 alongside A2's SUBMIT, active only when owner is low. It feeds the same approval step as PW2 / F-j.

proposals.behaviour: Staff apply a stricter completeness and readiness screen to requests from an unfamiliar or newly appointed contact, and send them back for resubmission. The 5YPP scoring puts 5 of 31 points on readiness. A request with no named lead, no committed delivery schedule, or no confirmation that Signal Shop capacity exists is scored down or returned.
proposals.trigger: The request comes from an applicant with vacancy status (the owner post is empty, or a covering staff member has no track record), and staff know the applicant's delivery staffing is frozen.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a pre-board, staff-level rejection or delay step. The delay is extra months in the review stage. The rejection probability rises when applicant capacity is low (strain high or owner low). It lengthens the cycle and can push a request past a window or past a board date. It is a different mechanism from the board veto in F-j.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. The 02 D3.1 SUBMITTED step has an eligibility review, and F-j covers a board veto or deferral. Neither makes staff screening depend on the applicant's capacity or on whether the contact is vacant. The model does not note that readiness is scored.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 lines 185-186: staff review, then CAC, then board; the score weights readiness at 5. 01 §2.3 line 181 and 01 §2.1 (the 2023 'Signal Shop staffing is often the limiting factor') plus 01 §3 P1 (staffing freeze, 2024-07/10) support staff awareness of the capacity limit. No document shows staff actually returning a request on this ground.
proposals.parameter: q_staff_return
proposals.range: Probability U(0, 0.4) that an APS request is returned or scored down when owner = none or strain > threshold. Extra delay d_return U(1, 4) months. Setting it to 0 gives the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 SUBMITTED -> eligibility review, adding a capacity-conditional REJECTED / RETURNED branch before the board. It uses the same strain(t) variable already in 02 D3.2 M-B.

proposals.behaviour: Staff reprogram, sweep, or pre-commit the thin EP17 uncommitted balance (about $0-0.5M a year) to other queued items while no APS request exists. Examples are controller failures, TSP, and hardware replacement. This is a unilateral staff recommendation in the next allocation or amendment package. The slack then no longer exists when an APS request finally arrives.
proposals.trigger: Slack in FY26-28 sits unused for several months, the 5YPP is over-committed, and competing sponsors or projects have deficits. A vacant APS owner means nobody defends the line.
proposals.effect_in_model: The money pool available to PW2 / PW6 depreciates over time. Late arrival of an APS request is penalised, because the fund has already been absorbed, which pushes APS toward a full Prop L amendment (F-j) or toward other funds. It also strengthens the 'not applied -> no money' loop.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.6 PW6 has q_sg017_block, a probability that SG017 money is taken by controller failures. F-k covers a director's 10% allocation or SG000 reserve being unusable. Neither is a time-decaying erosion of the Prop L balance caused by staff recommendations when the line is undefended.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 179 and line 613: EP17 is over-committed about 202%, FY26-28 uncommitted balance about $0-0.5M. 01 §2.2 line 126: the existing $1M hardware line went to about 98 controllers with firewall defects, which shows reallocation to system faults happens. 01 §2.3 line 180: no repeat of this level of over-commitment is expected. No document shows staff sweeping a line whose owner is vacant, so the sweep step has no document support.
proposals.parameter: lambda_sweep
proposals.range: Monthly hazard U(0, 0.04) that a fraction f_sweep U(0.2, 0.6) of the uncommitted EP17 balance is taken by another claim while owner = none. Setting it to 0 gives the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D10 slack variable feeding PW2 and PW6. It generalises the one-shot q_sg017_block into a decay over time that is conditional on owner status.

proposals.behaviour: Staff hold a lone APS amendment and bundle it with the other amendments queued for a later board cycle, or fold it into the 2027 autumn 5YPP / Strategic Plan update instead of processing it as a standalone item. They tell the sponsor 'we will take it with the 5YPP update'. This is a hold by staff, not by the board.
proposals.trigger: Staff face heavy work (a Strategic Plan and 5YPP refresh starting 2027 autumn, a hiring freeze, SFCTA's own thin staffing), the APS request is small ($0.25-0.5M), and no named champion is pushing it.
proposals.effect_in_model: A request that could use the fast 3-4 month precedent route is put on the 2028 route instead. This lengthens the Prop L pathway delay, so more of the PW2 population falls to the general fund or HSIP pathways. The effect is greater when the owner is vacant, because nobody presses.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j has t_defer U(1, 12) months and an option to 'wait for next 5YPP (2027 autumn-2028)', but it is triggered by a board veto with probability q_veto. It is not a staff-side hold, and it does not depend on whether a champion is present.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 177: the 3-4 month D4 precedent only happened with a Board member's push. 01 §2.3 line 192: the next 5YPP window is 2027 autumn-2028. The ODD already takes a 5YPP window as a trigger. No document shows staff holding a request until the cycle, so the hold itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_bundle_wait
proposals.range: Probability U(0, 0.6) that a standalone amendment is held to the next 5YPP window when champion = none (champion = owner OR strong pressure). Delay equals the time to the window, capped at 12-18 months. Setting it to 0 gives the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-j and D3.6 PW2. It adds a staff-side hold before the board step with its own trigger (no champion), separate from q_veto.

proposals.behaviour: SFCTA staff act as surrogate sponsor: when the SFMTA owner post is vacant, programming staff scope APS into an SFCTA-sponsored vehicle (EP18 Safer and Complete Streets lists SFCTA as an eligible applicant), or into a corridor or NTP-type project SFCTA already manages, instead of waiting for an SFMTA request.
proposals.trigger: Owner vacancy plus hiring freeze (F-h / F-i active) AND a board-member or advocate ask reaches SFCTA directly (a D4 Lincoln Way style prompt), AND the vehicle (EP18 or NTP) has uncommitted headroom.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a second action-taker. Opens a new money entry that does not pass through A2's task state machine (D3.1). When the switch is on, an APS batch can enter the Fs (with signal works) or local-batch path with a delay t_sfcta_lead, without any SFMTA submission.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 states SFCTA only allocates on requests from the applicant (D3.6 PW6, F-j, F-k); only A2 acts. PW6 (SG017) and PW2 (5YPP amendment) both start from an SFMTA request. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 (rows 169-170, 177): 'EP18 ... applicants SFMTA, SFPW, SFCTA'; D4 used an NTP $500k to design two APS-bearing signals with a 3-4 month 5YPP revision (LW p.15-18). Counter-line, same section: 'only allocates on requests from the applicant' (SP p.22). So the document supports eligibility and a precedent, but there is no document support that staff do this on their own initiative.
proposals.parameter: p_sfcta_lead (switch sw_sfcta_sponsor in {0,1}, plus probability U(0, 0.3) per year while the vacancy lasts); sized by a_sfcta_lead U($0, $500k) per instance
proposals.range: switch {0,1}; p_sfcta_lead U(0, 0.3)/yr; a_sfcta_lead U($0, $500k)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 task state machine (adds an exogenous instance-creation event), D3.6 adds a PW7 'SFCTA-led' path, D3.2 mechanism matrix

proposals.behaviour: Readiness-based capacity discount: seeing the SFMTA sponsor has no named lead and a frozen headcount, staff mark the request 'low readiness / delivery risk' in the 5YPP scoring and staff recommendation. In response they push for a reduced-scope, tranche or conditional allocation (design only, or a smaller batch), or tell the sponsor to resubmit after staffing is restored.
proposals.trigger: A request or amendment arrives while the vacancy flag (F-h) or the freeze (F-i) is on, and the sponsor's recent delivery record is weak (Fi stock falls, 0 installs in the last 4 periods).
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the approval probability for a local-field request, or shrinks the approved batch size, as a function of vacancy and strain. This hits the pathways PW2/PW6 even when the board is in favour.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j's q_veto and t_defer are board-level, unconditional probabilities. q_sg017_block covers priority use of money. Nothing makes SFCTA staff's recommendation depend on the sponsor's vacancy or delivery state. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: the 5YPP scoring puts 'readiness' at 5 of 31 points (EP17-5YPP p.12-13); 'Signal Shop staffing limits are often the limiting factor on delivery speed' (EP17-5YPP l.354-356, p.9); also the 'one-time over-advance' remark (p.11). There is no document of staff actually discounting a request for vacancy, so that link has no document support.
proposals.parameter: theta_ready_haircut: multiplier on q_veto (or on batch size) when vacancy_flag=1
proposals.range: q_veto_eff = q_veto + theta_ready_haircut*vacancy_flag; theta_ready_haircut U(0, 0.4); batch shrink factor U(0.5, 1.0)
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (amendment veto/defer), D3.2 local-field batch size A_local, D10 q_veto row

proposals.behaviour: Holding for the cycle: staff steer a mid-cycle APS amendment into the 2027 autumn-2028 5YPP rewrite instead of processing it separately. Their reasons: the 5YPP and its headroom are tight (FY26-28 uncommitted $0-0.5M/year), amendments are a workload, and without a sponsor contact nobody is lobbying.
proposals.trigger: A pending amendment or request, plus vacancy, plus the 5YPP window within about 12-18 months (so waiting is cheap and plausible).
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes the amendment's resolution date to the next cycle (a deterministic wait to 2028) instead of a random t_defer of 1-12 months. It removes the amendment from F-j's draw entirely, and shifts the local-field money later.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.6 PW2 already routes 'reject or postpone beyond theta_defer months' to the next 5YPP or the general fund; F-j has t_defer U(1,12). But the deferral is a board veto draw, not a staff-initiated, vacancy-triggered, fixed-date hold. Keep only if framed as a conditional jump to the cycle date. Weak-to-medium.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: 'The next five years are not expected to be over-advanced to this degree' (EP17-5YPP p.11); next 5YPP 2027 autumn-2028 (SP p.8, p.10, p.46); allocation lead time 8-13 weeks (calendar). No document support for staff doing the redirect.
proposals.parameter: p_hold_to_cycle (staff-initiated hold)
proposals.range: p_hold_to_cycle U(0, 0.6) when vacancy_flag=1 and months_to_5YPP <= 18; wait = months_to_cycle
proposals.rule_modified: F-j, D3.6 PW2 (turns the postponement into a fixed date), D10 t_defer

proposals.behaviour: Accommodating informal contact-point drift: with the owner gone, staff keep processing allocation requests but move the 'who answers for APS' role to the SFMTA budget or finance contact, or to a project manager of a larger signal project. APS requests then go through only as add-on scope lines of those people's projects (riders), and no stand-alone APS request is prepared.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy persists beyond a few months and the SFCTA staff member still needs a named sponsor contact for every request on the allocation form.
proposals.effect_in_model: APS gets no stand-alone task. The IDLE task of the owner is replaced by a rider mechanism whose chance to start depends on the parent project's cycle. It raises the Fs/parent path share and lowers stand-alone submissions.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. Fs / absorbed-into-project path and 'owner steps down one tier' (F-h) exist, but there is no inheritance of the task by another role; D3.1 says that a deflected task 'is not taken over by neighbouring nodes (they have no take-over rule)'. This proposal explicitly adds the take-over. Weak evidence; keep as a switch.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 decision rule: allocation is 'based on an application package prepared and submitted by an eligible sponsor; SFCTA staff review -> CAC -> board' (SP p.22). No document shows staff redirecting to another contact, so this part has no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_rider_inherit (switch) and p_rider U(0, 0.4)/year
proposals.range: sw_rider_inherit {0,1}; p_rider U(0, 0.4) per parent-project allocation event
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 (removes the 'no take-over' sentence), F-h, Fs entry rate in D3.4

proposals.behaviour: Fund swap: if HSIP C13 funds the SG015 visibility upgrade, the Prop L EP17 visibility line (about $0.4M/yr) is no longer needed for that scope. Programming staff recommend moving part of that freed Prop L money into an APS install line through an administrative or fast 5YPP amendment.
proposals.trigger: C13 award list is published (2027-03/04) and SG015 is on it. Applies only when SG015 is also funded by Prop L as a local backstop or match. Staff see an uncommitted gap and an already-eligible EP17 purpose.
proposals.effect_in_model: Creates a second route into the Prop L APS line. That line currently opens only from the $0-0.5M/yr uncommitted margin. The new route adds a one-off tranche, which raises the chance and size of PW2 or PW6 funding conditional on HSIP success. It also couples the Prop L path to the HSIP path, so the two are no longer independent in the path comparison.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in 02. F-j covers a board veto or delay of an amendment. F-k covers director reserve use. PW2 starts from the uncommitted margin. PW1 and PW2 are sequential fallbacks, not a swap. Nothing frees programmed Prop L money when SG015 wins in HSIP. Dropping criterion not met, so keep.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 l.179: EP17 5YPP FY26-28 gives visibility $0.4M/yr and has no APS install row. 01 l.239: SG015 is funded by HSIP C13 $1.1M (EST) plus SS4A. 01 l.442: the CIP lists SG015 and SG142 side by side with the same C13 source. No document says staff would swap funds, so the behaviour is inference.
proposals.parameter: q_swap (probability, applied once after C13 results) and swap_frac (share of the freed visibility money moved to APS)
proposals.range: q_swap U(0, 0.4); swap_frac U(0, 0.5); both 0 reproduces the baseline
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2 / F-j (opening the Prop L APS line): adds a conditional funding source to the uncommitted-margin rule, triggered by the SG015 outcome in D3.3

proposals.behaviour: Staff hold the line: before the board sees any APS amendment, SFCTA staff ask SFMTA to wait for the C13 result and give it priority. The amendment is not scheduled until HSIP has said yes or no.
proposals.trigger: The C13 deadline is next week and SG142 is ineligible. HSIP money is federal, and the Prop L EP17 programming is over-advanced by about 200%. An amendment request arrives before the C13 outcome is known.
proposals.effect_in_model: Delays the PW2 start by t_hold (until about C13 results, roughly 5 months out) with probability q_hold. This shifts the clock before the board vote, not the vote itself. It lowers the chance of a Prop L amendment overlapping with HSIP and changes the order of PW1 and PW2 in the path comparison.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j has a board-stage delay (q_veto, t_defer). The staff-stage gate before the board is not written down, and neither is a gate tied to the C13 outcome. The model has no staff pre-screening step. Keep it, narrowed to the pre-board hold.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 l.185: grants rest on an applicant-prepared package, and staff review comes before the CAC and the board. 01 l.179-180: 5YPP over-advanced by about 202%, and the next five years are not expected to repeat that. 01 l.421: C13 awards come about 2027-03/04. No quote shows a staff hold, so it is inference.
proposals.parameter: q_hold (probability) and t_hold (months)
proposals.range: q_hold U(0, 0.7); t_hold U(2, 6) months, capped at the C13 award date
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2 start rule and the F-j timing branch; adds a staff-stage pre-gate before the board vote

proposals.behaviour: Staff steer the applicant before the deadline: they tell SFMTA that a standalone APS ask (SG142) is ineligible in HSIP and suggest bundling APS with the SG015 carrier or with a signal-project scope that already has a CRF.
proposals.trigger: SFCTA staff see the CIP list SG015 and SG142 on separate rows with the same C13 source. They also see the C13 deadline is days away and a standalone APS row will be rejected.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the probability that the A2 task chooses PW1-style bundling in this window instead of missing it. It acts on p_start and on the bundling choice for the first C13 instance. It changes the A2 task state machine, which now takes an outside nudge as an input.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in 02. PW1 is the bundling path, but it is chosen by A2 and the pathway rules, not by an SFCTA staff nudge. D3.1 only has pressure from advocates (pressure(t)). Keep as low-support.
proposals.evidence: No document support for staff steering. Related context: 01 l.442-444 says the files do not show whether SFMTA planned to merge SG142 and SG015, and that the SG015 corridor scope covers only about 1 unfunded C-type intersection. This also limits the effect size of the nudge.
proposals.parameter: p_steer (probability the nudge happens and is accepted before the deadline)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.3); applied once per HSIP window; added to the logistic p_start as an additive term with weight beta_steer
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start formula and the D3.3 PW1 candidate selection (bundling choice)

proposals.behaviour: Zero-sum offset demand. Staff will not bring a stand-alone EP17 amendment that adds an APS line unless the sponsor names which already-programmed line (for example the visibility line, hardware replacement, or a pipeline item) gives up money. EP17 FY24-28 is over-programmed, so any new row is a swap, not an addition.
proposals.trigger: A request or 5YPP amendment that adds a new APS row while EP17 has no uncommitted headroom (headroom is roughly 0 to 0.5M per year). It bites hardest when the same cycle already has the SG015 visibility upgrade planned.
proposals.effect_in_model: The amendment path (F-j, PW2) is gated by a second condition that the board vote never sees. If the offset is not supplied, the amendment is not agendized at all. If it is supplied, it shrinks or delays SG015 or the SG017 hardware line, which cuts the partner scope that PW1 and F-g rely on. This links the Prop L amendment to a loss on another SFMTA line.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-j covers only board veto or deferral (q_veto, t_defer). D3.2 and D10 have no offset rule. PW6 has q_sg017_block, but that is a staff-side priority diversion to failures, not an offset demand on a new row.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3, line 179: EP17 2023 5YPP commits $27.49M against $8.52M pay-as-you-go, 202% ahead, with no APS install row. Line 180: 'the next five years are not expected to be this far ahead'. Line 411: Prop L headroom is $0-0.5M per year. Allocation decisions rest on the applicant's package (line 185).
proposals.parameter: p_offset_required in [0.3, 0.9] (inferred). Plus offset_target in {visibility, hardware, pipeline}, which sets which partner line loses money, and a deferral t_offset U(1, 6) months when no offset is supplied.
proposals.range: p_offset_required in [0.3, 0.9]; t_offset U(1, 6) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (adds a staff gate before the board vote) and D3.6 PW2 (the Prop L amendment start). Also the coupling to F-g (partner scope reduced when offset_target = visibility).

proposals.behaviour: Fold-into-the-update deferral. Staff advises SFMTA to hold the APS request and include it in the next strategic plan and 5YPP cycle (kick-off autumn 2027, adopted 2028) instead of processing a stand-alone amendment now. This works as a polite 'wait for a better window' without any vote.
proposals.trigger: A near-term amendment request arrives while a full 5YPP update is less than about 12 to 18 months away, and there is no visible-failure urgency. It is stronger when the HSIP deadline is imminent and staff can say a missed HSIP cycle is not an emergency, because the C14 window exists.
proposals.effect_in_model: The Prop L route moves from a 3 to 4 month precedent to a wait of up to about 12 months. This has two effects. PW2 reaches its fallback (general fund, then HSIP) later or never. The local-first pathway looks slower than the precedent suggests, so PW1 (HSIP-first) is favoured.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j mentions waiting for the next 5YPP, but only after a board veto or deferral. Staff-initiated deferral before any board action is not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 192: next strategic plan and 5YPP start in autumn 2027, adopted 2028. Line 411: a 5YPP revision can run at any time, with a 3-4 month precedent, or wait for 2028. Line 177: the Lincoln Way precedent was 3-4 months, but it used NTP money and a district supervisor sponsor. Line 185: staff review comes before the CAC and the board.
proposals.parameter: q_fold in [0.2, 0.7] (inferred). Staff probability of redirecting a stand-alone amendment into the next 5YPP. It is reduced when pressure(t) or a visible-failure signal is high.
proposals.range: q_fold U(0.2, 0.7), multiplied by (1 - pressure_visible)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j and D3.6 PW2. It adds a pre-board branch with delay t_fold = months until the next window, replacing t_defer for this branch.

proposals.behaviour: Conditional or contingent programming. Staff will program Prop L as local match, or as gap cover, only on the condition that the HSIP award comes through, with a reversion clause if the federal money is not awarded or the project is not delivered. This avoids committing Prop L to something ineligible on its own (an APS-only line).
proposals.trigger: The HSIP bundle (APS plus SG015 visibility) is submitted. Staff are asked for a match or a top-up commitment, but APS-only is ineligible, so the money may become stranded if the bundle fails BCR.
proposals.effect_in_model: It turns the top-up in F-e and F-f (q_topup) from a request-time lottery into a conditional pre-commitment. This raises q_topup for projects that win an award and keeps the money unspent for those that do not. It can also shorten the pause t_pause. Prop L is a second-stage gate rather than a first-stage one.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-e and F-f treat the top-up as a post-hoc request that is approved with probability q_topup. No pre-commitment, no reversion, no condition on award.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.4 line 203: HSIP reimburses 90%, with 10% local match, and staff hours count as a soft match. Line 240: the Tenderloin SS4A example had a federal share plus a Prop L share, which is a precedent for Prop L as a named match. Line 185: allocation is based on a prepared applicant package, so staff can set conditions in the package.
proposals.parameter: sw_contingent_match in {0, 1}, and q_topup_cond in [0.5, 0.95] (inferred) used in place of q_topup when the switch is on. The reversion clause releases funds with probability 1 - P(award).
proposals.range: switch 0/1; q_topup_cond U(0.5, 0.95); requires an award event
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-e and F-f (the q_topup draw), and D3.3 (it conditions which local funds appear in the cost plan).

proposals.behaviour: Neighbourhood Transportation Program (NTP) channelling. Staff points a supervisor or district office toward a small NTP planning or design grant for APS work, as a low-cost side route that does not need a 5YPP amendment. This is not a normal EP17 allocation.
proposals.trigger: A supervisor-level sponsor appears (pressure from advocates or a visible incident), the amendment path is slow or gated by offset, and staff want to show a response without moving the main lines. The grant would be sized as design or planning for a single corridor or district.
proposals.effect_in_model: It adds a seventh local route (PW7) that pays only for design or planning, so it does not by itself cause installs. It can speed up the design stage for a few intersections (reduces t_des) while leaving the construction funding problem unsolved, so its effect depends on whether an HSIP or Prop L construction source exists afterwards.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. The model list of pathways PW0-PW6 and the failure paths F-a..F-m contain no NTP route, and a search of 02 for NTP finds no match. Evidence 01 mentions NTP as a channel but the model does not use it.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 177: a district supervisor used a $500k NTP to design two signals that included APS at Lincoln Way, and the 5YPP revision took 3-4 months. Line 48 lists the NTP5 5YPP document, with a $700k per district per 5 years limit (line 69). Line 269: supervisors can move money through NTP recommendations.
