proposals.parameter: sw_ntp in {0, 1}, with ntp_cap = $700k per district per 5 years (from the evidence) and p_ntp_use in [0, 0.3] (inferred) as the annual chance a district uses it for APS design.
proposals.range: p_ntp_use U(0, 0.3) per district-year; ntp_cap fixed at 0.7M per 5 years
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 (adds PW7) and D3.4 (shortens t_des for the covered intersections, leaves construction unfunded).

proposals.behaviour: Offset-swap: staff, when told SG015 visibility is going to HSIP C13, treat the Prop L EP17 visibility row (about $0.4M/yr in the 5YPP) as partly redundant and propose reprogramming the freed share to APS inside the same 5YPP amendment. This answers the 'no uncommitted balance' objection, since EP17 is about 202% over-programmed.
proposals.trigger: The SG015 HSIP C13 application is submitted or awarded, and a local APS amendment is requested. Staff also need a zero-sum offset for it.
proposals.effect_in_model: Creates a new local-money source for APS that depends on the HSIP outcome of the SG015 package. A_local rises only if SG015 is HSIP-funded and APS is not. It makes PW2 (local-first) and PW6 easier to start, and ties PW1 failure to PW2 success.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. PW6 (02 D3.6) uses only SG017 ($500k FY27/FY28) and q_sg017_block. D10 has no link from the visibility row to A_local. F-k (q_dir) covers only the director's 10% and the SG000 reserve.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 'EP17 2023 5YPP ... visibility ($0.4M/yr) ... no APS install row' (about l.179). 01 s3 SG015 'HSIP C13 $1.1M - EST' (l.239, l.442). The 5YPP row and the CIP SG015 row are not confirmed to be the same project, so the link is an inference. Partial document support only.
proposals.parameter: f_swap, with optional switch sw_swap (0/1). While SG015 is in a HSIP package, a share f_swap of the EP17 visibility row, $0.4M/yr x f_swap, is added to A_local for APS. If SG015 is not funded by HSIP, f_swap = 0.
proposals.range: f_swap U(0, 0.5); 0 is the control
proposals.rule_modified: D3.2 / local-field A_local (allocation balance); D3.6 PW2 and PW6 starting conditions; D10 table, one new row.

proposals.behaviour: Contingent allocation / match timing: staff will not release or pre-program the 10% local match (or any Prop L share) for an HSIP project until it is awarded (about 2027-03/04) and the allocation request cycle is done. This opens a gap between award and a complete funding plan.
proposals.trigger: An HSIP award arrives for a package that needs a Prop L or local match. The allocation request calendar (8-13 weeks, no August meeting) and staff review time still apply.
proposals.effect_in_model: Delays CON E-76, or the start of the PE or CON step, by a gap t_match. If staff also require the match to sit in an approved 5YPP line first, the gap grows with the 5YPP window (2027 autumn to 2028). That adds to the schedule risk in 01 critic C3 (SG142 planned 2027-07 start, approval 2027-03/04, plus 15-28 months).
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. D3.4 CON E-76 = max(design, PIF, cycle start + t_con). The 10% match is treated as available, and q_topup covers overruns only (F-f, F-e). F-g is partner delay, not match timing.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 'allocation based on a prepared and submitted application package; staff review -> CAC -> board' (l.185); allocation lead time 8-13 weeks (l.193); HSIP 10% local match (l.203, D10 l.604). No document says staff delay the match: no document support for the behaviour itself.
proposals.parameter: t_match_gap, added to the CON E-76 formula. Switch sw_match_5ypp = 1 adds the wait for the next 5YPP window. Default 0.
proposals.range: t_match_gap U(0, 6) months; with sw_match_5ypp = 1, U(0, 18) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 HSIP row (CON E-76 definition); F-d milestone red-flag timing; D10 table.

proposals.behaviour: Staff-facilitated route that does not need an SFMTA application: SFCTA is itself a listed applicant for EP18 (Safer and Complete Streets), and staff can steer a district office toward the NTP ($700k per district over 5 years) as a one-off route. This is use of an unlisted fund by someone other than the stalled actor.
proposals.trigger: HSIP C13 gives no APS award, or SFMTA deflects (DEFLECTED). Advocacy pressure stays high, and a board member asks staff what is possible.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a bypass for the 'no one applies, so no money' loop. A small, lumpy money inflow (about $0-700k) appears, tied to a district. It needs staff and board-member action, not an A2 task. It would sit as a branch under the PW1 -> PW2 fallback chain.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. A grep of 02 for NTP, EP18 and TNC returned nothing. Pathways PW0-PW6 include only SG017, EP17 amendment, general fund, director's 10%, and HSIP. D3.1 has A2 as the only behavioural actor.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: EP18 applicants 'SFMTA, SFPW, SFCTA' (l.170); NTP $700k/district (l.171, NTP5 p.7-8); D4 NTP $500k for Lincoln Way, 5YPP revision in 3-4 months (l.177). Direct support for the mechanism, not for this staff behaviour.
proposals.parameter: q_ntp_route, per-year trigger probability after a PW1 failure. Companion parameters a_ntp (amount) and t_ntp (lead time, precedent 3-4 months). Switch sw_ntp (0/1), 0 as control.
proposals.range: q_ntp_route U(0, 0.3); a_ntp U($0, $500k); t_ntp U(3, 8) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 add branch PW7 'third-party route' and a row in the PW1 'still failing' column; D3.1 optionally an event that bypasses A2; D10 table.

proposals.behaviour: Triage by readiness: in the week before the deadline, staff pre-screen the SFMTA proposals and in effect advise submitting only a package that passes BCR >= 5.0 (the SG015 + APS bundle) and keeping the APS-only line out. Staff log the APS-only line as 'ineligible, wait for 5YPP' rather than a rejection. This changes which application instances exist, not which are rejected.
proposals.trigger: Pre-deadline consultation (about a week before). The APS-only line (SG142) fails eligibility (INS13), and the SG015 package is eligible.
proposals.effect_in_model: Shifts the split m and the set of instances before SUBMIT. It lowers wasted preparation (D_prep + delta_split) and removes a REJECTED record (F-a / F-c). It also removes any chance of a rare exception approval. It acts as an upstream filter on the PW1 start.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-a covers BCR < 5.0 as 'cannot submit', and D3.3 has an eligibility review event after SUBMIT. Staff advice before the preparation window is not a rule, so only the earlier timing is new.
proposals.evidence: 01 s5 'SG142 pure APS is ineligible in C13 and exceeds the $360k cap' (l.420); 01 s2.3 'staff review' of applications (l.185). No document supports SFCTA staff pre-screening HSIP applications (HSIP is a Caltrans programme), so the role is unverified.
proposals.parameter: q_prescreen, probability that SFMTA drops or reshapes an ineligible instance before the deadline when advice is given. Companion d_advice is the lead time in months.
proposals.range: q_prescreen U(0, 0.7), default 0; d_advice U(0.25, 1) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING -> SUBMIT transition (which instances are submitted); F-a recovery path; D10 table.

proposals.behaviour: Staff-level 'orphan deferral' of APS-bearing requests. With the informal APS owner gone, SFCTA programming staff treat any amendment or allocation request that adds new-install APS to a 'replace'-only line (SG017 / EP17) as higher-risk (no named sponsor, no one to answer scope questions) and quietly shift it to the next scheduled 5YPP cycle or ask for a resubmittal, rather than bringing it to the board now.
proposals.trigger: Vacant sponsor-side post (owner departure) AND hiring freeze AND the request touches scope beyond the 5YPP wording (new-install vs replace). Staff have no contact to resolve ambiguity; the cheapest safe action is to defer.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the delay and rejection probability on PW6 (SG017 route) and PW2 (Prop L amendment) before the board ever votes. It acts at the staff-review stage, not as a board veto. Lengthens time-to-approval and moves requests to the 2027-fall to 2028 5YPP window.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j (board veto or deferral, q_veto / t_defer) and PW6's q_sg017_block (scope limited to 'replace') exist, but both sit at the board or at the grant-scope stage. A staff-stage, sponsor-vacancy-conditional deferral is not modelled, and q_veto is not conditioned on whether a sponsor owner exists. Keep as a conditional modifier, not a duplicate.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: allocations are made 'based on a complete application package prepared and submitted by the eligible sponsor'; staff review, then CAC, then board (SP p.22 s2.7). 01 s2.3: the 5YPP description says 'replace' only, while the CIP27m scope text allows new APS (01 l.446). No document support for the vacancy-conditional behaviour itself.
proposals.parameter: q_staff_defer_orphan
proposals.range: U(0, 0.5), applied only while owner_vacant = 1. If it fires, the request is held until the next scheduled 5YPP window or for t_staff_hold = U(3, 9) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j and D3.6 PW6 / PW2. Adds a staff-review gate before the board step, scaled by owner_vacant.

proposals.behaviour: Co-sponsor substitution: SFCTA staff, seeing a pending APS need but no applicant, informally steer the board member from the affected district or a CAC member toward an NTP-funded (neighborhood transportation program) route. They offer a small NTP-style design amendment for a corridor that includes APS, instead of waiting for SFMTA to file a sponsor request.
proposals.trigger: The sponsor is absent while public or board pressure on APS continues. Staff prefer a fast, board-member-driven small-dollar route that does not depend on SFMTA staffing, and that route exists.
proposals.effect_in_model: Opens a small, unplanned local funding line of about $0.5M per event, only for intersections that are on a corridor and already have a design champion. It bypasses the SFMTA-initiated PW2 entirely and produces design-only money, which still needs a delivery sponsor later (hits the F-e/F-f delivery bottleneck).
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 mentions the D4 NTP precedent only as a 3-4 month amendment timing for F-j. It does not model SFCTA staff initiating a bypass route, or NTP as a funding pathway for APS.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: a D4 supervisor used NTP $500k after Prop K to design two new signals with APS at Lincoln Way, with a 3-4 month 5YPP revision (LW p.15-18). 01 s2.3: NTP is $700k per district per 5 years, and the mayor and board can 'indirectly move money via NTP recommendations' (NTP5 p.7-8, 01 s2.12 line 269). That staff initiate this is no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_ntp_steer
proposals.range: U(0, 0.3) per year per district with pending APS and owner_vacant = 1. Payout a_ntp = $0.25-0.5M, limited to design (PREPARING phase) with delivery still needing a sponsor
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 adds a new pathway PW7 'NTP bypass'. Modifies the D3.1 PREPARING initial condition (design done early but delivery open).

proposals.behaviour: Scope-narrowing in standard conditions (reframing) on any allocation that does reach staff: staff attach conditions such as 'APS only at intersections where existing conduits and poles are confirmed satisfactory' or 'sponsor to deliver within N months', and require a sponsor-side staffing or delivery plan. With no APS owner to supply it, the request cannot satisfy the condition and is cut back to the replace-only portion.
proposals.trigger: A request that includes new-install APS reaches staff review while the 'delivery capacity' evidence from the sponsor is thin (Signal Shop staffing constraint documented, hiring freeze).
proposals.effect_in_model: Reduces the number of APS intersections funded per approved grant (a thinning factor), without failing the whole grant. Funded dollars flow to non-APS items such as controllers. Net effect: even approved SG017 funds produce fewer APS installs.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 q_sg017_block (scope limited to replace, or money used for faulty-controller priority) and a_sg017 give an all-or-nothing block and a dollar cap. A per-grant APS thinning fraction tied to sponsor delivery capacity is not modelled. Keep as a continuous modifier on a_sg017.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: Signal Shop staff limitations 'often a limiting factor in project delivery speed' (EP17-5YPP l.354-356, p.9). 01 s2.3: EP17 hardware replacement $1M went to about 98 controllers with a firewall defect, though 2023 PIF listed APS replacement as eligible (OCT25 p.7, EP17-5YPP p.70). No document support for the specific condition-setting behaviour.
proposals.parameter: f_aps_thin
proposals.range: U(0.3, 1.0) multiplier on a_sg017 and on any Prop L grant APS share; lower when owner_vacant = 1 and strain(t) is high
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 (a_sg017) and D3.4 delivery batch size from locally funded grants.

proposals.behaviour: Waiting for the better window: because EP17 is over-programmed now (about 202% ahead) and the next 5YPP is expected not to be, staff advise any would-be APS sponsor (and the board) to hold APS for the 2027-fall to 2028 5YPP and to put it in the strategic plan line, not to amend the current plan. Staff also decline mid-cycle amendments that draw down the thin FY26-28 uncommitted headroom ($0-0.5M per year).
proposals.trigger: Mid-cycle amendment request when headroom is near zero and the 5YPP development schedule is within roughly 12-24 months; a vacant sponsor post removes any urgency from the applicant side.
proposals.effect_in_model: Collapses PW2 and PW6 timing into the single 2028 window as the default, with mid-cycle approvals becoming rare. This is a recommendation effect that changes t_defer and q_veto, not a board decision.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j has 'wait for the next 5YPP round (2027 fall-2028)' as a fallback after a veto, and D10 has EP17 uncommitted headroom of $0-0.5M. But the staff-side recommendation to wait is not a separate switch, and the veto/defer probabilities do not depend on how close the next 5YPP window is. Keep only if folded in as a modifier of q_veto, not a new fund.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'the next five years are not expected to see this degree of advance programming' (EP17-5YPP p.11); EP17 FY26-28 about $2.80M per year all committed with no APS install line (EP17-5YPP p.10-11, p.14); next strategic plan and 5YPP start 2027 fall, pass 2028 (SP p.8, p.10, p.46). That staff actually give this advice is no document support.
proposals.parameter: w_wait_window
proposals.range: Switch 0/1 plus a scalar: if 1, mid-cycle amendment approval probability multiplied by (1 - U(0.2, 0.8)) whenever months to next 5YPP window <= 24 and headroom < $0.5M
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (q_veto and t_defer made conditional on window distance and headroom); D3.6 PW2 start-time default.

proposals.behaviour: Staff turn the supplement request into a negotiated partial grant with a descope. They recommend funding only part of the gap, or only the sites whose conduit and ramp cost is lowest. The costliest sites are sent back to the next 5YPP cycle as new competing requests under the scoring rubric. The rest of the batch keeps moving. The project is not fully funded and not terminated.
proposals.trigger: Design finishes, the actual cost exceeds plan x (1 + kappa_cont), and the gap is large relative to the line's uncommitted balance. The board packet needs a recommendation that fits the balance.
proposals.effect_in_model: The F-f overrun branch gets a third outcome besides 'full top-up' and 'terminate'. The top-up covers a fraction phi_top of the gap. Sites are then ranked by cost per site and the highest-cost ones are dropped from the batch. They return to the backlog pool tagged 'deferred', not 'TERMINATED', and may re-enter at the 2027-autumn to 2028 5YPP window. This changes how many sites are installed and which sites, and it keeps the project alive. The model has no such middle state.
proposals.already_in_model: Not covered. D3.5 F-f only has q_topup, a binary draw, followed by TERMINATED of the project or intersection. D3.4 'Project termination' has no partial-funding state. The 2027-autumn 5YPP window exists in F-j and PW2 but is not used as a destination for deferred overrun sites.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 (l.185) says allocation is 'based on the application package prepared and submitted by an eligible applicant', with SFCTA staff review before CAC and the board. This supports staff shaping the package. 01 l.192 gives the next 5YPP window as 2027 autumn to 2028. 01 l.179-180 says the EP17 line has no spare, with $0 to $0.5M per year uncommitted, so full cover is unlikely. No document directly shows partial grants with a descope, so that mechanism is inferred.
proposals.parameter: gap_mode in {full_or_terminate (current), partial_descope}; phi_top ~ U(0.3, 1.0), the share of the gap covered; defer_to_next_5ypp in {0,1}.
proposals.range: phi_top U(0.3, 1.0). Sensitivity: when phi_top = 1 the rule reduces to the current q_topup success, and when phi_top is 0 it reduces to the current failure.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f ('over-budget' branch) and the TERMINATED rule in D3.4.

proposals.behaviour: Staff look for money inside the existing 5YPP before asking for new money. They reprogram unspent or slipping balances from other lines in the same Prop L program into the APS batch. Candidates are lines whose projects have been delayed by staffing or by long lead times. They do this through an administrative or minor amendment, not a full 5YPP amendment. The overrun is covered by sibling lines, and the line is repaid in a later year.
proposals.trigger: A gap is reported, and the same program has lines with unspent cash or delayed deliverables. Staff prefer a swap that needs no new revenue and no major board action.
proposals.effect_in_model: The funding source of the gap changes. A reprogramming pool, B_reprog(t), funds part of any overrun before q_topup is drawn. This lowers termination, but the donor line's projects slip. It adds a coupling between the APS gap and the delivery of other signal work, which the model does not currently represent.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly, and only the SG017 route. PW6 puts new APS into SG017 at allocation time, with q_sg017_block and a_sg017. That route is a planned allocation choice, not a mid-project overrun source. No rule moves money between lines to cover an overrun. DROP none, but keep the scope narrow.
proposals.evidence: 01 l.179 says the EP17 5YPP has committed $27.49M against pay-as-you-go $8.52M, about 202% over-advanced. This suggests little free cash but also lines that can be reshuffled. 01 l.181 says Signal Shop staffing limits delivery speed, so some lines slip. 01 l.446-447 says SG017 funds went to controllers, not APS. No document shows reprogramming used to cover overruns, so this is inferred.
proposals.parameter: q_reprog (probability that a reprogramming swap is available and used for an overrun) and a_reprog (dollars available per year).
proposals.range: q_reprog U(0, 0.5); a_reprog U($0, $400k) per year. Tie the upper end to the SG017 FY27 and FY28 $500k lines (01 l.446). Set both to 0 for the control run.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f: insert a funding step between 'within contingency' and 'top-up request (q_topup)'.

proposals.behaviour: The top-up decision is shared and cumulative across projects, and it is made on the board calendar. Each approved supplement consumes a limited discretionary pool and raises staff caution about precedent. Later requests face a lower success chance and longer waits. Staff also hold requests until the next scheduled allocation cycle, and there is no August meeting. Staff may also ask SFMTA to show it has first tried its own sources before SFCTA tops up.
proposals.trigger: Several overruns arrive in the same period, or a recent top-up (for example a large supplement to another street project) is on record. The packet must pass staff, CAC and the board.
proposals.effect_in_model: q_topup is no longer an independent draw. It becomes q_topup_eff = q_topup x max(0, 1 - n_recent / N_pool), where n_recent counts approved top-ups in the last 24 months. A wait t_cycle is added before the decision, so a request filed just after a meeting waits for the next one. Variance across runs rises because early requests succeed and late ones fail. Batching of requests over time also becomes possible.
proposals.already_in_model: Not covered. F-e and F-f use q_topup as a per-case probability, with only t_pause after a denial. No wait before the first decision and no shared pool or precedent effect appears in D3.5 or in the D10 q_topup row (U(0, 0.7)).
proposals.evidence: 01 l.193 gives the lead time from application to allocation as 8 to 13 weeks, with no August meeting. 01 l.185 gives the review chain of staff, CAC and board. 01 l.319 records the duty 'SFMTA will seek additional funds through federal, state and local sources', which supports a first-try-your-own-sources condition. 02 F-f cites the 13th St supplement of $2.7M as the precedent. Whether it limits later requests is not documented, so the pool and precedent effect are inferred.
proposals.parameter: N_pool (number of top-ups the pool can absorb before q_topup reaches zero) and t_cycle (wait to next decision meeting, in months).
proposals.range: N_pool integer in {2, 3, 5, 8}; t_cycle U(1, 4) months, with 0 as the current behaviour. Compare with the independent draw as the control.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-e and F-f (q_topup draw) and the event queue in O3 (add a decision-meeting calendar).

proposals.behaviour: Conditional approval with descoping: staff do not answer an overrun with a binary top-up or terminate. They recommend funding only the sites that still fit the original envelope plus contingency, and push the costliest sites (new conduit, new curb ramps) to a later cycle or another fund.
proposals.trigger: Design-complete cost discovery (F-f) leaves a gap above contingency, and the board packet needs a recommendation staff can defend against the 5YPP scoring criteria (readiness, cost-effectiveness) and the 12-month commitment rule.
proposals.effect_in_model: Replaces the two-way split in F-f (full top-up with probability q_topup, else the whole project or site is TERMINATED) with a partial outcome. The cheapest sites in the batch continue, and only the sites with excess cost return to the backlog pool. Fewer sites are installed, but the batch is not lost. It also keeps top-up demand smaller, which helps later requests pass.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-f says that without a top-up 'the project / that intersection is TERMINATED and goes back to the backlog'. The 'that intersection' wording hints at per-site termination, but no rule ranks sites by overrun, and there is no staff-driven partial funding. D3.2 sizes batches by plan cost x (1 + kappa_cont) only at the start. This is a different trigger point (post-design), so I keep it.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 'Decision rules': allocations are 'based on the application package prepared and submitted by the eligible applicant', with SFCTA staff reviewing first. 01 s2.3 constraints: the strategic plan already cut projects to 85-89% of priority 1, which is a precedent for scoping to fit money. 01 s2.3 'Decision rules': 5YPP scoring includes readiness 5 and leverage 4. No document support for descoping APS sites specifically.
proposals.parameter: p_descope
proposals.range: U(0, 0.8). Given an overrun beyond contingency, probability that staff recommend a partial award (drop the worst-overrun sites until the gap is at most the available top-up) instead of the binary top-up/terminate draw.
proposals.rule_modified: F-f funding-gap branch (the q_topup draw); adds site-level termination ordered by the per-site overrun draw.

proposals.behaviour: Internal EP17 reprogramming: staff look for the gap inside EP17 by moving money from other lines (hardware replacement, visibility, a contingency or reserve line) through a 5YPP amendment. This is a zero-sum transfer, not new money. Staff approve it only if the donor line has slack.
proposals.trigger: An overrun beyond contingency arrives when EP17 FY26-28 is fully programmed with no uncommitted slack, and the next 5YPP is a year away.
proposals.effect_in_model: Gives the gap a third source. q_topup stops being a single probability and becomes a draw limited by donor-line slack in each fiscal year. A transfer takes funding from the failure-driven lines (controllers, hardware), so the model gets a real competitor for the same dollars. Approval time follows the amendment path (about 3-4 months).
proposals.already_in_model: Not fully. PW6 (D3.6) puts new APS inside the existing SG017 hardware line without an amendment. F-j covers a board veto or delay of an amendment that reopens the local special line. Neither covers reprogramming existing EP17 lines to fill a cost gap after allocation. F-f's q_topup has no source or ceiling.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: FY26-28 about $2.80M/yr is allocated to TSP, conduit, signs, hardware replacement ($0.5M/yr) and visibility ($0.4M/yr), with 'no APS installation line'. 01 s2.3: the 5YPP is 'about 202% ahead' of pay-as-you-go. 01 s2.3: controllers got EP17 hardware money after two outage events, so failure-driven projects have priority. 01 s2.3: a Lincoln Way 5YPP amendment took 3-4 months. No document support that staff move money specifically to cover an APS overrun.
proposals.parameter: slack_ep17 and q_realloc
proposals.range: slack_ep17 per year U($0, $0.5M), matching the model's uncommitted margin in D1. q_realloc U(0.1, 0.7) is the probability that staff propose an internal transfer first. The top-up approved is min(gap, slack_ep17).
proposals.rule_modified: F-f top-up source rule (replaces the flat q_topup); the amendment timing t_defer in F-j also applies.

proposals.behaviour: Timing the request to a window: staff advise holding the overrun request, or folding it into the next 5YPP update (2027 autumn to 2028) or a regular allocation cycle, instead of sending a stand-alone amendment now. A standard allocation is also a lower-friction approval than an amendment during an over-programmed period.
proposals.trigger: The overrun is discovered while the 5YPP is over-programmed ahead of revenue, and the staff view is that a larger packaged request later will do better than a small one now.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a mandatory wait, t_wait, before a top-up request can be approved. It also exposes the project to the cost of delay: unit-cost growth (costpress) and the 12-month post-allocation commitment clock. This could push projects into TERMINATED even though a top-up would eventually be approved. It also makes the success of a request depend on the fiscal-year calendar.
proposals.already_in_model: Only partly. F-e has t_pause (3-12 months) and then one retry. F-j has t_defer after a board veto. Neither lets staff choose to wait for the next 5YPP window before a first request, and the wait is not tied to the 2027-autumn 5YPP start. So it is a different trigger.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 'Adjustable parameters': next strategic plan + 5YPP starts 2027 autumn, adopted 2028; lead time 8-13 weeks from application to allocation with no August meeting. 01 s2.3 constraints: 'the next five years are not expected to see this level of advance'; construction allocation requires commitment within 12 months. No document support that staff delay a request on purpose.
proposals.parameter: p_wait_5ypp
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6): probability that staff steer the first top-up request to the next 5YPP cycle. If chosen, t_wait is set to the months remaining until the 5YPP adoption date (about 12-24 months from now). If not chosen, the normal 8-13 week allocation lead time applies.
proposals.rule_modified: F-f top-up request timing, plus the interaction with costpress(t) and the 12-month commitment limit in D3.4.

proposals.behaviour: Funding-neutral amendment rule (zero-sum offset). Staff tell SFMTA that any 5YPP amendment adding APS must move money out of another EP17 line (TSP, visibility, pipe/hardware replacement) rather than add new money, and may condition approval on SFMTA naming which line gives way. APS then competes inside EP17 against SFMTA's own priorities.
proposals.trigger: An APS amendment or allocation arrives while FY26-28 uncommitted headroom is near zero and EP17 is overprogrammed against pay-go; fires at staff review, before the board sees it.
proposals.effect_in_model: F-j treats approval as a single board draw (q_veto, t_defer). With this switch the approved amount is capped at min(request, headroom + donor_share * donor line), and the request is blocked or deferred when the donor-line owner objects. Lowers PW2/PW6 success where headroom is 0 and shifts failure from the board to staff.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j covers board veto and deferral; D10 uses headroom $0-0.5M/yr; q_sg017_block covers money consumed by controller failures. None models a staff-imposed offset or a donor-line veto, so kept as distinct.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: EP17 2023 5YPP committed $27.49M against pay-go $8.52M (about 202% ahead); FY26-28 about $2.80M/yr all assigned to TSP, pipes, signs, hardware replacement ($0.5M/yr), visibility ($0.4M/yr); no APS install line (EP17-5YPP p.10-11, p.14). Headroom: only by changing the hardware row or amending the 5YPP. No document shows staff imposing an offset; rule is inferred.
proposals.parameter: q_offset (probability staff require a funding-neutral offset) and donor_share (fraction of the donor line movable)
proposals.range: q_offset U(0,1); donor_share U(0,0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: F-j and the Prop L steps of PW2/PW6

proposals.behaviour: Partial approval, haircut and cash-flow back-loading. Staff recommend a reduced or phased allocation: fewer intersections than requested, design-only first, or the same total programmed in later fiscal years, to fit pay-go.
proposals.trigger: A request exceeds what the year's pay-go cash flow supports (normal while EP17 is ahead of pay-go; FY28/29 pay-go about $2.0-2.8M/yr).
proposals.effect_in_model: F-j and the Prop L branch of PW2/PW6 are all-or-nothing (approve, veto, defer). Haircut and delay lower installed_5y without any veto event, widen recovery_time, and design-only phasing adds a second request cycle.
proposals.already_in_model: No for Prop L. Only the HSIP branch has partial funding of the marginal application (D3.3 line 195). F-j t_defer is a delay after a veto, not a delay inside an approval.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 5YPP programmed by year against pay-go, about 202% ahead; 'the next five years are not expected to see this degree of front-loading' (EP17-5YPP p.11). Staff haircutting itself: no document support.
proposals.parameter: h_prop (fraction of request programmed) and d_cash (months of cash-flow delay)
proposals.range: h_prop U(0.3,1.0); d_cash U(0,24) months
proposals.rule_modified: F-j approval branch; PW2 and PW6 Prop L steps

proposals.behaviour: Scope-condition steering on other signal grants. Staff attach APS-inclusion language to EP18 corridor or EP17 signal allocations (or strip it by limiting SG017 to 'replace'), so APS rides along with parent projects without a standalone APS request.
proposals.trigger: An EP17/EP18 allocation touching signals reaches staff review while advocates press in public; acts at allocation-memo drafting where scope wording is set.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes the inflow share of Fs/parent-project intersections, which is currently given rather than driven by staff behaviour. PW6 only has a 'staff narrows scope to replace' failure branch; this makes both directions explicit.
proposals.already_in_model: Half. PW6 failure branch (scope limited to 'replace') and q_sg017_block exist (02 D3.6 PW6). The positive direction (APS-inclusion condition on EP18/EP17 allocations) and its effect on parent-project bundling are not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 446: SG017 CIP scope text allows new APS where poles/conduit are fine, while EP17 5YPP says only 'replace'; Contract 35 $5.35M for 17 sites incl. APS, C66/C67 new signals mostly include PCS+APS (OCT25 p.3, p.26-27). 01 section 2.3: CAC memos show no question about APS absence, so staff do not visibly push now.
proposals.parameter: q_cond (probability staff add an APS-inclusion condition to a signal-related allocation); s_narrow (probability staff narrow SG017 to replace-only, would subsume q_sg017_block)
proposals.range: q_cond U(0,0.6); s_narrow U(0,0.8)
proposals.rule_modified: Fs/parent-project inflow; PW6 failure branch

proposals.behaviour: Redirecting to the next planning window before filing. In informal pre-application contact, staff advise SFMTA to hold an APS request for the 2027-28 5YPP update instead of filing an amendment, so no formal vote occurs and no veto record exists.
proposals.trigger: Pre-application inquiry or advocate pressure arrives while the 5YPP update window (autumn 2027 - 2028) is within about 12-18 months.
proposals.effect_in_model: Removes the amendment attempt from PW2/PW6 without a q_veto event, reinforces SFMTA's 'no money' reply, and moves the path to the 2028 round. Raises P(wait until 2028) and the recovery_time floor. Makes F-j two-stage (informal screen, then vote).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j lets a rejected amendment wait for the next 5YPP, but staff screening that stops filing before any vote is absent, so q_veto is the only way an amendment is lost.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: allocation is based on the sponsor's package (SP p.22); 2026-01, 05, 06 Prop L allocation memos contain no EP17 signal request (l.190); no CAC question on APS absence (inferred absence). No document shows staff discouraging a filing; hypothesis for sensitivity testing only.
proposals.parameter: q_screen (probability staff informal screening redirects an amendment to the next window), scaled by months to window
proposals.range: q_screen U(0,0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (adds a pre-vote screening step); PW2 entry

proposals.behaviour: Zero-sum offset rule for any 5YPP amendment that adds an APS line. Staff will not recommend adding a line unless SFMTA names a line to cut or delay (TSP, hardware replacement, visibility, pipeline). Staff then tell the board the amendment is 'cost-neutral'. The amendment therefore costs SFMTA an internal fight over what to drop.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA (or advocates through SFMTA) asks to restore a dedicated APS line while EP17 FY24-28 is already over-programmed and the uncommitted balance is about 0-0.5M per year.
proposals.effect_in_model: In PW2 and PW6 (fallback) the amendment no longer opens with a free A_local draw of U(0.5M, 2M). Usable APS money is capped by the cuttable share of already-programmed EP17 rows. The amendment also needs an extra 'SFMTA names the offset' step (a delay) and can stall if no internal owner gives up money. This lowers money_flows_5y for the local-first path and raises the value of HSIP-first.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j (02 D3.5) covers board veto or deferral (q_veto, t_defer). D10 sets A_local at U(0.5M, 2M) times an APS share when dedicated_line=1. Neither has an offset requirement or a staff-side gate before the board. Not dropped, because the zero-sum constraint is absent from the 02 text.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3 (constraint rows): EP17 2023 5YPP commits $27.49M against pay-go $8.52M, about 202% ahead; FY26-28 about $2.80M per year all given to named rows; 'no APS install row' (EP17-5YPP p.10-11, p.14). Also 'the next five years are not expected to have this much front-loading' (p.11). 01 section 5 parameters: EP17 uncommitted balance $0 / about $0.5M per year. No document shows staff demanding an offset explicitly, so the rule is an inference from the over-programming figures.
proposals.parameter: offset_required (switch 0/1) with offset_share ~ U(0.1, 0.6): the fraction of A_local that must come out of existing EP17 rows. Also t_offset ~ U(1, 6) months for SFMTA to settle the offset. If offset_required=1, A_local_effective = min(A_local, offset_share x programmed_EP17_per_year); the same cap also applies to PW6 when the SG017 line is the source.
proposals.range: offset_required in {0,1}; offset_share U(0.1, 0.6); t_offset U(1, 6) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j, D3.6 PW2 and PW6 openers, D10 A_local and a_sg017

proposals.behaviour: Two-stage allocation with a commitment clock. Staff approve only a design-phase allocation for APS, and require 95% plans, environmental clearance and permits before recommending construction money. Money allocated must be committed within 12 months or it lapses. The effect is that one 'funded' APS batch really needs two separate approvals.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA's first Prop L request for new APS installs, or a first SG017-based request for APS.
proposals.effect_in_model: A funded local batch is not a one-time gate. After design (t_des), the batch needs a second SFCTA construction allocation with its own approval probability and lead time of 8-13 weeks per cycle (no August meeting). If the 12-month commitment clock runs out (design late, Signal Shop strained), the funds lapse and the batch returns to the pool. This adds a new failure and delay path between 'funded' and 'installed'.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.4 internal row: a locally funded batch is first 'designing', then t_des, then the overrun is found (F-f). F-f covers overrun top-up (q_topup). There is no second approval step and no lapse deadline. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'construction allocation needs 95% plans, environmental clearance, permits; must be committed within 12 months of allocation' (SP p.19-23); allocation lead time 8-10 weeks (allocation request calendar); 'allocation based on a complete package prepared and submitted by an eligible sponsor' (SP p.22). 01 section 2.1 line 11: Signal Shop staffing is 'often the limiting factor' (EP17-5YPP l.354-356).
proposals.parameter: q_stage2 (probability the second, construction allocation is approved on the first try) and t_commit (months allowed before lapse). Switch two_stage in {0,1}. If two_stage=1 and design completion exceeds t_commit, the batch lapses with probability q_lapse and re-enters the task state machine at IDLE.
proposals.range: q_stage2 U(0.6, 0.98); t_commit fixed 12 months, with a sensitivity of 12-18; q_lapse U(0.3, 1.0); two_stage in {0,1}
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 internal-delivery row (local batch) and F-f; adds a new step before the Fi -> I queue

proposals.behaviour: Informal fund steering. When asked 'where can this go?', staff point the request at a neighbouring Prop L mechanism instead of EP17: (a) a district Neighbourhood Transportation Improvement Program (NTP) planning or capital grant sponsored by a Board supervisor, (b) folding APS into an EP18 Complete Streets or signals corridor project, (c) the SFCTA half of the TNC tax, which is clearly eligible. The request is reframed as a district safety project rather than a citywide APS programme.
proposals.trigger: The advocate pressure event (the moment SFMTA says 'no money'), when staff are asked by a supervisor's office or by SFMTA how to fund a visible cluster of intersections.
proposals.effect_in_model: Opens a 'sponsor-reframed' channel next to HSIP and the dedicated line. It funds a small number of intersections per district per cycle (not the whole 76), and funding depends on political sponsorship, not on BCR. It also adds an extra funding source with its own approval time (3-4 months in the Lincoln Way precedent) and a ceiling of about $0.5M per project.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 has no mention of TNC, NTP or EP18 (grep returns zero). D3.3 only models HSIP, local dedicated line, general fund and SS4A; D3.6 PW4 lists 'corridor candidate (added at design)' but not an NTP or TNC route, and not staff-initiated steering. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: D4 supervisor used NTP $500k to design two new signals with APS on Lincoln Way, with a 5YPP amendment done in 3-4 months (LW p.15-18); NTP is $700k per district over 5 years (NTP5); the TNC SFCTA half is 'explicitly eligible' for signals and pedestrian safety, with $0 programmed to signals/APS so far (TNCm p.3, p.7, p.14; PROPD Sec. 3208). 01 section 3 bundling rows for 'Prop L corridor projects' and 'local dedicated line - TNC'.
proposals.parameter: q_steer (probability per pressure event that staff steer to an NTP/TNC/EP18 route and a sponsor accepts), with a_steer (dollars per success) and n_steer (intersections per success). Switch steer_route in {0,1}. Steered success lands in the same approval and delivery queue as a local batch.
proposals.range: q_steer U(0, 0.3) per pressure event; a_steer U($0.2M, $0.7M); n_steer U(2, 12); t_steer U(3, 8) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (adds a 'steered' exit) and D3.3 fund fields; adds one route to D3.6 as an optional PW4 branch

proposals.behaviour: Wait-for-the-window advice. Staff tell SFMTA and advocates that APS belongs in the next 5YPP and strategic plan cycle (autumn 2027 to 2028) rather than a mid-cycle amendment, because the board dislikes reopening 5YPPs in a tight year. The effect is that SFMTA does not start an amendment at all and holds the request for 12-24 months. This is advice, not a board veto.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event when the next-cycle window is less than about 24 months away, and the only open window is a costly mid-cycle amendment.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers p_start for the amendment task (PW2 and PW6) by an advised-wait factor until the window opens, then raises it. The money then arrives later than the model's current fast path (3-4 months after start).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j already lists 'wait for the next 5YPP' as a recovery after a veto or deferral (t_defer). That models a board outcome, not staff advice that stops the SFMTA task from starting. Not dropped, but it is a close neighbour and could be merged into proposal 1 as a pre-submission filter.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: next 5YPP window starts 2027 autumn, adopted 2028 (SP p.8, p.10, p.46); amendments can happen any time, with D4 done in 3-4 months (LW p.15-18); 'staff review, then CAC, then board' (SP p.22). No document shows staff giving this advice, so it is an inference ('no document support' for the behaviour itself).
proposals.parameter: q_wait_advice (probability staff advise waiting) and a multiplier w_adv on p_start for the amendment task while the window is closed. Rule: if the months to the next window are below theta_window, p_start_amend = p_start x w_adv.
proposals.range: q_wait_advice U(0, 0.6); w_adv U(0.2, 0.8); theta_window U(12, 30) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start formula (adds a gating term for the amendment task) and D3.6 PW2/PW6 openers

proposals.behaviour: Shared-pool crowd-out: SFCTA staff treat the thin EP17 uncommitted margin as one pool. Cost-overrun top-ups on already-approved signal projects, and controller or firewall-type failures, are ranked ahead of new-scope APS.
proposals.trigger: A top-up request or system-failure item arrives in the same fiscal year as an APS amendment or SG017 allocation request, while EP17 headroom is $0-0.5M/yr.
proposals.effect_in_model: The APS local-line amount a_sg017 / amendment size is reduced by the top-ups approved that year. This couples F-f, F-j, F-k and PW6 through one residual pool, so APS gets zero in years with many overruns.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D10 has q_sg017_block and F-f has q_topup, but neither is stated as a shared, depleting pool with a priority order. If the implementation already shares the pool, drop it.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 179: EP17 5YPP over-programmed by about 202%, FY26-28 headroom about $0.5M/yr. 01 line 447: FY25-26 SG017 money went to about 98 controllers. 02 F-f: 13th St top-up $2.7M (01 s2.11). Staff priority order itself: no document support.
proposals.parameter: w_crowd (switch/weight). Available APS amount = max(0, a_sg017 - w_crowd * approved top-ups and failure items that year).
proposals.range: w_crowd in {0, 0.5, 1}; 0 = current independent draws
proposals.rule_modified: F-f (top-up approval), F-k, PW6 and the D10 rows a_sg017 / q_sg017_block

proposals.behaviour: Informal staff pre-clearance and steering: before any amendment or allocation request is filed, staff tell SFMTA to wait for the 2027-28 5YPP cycle or that it is not ready. The request is never submitted, so no recorded rejection occurs.
proposals.trigger: The task is in PREPARING, SFMTA consults SFCTA, and headroom is below the request or the 5YPP has no APS row. Public pressure raises the chance a request gets drafted at all.
proposals.effect_in_model: A task moving from PREPARING to SUBMITTED is returned to IDLE or delayed to the next window with no REJECTED event. Lowers the effective submission rate and lengthens time to decision.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-j covers a board veto or deferral after submission; D3.1 has p_deflect only on the SFMTA side toward advocates; eligibility review comes after SUBMITTED.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 185: allocations are based on a package prepared and submitted by the applicant, staff review then CAC then board (SP p.22). Line 180: next five years not expected to be this far ahead. Staff discouraging APS requests: no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_steer (probability) and t_steer (months added)
proposals.range: q_steer U(0, 0.6); t_steer U(3, 12) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING to SUBMITTED transition; applies before F-j; PW2 and PW6 start conditions

proposals.behaviour: Offset-required amendments: staff support an EP17 amendment only if SFMTA names an equal-dollar reduction elsewhere in EP17, or accept only a reduced scope (for example only sites with usable poles and conduit). Outcome is partial approval.
proposals.trigger: An amendment is requested while the 5YPP is fully programmed (FY26-28 about $2.80M/yr, all rows assigned).
proposals.effect_in_model: Funded amount = min(request, donor slack) with an added delay; adds a partial-approval outcome rather than only accept/reject.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j has q_veto and t_defer; PW6 has scope limited to replace. Neither has partial approval or an offset mechanism.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 179: only about $0.5M/yr headroom, rows for TSP, hardware ($0.5M/yr) and visibility ($0.4M/yr) are assigned, no APS row. Line 177: D4 amendment took 3-4 months. Staff requiring offsets: no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_offset_req and f_offset
proposals.range: q_offset_req U(0.3, 0.9); f_offset U(0.3, 1.0) = share of request funded when an offset is required
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (adds partial outcome), PW2 amount, D10 local APS amount

proposals.behaviour: Windfall recycling: when an EP17 or EP18 signal allocation closes under budget, staff may propose redirecting savings to APS, a quiet unlisted source, instead of the overrun reserve.
proposals.trigger: An allocation closes with unspent funds while an APS request or amendment is open or recently denied.
proposals.effect_in_model: Small stochastic income to the local APS pool each year; a funding path outside HSIP and formal amendments.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-k covers the director's 10 percent and SG000 reserve on the SFMTA side only; nothing models SFCTA savings.
proposals.evidence: No document support for savings flowing to APS. 01 s3 line 378 shows $0.3-1.07M per site and a Prop L share gap, which makes underruns plausible but unproven.
proposals.parameter: a_sav (USD per year) and p_sav_aps (probability staff route it to APS)
proposals.range: a_sav U(0, 150k); p_sav_aps U(0, 0.4)
proposals.rule_modified: D4 local field pool, F-k (extra source), PW6 amount a_sg017

proposals.behaviour: Scope-shedding and re-phasing instead of a flat yes/no on the top-up: staff steer SFMTA to recommend a smaller allocation (fund only the sites with intact poles and conduit now, push conduit/curb-ramp-heavy sites to a later phase or a separate request) and condition the board action on that re-scoped list.
proposals.trigger: Design-complete overrun (F-f) exceeds contingency, and the top-up request is larger than the free FY26-28 EP17 headroom ($0-0.5M/yr, 01 §2.3 line 613).
proposals.effect_in_model: Instead of the binary q_topup (approved or the whole project/site TERMINATED), a partial outcome: the allocation is approved for a fraction of the batch, the most expensive sites are returned to the pending pool with a delay, and no TERMINATED event is raised for the funded remainder. This raises installed_5y relative to the all-or-nothing rule and shifts the cost of the overrun onto later coverage.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly but not this. F-f (02 D3.2/D3.5) says an overrun beyond contingency gets a top-up with probability q_topup, else the project or site is TERMINATED and returns to the pool; a re-request after t_pause exists in F-e only. The text speaks of 'project / that site' terminated but has no staff-brokered partial approval or phased split of an already-designed batch. Not covered by D3.1 split rules, which concern HSIP application bundling, not post-design allocation reshaping.
proposals.evidence: No direct APS document support. Indirect: 01 §2.3 line 185 (allocation is 'based on the application package prepared and submitted', staff review then CAC then board) shows staff shape what reaches the board; 01 §2.3 lines 178-181 and 613 show near-zero uncommitted headroom, which is the condition that forces trimming; 01 §2.11 cites the 13th St top-up of $2.7M as a precedent that large top-ups are granted whole, which is the contrast case. Otherwise 'no document support' for the partial-approval behaviour itself.
proposals.parameter: phi_shed (fraction of overrunning sites kept in the current allocation when the full top-up cannot be met), plus sw_rephase (0/1: deferred sites re-enter the pending pool after t_rephase months rather than being TERMINATED)
proposals.range: phi_shed U(0.4, 1.0); t_rephase U(6, 24) months; sw_rephase in {0,1}
proposals.rule_modified: F-f and F-e top-up branch: replaces the 'q_topup else TERMINATED' fork with 'q_topup full, else with probability q_partial approve phi_shed of the batch and return the rest to the pool'

proposals.behaviour: Funding the overrun by reprogramming within the same Prop L category (EP17) rather than by new money: staff identify a lower-priority line, such as the SG017 hardware-replacement allocation or a slow-spending signals line, and recommend a cross-line transfer or 5YPP amendment that moves funds to cover the gap, with the move timed to the next board cycle.
proposals.trigger: Overrun above contingency; the batch is already programmed in the 5YPP; EP17 has few free dollars but lines with unspent or delayed balances (for example deliveries slowed by Signal Shop strain, F-i).
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a funding source for the F-f gap that sits between 'contingency' and 'external top-up': a donor line whose balance depends on how much the donor project has actually spent. Gives a mechanism for the gap to close at no new-money cost but with a cost to the donor line (for example controller or hardware work slips). Creates a coupling between delivery delay on other EP17 lines and APS overrun resolution.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 (02 D3.6) uses SG017 as a source for new APS at the application stage, and F-k covers the director 10% / SG000 reserve; F-j covers the board vetoing an amendment. Neither models staff-initiated intra-category reprogramming as the fix for a post-design overrun, nor a donor line whose headroom depends on its own underspend.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 613 (uncommitted EP17 headroom $0-0.5M/yr, 'only by changing the hardware replacement row or amending the 5YPP'); line 447 (SG017 FY25-26 $1M went to controller replacement, FY27-28 use unknown); line 177 (Lincoln Way: 5YPP revision in 3-4 months). These support the existence of the donor row and the amendment route, but not staff choosing it for overruns: otherwise 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: q_reprog (probability staff offer an intra-EP17 transfer to cover an overrun) and f_donor (share of the SG017 line available as donor, linked to its unspent balance)
proposals.range: q_reprog U(0, 0.6); f_donor U(0, 0.5) of SG017 annual amount; adds t_reprog = 3-4 months (Lincoln Way precedent)
proposals.rule_modified: F-f gap handling (new second source after contingency and before q_topup), and interacts with q_sg017_block in PW6

proposals.behaviour: Gatekeeping through conditions and timing: staff hold or condition the top-up allocation (require a revised cost estimate, a delivery schedule, proof that other funds were sought such as HSIP or SS4A, or a combined request at the next quarterly cycle) and thereby add delay and a 'seek leverage first' step, even when they are not opposed to the project.
proposals.trigger: Request exceeds contingency and the sponsor has no stated fallback; the board calendar has gaps (no August meeting, 8-13 week lead time); the program is already heavily over-committed (EP17 5YPP committed about 202% of pay-as-you-go).
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a staff-stage delay and a re-submit loop before the board sees the request, plus a diversion option: the sponsor is nudged to pursue HSIP/SS4A match funds, which can move the site to another field or shorten reach. Raises time-to-construction and recovery_time without a board veto.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j covers board veto/deferral (q_veto, t_defer) and F-e has t_pause for re-application after an unfunded top-up. The staff-stage 'conditions' loop (a reviewer asking for more before the item goes to the board) is not modelled; the allocation lead time exists only as a calendar fact (01 line 193), not as a staff-triggered iteration count.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 185 (staff review, then CAC, then board); line 193 (8-13 weeks from application to allocation, no August meeting); line 179-180 (committed 202% ahead; 'the next five years are not expected to see this degree of front-loading'), which gives staff a reason to be cautious. No document evidence that staff impose conditions on APS overruns specifically: 'no document support' for the loop itself.
proposals.parameter: n_cond (expected number of staff-requested resubmission rounds before the item goes to the board) and q_divert (probability the sponsor is redirected to seek outside match funds first)
proposals.range: n_cond in {0,1,2} with probabilities U(0,1) summing to 1; each round adds t_round U(1, 3) months; q_divert U(0, 0.3)
proposals.rule_modified: Application/allocation instance lifecycle (D3.1) between 'submitted' and 'board decision', and F-j (adds a pre-board stage); the t_pause logic in F-e

proposals.behaviour: Bundling the overrun into a larger, politically safer request: staff recommend folding the APS conduit and curb-ramp costs into a corridor or signal-upgrade allocation (an EP18-type or already-approved corridor project) so the cost is absorbed in a bigger package that clears the board more easily, at the price of tying APS delivery to the host project's schedule.
proposals.trigger: Standalone APS overrun is small relative to the board's usual item size but large relative to EP17 headroom; a corridor project in the same area is scheduled or recently approved.
proposals.effect_in_model: Creates an alternative resolution for sites that share a corridor with an active host project: the gap is paid by the host's budget, the site installs on the host's schedule, and the site inherits the host's risk of delay or cancellation. Helps sites with a nearby host and delays those without.
proposals.already_in_model: Mostly not. PW1 and F-g model bundling with a partner project (SG015) at the HSIP stage only, with the partner delay/cancel risk; the post-design overrun resolution in Prop L is not allowed to move into a host project. Calling this a fully new mechanism is only partly true because F-g already supplies the partner-risk logic that could be reused.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 lines 168-170 (EP18 Safer and Complete Streets includes new/upgraded signals including pedestrian; applicants SFMTA, SFPW, SFCTA) and line 378 (Contract 35: Prop L $5.35M for 17 locations including APS, about $314k per site, versus $1.07M all-phase); 01 line 409 lists corridor projects as a bundling path for APS. The transfer of an already-designed standalone overrun into such a project is inference: 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: q_host (probability a site has a host project available in the same corridor/time window) and sw_absorb (0/1: whether an overrun can be re-assigned to a host project)
proposals.range: q_host U(0, 0.4); sw_absorb in {0,1}; inherits t_partner U(0, 24) and q_partner_cancel U(0, 0.3) from F-g
proposals.rule_modified: F-f gap handling (adds a third resolution route), F-g (reuse partner risk for Prop L host projects)

proposals.behaviour: Cash-flow deferral of approved allocations. EP17 5YPP is programmed about 202% ahead of pay-as-you-go, so SFCTA programming staff can approve a request in principle but schedule the cash (allocation year or reimbursement) into later fiscal years. The money is approved but not usable for years.
proposals.trigger: A qualifying APS-bearing request (SG017 hardware-replacement allocation or an EP17 amendment) arrives while EP17 or EP18 is overprogrammed, especially FY26-28 when committed lines already exceed annual revenue.
proposals.effect_in_model: Inserts an extra delay between the APPROVED event and the batch becoming funded and entering design (D3.4). Lengthens recovery_time, lowers installed_5y and coverage_10y under PW2 and PW6, and adds a second failure channel besides veto.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j models board veto or deferral of an amendment (t_defer), and PW6 has q_sg017_block (money used by priority controller work). Neither models staff-level cash-flow scheduling of an already approved allocation. Not covered, so kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'EP17 2023 5YPP (FY24-28) commits $27.49M vs pay-as-you-go $8.52M, about 202% ahead' (EP17-5YPP p.10-11, p.14); 'the next five years are not expected to see this level of advance' (p.11); FY26-28 about $2.80M per year all on other lines. No document shows staff deferring an APS allocation specifically.
proposals.parameter: q_cf_defer (probability an approved Prop L APS allocation is cash-flow deferred) and t_cf (months of deferral).
proposals.range: q_cf_defer U(0, 0.6); t_cf U(6, 36) months; 0 as control
proposals.rule_modified: Adds a step after the 'batch approved' event in D3.1/D3.4; new failure path F-n next to F-j. Prop L routes only, not HSIP.

proposals.behaviour: Condition-attaching or scope-bundling by SFCTA staff. Instead of waiting for a stand-alone APS request, staff add a condition to signal-touching allocations (new signals, EP18 corridor projects, signal upgrades) requiring APS at affected crossings, or encourage SFMTA to fold APS into them. A funder-side pull that creates Fs installs without an APS-specific ask.
proposals.trigger: An EP17 or EP18 allocation request or 5YPP amendment is reviewed that includes a signal at a pending-list intersection; equity and community-support scoring or CAC attention makes demanding APS inclusion easy.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the chance a pending C/N intersection goes Fs to installed with a parent project, raises parent project cost (fewer locations per grant), and creates a coverage path that does not depend on SFMTA's start rate p_start.
proposals.already_in_model: Mostly no. PW4 and D3.4 'merged into existing projects' cover SFMTA-side corridor design, PW5 covers an SFMTA design standard. The model has no funder-side rule; SFCTA is passive ('only funds submitted applications', 01 section 2.3). Kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'allocation is based on an application package prepared and submitted by an eligible sponsor' (SP p.22); 5YPP scoring gives equity 5, community support 5 (EP17-5YPP p.12-13); Contract 35 ($5.35M Prop L, 17 intersections with APS) and C66/C67 new signals mostly include PCS+APS (OCT25 p.3, p.26-27). No document says staff impose such a condition.
proposals.parameter: p_condition (probability a Prop L signal allocation touching a pending-list intersection carries an APS-inclusion condition), with cost multiplier delta_scope and extra parent delay t_parent_extra.
proposals.range: p_condition U(0, 0.5); delta_scope U(0, 0.3); t_parent_extra U(0, 6) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 'merged into existing projects' branch (raises pi) and the allocation approval step in D3.1; optionally new pathway PW7 'funder condition' beside PW4.

proposals.behaviour: Staff discretion over the TNC (Prop D) SFCTA half: staff either propose an APS/signal line in the annual TNC programming memo, or keep programming only fast-build and traffic-calming, and answer pressure by saying 'SFMTA has not applied', referring the matter back.
proposals.trigger: Advocate or board pressure becomes visible during annual TNC programming, or the SFMTA-side TNC-funded APS line (FY24 $0.5M) has run out.
proposals.effect_in_model: Switches the TNC lever on or off as a source with annual timing, outside the 2027-28 5YPP window. A staff refer-back resets the SFMTA task like DEFLECTED; a staff yes opens a new money window.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 01 C5 and section 2.3 put the TNC lever on the SFCTA board and the model carries it as a sensitivity branch. The only buck-pass rule is SFMTA's p_deflect (D3.1). No rule for SFCTA staff referring back or programming TNC money on their own initiative; that part is kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: SFCTA TNC half $36.25M, programmed $29.12M (fast-build $23.34M, calm streets $5.78M), signals/APS $0 (TNCm l.109-110, l.286); Prop D lists signal improvements for the SFCTA half (PROPD p.8-9); CIP23 recorded TNC money on APS (p.45). No document shows staff referral behaviour.
proposals.parameter: q_tnc_staff (per-year probability staff include an APS/signal line, with amount a_tnc) and q_refer_back (probability staff answer a pressure event by referring back to SFMTA).
proposals.range: q_tnc_staff U(0, 0.3)/yr; a_tnc U($0.3M, $1M); q_refer_back U(0, 0.8); control both 0
proposals.rule_modified: New funder-side action row in D3.2 (on under M-A and M-D) and a funding-source row for PW2; q_refer_back damps the effect of pressure(t) on the SFMTA task in D3.1.

proposals.behaviour: Sponsor-gated amendments. Staff hold mid-cycle amendments for the scheduled 5YPP window ('consider in the next cycle') unless a board member sponsors the item.
proposals.trigger: A mid-cycle request to create an APS line (PW2) arrives with no board sponsor; the Lincoln Way precedent had a district supervisor and NTP money.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes the amendment path available only with a sponsor, otherwise delayed to 2028. Moves PW2 failures from visible veto (F-j) to quiet waiting, making PW6 and HSIP relatively more attractive.
proposals.already_in_model: Weak overlap. F-j covers board veto or deferral with recovery 'wait for next round', but its trigger is a board decision, not a staff gate dependent on a sponsor. Kept only as the sponsor switch.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: D4 supervisor used NTP $500k and finished the 5YPP revision in 3-4 months (LW p.15-18); next strategic plan and 5YPP 2027 autumn-2028 (SP p.8, p.10, p.46); NTP access via board seats (NTP5 p.7-8). No document says staff refuse mid-cycle amendments without a sponsor.
proposals.parameter: sw_sponsor_needed (0/1) and p_sponsor (per-year probability a supervisor sponsors an APS amendment).
proposals.range: sw_sponsor_needed in {0, 1}; p_sponsor U(0, 0.5)/yr
proposals.rule_modified: PW2 start rule and F-j: without a sponsor, t_defer is set to months until the 2028 window.

proposals.behaviour: Conditional or phased approval (scope trim). Staff recommend funding only the sites that fit the existing envelope, or release funds in phases (fund sites without new conduit or ramps now, hold the rest).
proposals.trigger: Design complete; actual cost exceeds plan x (1 + kappa_cont); top-up request reaches staff; 5YPP line has near-zero uncommitted headroom (FY26-28 about $0-0.5M/yr).
proposals.effect_in_model: Turns F-f's binary q_topup (approved, or TERMINATED) into three outcomes: full top-up, partial top-up with costliest sites returned to the pool, or conditional release. Fewer sites delivered per dollar, fewer outright TERMINATED events.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-f has only top-up approved or not (then TERMINATED). F-e has t_pause and one re-request. D3.1 allows splitting at application time (delta_split) but not staff trimming scope after design.
proposals.evidence: No document support for staff scope-trim on APS specifically. Indirect: 01 s2.3 'allocations based on the application package prepared and submitted by an eligible sponsor; staff review -> CAC -> board' (SP p.22). Top-up precedent exists: 13th St +$2.7M (02 F-f citing 01 s2.11).
proposals.parameter: q_partial
proposals.range: U(0.2, 0.6) given a top-up request; k = sites fitting plan x (1+kappa_cont) + headroom; remaining sites return to pool (TODO, not TERMINATED) with re-entry delay t_reentry U(6, 24) months
proposals.rule_modified: F-f (gap handling after design-complete node) and TERMINATED transition in D3.1

proposals.behaviour: Re-sourcing the gap from other lines by programming staff: steer sponsor to cover the overrun by advancing/rescheduling another EP17 line or drawing on a sibling line (SG017 hardware, EP18) via a technical amendment without a full 5YPP cycle.
proposals.trigger: Gap above contingency; request would otherwise be denied for lack of headroom; other programmed lines slip or underspend.
proposals.effect_in_model: Effective headroom becomes fixed headroom plus slippage from other lines, usable only if staff agree. q_topup then depends on other projects' slack, not the APS line alone.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 uses SG017 only as an origin for new-install scope, not as a gap-filler. F-j is board veto of an amendment; F-k is director 10%/SG000. No rule lets staff move money between lines to cover an overrun of an allocated project.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: FY26-28 EP17 headroom about $0-0.5M/yr, 5YPP about 202% ahead of pay-go (EP17-5YPP p.10-11, p.14), so slippage is the only slack; Lincoln Way amendment in 3-4 months (LW p.15-18). No direct support that staff do this for overruns.
proposals.parameter: slack_swap (lambda_slip, S, q_swap)
proposals.range: lambda_slip U(0, 0.3)/yr chance another EP17 line frees S ~ U($0.1M, $0.6M); staff allow use for APS overrun with q_swap U(0.1, 0.5); added to headroom in q_topup
proposals.rule_modified: F-f (q_topup as function of headroom + slippage); new alternate-source branch before F-k

proposals.behaviour: Timing arbitrage: staff hold a modest overrun request and fold it into the next scheduled amendment or the 2027-28 strategic plan/5YPP cycle instead of a stand-alone supplemental allocation, raising approval odds at the cost of months.
proposals.trigger: Gap modest; a 5YPP development window opens within about 12 months; board calendar gaps (no August meeting; 8-13 weeks request to allocation).
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a HOLD state between gap detected and the top-up draw; project waits while costpress escalates cost; decision taken at the next window with higher approval probability.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-e has t_pause and one re-request; F-j has t_defer and waiting for next 5YPP, but only for opening the local line, not for a supplemental overrun. costpress exists (M-C1). The deliberate staff-timed hold that changes approval probability is not captured.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: next 5YPP window 2027 autumn - 2028; allocation lead time 8-10 weeks, no August meeting (allocation-request-calendar-2025/2026 p.1). No document support that staff intentionally delay.
proposals.parameter: p_hold, dq
proposals.range: p_hold U(0.1, 0.5) for gaps < g_small U(10%, 30%) of plan; q_topup_next = q_topup + dq, dq U(0.05, 0.25); cost grows at existing costpress during hold
proposals.rule_modified: F-f (new hold state before top-up draw); interacts with t_pause in F-e

proposals.behaviour: Precedent-dependent approval: after one top-up is granted, staff either grow stricter (contingency discipline) or looser (consistency) on later top-ups in the same 5YPP period.
proposals.trigger: A prior top-up approved in the same 5YPP period; second/third overrun arrives, e.g. several overrunning sites in one batch submitted in sequence.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes q_topup history-dependent, creating path dependence and order effects within a batch.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. q_topup is a constant per event (F-f, F-e); no memory of prior top-ups.
proposals.evidence: No document support. Only the single 13th St top-up precedent of $2.7M (01 s2.11 via 02 F-f); nothing on its effect on later requests.
proposals.parameter: phi
proposals.range: q_topup(n) = q_topup0 x (1 - phi)^n_prior, phi U(-0.2, 0.4) (negative = easier after precedent); n_prior = top-ups granted in current 5YPP cycle, reset each cycle
proposals.rule_modified: F-f (q_topup becomes a function of count of earlier top-ups in the same 5YPP period)

proposals.behaviour: Partial or token approval. The board passes the amendment, but staff size the restored APS line well below the ask. The money comes out of other EP17 lines, which are already about 202% over-programmed, so the cut is paid for by trimming lines like TSP or visibility. In the model F-j and PW2 treat the amendment as binary (pass, veto or defer). Real staff often recommend 'approve a smaller line'.
proposals.trigger: A competing demand is visible in the same item: controller replacement after an outage, with EP17 FY26-28 uncommitted headroom of only $0-0.5M per year. The over-programming makes a full-size line impossible without displacing someone.
proposals.effect_in_model: PW2 opens a local APS line, but the dollars are scaled by phi. The batch size is smaller (fewer C intersections installed per year), so the HSIP and general-fund fallback has to cover the rest. Timing is unchanged; volume falls.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. 02 D3.6 PW2 and F-j (line 229) only have approve / veto-defer. The only dollar cap is a_sg017 (D10), which belongs to PW6, not to the amendment.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 179 (EP17 5YPP over-programmed about 202%, FY26-28 all allocated, no APS line); line 183 (strategic plan cuts projects to 85-89%); line 411 (FY26-28 uncommitted headroom $0-0.5M per year). No document shows an actual partial-approval case, so the behaviour is inferred.
proposals.parameter: phi_haircut: fraction of the requested APS line that survives approval
proposals.range: U(0.2, 1.0); 1.0 reproduces the current binary model
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2 and D3.5 F-j: add a third outcome 'approved at phi times the request' with probability 1 - q_veto, replacing the binary approve

proposals.behaviour: Claw-back after a failure event. An APS line already restored is reprogrammed back to controller or hardware replacement after the next visible outage or firewall-type failure. Staff handle it as a routine 5YPP technical amendment, and it needs no new debate.
proposals.trigger: A controller-failure event, such as the 2022 and 2025 outages, while an APS line holds unspent money and the controller need is visible and urgent.
proposals.effect_in_model: The unspent balance of the APS line is moved to SG017-type hardware, and the remaining install batches shrink or stall. The APS state goes from FUNDED back to ZERO or LOW. The restored line also gets a lifetime, so the pathway's gain is not permanent.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j covers a veto before approval, and q_sg017_block covers money being used up before the request (PW6). Neither covers the removal of money after the line is approved.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 176 (outage-driven funding: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages); line 126 (EP17 hardware replacement $1M for about 98 controllers, with APS replacement once an eligible use); line 446 (SG017 scope text covers both APS and hardware).
proposals.parameter: q_claw: probability per outage event that the unspent balance of the APS line is reprogrammed away; plus lambda_outage, the event rate
proposals.range: q_claw U(0, 0.6); lambda_outage 0-1 events per year (needs calibration to the 2022 and 2025 events)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 delivery and D3.5: add a new failure path F-n 'funded line reduced after approval' that fires on the exogenous outage event

proposals.behaviour: Contingent or leveraged approval. Staff recommend approval only as local match for an outside grant, for example 'release Prop L APS money only after an HSIP or SS4A award'. This gives priority to requests that bring leverage and ties the local line to the federal path.
proposals.trigger: Over-programming, which makes staff look for leverage, plus the 5YPP scoring criterion for leverage.
proposals.effect_in_model: The local APS dollars (PW2) are released only if PW1 (HSIP) succeeds, which couples two pathways that the model treats as independent. If the grant is lost, the line sits dormant and the installs slip by the HSIP cycle (about 2 years).
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. PW1 to PW6 are separate branches with fallbacks only after rejection (D3.6), and no rule makes one pathway's money conditional on another's success.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 186 (5YPP scoring gives leverage 4 points, readiness 5); line 240 (Prop L used as a 20% match for a federal SS4A award, $1.4M of $7M); line 185 (grants follow a complete application package prepared by the applicant). Staff behaviour of making it a condition has no direct document.
proposals.parameter: q_cond: probability the amendment passes only as a match-contingent line; delta_wait: months to HSIP award
proposals.range: q_cond U(0, 0.7); delta_wait 12-30 months, taken from the HSIP cycle
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2: add a gate (local money available only when the HSIP application is awarded); also changes the sequencing between PW2 and PW1

proposals.behaviour: Staff-level gatekeeping or delay: staff do not docket the standalone amendment. They advise the applicant to wait and fold the APS line into the full 5YPP update (2027 autumn to 2028), or to use the existing SG017 scope, so the item is never put in front of the board.
proposals.trigger: The amendment competes with outage-driven controller needs, and a full update is only about a year away. Staff are the first reviewers (staff, then CAC, then board), so a pending cycle is a convenient reason to wait.
proposals.effect_in_model: The board never votes. F-j's veto fires before it can apply, with a longer fixed delay (until 2028) and not the 1-12 month t_defer. APS timing is pushed into the next cycle, which changes the PW2 versus PW1 order the model assumes.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-j models only a board-level veto or deferral (q_veto, t_defer). Staff screening before the board is absent.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 185 (staff review comes first, then CAC, then board); line 192 (next cycle: strategic plan and 5YPP start 2027 autumn, adopted 2028); line 177 (the D4 precedent went through a 5YPP revision in 3-4 months, so amendments can be fast when staff want them). No document shows staff declining to docket.
proposals.parameter: q_docket: probability that staff docket a standalone amendment (otherwise held to the 2028 update)
proposals.range: U(0.3, 1.0); 1.0 equals the current model
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j and D3.6 PW2: add a pre-board filter step before the veto draw; on no-docket, set t_defer to the time until the 2028 update

proposals.behaviour: Offset-or-placeholder approval: staff recommends the amendment only as a 'fund-neutral' reshuffle. The APS line is created at a reduced or token amount, either by cutting other EP17 lines (hardware replacement, visibility) or by programming it in a later fiscal year. Often it is made 'contingent' on SFMTA first landing leveraged money (HSIP, SS4A, ATP) before any allocation. The board then 'approves' the amendment, yet little usable money arrives soon.
proposals.trigger: EP17 is already over-programmed (FY24-28 about 202% ahead of pay-as-you-go, no uncommitted margin), and the same lines carry controller replacements after outages. A clean add of new money is not available, so staff must find an offset or shrink the ask.
proposals.effect_in_model: F-j and PW2 are binary (pass or veto/defer). This adds a third outcome: 'passed but diluted'. The local batch is funded at fraction phi_cond of the requested amount, and the first allocation is delayed until a leverage trigger fires. This lowers the number of intersections funded and shifts the funding timing, without counting as a failure at the amendment step.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j only has veto (q_veto) or deferral (t_defer). D10 sets uncommitted margin at $0-0.5M/yr but has no rule for a diluted approval or a conditional release. Nothing in 02 sections D3.5 or D3.6 covers it, so it is kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'EP17 2023 5YPP ... 超前约 202% ... 无 APS 安装行' (line 179); 'EP17 当期未承诺余量 $0 ~ $0.5M/年 ... 只能改硬件更换行或修订 5YPP' (line 613); 'SFCTA 战略规划把各项目砍到优先级 1 的 85-89%' (line 183), which shows trimming is the house habit. No document directly shows a conditional APS line, so there is no document support for the conditional-release part.
proposals.parameter: phi_cond (fraction of the requested APS line actually programmed) plus switch sw_leverage_gate (0/1: first allocation requires a matched outside grant).
proposals.range: phi_cond U(0.2, 1.0), with 1.0 meaning no dilution. sw_leverage_gate in {0, 1}, default 0.
proposals.rule_modified: F-j and PW2: after the 1 - q_veto draw, scale the local special-line batch size by phi_cond. If sw_leverage_gate = 1, the first allocation waits for an approved HSIP/SS4A application.

proposals.behaviour: Programming-year back-loading and cash-flow staging. Staff places the restored APS money in out-years (FY28 and later), or phases it, because near-term sales-tax cash is already committed. Approving the amendment is not the same as money being allocable now.
proposals.trigger: The pay-as-you-go cash curve is already used up in the early years of the 5YPP. The 'next five years not expected to be this far ahead' statement signals that cash only loosens later.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a lag between the amendment approval date and the earliest allocation request date. The local batch enters the design stage later, so the delivery clock and the PW2 'idle' signal (theta_defer, theta_idle) both start later. The PW2 pathway looks slower than the model currently shows, and it can trigger a premature switch to the general fund or HSIP.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.4 starts the local batch at 'receiving funds then design'. F-j has t_defer for a deferred decision, but that is a delay in the vote, not a delay in the programming year of an approved line.
