proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'EP17 ... FY26-28 每年约 $2.80M, 全给 TSP、管线、标志、硬件更换、可视性' (line 179); 'EP17 FY28/29 以后年现收现付 ~$2.0-2.8M/年' (line 194); 'FY26-28 未承诺余量 $0-0.5M/年' (line 411). Together these suggest the free cash is in FY28/29 and later. No document shows a staff programming-year decision, so that step has no document support.
proposals.parameter: delta_prog (months between amendment approval and the earliest allowed allocation).
proposals.range: U(0, 30) months. 0 means the current model behavior.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 local batch entry and PW2 signpost: the batch starts the design stage at approval + delta_prog, and theta_defer is measured from approval, not from the start of programming.

proposals.behaviour: Outage-driven reprioritisation as a recurring exogenous shock. A new blackout or controller failure makes staff and board move uncommitted EP17 money, or the money meant for the new APS line, to controller and hardware replacement. The risk is that this happens even after the APS line has been approved but not yet allocated.
proposals.trigger: A visible system failure (power outage with controller failures), at some yearly rate, while the APS line is approved but not yet allocated.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a shock process that, when it fires, reduces or freezes the APS local line (q_reassign share taken) and raises the effective veto and defer probability for any pending amendment. This makes PW2 and PW6 fragile in outage years, while HSIP-based pathways (PW1) are not affected.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. q_sg017_block in PW6 covers the case where SG017 money is used up by 'controllers and fault-priority projects'. But the outage is not a stochastic event in 02 (grep finds no outage or 停电 term), and the line created by PW2 itself is not exposed to the same raid. So the new part is the outage event and its effect on an approved PW2 line.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'Result is driven by visible failures: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 blackouts' (line 176). 01 section 2.3 line 126: EP17 hardware replacement $1M (FY25+FY26) for about 98 controllers with firewall defects, where PIF 2023 once listed APS replacement as an eligible use. Raiding an approved but unallocated APS line has no document support.
proposals.parameter: lambda_outage (yearly rate of an outage event) with q_reassign (share of the pending APS line moved to controllers when it fires).
proposals.range: lambda_outage U(0.05, 0.5)/yr. q_reassign U(0, 0.8).
proposals.rule_modified: F-j and PW2 (and PW6's q_sg017_block): at each outage event, apply the draw q_reassign to the pending APS line's unallocated balance, and add the same event to the q_veto term for the next amendment vote.

proposals.behaviour: Staff pre-screening and agenda gating before the board sees the amendment. Programming staff can decline to bring a stand-alone amendment, folding it into the 2027-28 5YPP/Strategic Plan update instead, or telling the sponsor to come back with a ready-to-allocate package (design cost, delivery plan, crew capacity). The board never votes, so no veto is recorded.
proposals.trigger: The sponsor is the only applicant for EP17 (SFMTA) and the request is a deviation from the adopted 5YPP while EP17 is over-programmed. Staff scoring puts readiness at 5 of 31 weight, and 'the allocation is based on a qualified applicant package'.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a pre-board filter with probability q_screen. A screened request returns to the sponsor with a wait of t_screen months, or is folded into the 2027-28 5YPP cycle. This is different from a board veto (F-j), because the sponsor's signpost for PW2 can read it as 'no response' and the clock for theta_defer starts without any vote.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j mentions 'wait for the next 5YPP round (2027 autumn-2028)' as a recovery path after a veto or a deferral, and D4 has a 3-4 month precedent. Staff-level gating before any vote, with the sponsor's resubmission cost, is not modelled, so I keep the pre-screen part only.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: allocation is 'based on an application package prepared and submitted by a qualified applicant; SFCTA staff evaluates, then CAC, then the board' (line 185); 5YPP scoring weights readiness 5 (line 186); 'the next strategic plan + 5YPP starts 2027 autumn, passes 2028' (line 192). There is no document showing that staff declined an amendment, so the screening step has no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_screen (probability staff does not forward the amendment to the board in this cycle) and t_screen (months before it can be resubmitted).
proposals.range: q_screen U(0, 0.5). t_screen U(3, 18) months.
proposals.rule_modified: F-j and PW2: add a pre-board filter before the q_veto draw. If screened, no vote occurs, the sponsor resubmits after t_screen or at the next 5YPP window, and the theta_defer clock runs from submission.

proposals.behaviour: Conditional or earmarked approval (scope rider). Staff recommend the SG017 allocation with a condition: keep the controller line first, and release the APS portion only after a deliverable is shown (named intersections, pole/conduit survey done, or a signed Signal Shop crew-capacity statement). The rest of the money is held back or given as a split tranche. This is neither a plain approval nor a veto: it keeps money moving but delays the APS part.
proposals.trigger: The request text lists new APS next to controller work, while the staff memo already shows the Signal Shop crew constraint and a backlog of about 98 firewall-defect controllers. Staff want to avoid funding a scope the applicant cannot deliver, and want to avoid paying for APS before intersections are screened for pole and conduit adequacy.
proposals.effect_in_model: A PW6 request that survives q_sg017_block does not release its full APS dollars at the board date. The APS share is released after a lag t_cond. If the APS-ready list is not yet screened for 'poles and conduit satisfactory' (the only intersections eligible in the CIP scope), that share falls to zero or lapses at fiscal year end. Net effect: a_sg017 becomes the money actually usable in the year, not the face amount.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.6 PW6 and D10 q_sg017_block cover the binary outcome (scope limited to replace, or money used up by controllers). F-j covers amendment veto or deferral. Nothing models a conditional release or a held tranche, so the proposal is kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 185: awards are 'based on the application package prepared and submitted by an eligible applicant', with staff review, then CAC, then board. 01 line 181 and line 354: the Signal Shop staffing limit is 'often a limiting factor'. 01 line 447: FY25-26 $1.0M went to about 98 controllers. No document shows staff attaching conditions to an award, so the condition mechanism itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_cond (probability that staff attach a conditional release to an SG017 request that includes new APS) and t_cond (months of lag before the APS share is released). The release also needs a screening flag.
proposals.range: q_cond U(0.1, 0.6); t_cond U(3, 12) months; release requires a screened-list flag, otherwise the APS share lapses at the end of the fiscal year.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 approval step and D10 a_sg017: effective APS money = a_sg017 * (1 - q_cond * lapse_if_unscreened), delivered after t_cond.

proposals.behaviour: Redirect to the cheaper channel. Staff steer the requester away from SG017 and toward the 5YPP amendment or a different line, saying SG017 is a replacement line. They may use the 'replace only' wording in the 5YPP description to do this. The aim is to protect the limited uncommitted balance and keep the request trail clean. The same staff may later accept an SG017 request that is framed as 'replacing end-of-life APS'.
proposals.trigger: A pre-submittal contact or draft request shows new APS in the SG017 scope. The 5YPP description says only 'replace', FY26-28 uncommitted balance is $0-0.5M a year, and staff do not want the precedent of treating the CIP scope as binding.
proposals.effect_in_model: A PW6 attempt is bounced before it counts as a submitted application. The agent loses D_prep months and the request returns to IDLE, or moves to PW2 (amendment) at a cost in delay. This is different from q_sg017_block, which fires at the allocation stage. Here the loss comes earlier and costs preparation time.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 PW6 and q_sg017_block only act at the allocation decision. F-j acts on an amendment that has already been submitted. A pre-submittal screening-out is not written down anywhere.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 446: the CIP27 scope allows new APS 'where the existing conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition', but 'the 5YPP description only says replace'. 01 line 613: EP17 uncommitted balance is about $0.5M a year and 'can only change the hardware-replacement line or amend the 5YPP'. No document shows staff steering a requester away, so the behaviour is an inference.
proposals.parameter: q_screen_out (probability that staff reject or redirect a PW6 draft before submission) and the follow-on path switch (to PW2).
proposals.range: q_screen_out U(0.1, 0.5). It is raised when the uncommitted balance is below $0.3M. On a hit, the agent loses D_prep and moves to PW2.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 / D3.6 PW6 step before SUBMITTED; adds a pre-submittal gate to the task state machine.

proposals.behaviour: Priority queue by risk, not by wording. Staff rank SG017 spending by failure risk: a controller with a known security hole outranks new APS, which has no failure trigger. So the controller backlog crowds out APS year after year, even when the scope text allows both. If the controller backlog clears, the rank flips and APS money opens up.
proposals.trigger: A visible failure list exists (98 controllers with firewall defects), and fiscal pressure from the 202% 5YPP front-load. The next five-year plan 'is not expected to have this level of advance'.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes q_sg017_block a state variable that depends on the size of the controller backlog B(t), not a fixed draw per run. When B(t) is positive, q_sg017_block is near its upper end. After B(t) is cleared, q_sg017_block drops sharply. This produces a window in which PW6 works that the static parameter cannot show.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D10 q_sg017_block (U(0.2, 0.9)) names 'money used up by controller and failure-priority projects' as a cause. But it is a single static draw per run, not tied to a backlog stock or its clearing. Kept as a refinement only.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 126: $1M of hardware replacement went to about 98 controllers with firewall defects. 01 line 447: FY27-28 use is 'unknown'. 01 line 179: EP17 is committed 202% ahead of pay-as-you-go. 01 line 69: staff move money only for visible system failures (inference). The backlog stock and its clearing rate have no document support.
proposals.parameter: B0 (controller backlog count at start), r_clear (controllers cleared per year) and q_block(B) = q_lo + (q_hi - q_lo) * 1[B > 0].
proposals.rule_modified: D10 q_sg017_block, turned into a time-varying function of B(t) in PW6 approval.

proposals.behaviour: Conditional or haircut approval of the amendment. Staff recommend a smaller APS line than requested (or a time-phased line, e.g. out-years only), instead of full approval or veto/deferral.
proposals.trigger: EP17 is already over-programmed (about 202% ahead of pay-go) and the 5YPP said the next five years should not run this far ahead. Staff must find room without cutting committed lines.
proposals.effect_in_model: A third outcome for the amendment besides approve or veto/defer. Funded fraction phi of the requested line goes into the Prop L pool, so fewer intersections are funded per grant and the local-first pathway (PW2) yields less. The residual is requested again later.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j (02 D3.6/F-j) only has all-or-nothing veto with delay t_defer. It has no scaled approval, so the behaviour is not covered. The pool cap of $0-0.5M/year uncommitted headroom (D10) limits the size but does not scale the approval.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'EP17 2023 5YPP committed $27.49M vs pay-go $8.52M, about 202% ahead'. 01 s2.3: 'Strategic plan cut projects to 85-89% of priority 1'. This shows trimming is a normal SFCTA tool. No document support for staff applying it to an APS amendment.
proposals.parameter: phi_amend (continuous), plus switch amend_mode in {0 binary as now, 1 scaled}
proposals.range: phi_amend U(0.3, 1.0); when amend_mode=1, the amendment outcome is approve with funded share phi_amend with probability 1 - q_veto.
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (Prop L amendment outcome) and PW2 step 1

proposals.behaviour: Offset requirement: staff make approval of the new APS line conditional on a matching cut to another EP17 line. In practice the cut falls on the hardware-replacement line SG017, the only line with free cash.
proposals.trigger: Over-programming means any new line must be funded by taking from an existing one. Controller replacements after outages are the line staff protect.
proposals.effect_in_model: Approving the APS line lowers SG017 funds by the same amount. This raises the chance that the next controller-failure request cannot be paid from the line (q_sg017_block goes up), and it reduces what PW6 can use. The local APS gain is paid for by a higher chance of hitting the unfunded outage-repair gap.
proposals.already_in_model: No. PW6 and q_sg017_block (02 D3.6) treat SG017 as a fixed $500k per year that may be used up by controllers. They do not couple the amendment outcome to the size of SG017.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'FY26-28 about $2.80M/year, all assigned to TSP, conduit, signs, hardware replacement ($0.5M/year), visibility ($0.4M/year)'. 01 s2.3: 'controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (inferred). No document support for the offset rule itself.
proposals.parameter: f_offset (switch 0/1) and share_offset (continuous)
proposals.range: f_offset in {0,1}; share_offset U(0, 1) = fraction of the APS line that is taken out of SG017 when f_offset=1.
proposals.rule_modified: F-j approval step and PW6 q_sg017_block

proposals.behaviour: Reprogramming of the APS line after an outage. Once a dedicated APS line exists, an outage that damages many controllers lets staff and the board move unspent APS money to controller replacement, before it is allocated.
proposals.trigger: A system-wide outage (the evidence names 2022 and 2025) and a request for emergency hardware money while the APS line still holds uncommitted funds.
proposals.effect_in_model: Unallocated APS balance is reduced by a fraction at each outage event. The recovered pathway PW2 then yields fewer installs than the amount programmed, which can make a won amendment look like a failure.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-k and q_sg017_block cover controller priority only against SG017 and the director's 10% reserve. Nothing reverses money already programmed to an APS line. Check whether D3.5 has an outage event at all; I found no outage term in 02.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'outcome is visible-failure driven: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (inferred, OCT25 p.7). 01 s2.2 decision rule: $1M for about 98 controllers with firewall defects. No document support for clawback from an APS line.
proposals.parameter: q_reprogram (probability per outage event) and outage_rate (events per year)
proposals.range: q_reprogram U(0, 0.6) of unallocated balance; outage_rate U(0.1, 0.5)/year, which matches two outages in about four years.
proposals.rule_modified: New rule between F-j success and delivery (D3.4); shrinks the available APS balance

proposals.behaviour: Tranche allocation tied to readiness: staff recommend the first grant covers design only, and release construction money only after 95% design, environmental and permits are in place. This follows the SFCTA rule that funds must be committed within 12 months of allocation.
proposals.trigger: Staff worry that the Signal Shop is capacity limited, so a large construction grant risks a lapse. A design-only first tranche is the cheap hedge.
proposals.effect_in_model: Money flows in two steps with a lag t_tranche between them. A second approval is needed (a second chance for veto), and an unspent grant can lapse. Delays installs relative to a single-grant model but cuts wasted funds.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. Delivery (D3.4) and F-e/F-f have funding gaps and top-ups, and 01 s2.3 lists the 95% design and 12-month commit rules, but the 02 sections I checked have no phased release or lapse rule for Prop L grants.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'construction allocation needs 95% drawings, environmental approval, permits; must commit within 12 months of allocation (SP p.19-23)'. 01 s2.3: 'Signal Shop staffing limit is often the limiting factor (EP17-5YPP l.354-356)'. No document support for applying this to APS specifically.
proposals.parameter: f_tranche (switch 0/1), t_tranche (months), q_lapse (probability)
proposals.range: f_tranche in {0,1}; t_tranche U(6, 18) months; q_lapse U(0, 0.25) that the second tranche is not released in time.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 delivery start and F-j (adds second approval point)

proposals.behaviour: Conditional or funding-neutral approval: staff recommend approving the restored APS line only as a placeholder, a capped line, or one that must be offset. The offset could come from other SFMTA lines (TSP, visibility, pipeline), from deferring other lines' cash flow, or from a later reprogramming. The board then approves an amendment that creates the line but gives it little spendable money.
proposals.trigger: The amendment reaches staff while EP17 FY24-28 is already committed far ahead of pay-as-you-go. Staff want to avoid new over-programming, and any new line must come out of something else.
proposals.effect_in_model: A_local does not jump to U(0.5M, 2M) x APS share once the line is 'restored'. It is scaled by a cap. A funding-neutral switch also forces the money to be taken from SFMTA's own other lines, which may lower the other lines' delivery. The line can read as open while real money is near zero.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j covers only a binary veto or defer (q_veto, t_defer). PW2 and D10 A_local cover the line being open or closed, with a fixed range. There is no partial or conditional approval and no offset rule, so the proposal is kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: the EP17 5YPP commits $27.49M against $8.52M pay-as-you-go, about 202% ahead, with no APS row. FY26-28 has about $2.80M a year, all assigned. 'The next five years are not expected to be this far ahead' (EP17-5YPP p.11). 01 s2.3 also records the strategic plan cutting projects to 85-89% of priority 1. No document records a conditional approval, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: a_cap (share of the requested APS line that is actually spendable) with switch sw_neutral (0/1). a_cap ~ U(0.1, 1.0), baseline 1.0. sw_neutral = 1 draws the money from a competing SFMTA line, reducing that line's per-year amount by the same dollars.
proposals.range: a_cap U(0.1, 1.0); sw_neutral in {0, 1}
proposals.rule_modified: Multiplies A_local in D10 when dedicated_line = 1 (PW2). Adds a branch to F-j between 'approved' and 'vetoed': 'approved but capped'. Subtracts the same dollars from the batch size of the competing line.

proposals.behaviour: Outage-driven pre-emption of approved or pending APS money: when a failure (a power outage that breaks controllers) occurs, staff move uncommitted EP17 dollars or the next hardware-replacement allocation to controllers. This can also hit a restored APS line after it exists, or delay its allocation request in the queue.
proposals.trigger: A stochastic outage or system-failure event, after which the replacement need becomes visible and urgent. It can occur before or after the amendment is approved.
proposals.effect_in_model: A random shock removes a share of the A_local and a_sg017 pool in the year it happens. The allocation request for APS is pushed back or has its amount cut. APS spending and controller spending are tied to one shared pool.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 has q_sg017_block, which covers money being used on controllers before APS can use it. But it is a one-time blocking probability on the SG017 line only. It does not cover shocks that recur after a dedicated APS line exists, and it does not apply to PW2's new line. So the new line is kept as a proposal.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'outcomes are driven by visible failures: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (OCT25 p.7, marked inference). 01 s2.1: EP17 hardware replacement of $1M (FY25+FY26) went to about 98 controllers with firewall defects. The model has no outage event; a grep of 02 for outage/停电 found nothing.
proposals.parameter: lambda_outage (outage events per year) and f_preempt (share of the uncommitted EP17 year's money moved to controllers when an event occurs). Applied to A_local and a_sg017 together.
proposals.range: lambda_outage U(0.1, 0.6) per year; f_preempt U(0.2, 1.0)
proposals.rule_modified: Adds an exogenous shock event to the O3 schedule. At each event it cuts A_local and a_sg017 for the current and next fiscal year and delays any pending APS allocation request by t_defer months (reusing F-j's t_defer).

proposals.behaviour: Sequencing the line behind readiness: staff hold the APS amendment or request until SFMTA shows delivery capacity (crew available, a specified list of intersections, a design package) or until the next 5YPP window. They treat 'restore the line now' as a poor fit with the staff's own 5YPP scoring, which rewards readiness and gives no weight to the strain on the Signal Shop crew.
proposals.trigger: The amendment arrives with no ready project list, with the Signal Shop limited by staffing, and with no APS application on file. Staff's own scoring puts readiness at 5 of 31 points.
proposals.effect_in_model: A readiness test gates the amendment at the staff stage, before it reaches the board. If strain(t) is high or specified is 0, the amendment is held for t_hold months, a different delay from the board's veto or defer. It also ties approval to A2 task state, not just to the board's vote.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-j treats the board as the only gate. Strain(t) enters p_start for A2 but not the SFCTA staff's recommendation. So the proposal is kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: 'allocations are based on applications prepared and submitted by eligible applicants'; staff review, then CAC, then board (SP p.22). 5YPP scoring: readiness 5, urgency 4, equity 5, community support 5, leverage 4, safety 4 (EP17-5YPP p.12-13). 01 s2.3: 'Signal Shop staffing limits are often a limiting factor' (EP17-5YPP p.9). No document says staff have held a request for capacity reasons, so the behaviour is inferred.
proposals.parameter: sw_ready_gate (0/1) and t_hold (months). When sw_ready_gate = 1 and strain(t) > theta_strain or specified = 0, the amendment is held for t_hold months before reaching the board.
proposals.range: sw_ready_gate in {0, 1}; theta_strain U(0.3, 0.8); t_hold U(3, 18) months
proposals.rule_modified: Adds a pre-board stage in PW2 and in the PW6 fallback ('amendment') step, before F-j. The hold time adds to the total delay; if t_hold runs past the 2027-autumn 5YPP window, the amendment merges into that cycle.

proposals.behaviour: Re-scoping instead of rejecting: staff steer the request into an existing eligible line, such as folding APS into the EP18 Safer and Complete Streets corridor projects or into SG017 'replace' scope, and write 'APS included in the signal upgrade' into the allocation conditions. The dedicated line is not restored; the money flows through other lines.
proposals.trigger: The board does not want a new line in an over-programmed EP, but an advocacy or ADA-liability concern keeps the request alive. Staff want to show a response without adding a commitment.
proposals.effect_in_model: Instead of the binary 'line opens / line stays closed', a third outcome: APS is tied to corridor or replacement projects, so only C-type intersections already in those projects get APS. Coverage depends on the parent projects' delay and does not rise on its own.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW4 allocates sources by intersection (bundled with a parent project) and PW6 uses SG017 for replacement. But both are SFMTA choices. The SFCTA staff steering a request into them as a substitute for the amendment is not a model rule. So only the staff-side steering switch is proposed.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: EP18 funds 'new, maintained, upgraded signals (including pedestrian)'; C35 $5.35M for 17 intersections including APS; C66 and C67 new signals mostly with PCS+APS (OCT25 p.3, p.26-27). 01 s2.1: 'all new signals and major signal upgrades include APS; installing with existing work is cheapest' (MDC23 p.6, MDC26 p.7). No document shows staff steering a line request this way.
proposals.parameter: q_redirect: the probability that, on an amendment request, staff steer it into PW4/PW6 routes instead of recommending the line. Draws f_bundle (share of the request that goes to the bundled route).
proposals.range: q_redirect U(0, 0.6); f_bundle U(0.2, 0.8)
proposals.rule_modified: Adds a branch before F-j. With probability q_redirect the amendment is replaced by a PW6 request (SG017 scope extension) or a PW4 bundled request; A_local stays at the current-state range U(0, 0.57M) and does not move to the dedicated-line range.

proposals.behaviour: Conditional or pilot-capped approval. Staff recommends approving SG017 but with a condition: controllers and failure-driven replacements are funded first, and any new-APS sites are capped (a few named sites) or released only after a progress report-back. The result is neither a clean approve nor a block. APS gets a small share of the money, released late.
proposals.trigger: The SG017 request lists new APS next to controller replacement. Staff sees ambiguity between the CIP scope ('may include new APS') and the 5YPP line text ('replace'). Staff also sees a history of controller-only allocations. Staff wants to avoid setting a precedent but also avoid an outright denial.
proposals.effect_in_model: PW6 now ends in three states: full pass, partial pass with a delay, or block. The cap lowers the APS money in the grant. The release gate adds a delay before APS sites enter the in-house queue. Reaching HSIP or the amendment falls back later, or not at all.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 §D3.6 PW6 and §D10 `q_sg017_block` / `a_sg017` give a binary block (Pr 0.2-0.9) and an APS share (0-250k). There is no partial approval, no conditions, and no release lag. The cap is only a static amount, not a staff decision with a gate and a delay.
proposals.evidence: No document support for conditional approval itself. Adjacent support: 01 §2.3 line 185 (grants follow staff review, then CAC, then board; staff is a real screening layer) and line 179 (EP17 5YPP has no APS line). The pilot idea is inferred from that setup.
proposals.parameter: `p_cond` (probability that a non-blocked SG017 grant is conditional) and `t_release` (months before conditioned APS funds can be spent). Optional `n_cap` caps sites per grant.
proposals.range: `p_cond` U(0.2, 0.7); `t_release` U(3, 12) months; `n_cap` in {2, 4, 8} sites.
proposals.rule_modified: §D3.6 PW6 and `a_sg017`. A conditioned grant sets `a_sg017` = min(`a_sg017`, `n_cap` x `u0`) and delays queue entry by `t_release`.

proposals.behaviour: Pre-submission steering. During informal pre-review, staff tells SFMTA to keep APS out of the SG017 request and use a proper 5YPP amendment or the next 5YPP instead. The reason given is scope purity and audit risk. SFMTA complies before any formal vote. The request arrives clean, and no denial is recorded.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA is drafting the request. Staff knows the 5YPP line says 'replace'. Staff prefers that money for the site-specific programming it already scored in the 5YPP.
proposals.effect_in_model: The `q_sg017_block` event moves from the grant step to an earlier signal. APS is removed from the request at drafting time. The A2 agent loses a try at PW6 and goes straight to PW2 (amendment), starting the F-j timeline earlier or later. Block events then stop appearing in the event stream. That changes how path-reach is counted.
proposals.already_in_model: No. PW6 and F-j only react after a request or an amendment is formally put to the board. No pre-request deflection by SFCTA is modelled. (Buck-passing is modelled only for A2 via `p_deflect`, §D3.1 / §D3.2.)
proposals.evidence: No direct document support. Related: 01 §2.3 line 185 says SFCTA acts only on applications 'prepared and submitted by the applicant'. 01 line 83 describes the 'no money / no application' loop, in which each side points to the other.
proposals.parameter: `p_steer`: probability that staff signals before submission and A2 drops APS from the SG017 request. Optional `t_steer`, the extra months before A2 starts the amendment route.
proposals.range: `p_steer` U(0.1, 0.6); `t_steer` U(0, 4) months.
proposals.rule_modified: §D3.6 PW6 entry. With probability `p_steer`, PW6 is skipped and the agent enters PW2 after `t_steer` months. This replaces the draw of `q_sg017_block` for that run.

proposals.behaviour: Cash-flow timing. Prop L EP17 is heavily over-programmed in the current 5YPP. Staff can approve the allocation but spread reimbursements across later fiscal years, or place it in the lowest-priority year. APS-related drawdowns slip behind controller work.
proposals.trigger: Programmed amounts run ahead of pay-as-you-go revenue. Staff manages the sales-tax cash balance. The SG017 request arrives in a year with a tight cash profile.
proposals.effect_in_model: The money exists on paper but is available later. This shortens the usable window of FY27/FY28 $500k and pushes installs from year 1 to year 2 or 3. It also lowers the chance that APS installs fit before the next 5YPP resets priorities in 2027-28.
proposals.already_in_model: No. §D10 treats SG017 as FY27/FY28 $500k each, available when granted. F-j/`t_defer` delay only the amendment vote. Nothing models the fiscal-year placement of reimbursements.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 179: the EP17 5YPP programs $27.49M against $8.52M pay-as-you-go, about 202% over-programmed. Line 180: 'the next five years are not expected to be over-programmed to this degree.' These support the cash pressure but not the staff tactic of spreading cash.
proposals.parameter: `t_cash`: months by which cash availability for an SG017 grant is pushed back, applied to the APS share only. Optional `s_cash`, the share of the grant moved to the later fiscal year.
proposals.range: `t_cash` U(0, 18) months; `s_cash` U(0, 0.6).
proposals.rule_modified: §D3.6 PW6 and §D3.4 delivery start. The earliest spend date for SG017 APS money is the grant date plus `t_cash`.

proposals.behaviour: Site-list and readiness gate. Staff asks for a named list of APS sites with a documented pole and conduit adequacy check before any APS line is allocated from SG017. Staff applies the 5YPP readiness criterion (weight 5), so unsurveyed sites are not ready and are dropped from the grant.
proposals.trigger: The CIP scope allows new APS only 'where poles and conduit are adequate'. Staff cannot confirm that condition from the request. Staff does not want to fund unidentified work with a replace-only line.
proposals.effect_in_model: APS in SG017 depends on a survey step. Sites not yet surveyed cannot take the money, and the survey itself costs Signal Shop time (strain). The number of eligible C-type sites at grant time falls to the surveyed subset. This also links PW6 to M-B (staff capacity).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 restricts SG017 to C-class intersections with usable poles and conduit, and §D3.1 / `c_full` carry pole and conduit needs as drawn facts. The model does not require a documented survey before funding, and does not charge survey time or labour.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 186 (5YPP scoring: readiness weighted 5). Line 185 (grant based on a submitted application package). 01 §2.1 / line 181 on Signal Shop staffing as a limiting factor. The explicit survey requirement as a staff demand has no document support.
proposals.parameter: `f_surveyed`: share of C-type backlog sites with a documented pole/conduit check at grant time. `t_survey`: months of crew effort to extend the check.
proposals.range: `f_surveyed` U(0.1, 0.7) at start; `t_survey` U(2, 9) months per batch.
proposals.rule_modified: §D3.6 PW6 eligibility filter. The set eligible for the SG017 APS share = C-type sites x `f_surveyed`. Unsurveyed sites need a survey task that consumes `K_crew` before they qualify.

proposals.behaviour: Conditional or tranched approval. Staff do not simply approve or block the APS part of the SG017 request. They recommend the allocation with a special condition: APS funds are released only after SFMTA delivers a site-level list showing poles and conduit are satisfactory, or only after the controller work in the same allocation is done. APS money is therefore available with a lag, and lapses back to the controller line if the survey is not delivered.
proposals.trigger: The request text copies the CIP scope ("install new APS where existing conduits and poles are satisfactory") but names no intersections. Staff want a defensible record because past allocations all went to controllers and the 5YPP description says only "replace".
proposals.effect_in_model: PW6 money becomes usable after a lag t_cond. If SFMTA cannot produce the survey before the condition deadline, the APS part reverts to the controller line. Signal Shop strain (M-B) lengthens the survey, so staff caution and SFMTA capacity interact. This is a third outcome between the existing 'APS allowed' and 'blocked'.
proposals.already_in_model: Only partly. 02 D10 has q_sg017_block (binary: scope limited to replace, or money used up) and a_sg017 (amount cap). Neither has a release lag, a deliverable condition, or a lapse back to controllers. The nearest rule is F-j, which covers 5YPP amendments only, not conditions on an allocation.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 185: grants are "based on the application package the eligible applicant prepares and submits"; 5YPP scoring puts readiness at 5 (line 186). 01 line 446: the CIP scope allows APS only where "conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition", with no site list. 01 line 181: Signal Shop staffing is "often the limiting factor" (a source of survey delay). No direct document shows SFCTA attaching a special condition to an SG017 allocation.
proposals.parameter: t_cond (months) with q_lapse. Staff add a condition with probability q_cond. Release is delayed t_cond. If SFMTA's survey time (which rises with strain) exceeds t_cond_deadline, the APS share lapses to controllers with probability q_lapse.
proposals.range: q_cond U(0.2, 0.8); t_cond U(3, 12) months; t_cond_deadline U(6, 18) months; q_lapse U(0.3, 1.0). All inferred.
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 (D3.6) and the a_sg017 availability rule (D10). Adds a delay and a lapse step before the 'SG017 APS available' event.

proposals.behaviour: Co-location requirement. Staff favor APS only at intersections where a controller or hardware replacement is already in the same allocation. The APS is treated as an add-on to a funded hardware job rather than a stand-alone new install. Sites eligible for SG017 APS then shrink to the overlap of the APS pending list and the controller replacement list.
proposals.trigger: Limited funds (FY27 and FY28 at $500k each) and the pending controller replacement list. The 5YPP scores readiness, leverage and asset need, and a co-located job is more ready and cheaper per site.
proposals.effect_in_model: The set of PW6-eligible C intersections is cut to an overlap fraction. If the overlap is small, SG017 funds go unused for APS even when q_sg017_block does not fire. It also shifts what staff regard as 'in scope'.
proposals.already_in_model: No. PW6 restricts sites only by pole and conduit condition ("existing poles and conduits usable"). D10 has no co-location or overlap term.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 447: FY25–26 SG017 money of $1,000,000 replaced about 98 signal controllers with a firewall vulnerability (OCT25 p.7). 01 line 126: a 2023 PIF made APS replacement an eligible use. 01 line 186: readiness and leverage are the largest scoring items. No document shows staff requiring co-location; this is an inference from how hardware lines are scored.
proposals.parameter: s_coloc (switch, 0 or 1) and rho_overlap (the fraction of otherwise-eligible APS sites that are also on the hardware replacement list).
proposals.range: s_coloc in {0, 1}, prior P(1) = 0.4; rho_overlap U(0.05, 0.5), inferred.
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 eligibility filter (D3.6) and the SG017 APS site list in the countdown-lpi-pending76 input (D2). Applied before the amount cap a_sg017.

proposals.behaviour: Event-driven reprogramming. Staff can move SG017 money to controllers or other failure-driven items mid-cycle, after the APS share has been approved or planned. The reprogramming happens when a visible failure occurs, such as a citywide outage or a cybersecurity finding on controllers.
proposals.trigger: A visible system failure (power outage, firewall vulnerability in controllers). The two such events already seen (2022 and 2025) each ended with SG017 money going to controllers.
proposals.effect_in_model: The APS share of SG017 becomes a stock that can be taken back at random times. This produces repeated losses of APS money and a time-varying chance of recovering it, not a single draw at the start.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D10 q_sg017_block includes "money used up by controller or other failure priority projects", but as one static probability drawn per run. 02 F-k covers the Director's 10% and the SG000 reserve, not SFCTA reprogramming of SG017. There is no event process, no reprogramming of an approved share, and no link to outage events.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 line 176: "outcomes are driven by visible faults: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages" (OCT25 p.7), marked as inference. 01 line 447 gives the FY25–26 controller allocation. No document shows reprogramming of an already-approved APS share.
proposals.parameter: lambda_fault (events per year) and f_take (the fraction of the unspent APS share taken back by each event). This replaces the one-off draw of q_sg017_block with a process.
proposals.range: lambda_fault U(0.1, 0.6) per year; f_take U(0.3, 1.0); both inferred from two events in four years.
proposals.rule_modified: q_sg017_block and a_sg017 in D10, plus a new exogenous event in the event table (O3). Interacts with F-k.

proposals.behaviour: Informal pre-application signal. Before SFMTA drafts the SG017 request, staff indicate whether adding APS will be treated as in scope. A negative or noncommittal signal causes SFMTA not to include APS at all. The request is never filed, so no rejection is recorded and the effect cannot be seen from outside.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA starts preparing the allocation request, and the history shows that allocations go to controllers. Staff know the 5YPP description says only "replace".
proposals.effect_in_model: The SG017 task's start probability p_start for the APS component moves up or down according to the staff signal. A negative signal looks like the existing 'not started' state, not like REJECTED. In the model, the blocking would then appear as the applicant's choice, which hides the funder's role.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.1 p_start has terms for owner, specified, oversight, pressure, enforce and strain. There is no funder-signal term. q_sg017_block acts after submission (at allocation), not before.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 185: grants follow "applications the eligible applicant prepares and submits", so funder influence before submission is invisible in records. 01 line 83: "saying no money" and "not having applied" form a loop, where no application means no money. 01 line 189: no CAC question on APS absence was seen (absence of record). No document shows a pre-application signal on SG017; this is an assumption.
proposals.parameter: beta_sig * sig_sfcta, where sig_sfcta in {-1, 0, +1} is drawn once per cycle and added to the p_start logit for the SG017 task. Probabilities of -1, 0, +1 set by q_neg, q_neu, q_pos.
proposals.range: beta_sig U(0, 2) in logit units; (q_neg, q_neu, q_pos) Dirichlet with mean (0.4, 0.4, 0.2). Inferred.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start logistic, applied to the PW6 task only; adds a funder signal that precedes the allocation request.

proposals.behaviour: Conditional approval with a ring-fenced APS sub-scope. Staff recommend the SG017 allocation but split the line (up to a share of the $500k for new APS at sites with adequate poles and conduit, remainder for controllers) and add a reporting or reversion condition. This is a third outcome between full pass and 'limit to replace'.
proposals.trigger: The request text lists APS in scope while allocation history shows only controllers. Staff want to avoid controller-failure risk and also avoid a visible 'APS never funded' gap if CAC, a board member or advocates ask.
proposals.effect_in_model: PW6's binary outcome (APS in scope or blocked) becomes a split: a fixed share of the SG017 line is reserved for APS, with a reversion clause (unspent APS money returns to controllers after N months). Changes how much money reaches the APS task state machine, and when.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 and q_sg017_block (02 line 245, D10 line 375) treat the grant as binary with a_sg017 as the usable amount. No staff-shaped condition, reversion clause, or coupling to outstanding controller risk. Keep because the split outcome is absent.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 3 lines 446-447: CIP scope allows new APS where conduit and poles are fine, but FY24 and FY25-26 grants went to cabinets, detectors, RRFB and ~98 controllers. 01 section 2.3 line 185: grants are based on the application package, with staff review first. No document shows a conditional grant, so the mechanism itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_cond_split (switch) with a_aps_ring and t_revert
proposals.range: a_aps_ring U(0, 0.5) of the SG017 line; t_revert U(6, 24) months
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 branch and D10 q_sg017_block / a_sg017 (02 lines 245, 375): the grant draw gets a third outcome, 'split with ring-fence', and the ring-fenced amount replaces a_sg017 for that year; reversion adds an expiry to the APS money.

proposals.behaviour: Pilot-as-precedent. Staff or the sponsor frame the first APS use of SG017 as a small pilot to be reported back before the next 5YPP. A delivered pilot lowers the cost of later requests; a late or over-budget one raises the bar.
proposals.trigger: Staff want to say yes with limited exposure, and the next 5YPP window (2027 autumn to 2028) is near. The sponsor wants a 'delivered' record before that round.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a per-channel precedent state. A delivered SG017 APS batch lowers later q_sg017_block and q_veto; a late or over-budget batch (F-e, F-f, strain) raises them.
proposals.already_in_model: No. The model has no feedback from delivery back to approval probabilities. D4 Lincoln Way is used only as a timing prior (F-j), not as a precedent effect.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3 lines 177 and 179-180: D4 amendment passed in 3-4 months; the 5YPP says the next five years will not be as far ahead. Line 186 scoring gives readiness 5. The feedback effect has no document support.
proposals.parameter: delta_prec (approval probability reduction after a delivered batch) and penalty_late (increase after a late batch)
proposals.range: delta_prec U(0, 0.3); penalty_late U(0, 0.2)
proposals.rule_modified: D10 q_sg017_block and q_veto, drawn at each later SG017 grant or amendment decision; needs a per-channel precedent counter.

proposals.behaviour: Steering to the 5YPP window. Staff approve a controller-only allocation now and signal that APS belongs in the 2027-28 5YPP update, so the sponsor adds an APS line there instead of relying on the SG017 scope text.
proposals.trigger: The APS part of the request is thin on sites and cost, controller risk is the visible priority, and the strategic plan and 5YPP cycle is 12-18 months away. Redirecting is the lowest-friction option.
proposals.effect_in_model: A soft deferral before any rejection: the SG017-APS attempt fails with an effective delay to the 2028 5YPP adoption, and the fallback becomes a new APS line in the 5YPP scored on readiness, urgency, equity and community support, not a mid-cycle amendment.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j has t_defer or 'wait for the next 5YPP' only after a board veto (02 line 229), and PW6 falls to an amendment (line 245). Staff-initiated redirect before any rejection, with the 5YPP as default fallback, is not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3 line 192: next strategic plan and 5YPP start autumn 2027, adopted 2028. Line 189: no CAC memo reviewed asks about the APS gap (inferred absence), so little pressure to act sooner. 01 line 69: the Prop L window is the next 5YPP window.
proposals.parameter: p_stage_5ypp, probability staff redirect an SG017-APS request to the next 5YPP
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6); t_wait fixed at months to the 2028 adoption date
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 failure branch and F-j fallback choice (02 lines 229, 245): with probability p_stage_5ypp the fallback is 'PW2 at the 5YPP date' instead of 'amendment'.

proposals.behaviour: Slack reallocation inside EP17. Staff or the board find APS money by shifting funds between EP17 lines (for example from a line that cannot spend because of Signal Shop capacity) through a light reprogramming, instead of SG017 or a full amendment.
proposals.trigger: An EP17 line is underspending under staffing strain while APS demand is visible; moving money within the same category is lighter than an amendment.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a local money source not tied to SG017's $500k per year: EP17 slack that grows with strain(t), capped by line sizes (FY26-28 about $2.8M a year across lines).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 line 64 covers $0-0.5M a year of uncommitted headroom and F-k covers the director reserve. Strain-linked reprogramming within EP17 is not modelled; borderline, since it could be read as an amendment already.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3 lines 179 and 181: EP17 is ahead of pay-as-you-go with fixed lines, and Signal Shop staffing is often the limiting factor. 01 line 613: headroom can change only via the hardware row or a 5YPP amendment. No document support for reprogramming itself.
proposals.parameter: k_slack, the share of strain-driven underspend in other EP17 lines available for APS: a_slack(t) = k_slack * strain(t) * other-line total
proposals.range: k_slack U(0, 0.1)
proposals.rule_modified: Local money availability in D10 (a_sg017 and the uncommitted headroom row, 02 lines 64, 375); adds one source to the local budget in PW2 / PW6.

proposals.behaviour: Lead-time-gated nudging. With the HSIP C13 deadline a week away, MOD/MDC staff ask SFMTA to fold the SG142 APS scope into the SG015 12-inch-head application (a SI02-carrier BCR bundle), instead of leaving SG142 as an APS-only line. The nudge only works if it arrives before the applicant's package is frozen. A request sent inside the remaining prep time turns into a commitment for the next window (C14) and does nothing for this one.
proposals.trigger: Window deadline minus the date the advocacy request is delivered, measured against the applicant's remaining prep time (D_prep plus (m-1)*delta_split). Fires when the window is open and APS-only status is known.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure aimed at a specific window is split by lead time. If lead >= remaining prep time, it adds beta_pr * pressure to p_start and may raise the chance the APS rides in the SG015 bundle (PW1 start). If lead < remaining prep time, it adds nothing to this window and is stored as a carry-over bump to the next window's p_start (the first-window version is hard-coded in PW1).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. pressure(t) enters p_start (02 D3.1) and PW1 is a fixed starting scenario (02 D3.6). Neither makes the effect of pressure depend on how long before the deadline it lands. No rule drops a late request or moves it to the next window, so this part is new.
proposals.evidence: No document support for lead-time effects. Related facts: 01 section 2.7 says the MDC is advisory only, with about one letter or resolution a year and none for APS. 01 section 3 (line 420) says SG142 as written is ineligible in C13 and only a carrier-based BCR application could qualify. 01 line 421 says C13 approval is expected 2027-03/04.
proposals.parameter: lead_min_months: minimum lead before the deadline for a nudge to count in this window.
proposals.range: U(0, 3) months; 0 reproduces the current model. Carry-over bump to the next window: gamma_carry in [0, 1].
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start (the pressure(t) term) and D3.6 PW1 start. Adds a lead check and a carry-over to the next window.

proposals.behaviour: Spending scarce advisory attention on curb ramps instead of APS. The office has capacity for roughly one letter or resolution a year. It sends that letter where a federal transition-plan obligation exists (curb ramps) and not where none exists (APS). So even an APS-friendly staff member produces zero APS pressure in most years.
proposals.trigger: A curb-ramp funding decision in the same year as the APS window. The two compete for one yearly slot. Ramp items are more likely to win because they carry a federal time-table duty.
proposals.effect_in_model: Advocacy pressure events for APS are drawn from a yearly attention budget shared with ramps. With probability a_ramp the slot goes to ramps and the APS pressure event is dropped that year (lambda_press multiplied by 1 - a_ramp). The 'quiet' state F-m would then be an outcome of competing demands as well as random silence.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-m generates silence at random (lambda_quiet, t_quiet, 02 D3.5) but has no cause tied to competing agenda items. C2 produces pressure at an unknown rate with no budget (02 O2 line 61).
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7: 'both letters (2025-04, 2026-04-16) went to curb ramps, no APS letter' (line 279). Ramps have a time-table duty under 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) and APS has none (line 284). The 2026-07-17 APS agenda item drew no public comment (line 287).
proposals.parameter: a_ramp: probability that the yearly attention slot goes to ramps.
proposals.range: U(0.5, 1.0), with a 0 control. Alternative: attention slots per year n_slots in {1, 2}.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure events and D3.5 F-m. lambda_press is scaled by (1 - a_ramp) in years with a competing ramp item.

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS from 'cost' to 'compliance exposure' before any lawsuit is filed. A staff memo or hearing item cites the New York federal court order (as the office's deputy director did) and ties APS to the ADA transition plan and to the safety evidence behind the HSIP application. The aim is to shift the agency's answer from 'no money' to 'what is the cheapest eligible vehicle'.
proposals.trigger: The agency's first answer is a cost or no-funds deflection, and a hearing or memo window exists. This is more likely when an application deadline is near.
proposals.effect_in_model: A reframe event lowers p_deflect for the next k months and raises the weight on the 'specified' term in p_start. It carries no lawsuit escalation, so it sits below D1's escalation tiers and does not touch enforce(t).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. p_deflect, enforce(t) and the D1 tiers (02 D3.1, D3.2, D3.6 PW3) cover deflection and litigation escalation. There is no cheap, non-adversarial reframing step that lowers deflection by itself. Drop this one if the team judges enforce(t) to cover it.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7: the deputy director explained NYC's speed by its court order and asked DPW and MTA to coordinate (line 282). A staff member proposed follow-up and a later support-letter recommendation (line 283), and no follow-up was observed. The deflection responses ('no money', 'expensive') are at line 131. Reframing as a distinct tactic has no direct support.
proposals.parameter: delta_reframe: multiplicative cut in p_deflect after a reframe event.
proposals.range: U(0, 0.4) cut, lasting t_reframe U(3, 12) months. Event rate: lambda_reframe U(0, 1) per year.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (p_deflect) and the D3.6 PW3 signal chain. Adds a non-escalating event.

proposals.behaviour: Proxy ownership: MOD/MDC staff step into the vacated informal-owner role by asking the transportation agency's leadership to name an acting owner or a single intake contact for APS requests, and by keeping a running list of open requests to feed that person.
proposals.trigger: F-h fires (owner leaves, post vacant) while the staff member sees that no one is acting on the request list. Stronger when the freeze (F-i) is also on, because the vacancy is expected to be long.
proposals.effect_in_model: During the vacancy the `owner` tier is not fully dropped. With probability p_proxy it is restored one tier (and `specified` may rise) after a lag. This raises p_start and lowers q_drop for PREPARING tasks. Effect size is capped, because the proxy is not a funded engineer.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-h (02 D3.5) drops `owner` one tier and restores it only when the post is refilled (t_vac). PW3 (D3.6) sets `owner`, `specified`, `oversight` upward, but only as a chosen policy pathway, not as a reaction by an actor to a vacancy. A reactive substitute during the vacancy is not written. Kept as a narrow proposal.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: MDC/ODA have advisory power only; ODA staff proposed to 'follow up with MTA and DPW and then suggest support letters' (MDC26t), and no follow-up was observed. That shows the intent exists and the follow-through is uncertain. No document shows a proxy owner actually being named. Mostly no document support for the behaviour itself.
proposals.parameter: p_proxy_owner (probability that a proxy restores owner by one tier during a vacancy), U(0, 0.4); lag t_proxy U(1, 6) months. Both inferred.
proposals.range: p_proxy_owner U(0, 0.4); t_proxy U(1, 6) months; at 0 the model equals the current F-h.
proposals.rule_modified: F-h recovery path in D3.5, and the owner term in p_start (D3.1).

proposals.behaviour: Reframing and riding: the staff member steers the request away from 'APS as a standalone funding ask' toward the curb-ramp / ADA transition-plan channel, where MDC letters already exist and a federal timetable obligation exists. The aim is to add APS to the scope of ramp funding or ramp letters.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy means no engineer will write a standalone application, so the only workable route is a channel that already has a funded owner (the public works department's ramp program). Triggered when F-h is active and pressure on the standalone APS channel has failed (high p_deflect).
proposals.effect_in_model: A share of pressure events is routed to the ramp channel. For C-type intersections with a ramp project, a rider lets APS be added as scope (a cost add-on handled by `q_ramp`). In the state machine, the deflection probability for that routed pressure falls, and it does not depend on the vacant post.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW4 (D3.6) bundles APS into parent projects chosen by intersection, and D3.3 has a `q_ramp` cost add-on. But neither models an advocate or staff actor actively re-labelling the request to move it onto the ramp channel. The effect on `p_deflect` is not written. Kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: both MDC support letters (2025-04, 2026-04-16) were about curb ramps and none for APS; ramps have a federal transition-plan timetable (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)) and APS does not (MDC26 p.10); ODA staff said the ramp budget 'will grow a lot'. Document support for the channel difference. No document support for staff actually re-framing APS as a ramp rider.
proposals.parameter: sw_ramp_rider (0/1) plus p_reframe, the share of pressure events routed to the ramp channel; and delta_deflect, the reduction in p_deflect for routed pressure.
proposals.range: p_reframe U(0, 0.5); delta_deflect U(0, 0.5) multiplicative on p_deflect; default sw_ramp_rider = 0.
proposals.rule_modified: Pressure event routing and p_deflect in D3.1; PW4 route list (D3.6).

proposals.behaviour: Window-timed pressure: the staff member does not spread letters or hearings evenly. They hold them back and release them just before a known decision window (the Prop L five-year program update, the next HSIP call, a budget hearing), and skip low-value moments during the vacancy.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus freeze make immediate pressure useless (the task cannot start), so the staff member waits for a window where a decision-maker can act. Known windows exist in the model's event table.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure arrives in pulses concentrated in the w_sync months before each window, with the same total per year. The pressure term in p_start is then high exactly when a window is open, and weak when it is not.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-m (D3.5) interrupts advocacy at a yearly rate and restores the old rate; C2 (O2) produces pressure events at an unknown but unsynchronised rate. Timing relative to windows is not in 02.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: MDC has 'about one influence opportunity per year' and the rule for when it activates is 'unknown' (inferred); ODA staff said they would come back to the support-letter later (2026-07), and nothing was seen afterwards. The 5YPP and HSIP window dates are in 02 D3.6 (for example 2027 autumn to 2028 for the 5YPP, 2028-07 for C14). No document shows deliberate timing.
proposals.parameter: press_sync: share of yearly pressure events released inside w_sync months before a window (0 = uniform as now).
proposals.range: press_sync U(0, 0.8); w_sync U(2, 6) months.
proposals.rule_modified: Generation of pressure(t) events (C2, O2/D3.2) and its use in p_start.

proposals.behaviour: Freeze exemption request: the staff member asks that the vacant post be classed as essential (ADA compliance, a legal exposure) so it can be filled despite the freeze, or that the work be moved to a contractor or another unit.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus a hiring freeze that covers 'non-essential' hiring, at a point when staff can argue the post is mandated or that legal risk is rising (for example a court order elsewhere that ODA already cited).
proposals.effect_in_model: With probability q_exempt per quarter the vacancy ends early or, alternatively, K_crew / strain are relieved by temporary outsourcing. Shortens effective t_vac and lowers strain_end for this post only.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-h has t_vac (3 to 18 months) and F-i has strain_end and says 'or move to outsourcing (same as F-e)'. But F-e outsourcing is only used after a PIF denial; there is no exemption lever driven by an outside actor, and t_vac is not linked to the freeze. Kept as an exemption switch on t_vac.
proposals.evidence: 01 §5 parameters (line 549 and 584): the freeze covered 'non-essential' hiring (2024-10) and was later changed to phased hiring in 2025 Q1; the 9145 eligible list had 41 people, so posts can be filled once allowed. This supports that exemptions are conceptually possible. No document shows an exemption request for an APS post.
proposals.parameter: q_exempt: per-quarter probability that the vacancy is exempted from the freeze while it lasts.
proposals.range: q_exempt U(0, 0.15) per quarter; effect: sets the remaining t_vac to U(2, 6) months.
proposals.rule_modified: F-h t_vac and F-i strain_end in D3.5.

proposals.behaviour: Last-minute formal letter to the application owner: the MDC support staff draft and push an MDC support letter or resolution that explicitly names the SG142 + SG015 bundle (needs a carrier), timed to arrive before the HSIP C13 deadline. Model has MDC only as an advocacy channel that adds generic pressure; nothing ties pressure to the deadline or to a specific bundling request.
proposals.trigger: Within a short lead time (<= ~2 months) before an HSIP window closes AND the capital plan shows an ineligible APS-only line next to a carrier line in the same cycle (SG142 / SG015).
proposals.effect_in_model: In the PREPARING state for the HSIP field, raises the probability that the task chooses the bundled (carrier + APS) application instead of the APS-only line, and shortens D_prep slightly (the owner gets a ready framing). Without this the model cannot represent a cheap, deadline-timed nudge that works through form, not through generic pressure.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: C2 advocates incl. MDC as a pressure source (02 O2 line 61), and pressure(t) enters p_start (D3.1). Not captured: targeted, deadline-timed pressure that changes the packaging choice rather than the start probability. Kept because pressure(t) cannot do this.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: MDC tools are advisory only (resolutions, hearings, support letters); 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 letters exist but only for curb ramps; ODA staff said in 2026-07 they would return with a support-letter recommendation, none seen by 2026-09-18 (01 lines 279, 283, 309). 01 s2.7.1 line 311 says activation rule is unknown and to test zero and non-zero. Whether such a letter changes packaging: no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_mdc_letter in {0,1} and q_letter_bundle in U(0, 0.3) (added probability that a pending HSIP-window PREPARING task picks the carrier-bundled variant, applied once when the letter fires); letter fires with prob p_letter U(0, 0.5) per window.
proposals.range: p_letter U(0,0.5); q_letter_bundle U(0,0.3); default sw=0 (matches observed zero APS letters)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING branch (packaging choice) and D3.3 packing algorithm candidate step; MDC activation rule listed as unknown in 01 s2.7.1

proposals.behaviour: Cross-agency carrier brokerage: MOD/MDC staff broker a call between the signal shop and the SG015 owner to add the APS items to the SG015 visibility package, including corridors beyond the five named ones, instead of waiting for SFMTA to design it. Informal side deal that widens the pool of intersections that qualify for PW1.
proposals.trigger: SG015 is planned in the same cycle and PW1 coverage is tiny (about 1 intersection); an outside actor that has no packing authority notices the coverage gap.
proposals.effect_in_model: Enlarges the PW1 candidate set (corridor restriction in D3.3 step 1) by a share of other C-type intersections; leaves BCR, cost and cap rules unchanged. Moves the C14 re-pack forward into C13.
proposals.already_in_model: PW1 widens the candidate set only after C13 fails (move to C14, D3.6). Nothing lets an external actor widen it inside C13. Kept for that reason.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 439-442: SG015 and SG142 are listed side by side in the same cycle with the same funding source; line 421 notes SG142 as written is not eligible and only a carrier-based BCR application could qualify. Role of MOD as broker: no document support (01 s2.7 gives MOD only list-provision and advice roles, lines 279-283).
proposals.parameter: x_broker U(0, 1): fraction of non-SG015 C-type backlog intersections added to the C13 candidate set; fires with probability p_broker U(0, 0.3) per window before the deadline
proposals.range: x_broker U(0,1) conditional on fire; p_broker U(0,0.3)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 packing algorithm step 1 (candidate set), PW1 start

proposals.behaviour: Reframing the request into a funded category: MDC staff steer the ask away from 'APS' towards 'accessible pedestrian infrastructure / PROWAG compliance' so it can sit in the curb-ramp (ADA transition) pipeline, which has a legal schedule and a funding line, and APS items ride along with ramps. The model treats ramps only as a conditional add-on cost (q_ramp), never as a funding route.
proposals.trigger: APS-only is ineligible for HSIP and curb ramps are the only accessibility item with a federal schedule duty and an MDC-tracked budget; ODA flagged the PROWAG update and a coming ramp-budget increase.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a route in which a share of APS intersections is attached to ramp-program work (DPW/SFMTA coordination) and is funded on that line, bypassing both HSIP and local APS lines; reduces requested HSIP scope and local top-up need but adds a delay term from DPW coordination.
proposals.already_in_model: No. Fs / bundled-with-parent (D3.3 table row) covers parent projects and PW4 covers 'merged' sources, but no ramp-program route and no reframing mechanism. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 281 (MOD co-funded and ranked DPW curb ramps via the ADA transition plan), line 284 (ramp federal schedule duty exists; no APS equivalent), line 282 (ODA cited ramp budget rising, asked DPW and MTA to coordinate), line 308 (PROWAG listed). That reframing would move APS money: no document support.
proposals.parameter: r_ramp U(0, 0.4): share of APS backlog intersections that become eligible to ride on the ramp program; delay t_ramp U(6, 36) months
proposals.range: r_ramp U(0,0.4); t_ramp U(6,36); on/off switch sw_ramp_route
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 / PW4 funding-source assignment; new row in the routing step

proposals.behaviour: Credible-deadline escalation: staff use the C13 deadline and the Caltrans advisory committee's statement that HSIP does not fund APS-only projects, plus a peer city's disability-commission letter, as a leverage point to ask the owner to pre-commit in writing (named lead, date for bundle decision). If the owner declines, the staff move to the next-window plan instead of repeating pressure.
proposals.trigger: A window close within weeks, with the known eligibility rule already stated publicly by the funder.
proposals.effect_in_model: A one-time commitment event that raises owner/specified for one window (not permanently) and creates a signpost: if no commitment by the deadline, the PW3 accountability track starts earlier and with higher stakes. Model has PW3 triggered only after theta_idle months of no application.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: PW3 'accountability first' and its theta_idle trigger (D3.6). Not captured: a deadline-anchored one-shot with a window-scoped boost. Weak-to-medium proposal; keep only if the team wants a window-scoped version.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 207: the advisory committee told a peer city's disability commission 'HSIP does not fund APS-only projects' and 'will study again'; line 311: no APS action seen from MDC in 2024-26. Window-scoped commitment effect: no document support.
proposals.parameter: theta_window_commit U(1, 3) months before deadline at which a commitment request fires; boost_owner U(0, 1) applied for that window only
proposals.range: theta_window_commit U(1,3); boost_owner U(0,1); expires after the window
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW3 trigger and D3.1 p_start (window-scoped additive term on owner/specified)

proposals.behaviour: Convert the MDC into a brokered 'bundle-with-SG015' push: the MOD/MDC staff member drafts an advisory letter or resolution that asks SFMTA to re-scope the C13 application so APS rides with the SG015 12-inch head (SI02) carrier and/or a new SI18PB countdown head, before the deadline. This is the only lever a no-binding-authority body has in the final week.
proposals.trigger: Deadline within about 1 month (C13 closes 2026-11-02) AND the SG142 APS-only line is known to be ineligible AND SG015 sits in the same cycle. Fires once per cycle, only if the advocacy state is non-zero or the staff member has an open MDC agenda slot.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the chance that the A2 PREPARING task for the HSIP window produces a bundled (carrier + APS) instance instead of nothing (F-a/MISSED) or an ineligible APS-only submission. Adds a one-off shift to p_start and to the share of PW1-style bundling at C13 even on PW0. Without it, advocacy enters only through the undifferentiated pressure(t) term.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW1 (02 D3.6) bundles APS with SG015 and pressure(t) exists (D3.1), but PW1 is an exogenous scenario choice set by the modeller, not triggered by an actor. C2/MDC is only a pressure source (02 line 61). Kept as an endogenous trigger, not a duplicate of PW1.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7 row 'ODA staff proposed follow-up with MTA/DPW then recommendations and support letter' (follow-up not observed); 2.7.1 note that the MDC activation rule is an unknown parameter to test at zero and non-zero; 2.4 QA13 Q1-Q4 (APS may ride with a new countdown head); line 442 (SG015 and SG142 side by side, same fund source). The staff member's own role is not documented beyond this: partly no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_mdc_rescope: probability that, in a cycle with an open deadline within 1 month and a nonzero advocacy state, the staff action causes the A2 task to prepare a bundled APS+SG015 instance.
proposals.range: 0 to 0.4, scan {0, 0.1, 0.25}; 0 is the control. Optional lag t_letter U(0.5, 2) months.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 task state machine (additive term in the p_start logit + bundled-instance flag at PREPARING); lets the D3.6 PW1 starting move occur endogenously from PW0.

proposals.behaviour: Reframe the request under a label the funder or budget office already recognises (pedestrian signal safety / countdown heads, or accessible curb ramp and barrier removal) instead of 'APS', so it can be funded from a pool with a legal duty or a stated capital priority.
proposals.trigger: Repeated deflection ('cost', 'no money') on the APS label AND an adjacent label has a funded line or legal duty (curb ramps have a 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) timetable; APS does not). Fires when the APS path was refused or deflected in the last window.
proposals.effect_in_model: Moves a fraction of APS demand into another funding pool or task field (curb-ramp/ADA general-fund line, or HSIP BCR via SI18PB) at the price of dilution: APS becomes a minor add-on, so units delivered per dollar fall and timing follows the parent project. Changes where money flows, not only how much pressure exists.
proposals.already_in_model: Only partly. Fs bundling and PW4 (parent project/corridor route) exist, and the ADA general fund appears as a late fallback in PW2/PW3. No rule lets an advocate actively relabel an APS request into another category, nor a dilution cost for doing so.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7 row on no federal APS retrofit timetable vs curb ramps; both MDC letters (2025-04, 2026-04-16) went to curb ramps, no APS letter; 2.6 rows 'ADA public right-of-way $55M (FY26-30)' and mayor's budget lists curb ramps and barrier removal as priority. Observed pattern is the letters; the relabelling intent is an inference.
proposals.parameter: sw_reframe (switch) with q_reframe: share of deflected APS pressure that goes to an alternate field instead of 'no effect', and a dilution factor d_reframe on APS units per dollar.
proposals.range: q_reframe 0 to 0.3; d_reframe U(0.3, 0.8); off = 0.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.2 mechanism switch matrix (new row) and the D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (the 'no lasting effect after r months' clause).

proposals.behaviour: Window-waiting: staff and council withhold pressure in a window that cannot be made eligible in time and save it for the next window (C14, SG143 line) or budget season, timing it to the start of preparation rather than just before the deadline.
proposals.trigger: In the last weeks before a deadline, the preparation time needed for a re-scoped bundle (D_prep + (m-1)*delta_split) exceeds time left, so MISSED is likely; or the next window is within about 24 months.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure events are scheduled t_lead months before the next window opens instead of at random times. Avoids spending the roughly one effective yearly pressure event on a lost window and makes pressure land in the design phase of the next cycle.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-m (02 line 232) makes quiet periods happen to advocates exogenously, and D3.6 moves to the next window after a failure, but no actor chooses to hold pressure for a better window or times it to the preparation phase; pressure(t) just decays over k months.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7 'about one letter/resolution a year'; 2.4 event row C13 solicitation 2026-07-01 to deadline 2026-11-02; line 224 (CIP carried SG136 with HSIP C12 money but no SF APS application was ever filed), consistent with pressure arriving too late or never; QA13 Q48 (planning may be finished after submission). No document shows staff intentionally waiting.
proposals.parameter: pressure_timing in {reactive, pre_window}; when pre_window, the yearly advocacy event is placed t_lead before the next window opens.
proposals.range: t_lead U(3, 9) months; compare against reactive baseline.
proposals.rule_modified: O3/D2 event table for advocacy pressure events (timing of events feeding pressure(t) in D3.1); logit coefficients untouched.

proposals.behaviour: Coalition seeding toward the funder: the staff member shares the eligibility facts with blind-advocacy groups and with the Caltrans advisory committee (as another city's disability council did), so the APS-only rule is raised as a rule-change request, not only worked around locally.
proposals.trigger: A rule-based obstacle outside local control (funder eligibility) AND an external precedent exists (another disability council already wrote to the funder). Fires when APS-only ineligibility is the binding constraint at C13.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a small slow long-run path where HSIP eligibility changes in a later cycle (APS-only or APS with a weak carrier allowed). Would not help C13 but changes C14/C15 outcomes and the relative value of PW1, because the rule is currently fixed for all cycles.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.3 explicitly deletes a rule-relaxation switch ('no landable rule'). A weak probabilistic version is therefore a conscious omission, not an oversight; weigh before adopting, and report only as a scenario.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.4 row: advisory committee reply to the Sacramento disability council, 'HSIP does not fund APS-only projects' and 'will study further' (2025-12 minutes p.3); row C10 funded one APS-only special project; 2.5 'the exclusion is a state design choice, not federal'. No document shows the SF office doing this.
proposals.parameter: p_rule_relax: per-cycle probability, from C15 onward, that HSIP lets APS-only or weak-carrier APS qualify.
proposals.range: 0 to 0.15 per cycle, default 0; scenario only.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 eligibility clause 'pure APS ineligible' and the 'no rule-relaxation switch' note; affects only cycles after the current deadline.

proposals.behaviour: Equity-priority site insertion. MOD staff hand SFMTA a disability-priority site list and ask that those intersections be named in the HSIP APS-carrier package even though they are low-crash. It is a request, not a veto, but SFMTA may comply partly.
proposals.trigger: Package is being finalised before the C13 deadline (or the C14 repack) and the staff member sees that the BCR-sorted list leaves out intersections the disability community cares about.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds n_equity forced low-BCR intersections to the C or N package before the BCR check. Package BCR drops, so more packs fall under 5.0 (F-a, submission fails) or the cut-off (F-b). It is a feedback that can hurt funding, the opposite of usual advocacy effect.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. D3.3 freezes packing as strictly BCR-descending with a stop rule when package BCR < 5.0 (step 3); no actor can inject sites. 02 mentions MDC only as a channel in C2 (line 61).
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7: 'MOD provides the City public project site list for APS scoring' (TOOL p.8); EP26 names people with disabilities as an equity target ($47M, EP p.13-14). No document shows MOD pushing sites into an HSIP package, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: n_equity (integer) applied with probability p_equity
proposals.range: n_equity in {0,1,2,3}; p_equity U(0, 0.4); 0 is the control
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 route A packing algorithm step 3 (forced candidates ahead of BCR sort); outcomes F-a / F-b

proposals.behaviour: Support-letter channel aimed at the Prop L amendment decision. The Council issues a resolution or letter to the SFCTA board / CPC asking it to adopt the APS line amendment, instead of aiming at HSIP (where letters are ignored).
proposals.trigger: HSIP route looks closed (APS-only ineligible, tight window), or a Prop L amendment (PW2 / PW1 fallback) is placed on a board agenda.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the veto chance in F-j and shortens t_defer for a period after a letter. Letters are rare, event-gated shifts bounded by the Council's meeting rhythm.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: MDC is folded into C2 advocacy pressure (02 line 61) and F-j has q_veto and t_defer, but nothing links MDC letters to F-j. Only the link is proposed.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7: MDC tools are 'resolutions, hearings, support letters to CPC'; the 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 letters exist but are for curb ramps, 0 APS letters. 01 section 2.x records 'only BCR ranks; support letters for reference only' for HSIP (QA13 Q32, Q68), which is why the target must be Prop L.
proposals.parameter: sw_mdc_letter (0/1), letter rate lambda_letter, multiplier m_letter on q_veto and t_defer for 6 months after a letter
proposals.range: lambda_letter U(0, 1) per year; m_letter U(0.5, 1.0)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (q_veto, t_defer); PW2 trigger; PW1 second fallback

proposals.behaviour: Re-hang APS on the ADA transition-plan frame. MOD staff, who co-funded and ranked curb ramps under the ADA transition plan, ask for APS to be listed as a scheduled item with a dated target, so it has a duty clock like curb ramps.
proposals.trigger: Staff compare the curb-ramp track (has a 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) clock, gets budget and letters) with APS (no clock), usually after a failed or ineligible funding round.
proposals.effect_in_model: If adopted (probability p_tp, after delay t_tp), specified steps up one tier and enforce(t) gets a floor, so p_start rises for every field and the lawsuit step in PW3 becomes cheaper. It is a legal-baseline change, not extra pressure decay.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. PW3 sets pre-funding deadline + named owner + reporting as generic accountability parameters, not a re-framing into the transition plan; D1 enforce tiers come only from litigation. Overlaps PW3, so best written as a variant of it.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7: 'ramps have federal transition-plan duties (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)); in the materials read, APS has no corresponding federal retrofit deadline' (labelled inference); MOD co-funded and ranked ramps (2008 plan p.3).
proposals.parameter: sw_tp_frame (0/1) with adoption probability p_tp, delay t_tp, and enforce_floor
proposals.range: p_tp U(0, 0.5); t_tp U(12, 36) months; enforce_floor U(0.1, 0.4)
