proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start terms beta_spec and beta_enf; PW3 (adds a pre-litigation branch)

proposals.behaviour: Window-timed advocacy and abstention. With the C13 deadline one week away and APS-only ineligible, MOD staff judge nothing can change the C13 package and do not push now; they save effort for the next window (C14) and press 6-12 months ahead of it.
proposals.trigger: Time remaining to deadline is shorter than the prep time of a new package (D_prep), and the carrier (SG015) is already set.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure events are shifted: near zero when remaining prep time exceeds the time to deadline, concentrated in a lead window before the next opening. This changes the chance that a pressure event meets an open window.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. Pressure is a rate event with decay k, F-m adds quiet periods, and D3.6 moves to the next window after a signpost. Timing of advocacy relative to the window is not modelled; only that window-aware targeting is proposed.
proposals.evidence: No document support for targeting. 01 section 2.7 shows ODA staff proposed follow-up with MTA and DPW after 2026-07-17, 'follow-up not observed', and the 2026-07 meeting had 0 public speakers, consistent with low untimed activity.
proposals.parameter: sw_window_aware (0/1) with lead_months and a pressure-rate multiplier
proposals.range: lead_months U(3, 12); multiplier U(0.2, 1.0) when prep time exceeds gap to deadline, U(1.5, 3.0) inside the lead window
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure(t) term in p_start (event timing) and the F-m quiet-period generator

proposals.behaviour: Surrogate or interim-owner designation. While the engineer's post is vacant, MOD/MDC staff ask the SFMTA director or the Signal Shop supervisor to name an interim owner or a single point of contact. Alternatively MOD keeps its own shadow tracker of the request list, which sets up the next ask. Both are attempts to rebuild the 'owner' role from outside the agency.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy begins (F-h fires), i.e. the owner tier drops. The effort grows when MDC or advocates notice that no one is answering. It is more likely when a MOD staff member has a standing relationship with the Signal Shop.
proposals.effect_in_model: Partially restores the owner term in p_start during the vacancy, which shortens the effective owner-less spell. With probability q_proxy the owner tier steps back up (weak to partial) after a lag t_proxy, even though t_vac has not ended. It also leaves a record that makes later deflection (p_deflect) a little costlier.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-h (02 D3.5) drops owner one tier and restores it only when the vacancy ends (t_vac). In D10, owner is a tier that only SG105 ending, F-h or PW3 start can change. No actor outside the agency can restore it. PW3 raises owner as an exogenous policy start, not as a reaction to a vacancy. So the actor-driven, vacancy-triggered version is not in the model.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: ODA staff proposed 'follow up with MTA and DPW, then recommend support letters' (MDC26t); a 2006-03 resolution asked for a six-month reply and priority for the earliest request; MOD supplies the site list for APS scoring (TOOL p.8). 01 §2.1: one associate engineer scores all requests, so the single-person dependency is documented. There is no document showing MOD ever named or substituted an owner, so the substitution itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_proxy_owner (probability that a vacancy triggers an interim owner or surrogate arrangement) and t_proxy (lag in months). Together they set the share of the vacancy spell with owner partially restored.
proposals.range: q_proxy_owner U(0, 0.6), baseline 0 as a control; t_proxy U(2, 9) months; restored owner level 0.5 (partial), not 1.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-h (the restore condition) and the owner term in the p_start logistic (D3.1). Applies in M-A and M-D.

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS as a curb-ramp or ADA-transition-plan rider. MOD/MDC staff steer scarce advocacy effort toward the channel that already has a federal transition-plan time obligation and where MDC has sent support letters. They ask that APS be listed as an accessory item (audible signal at ramp locations) in the ramp funding request, because the owner-less APS channel cannot take a request right now.
proposals.trigger: The vacancy means the APS channel has no counterpart, and the existing evidence shows MDC support letters only for curb ramps (2025-04 and 2026-04-16). The ramp budget is expected to grow, which is a window. It is stronger when the APS channel is judged dead for at least t_vac.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a new bundling route: a share of pending APS intersections is attached to a curb-ramp project (parent) and travels on its timeline and funding (D3.4 'bundled into existing project' timing t_parent), instead of waiting for an APS-specific application. It also moves MDC advocacy effort from lambda_press on APS to ramps (the APS pressure falls).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.4 and PW4 handle 'bundled into a parent project' with pi and t_parent, and q_ramp is only a cost add-on for ramp work needed by APS installs. The model has no route where the request is deliberately reframed and attached to the ramp funding line by an advocate. Not found in 02 D3.2-D3.6, so I keep it.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7 lines 279 and 284: MDC letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 are both for curb ramps and none for APS; ramps have a federal transition-plan deadline (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)) and APS has no matching obligation; MOD co-funded and ranked DPW ramps in 2008 (S/sf-ada-transition-plan-curb-ramps-2008 p.3); ODA said the ramp budget 'will rise sharply'. 01 §2.1: curb work is triggered together with APS (MDC26 p.4), so a physical link exists. No document shows the rider move itself was tried.
proposals.parameter: p_ramp_rider (probability per MDC/ODA action that a vacancy-period request is reframed under ramps) with share s_rider of pending intersections that become eligible.
proposals.range: p_ramp_rider U(0, 0.5); s_rider U(0, 0.3) of C-type intersections that need a ramp; baseline 0 as a control.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 bundling into existing projects (adds a rider route with its own t_parent-like delay) and the pressure term in D3.1 (diverts part of lambda_press away from APS).

proposals.behaviour: Pressure bypass to budget decision-makers. Because the agency counterpart is missing, MOD/MDC staff send the request upward or sideways to a body that controls money (the CPC, the Mayor's budget office, the Board of Supervisors budget committee, or SFCTA board), usually as a support letter or an ask in the budget cycle, rather than to the Signal Shop.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus hiring freeze makes the Signal Shop unable to receive requests. A budget season window (annual general-fund request) or an SFCTA 5-year program amendment is open. MOD staff already write letters to the CPC, so this is a cheap move.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure events during the vacancy no longer go into the SFMTA task machine (where they are deflected with p_deflect or decay). They are instead routed to a budget-side node: with probability q_bypass they raise the chance that the general-fund request or the Prop L amendment is put on an agenda (reducing t_defer or q_veto for F-j, lifting q_dir for F-k). The cost is that the bypass can offend the agency, which is not modeled.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j, F-k and PW2 (local-first) treat the Prop L amendment and general fund as downstream fallbacks triggered by signposts, with no actor pushing them. D3.1 sends all pressure to the SFMTA A2 task machine only. A letter-writing push by an advisory body to the money nodes is not found in 02, so I keep it.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: MDC tools are resolutions, hearings and support letters to the CPC; two letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 went to the CPC for ramps; ODA offered to recommend a support letter after 2026-07 and none appeared by 2026-09 (§2.7.1 row 2026-09-18). 01 §2.6 covers CPC and general fund. 01 §2.7: MDC activation outside events is unknown, so q_bypass should include 0.
proposals.parameter: q_bypass (probability that a pressure event during a vacancy is routed to budget bodies) and its effect size on t_defer and q_veto.
proposals.range: q_bypass U(0, 0.5), baseline 0; effect: multiply t_defer by U(0.5, 1) and q_veto by U(0.5, 1) when it fires.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure routing (pressure(t) split between SFMTA and budget nodes) and D3.5 F-j and F-k parameters.

proposals.behaviour: Seeking a hiring-freeze exemption for the post, framed as an ADA or settlement-compliance position. MOD/MDC staff argue that the vacancy exposes the city to ADA and litigation risk (PROWAG, peer-city suits) and ask the Mayor's office or department head to exempt or backfill the single APS scoring position.
proposals.trigger: Hiring freeze in force with the post vacant, and visible litigation risk from peer cities (NYC, Chicago, DC). Increases with a recent PROWAG or lawsuit news item and when MDC has a meeting on the calendar.
proposals.effect_in_model: Shortens the effective vacancy and the freeze for this post only: t_vac is multiplied by a factor below 1 with probability q_exempt, and strain_end is brought earlier for the Signal Shop headcount tied to APS. It does not change the general freeze.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-h makes t_vac an exogenous spell (U(3, 18) months) and F-i makes strain_end an exogenous date. Neither responds to anyone lobbying for an exemption. D3.5 does not have an actor-driven exit from the freeze.
proposals.evidence: No document support for an exemption request. Indirect lines: 01 §2.1 (one associate engineer scores all requests; the Senior engineer cites the 'litigation environment' as a reason, MDC26t); 01 §2.1/§2.3 (SFCTA 2023 wrote that Signal Shop staffing is often the limiting factor); 01 §2.10 on external enforcement and peer-city suits. The behaviour is inferred, not observed.
proposals.parameter: q_exempt (probability of an exemption or fast backfill) and f_vac (multiplier on t_vac when granted).
proposals.range: q_exempt U(0, 0.4), baseline 0; f_vac U(0.3, 0.8) applied to t_vac (U(3, 18)). Optional link: strain_end shifts earlier by U(0, 6) months when granted.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-h (t_vac) and F-i (strain_end), and thereby the m_B strain term in D3.1 for M-B and M-D.

proposals.behaviour: Shadow ownership. MOD staff informally take over the vacated owner role: keep their own list of pending intersections and request ages, check the remaining Signal Shop staff for open items, and route live 311 or letter requests to a named contact. The post stays vacant on paper, but someone is chasing.
proposals.trigger: The F-h vacancy starts (owner drops one tier) and the hiring freeze (F-i) makes t_vac long. It fires only if the MOD staff member has slack, and is more likely after a salient public event such as a new request or advocate contact.
proposals.effect_in_model: Partly restores the owner tier lost in F-h from the vacancy month onward. This raises p_start through beta_own and lowers q_drop for PREPARING tasks. Capped, because MOD cannot prepare an application itself; it only stops the task being forgotten.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-h and D3.1 give owner a fixed drop and a fixed recovery on refill (t_vac). No other actor can substitute for the owner. C2 treats MDC only as an advocacy channel that produces pressure. F-m can lower pressure but nothing raises owner.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: ODA staff proposed, after 2026-07-17, to follow up with MTA and DPW and then give advice and support-letter suggestions (follow-up not observed). 01 s2.7: ODA deputy director asked DPW and MTA to coordinate strategy. 01 s2.7.1: no APS item on 2026-09-18. Intent is documented, follow-through is not, so the behaviour itself is inference.
proposals.parameter: proxy_owner_fill = fraction of the F-h owner drop offset while the post is vacant; plus activation probability q_proxy per vacancy.
proposals.range: proxy_owner_fill U(0, 0.5) with 0 as the current-model baseline; q_proxy U(0, 0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: F-h (owner step-down) and D3.1 p_start (beta_own * owner)

proposals.behaviour: Reframe APS as an ADA transition-plan item beside curb ramps. MOD asks for APS to be listed with curb ramps in the ADA transition plan and Public Works coordination, to borrow the curb-ramp legal timetable and budget line. The request goes to funders as an ADA compliance gap, not a discretionary safety add-on.
proposals.trigger: A budget or council hearing where curb-ramp funding is rising and APS has no line; a federal accessibility update (PROWAG) in the director's report; or an APS-only item rejected by SFCTA or HSIP.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the specified and enforce(t) inputs of p_start for affected fields (a legal timetable makes the task 'specified'). May move some C-class intersections into a curb-ramp parent project, at the cost of added delay t_partner. It creates no money by itself; it changes who must answer.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly, but not this move. PW4 allocates intersections to parent projects and PW3 raises specified/oversight as a policy design. But no actor in 02 reframes the request type or reassigns APS into the transition-plan class. Keep only the reframing act (success probability, delay), not the parent-merge mechanics.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: curb ramps carry a federal transition-plan duty (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)); APS has no corresponding federal retrofit timetable (inference). MOD co-funded and ranked curb ramps in 2008. MDC wrote curb-ramp letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04-16, none for APS. The APS reframing itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_reframe_ada (0/1), p_reframe_success per year, delta_reframe delay in months; on success specified += 0.2 for the affected fields.
proposals.range: p_reframe_success U(0, 0.3)/yr; delta_reframe U(0, 12) months; specified bump 0.2
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start (beta_spec*specified, beta_enf*enforce(t)) and PW4 allocation

proposals.behaviour: Time the ask to a funding window and hold it during the vacancy. MOD does not spend its one annual letter or resolution on a weak moment. It saves the APS support letter for a decision point where it can matter (FY27/28 budget, Prop L amendment, 2027 autumn 5YPP) and may wait until a new owner exists to receive the pressure.
proposals.trigger: A known decision date within W months (Prop L amendment F-j, 5YPP update, budget cycle, HSIP round close) combined with an empty owner post.
proposals.effect_in_model: MDC-channel pressure events stop being a constant stream. They are lowered during the vacancy and then spike just before the window. The same total pressure then raises p_start more at windows and less otherwise (changes the timing of pressure(t)).
proposals.already_in_model: No. C2 produces pressure at an unknown constant rate lambda_press. F-m has only random quiet periods (lambda_quiet, t_quiet), not strategic timing tied to windows or vacancy.
proposals.evidence: 01 s1.1 and s2.7: roughly one influence opportunity per year; activation rule listed as unknown. 01 s2.7.1: curb-ramp letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 may be budget-season timed (my reading). No document says MOD delays APS letters on purpose.
proposals.parameter: align_window (0/1); w_pulse pulse width before each window; g_pulse multiplier on lambda_press in the pulse; h_hold reduction of the rate while owner is vacant.
proposals.range: w_pulse U(1, 4) months; g_pulse U(1, 3); h_hold U(0, 0.8)
proposals.rule_modified: C2 pressure generation, pressure(t) decay, F-m

proposals.behaviour: Seek capacity outside the frozen post. MOD, with MDC backing, asks for APS design or request tracking to be done through a Public Works or inter-departmental work order, an on-call consultant, or a grant-funded temporary position, none of which depend on the frozen permanent post.
proposals.trigger: strain(t) is high, the vacancy has lasted past a threshold, and a deadline (HSIP round) or advocate complaint is near.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers strain(t) or adds small external preparation capacity. It shortens D_prep, not installation crew capacity. It costs money from an unlisted source and arrives after a lag.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-e and F-i allow outsourcing of construction (t_contract, kappa_contract) as the freeze recovery. That is SFMTA outsourcing construction, not a third party borrowing capacity for preparation. If other runs judge F-i's outsourcing branch enough, drop this one.
proposals.evidence: No document support for MOD doing this. 01 s2.1 and s2.2 give the staffing limit (SFCTA 2023 says Signal Shop staffing is often the limiting factor; hiring limits since 2024-07). 01 s2.7: ODA asked DPW and MTA to coordinate is the nearest hint. Speculative.
proposals.parameter: q_ext_capacity per vacancy, lag_ext, r_ext (cut in D_prep), d_strain (cut in strain).
proposals.range: q_ext_capacity U(0, 0.3); lag_ext U(3, 12) months; r_ext U(0, 0.4); d_strain U(0, 0.3)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.2 strain(t) term in p_start (M-B switch) and D_prep in D3.1 preparation time

proposals.behaviour: Converting a verbal exchange into a written, countable record: after the meeting the staff member drafts a follow-up (formal data request or a 'pending items' letter) asking SFMTA for a per-intersection cost/status breakdown of the ~76 intersections and a named funding path for each, with a reply deadline. This turns the 'costly / no money' answer into a document that can be tracked, and a refusal to give per-intersection reasons itself becomes a visible event.
proposals.trigger: A deflection event (the 'cost / no funds' reply) occurs at a council meeting; the staff member then decides whether to follow up in writing.
proposals.effect_in_model: With probability q_followup after a DEFLECTED event, a written request is filed. It (a) lowers p_deflect for the next r*2 months because a vague reply is now harder (a written per-site answer must be given), (b) adds a one-off boost to oversight(t) that decays like pressure, and (c) can turn the specified flag on for the intersections named. Without it, the DEFLECTED episode leaves no trace (D3.1: 'this pressure leaves no effect').
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. p_deflect is a fixed probability per pressure event and a deflection leaves no effect (02 D3.1); oversight is a static policy level changed only by PW3 (02 D3.6), not by an actor's follow-up. The follow-up that converts a deflection into a record is not in the rules. Not dropped, because the state-dependence is new.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7 row 'ODA 职员在 2026-07-17 后提议「与 MTA、DPW 跟进……再提出建议和支持信建议」' (后续未观察到). 01 §2.1 row 'Technical Challenges & Cost' and '请求名单上其余路口 selected based on funding' show a stated reason with no per-site detail. No document shows the follow-up actually being filed.
proposals.parameter: q_followup (probability a written follow-up is filed after a DEFLECTED event) with companion d_defl (multiplier on p_deflect for the next 2r months after a follow-up)
proposals.range: q_followup U(0, 0.6), 0 as the control (current model); d_defl U(0.3, 1.0)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch: replace 'this pressure leaves no effect' with 'with q_followup, set oversight pulse and p_deflect*d_defl'; also the p_start term beta_ov*oversight in D3.1

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS as a curb-ramp / ADA transition-plan item and hosting it in the DPW ramp program, which the office already co-ranks and for which a federal transition-plan time-table duty exists. The staff member steers the request from SFMTA's signal list to ramp projects, so the intersection is dug once and APS poles/pipes ride along.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA keeps saying APS cost is high (pipe ~$200k and ramp ~$200k are the stated cost drivers), and a curb-ramp project is already scheduled or funded at one of the unfunded intersections.
proposals.effect_in_model: A new host route: an unfunded C or N intersection with an upcoming DPW ramp job gets APS added to that job. Effect on the intersection: move from the pool to a 'ramp-hosted' state, with a lower marginal APS cost (q_ramp and pipe removed from the cost, since they are paid by the ramp budget) and a delay t_ramp_host. It adds a new inflow of funded intersections that does not go through SFMTA's p_start or HSIP.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. Fs / 并入已有项目 covers APS attached to SFMTA signal projects, and PW4 assigns sources by intersection (02 D3.4, D3.6). A ramp-driven host managed by another agency (DPW) with cost-sharing is not a node in the 02 rules; q_ramp appears only as a cost item. Kept as a new host type.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: MOD 2008 co-funds and ranks DPW curb ramps; ramps have a 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) time-table duty while APS has none; the 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 MDC letters were for ramps only. 01 §2.1: a senior engineer says not touching existing ramps is 'five times faster'; ramp and pipe each about $200,000.
proposals.parameter: lambda_rampHost (annual rate at which an unfunded intersection is matched to an upcoming DPW ramp job) and f_shared (share of pipe/ramp cost carried by the ramp budget)
proposals.range: lambda_rampHost U(0, 0.05) per intersection per year; f_shared U(0, 1); t_ramp_host U(6, 36) months. 0 = current model
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 delivery table: add a 'ramp-hosted' row; D3.3 N-type cost table: c_full reduced by f_shared*(c_pipe + c_ramp) for the hosted intersections; D1/O2 state list gets one more host state

proposals.behaviour: Spending the office's single scarce advocacy channel on APS rather than ramps. The council gets about one letter or resolution per year; the staff member decides which item the letter and the agenda slot go to, and whether to address it to the capital planning committee or the transportation board, where equity criteria name disabled people.
proposals.trigger: The yearly letter/resolution slot, and the capital-plan or Prop L amendment calendar (F-j, PW2, PW6).
proposals.effect_in_model: Each year the MDC channel chooses one target: ramp (no APS effect), APS, or none. If APS, a pressure pulse is added at a window with more weight than ordinary pressure events (it carries a formal body's name), and it lowers q_veto (F-j) or raises q_dir (F-k) for the next decision if timed within t_align months of that decision. Otherwise the pulse is zero.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. C2 says advocates (including MDC as a channel) produce pressure events at an unknown rate and the table lists lambda_press (02 O2 line 61, D10 line 340); the MDC influence channel is 'about one letter per year' in 01. There is no choice between APS and ramp, and no timing against a funding decision. Kept for the choice and the timing.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: 'MDC 影响渠道: 0 约束力; 每年约 1 次信/决议'; 'two letters, both for ramps, no APS letter'; 'ODA 2026-07 表示要回头建议写支持信' not observed afterwards. 01 §2.4-style row: EP26 equity projects name disabled people as a target ($47M).
proposals.parameter: p_letter_APS (probability the yearly letter targets APS) and w_letter (weight of that pulse relative to an ordinary pressure event)
proposals.range: p_letter_APS U(0, 0.8) (current evidence suggests 0 in 2025-26); w_letter U(1, 5); t_align U(0, 6) months
proposals.rule_modified: pressure(t) definition (D3.1) with an extra weighted pulse; F-j q_veto and F-k q_dir get a multiplier when a letter falls within t_align of the decision

proposals.behaviour: Accepting a symbolic or partial answer to close the issue (satisfying): the staff member lets SFMTA offer a small gesture, such as a review commitment, a prioritised short list, or a 'we will study' reply, and treats the matter as handled, so the pressure stops although no money was committed.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA's reply to the meeting includes a soft commitment (a study, a ranked list, a promise to report back) while the unfunded count is unchanged.
proposals.effect_in_model: After a soft commitment the advocacy side goes quiet for t_accept months (pressure stops, the same state as F-m) and the commitment decays: with probability q_nofollow it is never reported on, and the next report is the old one. Net effect: pressure(t) is cut while the task state stays IDLE, so p_start falls without any change in owner or oversight.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-m has advocacy going quiet through a random hazard lambda_quiet (02 D3.5), independent of what the agency said. Quiet caused by accepting a gesture, and tied to the agency's reply, is not generated. Evidence of the mechanism is indirect: 'Caltrans: will study again' (01 line 207) is a gesture of the same kind from another agency.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.4 line 207 (Caltrans advisory committee: 'HSIP does not fund APS-only projects', 'will study again'); 01 §2.7: ODA proposed follow-up 'not observed afterwards'; MDC 2018-2026 agendas show APS only twice as an information report, no action item. No document shows the council accepting a gesture; marked as inference.
proposals.parameter: q_accept (probability the advocacy side stands down after a soft commitment) with t_accept (stand-down months)
proposals.range: q_accept U(0, 0.7), t_accept U(6, 36) months; 0 = current model. Soft commitment itself occurs at a rate tied to each DEFLECTED event, q_soft U(0, 0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: F-m: add a second trigger (soft commitment from a DEFLECTED event) that sets lambda_press to 0 for t_accept; D3.1 DEFLECTED branch gets a q_soft sub-branch

proposals.behaviour: Interim steward / ready-made application kit. While the engineer post is vacant, the Mayor's Office on Disability (MOD) staff member quietly hands the next preparer (or whoever inherits the task) a pre-assembled kit: the site list MOD already compiles for APS scoring, a prioritised complaint-and-request roll-up, draft support-letter text and the Capital Planning Committee ask. This is a substitute for the missing owner, not pressure on it.
proposals.trigger: owner has just dropped (F-h vacancy) and the hiring freeze is on (F-i), so the task is stuck at IDLE or PREPARING with q_drop risk. MOD sees that the council's only link to the funding process has gone.
proposals.effect_in_model: During the vacancy, preparation of one application instance is shorter, and the chance that a running PREPARING task is aborted falls. The kit cannot create ownership, so p_start does not rise through beta_own. It only makes a start cheaper and an abort less likely.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-h (02 D3.5) only drops owner one tier and aborts PREPARING with q_drop, then restores after t_vac. The model has no actor who substitutes for the missing owner. C2 in 02 O2 only produces pressure events. D_prep is a fixed U(1,6) with no external assistance term.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7: MOD 'provides the City public projects site list for APS scoring' (TOOL p.8). 01 section 2.1: one associate engineer scores all requests, so the preparation knowledge sits in one head. Whether MOD ever assembles application material is not documented, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: `delta_assist` (months removed from D_prep) and `dq_assist` (reduction of q_drop), both active only when owner = 0 and a switch `mod_steward` = 1.
proposals.range: delta_assist U(0, 2) months with D_prep floored at 1; dq_assist U(0, 0.5) proportional cut; switch {0,1}.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING duration formula D_prep + (m-1)*delta_split, and F-h q_drop in D3.5.

proposals.behaviour: Window-synchronised pressure. Instead of generic advocacy, the disability council and MOD staff time a hearing item, resolution or support letter to a known decision window: the HSIP C13 deadline (2026-11-02), the 2027 autumn Prop L 5-year plan round, a Prop L amendment, or the two-year budget submission. The pressure lands when a task could actually be started.
proposals.trigger: A funding window is within about w_sync months and the owner is vacant. MOD staff judge that a letter only matters if someone can act on it that cycle. The earlier promise of a follow-up letter makes a timed letter the natural move.
proposals.effect_in_model: The same annual pressure mass is moved to the months before windows, so pressure(t) is high at the moment p_start is evaluated and low otherwise. With a short decay constant k, unsynchronised pressure wastes itself between windows. Synchronisation can therefore raise the start probability without changing lambda_press.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.1 and D10 draw pressure events at an exogenous rate lambda_press (U(0,0.5)/yr) and decay them with k. They are independent of the window calendar. F-m only switches pressure off at random. Support letters to CPC or SFCTA do not appear as an event type anywhere in 02.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7: MDC tools are only resolutions, hearings and letters; 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 letters went to curb ramps and none for APS (0 APS letters). The ODA staff proposal after 2026-07-17 to come back with 'recommendations and a support letter' was never seen (2026-09-18 agenda has no APS). 01 section 2.7.1 marks this as an unknown activation rule to be tested at zero and non-zero. The letters being time-aligned to funding cycles is an inference from the ramp-letter dates, not a document statement.
proposals.parameter: `sync_share` = fraction of lambda_press mass relocated to the w_sync months before each window opens or closes; `w_sync` = width of that lead time.
proposals.range: sync_share U(0, 1) (0 = current model); w_sync U(1, 6) months.
proposals.rule_modified: Generation of pressure(t) in D3.1 (the pressure term of p_start) and its link to the event calendar in O3.

proposals.behaviour: Escalating past the deflecting node. When front-line staff answer 'no money, very costly', the council's staff go over their heads to the SFMTA Board, the Mayor's budget office or the Capital Planning Committee. They ask for a written funding source and an owner named in the reply, which makes a bare 'cost' answer harder.
proposals.trigger: Pressure event hits an A2 that is in DEFLECTED state or the post is vacant. A pattern of 'cost' replies has already been seen at the 2026-07 hearing. MOD staff choose a different audience for the next request.
proposals.effect_in_model: For an escalated event, p_deflect is lower (the answer has to name a source or owner) and the DEFLECTED dwell time r may be shorter. Non-escalated events behave as today. Escalation also uses up an event budget, so only some pressure events can be escalated.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.1 treats every pressure event as aimed at A2, with the same p_deflect U(0.5,0.95). PW3 (02 D3.6) changes owner, specified and oversight as a policy design, not as something the advocate's staff do on their own. D1 enforcement ladders go to negotiation and litigation, not intermediate escalation.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7: the ODA director spoke at the SFMTA Board on 2026-10-06 (on another issue), so an access route to the Board exists. 01 section 2.1: the senior engineer's reply to advocacy is cost-focused ('selected based on funding'). The mechanism is a 'buck-passing' counter-move and has no direct quote that MOD does it for APS, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: `q_escalate` = probability that a pressure event is escalated; `dp_esc` = reduction of p_deflect for escalated events.
proposals.range: q_escalate U(0, 0.5); dp_esc U(0, 0.4) with p_deflect floored at 0.1; both 0 in the baseline.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (pressure event -> DEFLECTED with p_deflect) and the p_deflect row of D10.

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS as part of the ADA right-of-way programme. The council's staff ask that APS be counted inside the city's ADA public right-of-way capital line or the curb-ramp prioritisation that MOD already co-sets, rather than inside the street-safety or signal lines. The request moves to a pot where disability is the stated purpose and the ADA transition language applies.
proposals.trigger: HSIP rules exclude pure APS (C13 Q3) and the Prop L APS line has only $0-0.5M unallocated. Curb-ramp budgets are expected to rise. MOD staff already sit on the ramp-ranking side, so adding APS to that conversation is cheap while the signal engineer is absent.
proposals.effect_in_model: A new local-money lane appears: a share of the ADA right-of-way pay-go line, or APS added to scheduled DPW ramp work at the same intersections, so some C-type intersections get APS as an add-on carrier. It can also partly cover the ramp +$200k add-on. Success depends on a ramp project existing at the site; otherwise nothing happens.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. Ramp cost appears only as a cost add-on (q_ramp, 02 O2 line 51), and PW4 has parent-project routes. The model has no ADA right-of-way funding source and no DPW ramp project as a parent that carries APS. The 'general fund' lane is only the 25 percent street-safety share, so the reframed pool is not covered.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.6: general fund pay-go ADA public right-of-way $55M (FY26-30), $71M (FY31-35) (CP-I p.4); capital plan says accessibility capital 'is typically reflected in other departments' budgets, including transportation and signals (APS)' (CP-T p.11). 01 section 2.7: MOD co-funded and ranked DPW curb ramps in the 2008 transition plan (p.3), the ODA deputy asked DPW and MTA to coordinate strategy, and APS has no matching federal retrofit deadline (the contrast with ramps). 01 section 2.1: digging triggers ramp work.
proposals.parameter: `b_ada` (annual ADA right-of-way money available to APS) and `lambda_ramp` (annual rate at which a pending C-type site coincides with a scheduled ramp project); switch `ada_reframe` = 1.
proposals.range: b_ada U($0, $300k)/yr; lambda_ramp U(0.01, 0.08)/yr per site (same order as lambda_hw); switch {0,1}.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.2 funding-lane list (new local lane) and the PW4 / PW5 parent-event generator in D3.6.

proposals.behaviour: Strategic silence during the vacancy. With nobody named to answer, council staff hold requests, letters and agenda items until a new owner or a post-freeze window appears. The aim is to avoid a wasted request or a 'cost' reply on record, and to avoid giving the department an easy reason to say the issue was handled.
proposals.trigger: owner = 0 and strain > 0 (vacancy plus hiring freeze). MOD staff judge that the person who would receive the letter is gone. There was also no APS item at the 2026-09-18 meeting after the July promise.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure intensity depends on state: it falls while owner = 0, then catches up as a burst once the post is filled, or once the freeze ends. In the vacancy the model's pressure(t) term shrinks and a task that depends on pressure stays IDLE longer; after rehire p_start jumps. This can make a vacancy longer in effect than t_vac suggests.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-m (02 D3.5) stops pressure at random at rate lambda_quiet for t_quiet, independent of the owner state. lambda_press is a constant in D10. Nothing links the advocates' activity to whether an owner exists.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7.1: no APS action at the 2026-09-18 meeting, after a stated plan in July; the 'activation rule' is listed as unknown and to be tested at zero and non-zero. The link to the vacancy is an inference. No document says that staff wait deliberately, so this is weak support.
proposals.parameter: `gamma_silence` = multiplier on lambda_press when owner = 0; `burst` = extra pressure released in the month after a rehire.
proposals.range: gamma_silence U(0.2, 1.0) (1 = current model); burst U(0, 2) in units of one pressure event.
proposals.rule_modified: Event generation for C2 pressure in D3.1 and the lambda_press row of D10 (makes it state-dependent on owner).

proposals.behaviour: Follow-up promise as a pressure sink. After the council exchange (advocates push, SFMTA says no money), the Office staff reply 'we will follow up with SFMTA and DPW and come back with recommendations or a support letter'. The pressure is logged as 'handled' and moves to a slow offline channel. Advocates stand down for a while, and the follow-up often never reaches an agenda.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event at a council meeting that ends in SFMTA's 'costly, no money' answer. The staff role has no binding tool and wants to keep both sides cooperative.
proposals.effect_in_model: Part of the pressure events that SFMTA does not deflect (the 1 - p_deflect branch) are absorbed by the advisory channel instead of being added to pressure(t). Pressure is suppressed for t_followup months, and with small probability the follow-up ends in a real support letter. This lowers the effective pressure input to p_start.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. 02 D3.1 only has SFMTA-side DEFLECTED (p_deflect, r months) and pressure(t) decay with k. F-m (D3.5) interrupts advocacy with a random quiet period, not as a result of an advisory body absorbing it. 01 section 2.7 treats MDC/ODA as an information channel with an unknown activation rule, but 02 has no absorption of other actors' pressure.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7 table: 'ODA staff after 2026-07-17 proposed to follow up with MTA and DPW and then give recommendation and support-letter suggestions' (follow-up not observed); 2.7.1 row 2026-09-18: agenda, ODA report and LightHouse presentation contain no APS item and no support letter, two months after the promise.
proposals.parameter: p_absorb (probability a non-deflected pressure event is routed into the follow-up channel instead of pressure(t)); with t_followup and q_letter_after. Switch sw_absorb in {0,1}.
proposals.range: p_absorb U(0, 0.7); t_followup U(2, 12) months; q_letter_after U(0, 0.4)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure branch (1 - p_deflect): split into pressure(t) increment vs. absorbed; also D3.5 F-m. Relevant to M-A and M-D.

proposals.behaviour: Piggyback APS on the curb-ramp support letter. The only support letters the advisory body sent were for curb ramps. Staff add an APS line to the next ramp funding letter to the capital planning committee, or ask for one combined 'accessible right-of-way' letter, instead of a stand-alone APS letter.
proposals.trigger: The annual spring letter window (letters dated 2025-04 and 2026-04-16) and the capital planning budget cycle; SFMTA's 'no money' answer makes a funding letter the remaining tool.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the success of local-money lines: lowers q_veto in F-j (Prop L amendment) and raises the chance that the general-fund annual request (PW2 fallback) is listed, by delta_letter, only if a letter with the APS rider is sent in the window. Cost: if the rider dilutes the ramp letter, ramp priority drops.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-j has q_veto fixed and independent of any support letter. PW2 has no letter signpost. pressure(t) has no actor-specific channel to the capital planning body.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7 table: 'two letters (2025-04, 2026-04-16) both for curb ramps, no APS letter; APS letters 0'; 'tool only advisory: resolutions, hearings, support letters to CPC'; 2.7 inference 'about one chance of influence per year'.
proposals.parameter: delta_letter (reduction in q_veto and in probability the general-fund request is dropped); p_rider (probability per year an APS rider is attached to the annual letter). Switch sw_rider.
proposals.range: delta_letter U(0, 0.25); p_rider U(0, 0.6) per year, active only in the April window
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (q_veto) and PW2 branch 'general fund request not listed'; MDC annual-opportunity event in O3.

proposals.behaviour: Reframe APS as an ADA transition-plan item. Staff argue missing APS is an access-programme gap and push for APS to be added as a dated line (count or percent by year) in the City's ADA transition-plan or capital-plan update, the way curb ramps are. This turns an optional safety project request into a compliance-style item.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA's cost framing; staff know ramps carry a transition-plan time schedule and APS does not; other-city court orders are cited at the council.
proposals.effect_in_model: With probability p_reframe a plan line is created, raising owner and specified for the SFMTA APS task (named unit, dated target) and adding a mild step to enforce(t), after t_plan months. If no money is attached, only specified moves.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 PW3 raises owner/specified/oversight and escalates D1 tiers, but as an advocates' strategy; no route lets a city-side disability office create it through an administrative plan update. Effect variables exist, actor and trigger are new.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7 table: 'ramps have a transition-plan schedule obligation (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)); in the materials read APS has no matching federal retrofit schedule (inference)'; 'MOD (2008) co-funded and ranked DPW curb ramps, which entered a 10-year capital plan'; 2006-03 resolution target 25% by 2010 missed (9-10%).
proposals.parameter: p_reframe (per year), delta_spec added to specified, delta_enf added to enforce(t), lag t_plan. Switch sw_reframe.
proposals.range: p_reframe U(0, 0.3)/yr; delta_spec U(0.1, 0.5); delta_enf U(0, 0.15); t_plan U(6, 24) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start terms beta_spec*specified and beta_enf*enforce(t); D1 initialization of owner/specified.

proposals.behaviour: Steering the public-facility site list. Staff supply or update the 'city public project' site list that gives extra scoring points to requests, choosing which pending intersections are on it, so some of the ~76 move up the order. A quiet administrative lever instead of a public fight.
proposals.trigger: Advocates demand to know why most of the 76 are unfunded; with no new money, the visible alternative is to change who goes first within existing money.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes ranking of pending intersections in the internal install queue and which intersections enter the first packaged applications (Route B special project, local batch). Total funding unchanged; changes which intersections end in never_served.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. D3.3 packaging orders by BCR, Route B by tier and fatal/serious crash count; D3.4 internal queue has no score-bonus term and does not use the facility list.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7 table: 'MOD provides the city-public-project site list for APS scoring (TOOL p.8)'. The behaviour itself (editing the list under pressure): no document support, only the lever exists.
proposals.parameter: phi_list (share of pending intersections re-weighted) and bonus_list (score bonus on queue order). Switch sw_list.
proposals.range: phi_list U(0, 0.3); bonus_list U(0, 1) in units of one rank group
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 candidate ordering for Route B and local batch; D3.4 internal queue order.

proposals.behaviour: Ramp-linked reframing. Staff stop arguing APS as a standalone SFMTA cost item and attach it to the curb-ramp program that the office already co-funds and ranks with DPW. The ask becomes: when a ramp project touches a signalised intersection on the request list, the signal's pedestrian push-button or APS is added to the same work order, paid from ramp or ADA-transition money.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA says APS is costly and there is no money, while the ramp budget is rising (ODA deputy: ramp budget 'will go way up') and a ramp project is scheduled at a listed C-type intersection.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a new external event stream: a DPW ramp project occurs at a pending C-type intersection at rate lambda_ramp. APS rides along as an add-on only with probability p_ramp_link. Cost is split: share f_ramp_pay is paid by the ramp budget, and the rest is booked as extra budget in cost_by_actor. The intersection goes into the internal construction queue and is subject to K_crew. Without p_ramp_link > 0, the ramp stream never touches APS.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. PW4 'merged into a parent project' and the 'Fs' state cover SFMTA signal projects. PW5 covers button or hardware swaps. Neither has DPW ramp projects as a trigger, and the ramp budget is not a funding source. Ramps appear in D3 only as a cost item (q_ramp, $200k). Partial overlap with PW4, so rewrite it as a separate trigger.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 lines 280-281: the office co-funds and ranks DPW curb ramps (ADA transition plan 2008). 01 s2.7 line 279: MDC letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04 were all about ramps, none about APS. 01 s2.7: ramps carry a federal transition-plan time obligation and APS does not. Whether the ramp budget may legally pay for APS has no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_ramp_link
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6), with lambda_ramp U(0.02, 0.1)/yr per C-type intersection and f_ramp_pay U(0, 1)
proposals.rule_modified: Adds a new event type beside PW5 in D3.6 and a new funding source in D3.4; adds a PW7 'ramp-linked' row

proposals.behaviour: Targeted support letter or resolution that is timed to a funding window. The council sends a letter to the capital planning body or the transport authority board supporting an APS line in the Prop L plan amendment, sent just before the amendment vote or the next 5-year plan cycle, instead of a general expression of concern.
proposals.trigger: After the meeting, the advocates' complaint is on record and a Prop L amendment (F-j) is pending or the next 5YPP cycle is open. In 2026-07 the office's staff said they would come back to 'recommend a support letter'.
proposals.effect_in_model: Letter is sent with probability p_letter per window; the base rate is zero because the letter does not exist yet. If sent while the F-j amendment is open, it lowers q_veto by delta_letter and shortens t_defer. If sent outside the window, it has no effect other than adding to pressure(t). F-j currently treats q_veto and t_defer as fixed priors, so this makes them depend on an actor's action and its timing.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j in D3.5 has q_veto U(0,0.5) and t_defer, and PW2 starts with the amendment. But no actor changes q_veto, letters are not modelled, and the council is not a model actor beyond generic pressure(t). Keep only the endogenous effect.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 line 279: only ramp letters exist, 0 APS letters. 01 s2.7 line 287: ODA staff proposed a follow-up with the transit agency and DPW, then a letter recommendation, and no follow-up has been observed. 01 s2.7 line 291: council influence is about one letter or resolution per year. Whether a letter actually moves the vote has no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_letter
proposals.range: U(0, 0.8) per open window; delta_letter U(0, 0.3) subtracted from q_veto; zero outside the window
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (q_veto, t_defer); PW2 start condition

proposals.behaviour: Turn the verbal reply into a minuted follow-up. Staff ask that the council record a specific action item: SFMTA to return with a funding-status table for the roughly 76 intersections (funded, source, or not applied for), or that an agenda item is scheduled. This converts a dismissal at the meeting into a standing oversight item.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA answers 'costly, no money' in the meeting without naming a source for each intersection (the slide deck says remaining intersections are 'selected based on funding').
proposals.effect_in_model: With probability q_followup the follow-up is minuted and delivered, which adds delta_ov to oversight for T_ov months, then decays; this does not set specified or owner. With probability 1 - q_followup the intent dissipates, which is the observed pattern. It also raises p_start only through the existing beta_ov term, and may lower p_deflect by delta_defl because the reply now needs a source.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. oversight is a static U(0.05,0.6), and PW3 raises it by 0.3 as a jump from an accountability package. No rule makes oversight a response to a single meeting, with decay or with follow-up failure.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 line 287: ODA staff proposed follow-up and then a letter, 'not observed afterwards' (this is the base rate for q_followup being low). 01 line 83: the circle 'say no money / no application' has no actor with resources to force an application. 01 line 130: the transit agency answered with a three-page cost presentation and 'selected based on funding'.
proposals.parameter: q_followup
proposals.range: U(0, 0.7); delta_ov U(0, 0.3); T_ov U(3, 18) months; delta_defl U(0, 0.2)
proposals.rule_modified: Oversight update in D3.1 (p_start via beta_ov) and p_deflect in M-A/M-D; adds a decaying oversight pulse

proposals.behaviour: Quiet legal-exposure briefing. Staff do not sue; they brief the city's own lawyers and the agency's leadership on the ADA exposure of leaving a long request list unfunded, citing the New York court order that the council has heard about. The goal is a pre-litigation internal commitment.
proposals.trigger: Advocates repeat the complaint and SFMTA keeps replying 'cost'; staff have no formal enforcement power, only an advisory role.
proposals.effect_in_model: A briefing event multiplies the external-enforcement rate epsilon_enf by kappa_legal for t_legal months, and with probability q_prelit raises owner or specified one level (a self-imposed commitment) before any suit. If nothing happens, no effect. This gives the 'enforcement' escalation a path that does not run through PW3's lawsuit.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. epsilon_enf is an exogenous annual escalation rate and PW3 starts with a deadline plus a named owner imposed from outside, then litigation. No internal-actor trigger raises epsilon_enf, and no pre-litigation commitment is modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 line 284: ODA deputy explained why NYC was fast by citing the federal court order. 01 s2.7: APS has no federal retrofit schedule obligation in the materials read, which weakens the lever (the model should allow that kappa_legal may be near 1). No document shows staff briefing city lawyers, so the briefing itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: kappa_legal
proposals.range: U(1, 4) multiplier on epsilon_enf for t_legal U(6, 24) months; q_prelit U(0, 0.3)
proposals.rule_modified: epsilon_enf update in D1/D3.6 PW3; owner/specified upgrade rule

proposals.behaviour: Cost-claim rebuttal. Disability Office staff answer 'APS is costly, no money' by publicly splitting the 76 intersections into cheap and expensive ones. Cheap ones are the C-type, where a packaged APS costs roughly $10-76k per intersection. Expensive ones are the N-type, where a full upgrade costs up to ~$554k. This takes away SFMTA's blanket cost answer for the cheap group. SFMTA can then no longer deflect to 'cost / no money' as easily.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event at a council meeting meets the cost answer, and staff have a per-intersection cost split ready (from the SFMTA list, peer-city unit costs, or a public-records request). It is more likely after a recent deflection.
proposals.effect_in_model: After a pressure event, with probability q_rebut the deflection probability for that actor drops by delta_defl. It recovers with time constant tau_rebut. Later pressure events then land in pressure(t) more often and less often in DEFLECTED.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in the model. D3.1 treats p_deflect as a constant per pressure event (D10: U(0.5, 0.95)), and the cost reply is just the DEFLECTED branch. D3.2 'costpress' acts on SFMTA's start rate, not on whether advocates can contest the cost claim. No rule lets a pressure event change later deflection.
proposals.evidence: 01 §1.1 (row for peer cities, ~line 78): peer-city unit costs of $10k-76k (packaged) and $52-65k (NYC). 01 §2.7 (~line 279): MDC tools are advisory only. 01 §2.1: the authors' first-hand note that agencies shift blame onto each other. No document shows any actor actually running a split-by-cost rebuttal. This is a red-team hypothesis, with document support only for the cost spread.
proposals.parameter: delta_defl (reduction in p_deflect after a rebuttal)
proposals.range: delta_defl U(0, 0.4); q_rebut U(0, 0.6) per pressure event; tau_rebut U(6, 24) months. Floor p_deflect at 0.1. At 0 the model reduces to the current one.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch: p_deflect becomes p_deflect(t) = p_deflect * (1 - delta_defl * rebut(t)). The M-A and M-D mechanism switches apply as before.

proposals.behaviour: Window-aligned pressure. Staff hold the political ask until it can be attached to a decision point, such as the biennial budget submission, the CIP or capital plan hearing, or an HSIP call. They do not spend it at an unrelated meeting. A letter to the capital planning committee at the right moment counts for more than the same pressure at an ordinary meeting. Staff may also push a pressure event back to wait for a better window.
proposals.trigger: The next funding window is less than a few months away, or the current meeting falls outside any window. A meeting exchange alone leads to 'save it for the budget cycle'.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure events are not purely Poisson. With probability w_align, an event that would fire is delayed until L_lead months before the next window opens. There it adds pressure(t) at weight 1 + w_boost. Events that are not delayed fire at the usual time but at weight 1. Pressure at the wrong time is partly wasted.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in the model. D3.1 and D10 make pressure a Poisson process (lambda_press) with exponential decay (k), with no link to calendar windows. D3.1 starts tasks only when 'window open' and U < p_start, but window opening and pressure timing are independent.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.6 (~line 279 and §2.7): the two MDC support letters (2025-04 and 2026-04-16) went to the capital planning committee, so they were timed to a capital-planning moment. 01 §3.1 (~line 412): the general-fund request is a two-year budget due 'before 5-01 of even years'. 01 §2.7.1: APS was on the MDC agenda only in 2023-07 and 2026-07, which shows unaligned meeting exchanges produced no action.
proposals.parameter: w_align
proposals.range: w_align U(0, 1) (probability that an event is held for a window); w_boost U(0, 1.5); L_lead U(1, 6) months. At w_align = 0 the model reduces to the current Poisson pressure.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 and D10: the schedule and weight of pressure(t) events (lambda_press, k).

proposals.behaviour: Follow-up leakage. Disability Office staff promise to follow up with SFMTA and the public works department and to propose a support letter. The promise often goes nowhere, because no one tracks it and the agenda moves on. The meeting exchange is therefore a pressure event that is weaker than its face value.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event comes from the council channel (MDC) rather than a directly accountable actor, and there is no calendar commitment or named owner for the follow-up.
proposals.effect_in_model: A pressure event from the MDC channel enters pressure(t) with probability q_follow only after a delay t_follow. Otherwise it is lost. This lowers the effective pressure rate. It also works as a switch for 'agenda item plus dated action'.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 O/C2 treats MDC as the advocates' channel producing pressure events at an unknown rate, and F-m covers a quiet period for advocacy as a whole. Nothing models a promised follow-up decaying inside the channel itself.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: the Disability Office staff member proposed 'follow up with MTA and DPW, then propose recommendations and a support letter' after 2026-07-17, but 'no follow-up observed'. The 2026-09-18 agenda, director report and presentation contain no APS item. 01 §2.7.1 notes this is only 'not observed within the searched range' and is not proof of zero activity. So this hypothesis has direct but weak support.
proposals.parameter: q_follow
proposals.range: q_follow U(0, 1); t_follow U(1, 6) months. PW3 starting settings (named owner, dated commitment) set q_follow = 1. At q_follow = 1 and t_follow = 0 the model reduces to the current one.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure-event entry into pressure(t), for events from the MDC channel only. Interacts with lambda_press and lambda_quiet (F-m).

proposals.behaviour: Reframe APS as part of the ADA transition plan and the general-fund ADA public right-of-way line. Staff argue that APS belongs under the same federal ADA schedule duty and the same $125M/10-year general-fund stream already used for curb ramps. APS currently has neither a federal schedule duty nor its own earmarked line. Staff also point to peer cities where court orders drove progress.
proposals.trigger: Staff compare APS with curb ramps in front of the council. Ramps have a federal schedule duty and a large dedicated stream, and APS has none. Triggers include the ODA director's report listing the pedestrian-signal accessibility rulemaking and a staff member citing the NYC court order.
proposals.effect_in_model: With probability p_ada_frame per year, an ADA reframing event occurs. It adds a new funding source: a share s_ada of the ADA public right-of-way line becomes available to APS (increase A_local). It also raises 'specified' from 0 to 1 for the APS task for t_ada months, so the beta_spec term in p_start applies. This is not just a slightly higher pressure.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D1/D3.6 PW3 sets 'specified' and 'owner' as an accountability-first pathway, and PW2 uses the general fund as the third fallback (A_local U(0, 0.57M)). Nothing models staff pulling the ADA right-of-way line as a funding source for APS, or a reframing event that changes specified without a full PW3 start.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.6 (~line 257): general-fund ADA public right-of-way $55M (FY26-30) and $71M (FY31-35), $125M/10 years, which flows to curb ramps. 01 §2.6: the capital plan says accessibility capital is 'usually reflected in other departments' budgets, including transport and signals (APS)'. 01 §2.7 (~line 279): both MDC support letters went to curb ramps and none to APS. 01 §2.7: federal schedule duty exists for ramps (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)) and not for APS. The 2006 MDC resolution set a 25% target by 2010 and reached about 9-10%.
proposals.parameter: p_ada_frame
proposals.range: p_ada_frame U(0, 0.3) per year; s_ada U(0, 0.05) of the ADA right-of-way line (about $0-3M/yr; this fraction is inferred); t_ada U(6, 36) months. At 0 the model reduces to the current one.
proposals.rule_modified: D10 A_local (new source term) and D3.1 p_start (specified switched on temporarily). Does not change HSIP rules D3.3.

proposals.behaviour: Cost re-attribution to the curb-ramp programme. MOD staff reframe the over-plan conduit and ramp lines as ADA curb-ramp transition obligations, not APS costs. They push to move part of that cost to the DPW curb-ramp budget, or to schedule the sites with planned DPW ramp or paving work. MOD co-funded and ranked that programme in 2008. Curb ramps carry a federal transition-plan deadline and APS does not.
proposals.trigger: The design-complete cost discovery (F-f, overrun beyond the contingency) at a site whose ramp or conduit work is a large share of the cost. It is stronger when the ramp share exceeds some fraction of the cost.
proposals.effect_in_model: At the F-f funding-gap step, part of the above-contingency gap is paid from another budget instead of going to the q_topup request, which would otherwise end in TERMINATED. A shift takes t_shift months, and it may also shorten the construction wait if the work is bundled. That lowers the share of sites TERMINATED after design and raises the share of M-C sites installed.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-f says the same cost is counted once, and the only gap source is the q_topup top-up (the SFCTA 13th St precedent). PW4 'merge into existing projects' moves a site onto a parent project's schedule, but it does not split costs with a ramp programme. A grep of 02 finds no DPW. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7 line 281 (MOD co-funded and ranked the DPW curb-ramp programme, 2008 transition plan p.3). 01 line 284 (curb ramps have a 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) timeline duty, APS does not). 01 line 282 (ODA deputy director asked DPW and MTA to coordinate). 01 line 279 (both MDC letters, 2025-04 and 2026-04-16, were about curb ramps, none about APS). 01 line 117 (excavation triggers ramp work). The share of cost that can legally be reassigned has no document support.
proposals.parameter: phi_ramp_shift
proposals.range: Share of the ramp-and-conduit part of the F-f gap moved to the ramp budget: U(0, 0.5), default 0. Success probability q_shift U(0, 0.6). Delay t_shift U(1, 9) months. All inferred.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f: the gap above contingency is first reduced by phi_ramp_shift x ramp share with probability q_shift. Only the remainder goes to the q_topup request.

proposals.behaviour: Timed support letter or resolution aimed at the top-up decision. MOD staff use the one annual MDC advocacy slot at the moment the overrun is discovered. The letter goes to the funding body (SFCTA Board or SFMTA Board) that decides the supplemental request. It does not go to the agency that has to apply.
proposals.trigger: An F-f overrun or a pending q_topup request, together with an MDC meeting inside a window. The 01 notes say the MDC activation rule is unknown, so this is a probability.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises q_topup for a limited time for the affected batch, and can shorten t_pause. It does not change the start probability in D3.1.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. MDC is counted inside the generic advocacy channel C2, and pressure(t) only enters p_start (D3.1). The only enforcement boost is the lawsuit step in PW3. Nothing makes advocacy act on the top-up decision in F-f/F-e, so the targeted part is not captured. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 73 (MDC and ODA can only advise: resolutions, hearings, support letters; 'about one chance a year'; the rule for when they act is unknown). 01 line 283 (ODA staff proposed to 'follow up with MTA and DPW, then propose support-letter recommendations', not observed afterwards). 01 line 285 (2006 resolution). The effect on q_topup has no document support.
proposals.parameter: d_qtopup_letter
proposals.range: Additive change to q_topup while a letter is active: U(0, 0.25), default 0. Probability that a letter is issued within the window of an overrun, p_letter U(0, 0.4). Letter lifetime 6 months.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f and F-e: q_topup becomes min(1, q_topup + d_qtopup_letter) when a letter is active. Only the single event, the top-up request, is affected.

proposals.behaviour: Raising legal exposure. MOD staff or the Council pass the overrun to the city attorney, the ADA coordinator or the senior signal engineer as a litigation-risk item (the batch is the only funded APS stream, so a halt means no spending at all). They make a lawsuit risk visible in time to affect the supplemental decision.
proposals.trigger: The batch stalls: the overrun is above contingency and no q_topup has been granted, or the project is about to become TERMINATED.
proposals.effect_in_model: A temporary rise of enforce(t) at the moment of the stall. It raises both p_start for later windows and the chance of a top-up. It does not need the PW3 lawsuit.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. enforce(t) and eps_enf exist, but only PW3 raises it (negotiation then lawsuit, D1 tiers). A rise from a stalled batch inside a run is not captured. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 112 (the senior engineer names the 'litigation environment' as a reason for doing curbs together). 01 line 282 (the ODA deputy director explained NYC's speed by a federal court order). 01 line 92 (outside enforcement may have a large multiplier, rate unknown). The size and the trigger have no document support.
proposals.parameter: eps_flag
proposals.range: Jump in enforce(t) after a stall: U(0, 0.3), default 0, decaying over k months. Probability of use p_flag U(0, 0.3).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start (the beta_enf x enforce(t) term) and F-f (q_topup): a stall event adds eps_flag to enforce(t).

proposals.behaviour: Standing down after a promised follow-up. When the agency answers with 'cost is high, no funding' or 'we will study it', MOD staff accept the verbal promise and wait. The follow-up they proposed is not done, so the MDC channel stays quiet until the next scheduled meeting. This is a conflict-avoiding delay, driven by the answer.
proposals.trigger: A DEFLECTED event from D3.1, or a verbal commitment in answer to an overrun briefing.
proposals.effect_in_model: After such an answer, the MDC part of pressure(t) drops to zero for t_wait months with probability 1 - p_followup. This hurts the pathways that rely on pressure to restart a halted batch and pushes outcomes toward never_served. A switch p_followup = 1 gives the active version.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-m has random pressure interruptions (lambda_quiet, t_quiet), and DEFLECTED only ends the one pressure event ('no lasting effect'). Quiet that is caused by the agency's answer, and so correlated with it, is not captured. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 283 (the proposed follow-up and support letter were not observed afterwards). 01 line 288 (the next listed MDC date, 2026-09-18, page returns 404). 01 line 287 (no public comment at the 2026-07-17 item). 01 line 73 (no APS action found in 2024-26). The size has no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_followup
proposals.range: Probability of a real follow-up after a deflection: U(0, 0.6), default 0.3. Quiet period t_wait U(3, 12) months.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch and F-m: each deflection starts a quiet period of the MDC channel (pressure term set to 0) with probability 1 - p_followup.

proposals.behaviour: Ramp cost carve-out. MOD/MDC staff argue that the new curb ramps (and possibly conduit shared with ramp work) are an ADA transition-plan obligation, not APS cost, and push to move that line item to the DPW curb-ramp programme (which MOD co-prioritises and which has a federal timetable duty). The APS batch then keeps only the signal/APS hardware and the funding gap shrinks.
proposals.trigger: Design complete (t_des) and realised cost exceeds planned cost x (1+kappa_cont), i.e. the F-f gap that would otherwise go to a q_topup request or termination.
proposals.effect_in_model: At the F-f gap step, before the top-up request, a fraction of the ramp-related cost (the q_ramp $200k add-on) is reassigned to an external ramp budget. Gap is reduced, so fewer sites TERMINATED. Adds a new delay (ramp programme sequencing) for the affected site and a possible dependency on DPW schedule.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. 02 F-f only offers contingency, then q_topup, then TERMINATED. 02 line 51 and D10 treat q_ramp only as a cost add-on charged to APS; no other budget line can absorb it. (Cost 'counted once' rule in F-f is about double counting, not re-assignment.)
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 (lines 281, 284): MOD co-funds and ranks DPW curb ramps under the ADA transition plan; ramps carry a federal timetable duty (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)) while APS does not; ODA staff asked for DPW/MTA coordination (line 283-ish, 'ODA staff proposed follow-up with MTA, DPW'); MDC support letters so far all concern ramps (line 279).
proposals.parameter: q_ramp_shift (probability) and f_ramp_shift (share of ramp add-on moved to the ramp programme), with t_ramp_wait (months extra wait for the ramp programme)
proposals.range: q_ramp_shift U(0, 0.7); f_ramp_shift U(0.3, 1.0); t_ramp_wait U(3, 18) months. Set q_ramp_shift = 0 for control.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f funding-gap resolution (inserted between 'contingency' and 'q_topup'); D3.4 internal delivery start date for affected sites

proposals.behaviour: Partial descoping and sequencing instead of all-or-nothing termination. Staff advocate keeping the cheap sites in the batch and deferring the expensive conduit/ramp sites to a later cycle, so the council can say the batch 'delivered' while the costly sites are re-queued with a named owner and date.
proposals.trigger: Gap after contingency exceeds what q_topup would plausibly cover, but a subset of sites in the batch is still within budget; advocacy pressure(t) is non-zero.
proposals.effect_in_model: At F-f, instead of terminating each over-budget site independently, the batch is re-ranked by cost; sites are dropped from the top of cost until the batch fits, and dropped sites go back to the pool with a deferral flag (not a fresh TERMINATED). Changes the count of installs now vs later and creates a visible 'deferred but committed' state that could raise owner/specified for those sites.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 F-f says the project or 'that site' is TERMINATED and returns to the pool, and D3.4 says terminated sites return to the backlog. But there is no rule that picks which sites to drop by cost to save the rest, no deferral state, and no commitment attached to the deferred ones.
proposals.evidence: No document support for the descoping move itself. Indirect: 01 s2.7 MDC/ODA only have advisory tools (resolutions, support letters), consistent with asking for a re-sequenced commitment rather than money; 2006 resolution asked for priority by earliest request (01 s2.7, decision rule row).
proposals.parameter: sw_descope (switch) with theta_commit (months within which deferred sites must be re-funded)
proposals.range: sw_descope in {0,1}; theta_commit U(6, 36) months; with sw_descope=1 the deferred sites get specified=1 for their next attempt
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f termination rule (per-site termination replaced by cost-ranked batch trimming); D3.4 TERMINATED step (add DEFERRED state)

proposals.behaviour: Timed advocacy to hit a budget window. Rather than writing a support letter or resolution straight away, the Council times a resolution/hearing request to coincide with the next annual budget or Prop L allocation decision, so the top-up request for the overrun is considered when decision-makers are already choosing among items.
proposals.trigger: A funding gap is flagged (F-f) and the next local budget/allocation window is within a few months; letter is held until then.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises q_topup during a window and lowers it outside one. Today q_topup is a single flat probability; this makes it depend on the calendar and on whether advocacy pressure arrives inside the window. Also introduces an advocacy waiting delay.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. 02 has pressure(t) as a decaying sum that feeds p_start only (D3.1), and C2 advocates produce pressure at a constant rate lambda_press with no timing logic. q_topup (D10) is a flat U(0, 0.7) and not affected by pressure or calendar.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: MDC has about one influence opportunity per year (row 'MDC influence channel', 0 binding force); ODA staff said they would return to 'recommend and write support letters' later but follow-up was not observed (line 283-ish, 2026-07 and 2026-09 agenda rows). The 13th St top-up precedent is in 01 s2.11 (cited in F-f). Timing-to-window is no document support.
proposals.parameter: beta_topup_press (effect of recent pressure on q_topup, logit) and sw_window_timing (switch: letter held until next allocation window), with t_hold
proposals.range: beta_topup_press U(0, 2) logit per unit pressure; sw_window_timing in {0,1}; t_hold U(0, 9) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f top-up request (q_topup becomes q_topup = logistic(a + beta_topup_press * pressure(t)) x window indicator); C2 pressure event scheduling

proposals.behaviour: Informal pre-clearance of the overrun with the operating department before the formal request. Staff phone the project owner and the funding body so the top-up arrives pre-agreed (or is quietly rejected before it is ever formally filed). Outcome is that a share of overruns are resolved or dropped without a visible request event, and a share of 'quiet kills' occur with no TERMINATED log until later.
proposals.trigger: Overrun found at design completion and the owner's strain(t) is high or the owner has weak 'owner' level; relationships between MOD staff and the department are cooperative.
proposals.effect_in_model: Shortens decision time (q_topup resolved faster) and creates a hidden-failure lag: some projects stall in a 'not yet filed' state for t_stall months before TERMINATED. Changes timing outputs and the interpretation of 'never_served'.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-f goes directly from overrun to a q_topup request and then either approval or termination; there is no pre-request negotiation stage or unfiled stall. Closest rule is F-e t_pause (wait before re-requesting) but that applies only to the outsourcing differential, not to the general overrun path.
proposals.evidence: No document support (no source describes informal pre-clearance). Weakly consistent with 01 s2.1-type 'actors pass the buck, answer is no money' (line 131, author primary account) which suggests the formal route is often a dead end and informal channels matter.
proposals.parameter: t_stall (months overrun sits unfiled) and q_preclear (share of overruns settled informally before filing)
proposals.range: q_preclear U(0, 0.4); t_stall U(0, 9) months; q_preclear=0 for control
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-f between overrun detection and the q_topup request (adds an UNFILED state of length t_stall before the request or silent termination)

proposals.behaviour: Cost-shifting by re-attribution: the MOD/MDC staffer argues that the new conduit and curb-ramp work is ADA transition-plan (curb ramp) scope, not APS scope, and pushes to charge that share to the Public Works curb-ramp program. One project's cost is split across two lines and the overrun leaves the APS batch.
proposals.trigger: Design finishes and the overrun is discovered (F-f) with the gap above contingency kappa_cont. The staffer can point to the federal ramp-schedule duty that APS lacks.
proposals.effect_in_model: At the F-f funding-gap step, before the q_topup draw, a fraction of the gap tied to ramp/conduit moves to a second funder (the DPW ramp program). The APS gap shrinks, so TERMINATED is less likely. If the ramp budget refuses, the shift fails and adds t_shift months of delay. Cost is still counted once; only the payer changes.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. 02 D3.5 F-f counts pipe/ramp once in planned cost and sends any gap only to q_topup or TERMINATED. D3.4 has no cross-line cost transfer. F-g (partner unbinding) is a different thing.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: ramps carry a transition-plan schedule duty (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)) that APS lacks; MOD co-funded and ranked DPW ramps in 2008. 01 s2.11: DPW reserves for future APS but ramp construction does not trigger APS ('APS is MTA's business'); ramp budget FY27/28 $8.1M/$12.2M. No document shows such a shift actually happening.
proposals.parameter: q_ramp_shift U(0, 0.4) (probability the shift is attempted and accepted); f_ramp U(0.2, 0.7) (ramp/conduit share of the gap); t_shift U(1, 6) months; switch sw_ramp_shift 0/1.
proposals.range: q_ramp_shift 0-0.4; f_ramp 0.2-0.7; t_shift 1-6 months
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f gap resolution order becomes: contingency -> ramp shift -> q_topup -> TERMINATED.

proposals.behaviour: Triage by deferral instead of termination: the office/council pushes to keep over-budget sites on the list in a deferred queue that keeps their original request-age priority, while affordable sites go ahead. The site does not return to the pool as a fresh item.
proposals.trigger: Gap beyond contingency and the topup draw failed or is slow, for some sites in a locally funded batch.
proposals.effect_in_model: A failed-topup site enters DEFERRED, not TERMINATED. It keeps its queue rank and waits for the next funding window. Cheaper sites proceed, so installs continue. Changes who is served first and the never_served count.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.5 F-f sends failed topup to TERMINATED and D3.4 'project termination' returns the site to the pool in original state. There is no rank-preserving deferral and no choice of which sites to cut.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: the 2006-03 MDC resolution asks to prioritise the earliest requests. No document support for a deferral queue itself.
proposals.parameter: sw_defer_keep 0/1; p_defer_keep U(0, 1) (share of failed-topup sites put in DEFERRED); rank_rule in {cost-ascending, request-age}.
proposals.range: p_defer_keep 0-1
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.4 project-termination item 4 and F-f TERMINATED branch; site ordering in the install queue.

proposals.behaviour: Event-triggered advocacy: after a visible overrun or stall, the staffer helps prepare a Council support letter or hearing item to the budget bodies (CPC / Mayor's budget staff), which raises the chance of a top-up for that project. In the model pressure arrives at a fixed random rate regardless of cost events.
proposals.trigger: A project enters 'overrun beyond contingency' or 'topup pending'. The Council's next meeting gates when the letter can go out.
proposals.effect_in_model: On overrun, with probability p_react a pressure event is created after lag t_meet (0-3 months). It multiplies q_topup by (1 + g_letter) for that project only and adds to pressure(t). This gives a reactive channel that can be tested at zero.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. 02 D3.1 pressure(t) is driven by exogenous lambda_press (D10 l.340) with F-m interruptions. No pressure depends on a cost event.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: MDC sent letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 on ramp funding (so a funding-triggered channel exists for ramps); ODA staff proposed a support letter after 2026-07-17 but none was seen by 2026-09-18; 01 s2.8 shows little advocate activity, so p_react may be low.
proposals.parameter: p_react U(0, 0.5); t_meet U(0, 3) months; g_letter U(0, 0.5).
proposals.range: p_react 0-0.5; t_meet 0-3 months; g_letter 0-0.5
proposals.rule_modified: q_topup in 02 D3.5 F-f, plus a cost-event source added to pressure(t) in D3.1.

proposals.behaviour: Support-letter / framing action by the Mayor's Office on Disability (MOD) staff: draft or prompt a Disability Council (MDC) support letter to the SFCTA board and CPC that frames the APS line as an ADA access-parity item next to the curb-ramp transition obligation, rather than as one more competing capital request. The letter is a one-off event timed before the board vote.
proposals.trigger: The Prop L EP17 amendment is calendared at the SFCTA board (or a deferral is signalled). Fires with probability p_letter once per amendment event. A prior curb-ramp letter makes the habit more likely.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the chance that the amendment is vetoed or deferred (F-j) for that event only. It does not create money. It also adds to pressure(t) for k months. The letter's weight is capped, so it cannot undo a hard over-programming constraint.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. 02 has MDC only as a label inside C2 (line 61). F-j has q_veto and t_defer as exogenous draws with no advocacy-driven shift. PW3 raises owner/specified/oversight but has no letter event. No 02 rule gives MDC/MOD a discrete action.
