proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: ODA staff proposed to 'follow up with MTA, DPW ... then propose recommendations and support letters' after 2026-07-17, with no follow-up observed (line 283). The two letters actually sent covered curb ramps only, zero for APS (line 279). So letter activation for APS is undocumented; p_letter must span 0 to a modest value.
proposals.parameter: p_letter (P of an MDC/MOD support letter per amendment event) and delta_veto_letter (multiplicative cut to q_veto when sent)
proposals.range: p_letter U(0, 0.6); delta_veto_letter U(0.5, 1.0), where 1.0 means the letter has no effect. Baseline p_letter = 0 reproduces the observed 2024-26 silence.
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (q_veto, t_defer) and the pressure(t) term in p_start (D3.1)

proposals.behaviour: Scope-language lock-in: instead of fighting for a dedicated APS line at a time when EP17 is over-programmed, MOD staff push for written wording in the amendment or in the SG017 allocation request. The wording says the hardware-replacement line may fund 'install new APS where existing poles and conduit allow', and APS is named as a priority use. This blocks a later reading limited to 'replace'. MOD asks for words, not dollars.
proposals.trigger: Over-programming becomes visible in the amendment staff report, or controller-replacement outages make a dedicated line look unlikely to pass. It also fires before the FY27/FY28 SG017 allocation.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds an alternative outcome to F-j: 'amendment passes in scope-language-only form'. The dedicated line stays closed (PW2 only partly succeeds), but PW6 becomes safer. It lowers q_sg017_block. It does not stop outage-driven controller replacement from using the cash first.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 has q_sg017_block (scope limited to 'replace', or money taken by controller failures) as a fixed draw. 02 has no actor who acts to lower it, and no 'wording-only' result of the amendment. Keep only the actor-driven shift in q_sg017_block and the new outcome branch.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 446: the SG017 CIP scope text already allows new APS. Line 447: FY25-26 SG017 money went to about 98 controller replacements, and FY27-28 use is unknown. Together these show the exact fight a MOD staff member would see. No document shows MOD actually drafting wording, so mark that part 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: p_scope_lock (P that the amendment is passed or amended with APS-inclusive scope wording) and delta_block (relative cut to q_sg017_block when scope_lock = 1)
proposals.range: p_scope_lock U(0, 0.5); delta_block U(0.3, 1.0), with 1.0 meaning no effect
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 (q_sg017_block) and the F-j outcome set (adds a 'scope-wording-only' branch)

proposals.behaviour: Conditional trade: when the board signals a veto because outage-driven controller replacements must come first, MOD staff offer to accept deferral or a controller-first order in return for a dated commitment. The commitment could be a named APS tranche in the next 5YPP cycle, a reporting duty, or a trigger clause saying 'APS funds if controller backlog falls below N'. This turns a hard veto into a soft deferral that carries conditions.
proposals.trigger: A veto or reallocation toward outages is signalled (a draw from q_veto, or the controller-failure state is high). MOD agrees with probability p_trade.
proposals.effect_in_model: Converts a share of vetoes into deferrals. The deferral gets a fixed return date (the next 5YPP window, 2027 autumn to 2028). oversight is raised for the commitment period. Outages are served first and APS later. Cost: an APS-specific tranche in the next cycle is not guaranteed (a failure draw q_honor).
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-j already lists 'wait for the next 5YPP' as a recovery path, but only as a passive fallback after a veto. It has no conditional bargain, no conversion of veto to deferral, and no oversight increase tied to the trade.
proposals.evidence: no document support for this behaviour. Nearest lines: 01 §2.3 D4 precedent of a 3-4 month deferral (cited in 02 F-j), and 01 line 447 on controller-replacement priority. The bargaining behaviour itself is a hypothesis.
proposals.parameter: p_trade (share of signalled vetoes converted to conditional deferral) and q_honor (P the later commitment is honoured at the next window)
proposals.range: p_trade U(0, 0.5); q_honor U(0.3, 0.9)
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (adds branch: veto -> conditional deferral with oversight raised and a dated re-entry to PW2), plus oversight(t) in p_start

proposals.behaviour: Ramp-cost re-attribution (cost shifting to the curb-ramp program). Staff reframe the conduit and curb-ramp part of the overrun as ADA right-of-way / curb-ramp work, which has a federal transition-plan duty and a growing dedicated line, and ask Public Works / the ramp program (or the General Fund ADA right-of-way line) to carry that share. The APS line then only needs to cover the APS hardware remainder. Logic: 'the ramp is owed regardless of APS'.
proposals.trigger: Overrun found at design completion (F-f) where the excess comes from new conduit (q_pipe) or new ramp (q_ramp) items and exceeds contingency kappa_cont, before a top-up request is filed.
proposals.effect_in_model: In F-f, a share of the gap that is tagged ramp-type is moved to a second funder with its own acceptance probability, instead of the whole gap going to the single q_topup draw. Raises survival of the site, lowers the TERMINATED rate and the top-up needed from SFCTA/SFMTA. Adds a cost line to cost_by_actor for Public Works. Risk path: the ramp program queue delays the site (adds t_ramp_wait months).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.2/F-f counts pipe and ramp costs once and sends any gap above contingency to one q_topup request, then TERMINATED. 02 has no second funder and no re-attribution of the ramp share. 02 lines 51 and 357 (q_pipe, q_ramp) only add cost. So the behaviour is NOT captured; only the cost is.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 (ODA row ~line 282-284): ramps carry a federal transition-plan time duty (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)) while APS has none; ODA deputy said the ramp budget 'will rise a lot' and asked DPW and MTA to coordinate. 01 s2.11 (~line 373, 376): ramp lines $4.0M to $8.1M/$12.2M; DPW designs ramps with APS reserved but ramp construction does not trigger APS. 01 s2.6 (~line 256): the City ADA right-of-way allocation of $125M/10y flows to ramps. 01 line 117: excavation triggers ramp renovation. No document shows this has actually been done for APS overruns, so the behaviour itself has no direct document support.
proposals.parameter: phi_ramp_shift (share of the ramp-tagged gap that staff move to the ramp program) with q_ramp_accept (probability the ramp program accepts) and t_ramp_wait (extra delay)
proposals.range: phi_ramp_shift in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1}, with 0 as the current baseline; q_ramp_accept U(0.1, 0.8); t_ramp_wait U(3, 18) months
proposals.rule_modified: F-f gap-funding step (after contingency, before q_topup draw) and TERMINATED rule; adds a funder to cost_by_actor

proposals.behaviour: Event-triggered escalation through the advisory channel. When a site faces a funding gap, staff turn the case into a concrete advocacy product: place it on the Disability Council agenda, draft a support letter or resolution, and brief advocacy organisations so that a timed burst of pressure lands on the budget decision-makers. Pressure is concentrated on the specific gap rather than arriving at the random background rate.
proposals.trigger: Unfunded gap after contingency (F-f) or a TERMINATED project; also a long idle spell with no APS filing (the F-m quiet period) when a visible case becomes available.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds one pressure(t) pulse and increases q_topup by a bump that decays after k months. The pulse is conditional on the overrun event, whereas current lambda_press is exogenous and unrelated to project state. Escalation may also have a cost: staff capacity use (limits how many cases can be escalated per year).
proposals.already_in_model: Only partly. 02 C2 (line 61) and lambda_press/k/lambda_quiet generate pressure at a fixed random rate; 02 treats MDC as an information channel with an unknown activation rule to be tested at zero and non-zero. Nothing in 02 ties pressure or a letter to a specific overrun event or to q_topup. So the event-conditional coupling is new.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 (~line 279, 283, 311): the Council's tools are advisory only (resolutions, hearings, letters to the capital planning committee); two letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 both covered ramps, none covered APS; ODA staff proposed follow-up with MTA/DPW and a support letter after 2026-07-17 and no follow-up was seen; 01 line 311 says activation is an unknown parameter. The existence of a ramp letter (a funded-cause precedent) supports feasibility; no document shows APS letters or case-specific escalation.
proposals.parameter: p_escalate (probability staff escalate a given gap event) and delta_topup (increase in q_topup when escalated, decaying over k months)
proposals.range: p_escalate U(0, 0.8) (0 = baseline), capped by n_esc_max 1-2 per year; delta_topup U(0, 0.3) added to q_topup and clipped at 1; also adds one extra pressure pulse
proposals.rule_modified: F-f top-up draw (q_topup) and pressure(t) accumulator in D3.1 p_start; also links lambda_press to project state

proposals.behaviour: Strategic timing: hold the request for a better budget window instead of asking at once. Staff recommend that the overrun request not be filed now, but waited into the next capital budget / five-year program update or the annual ramp-line appropriation (a bundle with the ramp request), and may ask that the batch be paused or re-sequenced so that the overrun sites ride a later ask while the cheaper sites go ahead.
proposals.trigger: Gap exceeds contingency while the next appropriation or program-amendment window is more than a few months away, or when a recent request by the same office was just refused (a refusal makes an immediate re-ask costly).
proposals.effect_in_model: Replaces the immediate q_topup draw by a deferral: the affected sites wait until the next window, then draw q_topup (possibly with a different, higher probability because the request is built into the budget cycle). Sites in the same batch that have no overrun are released to proceed (re-sequencing). Adds delay but lowers TERMINATED rate, and shows a trade-off between speed and survival.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 F-e has a single pause t_pause then one re-request; F-f has one q_topup draw with no timing choice; F-j has deferral for the Prop L amendment only. Re-sequencing the batch to split overrun sites from the others is also absent (02 D3.1 splitting concerns application bundling, not post-award batches). Window-waiting for the F-f top-up is not written.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.6 (~line 256-258): the General Fund ADA allocation and the mayor's capital priority listing curb ramps and barrier removal; 01 s2.11 (~line 373): ramp lines step up in FY27/28 ($8.1M/$12.2M), which is a visible window. 01 s2.3 and 02 F-j record 3-4 month precedents for Prop L amendment timing. No document shows the office deferring a request; behaviour is hypothesised.
proposals.parameter: sw_wait_window (switch) with t_window_gap (months to next window) and q_topup_window (top-up probability when filed in a window)
proposals.range: sw_wait_window in {0, 1}, 0 = baseline; t_window_gap U(3, 24) months from the budget calendar; q_topup_window = q_topup + U(0, 0.25)
proposals.rule_modified: F-f top-up path: adds a deferral branch before q_topup; D3.4 internal queue (non-overrun sites released early)

proposals.behaviour: Information brokering that changes which gaps become visible: staff push the delivery team to run early joint scoping with Public Works and utilities (surveys of conduit and curb conditions) before design is complete, so that the cost surprise is found earlier or lands in a combined project. Under the same lens, staff also want conduit/ramp-heavy sites officially dropped or re-tagged as ramp-driven projects so they do not count as APS failures.
proposals.trigger: A prior batch showed an overrun at design completion; Council oversight asks for a status report.
proposals.effect_in_model: Moves the discovery time of overrun earlier (before funding is committed) and lets the site be re-routed (to ramp/capital bundle) rather than being awarded and then TERMINATED. Changes the shape of F-f from late-discovered to early-discovered, and reduces wasted design cost.
proposals.already_in_model: No for the early scoping. 02 D3.4 states 'no early investigation' ('不另设提前调查') and fixes discovery at the design-completion node. Weak overlap with PW4 (assign by intersection) but PW4 does not change discovery time.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.11 (~line 375-376): Contract 35 delays came partly from ramp design capacity and survey backlog; 01 line 117: APS needs existing countdown signals and excavation triggers ramp work. No document says staff push for earlier scoping; it is a hypothesis. 02 D3.4 explicitly excludes it as a modelling choice, so it is a design choice rather than an omission, and may be dropped if the team wants to keep it out.
proposals.parameter: p_prescope (probability that conduit/ramp conditions are pre-surveyed) with t_prescope lead time
proposals.range: p_prescope U(0, 0.6) (0 = baseline in 02); lead time t_prescope U(2, 8) months; effect: shifts the overrun draw to funding time with probability p_prescope
proposals.rule_modified: F-f discovery node in D3.4 (design-completion draw moved earlier) and TERMINATED rule

proposals.behaviour: Placeholder or token line: staff and the Council accept, or even propose, restoring the APS line in the 5YPP as a named line with a small or contingent amount (for example a reserve funded only if the over-programming clears), instead of the full dedicated amount. The line exists on paper but holds little money.
proposals.trigger: The board is over-programmed in EP17 and controller replacement after outages competes for the same dollars. A full-size ask looks likely to be vetoed or deferred, and a symbolic win keeps the issue on the agenda.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the chance of veto or deferral (F-j) because the amendment costs the board almost nothing. It also shrinks the local batch the line can fund and the rate at which it can fund it. The line can sit unfunded for months, so the PW2 signal 'amendment approved' fires without any APS money flowing. It also feeds a later argument for a top-up.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-j and PW2 treat the amendment as a binary pass or fail with the full dedicated line. The 'FY26-28 uncommitted margin $0-0.5M/yr' in O2 sets the budget but not a negotiable line size. The 'local special line open' state is binary.
proposals.evidence: No document support for the behaviour itself. Indirect support: 01 §2.7 shows the Council's tools are advisory only, with 0 APS letters, and 02 O2 gives the EP17 margin as $0-0.5M/yr.
proposals.parameter: line_size_ratio (rho_line): the share of the full dedicated line that the approved amendment actually funds. It can also be a switch, amend_form in {full, token}. Rule modified: F-j, where q_veto_eff = q_veto * (1 - a*(1 - rho_line)) with a in U(0.3, 0.8), and the local batch size in D3.4.
proposals.range: rho_line in U(0.1, 1.0); a in U(0.3, 0.8) (inferred)
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (q_veto and the PW2 trigger), plus the local special line budget in D3.4

proposals.behaviour: Logrolling or side deal with the controller side: staff and the Council publicly back the priority of replacing failed controllers, and in return seek informal board or staff commitment that APS gets a carve-out or a first call on later savings. This is an informal trade of support between two competing uses of the same fund, not a formal rule.
proposals.trigger: Controller replacements after outages are salient and politically hard to oppose, and the amendment is on the same board agenda. Opposing them would sink the amendment; supporting them could buy a vote.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers q_veto and t_defer for the amendment, and lowers the chance that the SG017 money is taken by failures (q_sg017_block, PW6). In return it moves controller projects ahead in the queue, so APS funding lags until the controller backlog is cleared. This gives a time lag in PW2 and PW6.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. q_sg017_block is a one-way exogenous probability that failures consume the money (02 D10, F-j and PW6). No mechanism lets an actor trade away the conflict. M-A to M-D contain no coalition rule.
proposals.evidence: No document support for a deal. 01 §2.7 notes the ODA deputy asked DPW and MTA to coordinate a strategy, and the 'follow up with MTA, DPW' proposal after 2026-07-17 was never observed. That shows coordination talk without action. 02 line 285 says SG017 was historically spent on controllers.
proposals.parameter: logroll_flag (0/1), with an effect size delta_logroll that cuts q_veto and q_sg017_block and adds a delay t_logroll to the first APS drawdown. Rule modified: F-j and q_sg017_block.
proposals.range: delta_logroll in U(0, 0.4) as a relative cut in q_veto and q_sg017_block; t_logroll in U(0, 18) months (all inferred)
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (q_veto), q_sg017_block (PW6), and the timing of the first APS drawdown

proposals.behaviour: Spec-first or APS-ready controller language: instead of fighting for money, staff ask that controller replacement purchases be specified as APS-compatible (the hardware and cabinet capability for later APS install), so a replacement does not lock in a non-compliant controller. Money for the APS buttons themselves is deferred.
proposals.trigger: The controller replacement budget is the one pot of money actually moving, and the APS line is blocked or delayed. Setting the specification costs the board little and creates a later cheaper APS install at that intersection.
proposals.effect_in_model: At replaced controllers, the unit cost u0 of a later APS install drops, and the intersection becomes eligible for the cheaper local or hardware-change route. It does not install APS at once. It raises the pool of C-type intersections that PW5 and PW6 can serve cheaply, and it pushes the first install later than a funded line would.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly captured: PW5 puts APS into a hardware or button replacement work order, and PW6 writes APS into the SG017 grant request. Not captured: an upstream spec change that only makes later installs cheaper without installing anything. Keep only this narrow part.
proposals.evidence: No document support for a spec change. The model's PW5 and PW6 (02 D3.6) use replacement events as the carrier, which implies the carrier idea. 01 §2.7 gives MOD only advisory tools, which is why a specification request fits its role.
proposals.parameter: ready_spec (0/1) with cost cut kappa_ready. Rule modified: the unit cost u0 for C-type intersections whose controller was replaced after the switch date, and the eligibility test for the 'existing poles and conduit usable' route in PW6.
proposals.range: kappa_ready in U(0.05, 0.3) as a cut in u0; applies only to intersections replaced after the switch date (inferred)
proposals.rule_modified: u0 for C-type intersections after controller replacement; PW6 eligibility test; PW5 hardware-change event

proposals.behaviour: Withdraw-and-retarget (waiting for a better window). When staff signal the amendment will lose to controller-replacement needs or the board will not add a line to an over-programmed EP17, the Disability Council side asks the proponent to pull or hold the amendment and re-file it as a priority in the 2027-28 5-year plan update, while keeping the item on the record via a letter or informational report.
proposals.trigger: A staff recommendation or board signal of denial/deferral on the amendment, or a recent outage that raises controller-replacement urgency; the next full 5-year plan cycle (starts 2027 fall) is visible on the calendar.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes the PW2 branch. Today the amendment is either approved, or vetoed/deferred and the path then falls through to General Fund or HSIP. With this switch the proponent can choose a third exit, 'hold for the 5YPP window', which delays the local line but avoids a recorded veto (q_veto) and avoids the fall-through to a worse fund. It also lets the amendment skip a loss in an outage-heavy month.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j (02 D3.5) lists 'wait for the next 5YPP round' as one outcome after a board veto or deferral, but it is something that happens to the proponent after the board acts. No rule lets the proponent withdraw before the vote and choose the timing. Not dropped because the voluntary, pre-vote choice is different from F-j.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'next strategic plan + 5YPP starts 2027 fall, passes 2028'; 'the next five years are not expected to have this level of over-programming' (EP17-5YPP p.11); EP17 committed $27.49M vs $8.52M pay-go. Also 01 section 2.3 D4 precedent: 3-4 months to get a 5YPP amendment through. No document shows a withdrawal in the APS case itself, so the behaviour is an inference.
proposals.parameter: p_withdraw_to_5YPP
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6), applied only when the pre-vote signal of denial or deferral exceeds a threshold (for example when q_veto drawn for this event is above 0.5, or when an outage event occurred in the previous t_outage months). If drawn, set the line's start to the 5YPP effective date and skip the veto/deferral branch.
proposals.rule_modified: PW2 trigger and F-j (02 D3.6 row PW2; D3.5 F-j): adds a pre-vote withdraw branch before q_veto is applied.

proposals.behaviour: Shrink-to-fit ask (symbolic or minimal line). Instead of a large dedicated APS line, the Disability Council staff supports a small, named line sized to the uncommitted headroom, or a 'floor' line, so that it displaces little of the controller money and so the board can say yes without choosing APS over controllers.
proposals.trigger: EP17 is over-programmed, so any big dedicated line directly competes with controller replacement; uncommitted headroom is $0-0.5M/yr.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the approval probability of the amendment and lowers the amount of APS money that arrives per year. Changes the size of the funded line from 'restored dedicated line' to a smaller line, so delivered intersections per year (D3.4) fall while the veto probability falls. Creates a trade-off the model can scan.
proposals.already_in_model: No. The model has a variable a_sg017 for how much of SG017 can go to APS (up to $250k) under PW6, but nothing for the size of the ask in the PW2 amendment or any link from ask size to q_veto. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: FY26-28 EP17 about $2.80M per year committed, with uncommitted $0-0.5M/yr (02 O2 line 64); the historical 19th Avenue APS project in Prop K EP33 was about $249k (01 section 2.3). No document shows anyone sizing an APS ask this way, so mark as no document support for the behaviour itself.
proposals.parameter: ask_scale (fraction of the full restoration line requested) with q_veto = q_veto0 * ask_scale^gamma
proposals.range: ask_scale U(0.2, 1.0); gamma U(0.5, 2.0). Funded APS dollars per year = ask_scale * line_full.
proposals.rule_modified: PW2 amendment rule and F-j: links the request size to q_veto and to the annual dollars that feed the local delivery batch.

proposals.behaviour: Controller-replacement rider: instead of competing with controller replacement, the Disability Council side asks that every controller replacement funded after an outage be 'APS-ready' (a specification or condition on the allocation), turning the competing use of money into a carrier of APS capability.
proposals.trigger: A controller-replacement allocation appears on the board agenda after an outage while the APS line is blocked; the Council staff can speak in public comment or send a letter at that meeting.
proposals.effect_in_model: Money for controller replacement stops being a pure 'block' and partly becomes an enabler: a fraction of replaced controllers lowers the cost or removes the technical barrier for adding APS at those intersections later (reduces u0 and raises the share of C-type intersections that can be done in-house). It can reduce the cost to the local batch in later years even if the dedicated line is never restored.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 puts new APS install into the SG017 allocation request and treats SG017 being used for controllers as a block (q_sg017_block, 02 D3.6 and D10). It does not model a condition on controller replacement making future installs cheaper. M-C2 in D3.2 (some C-type intersections cannot be installed locally because of technical reasons, share tau) is the closest existing barrier. Not dropped, because the model has no way to relax tau by controller replacement.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (OCT25 p.7, inference). 02 D3.2 row 'technically cannot install' (tau). No document support for an APS-ready condition being asked for.
proposals.parameter: rho_ready
proposals.range: U(0, 0.5) per year of controller replacement events: the share of controllers replaced after an outage that are APS-ready. Effect: tau is reduced by rho_ready * (replaced / C-type stock), and u0 is reduced by delta_u U(0, 0.3) at the replaced intersections.
proposals.rule_modified: M-C2 technical barrier (tau) and the u0 install cost in D3.3 and D3.4; an outage event now has a second effect besides consuming SG017 money.

proposals.behaviour: Side-channel through district funds and equity lines: the Council staff points advocates and a supervisor's office to the neighbourhood-level (district) program or the equity priority program, so a handful of APS intersections is funded by a district allocation without touching the EP17 line.
proposals.trigger: The EP17 amendment is deferred or looks likely to be denied; a district office is looking for a visible, small, disability-related project.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds an alternative small fund source outside the PW0-PW6 chain: a few APS intersections per year funded via the district route, with a short cycle (months) once chosen. Reduces dependence on the amendment, but only in some districts and only at small scale.
proposals.already_in_model: No. The grep of 02 for NTP, EP25 and EP26 returned no match; the fund list in O2 names only HSIP, EP17, General Fund/CIP, SS4A, and signal works. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: NTP (EP25) is $700k per district per 5 years; EP26 equity priority names persons with disabilities as a target ($47M); the D4 supervisor used $500k NTP in 2024-11 to design two signals with APS within 3-4 months (LW p.15-18).
proposals.parameter: p_district_route and n_district_per_year
proposals.range: p_district_route U(0, 0.3) per amendment-failure event (triggered after q_veto or t_defer); n_district_per_year U(0, 3) intersections for a funded event; cost per intersection uses the same full-cost c_full as in the local batch.
proposals.rule_modified: PW2 fallback chain (02 D3.6): inserts a district/equity branch between 'amendment vetoed' and 'General Fund annual request'.

proposals.behaviour: Letter-of-support and turnout campaign: MOD staff drafts a support letter for the Mayor's Disability Council (MDC) and recruits advocacy groups to the SFCTA board and Citizens Advisory Committee (CAC) so the amendment arrives with visible community backing. Support letters are the MDC's only formal tool.
proposals.trigger: The amendment is placed on a board agenda (or a date is announced). It is stronger when EP17 is already over-programmed, because staff expect resistance.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the chance and length of the board veto or deferral in F-j and PW2. Support is an endogenous event on the SFCTA node, separate from the generic advocacy pressure(t), which only feeds p_start in the task state machine. A letter also raises the 5YPP 'community support' and 'disadvantaged populations' scores, which weight 5 each out of 31.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j has exogenous q_veto and t_defer, and the advocacy pressure(t) variable exists. Nothing in the 02 rules (D3.1, D3.5 F-j, D3.6 PW2) links MOD or MDC letters to the veto probability. Keep it, but state it as a modifier of F-j rather than a new actor.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: the MDC has only advisory tools (resolutions, hearings, letters to the Capital Planning Committee); the 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 letters covered curb ramps only, 0 APS letters; after the 2026-07-17 meeting MOD staff proposed to 'follow up ... then recommend a support letter', with no follow-up observed. 01 s2.3: the CAC only advises and has backed EP17 5YPP and allocations consistently; no CAC question about the APS gap in the memos reviewed; 5YPP scoring puts disadvantaged-population and community-support criteria at 5 each. Behaviour rate: no document support for APS; the ramp-letter rate is the nearest anchor.
proposals.parameter: p_letter
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6) per amendment attempt; effect eps_letter U(0.1, 0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (D3.5): q_veto_eff = q_veto * (1 - eps_letter * letter), where letter ~ Bernoulli(p_letter) is drawn at the vote. Also shortens t_defer by the same factor.

proposals.behaviour: Conditional or partial amendment: the proponent accepts, or pre-negotiates, a reduced APS line (a smaller dollar amount or fewer fiscal years), a 'first call on savings' clause, or a ring-fence so controller replacements after outages cannot draw the money down. The board still approves, but weakly.
proposals.trigger: EP17 is over-programmed and controller replacements are outage-driven, high-priority claims. Staff foresee a flat refusal, so they trade amount for approval.
proposals.effect_in_model: Turns the F-j outcome from binary (pass or veto) into pass with a funded fraction f_line of the requested APS line. Separately, a ring-fence flag lowers the share of the line that outage-driven controller claims divert in later years. This changes how many C-type intersections the dedicated line can fund.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-j is veto or defer only. q_sg017_block (PW6) covers controllers taking the existing SG017 line, not the diversion of a new dedicated line after approval. Check that PW2 does not already assume full funding, then keep it.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: SFCTA responds to visible failure (controllers received EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages, OCT25 p.7, marked inference); EP17 is 202% ahead of pay-as-you-go; FY26-28 funds about $2.8M a year, all assigned to other lines; the strategic plan cut projects to 85-89% of priority 1. No document support that a partial or ring-fenced APS line was proposed.
proposals.parameter: f_line and q_ringfence
proposals.range: f_line U(0.2, 1.0) (1.0 = current model); q_ringfence U(0, 1), the probability that the diversion rate for the APS line is set to 0 rather than to the SG017 diversion rate
proposals.rule_modified: F-j and PW2 funding step. On approval, the local dedicated batch budget is multiplied by f_line, and each later fiscal year the line is reduced by the outage-diversion draw unless the ring-fence applies.

proposals.behaviour: Fund-source substitution to a district-discretionary or equity line: MOD staff steers the ask to a district supervisor, who funds APS from the Neighborhood Transportation Program (EP25) or the equity line (EP26), instead of or alongside the EP17 amendment. EP26 explicitly names people with disabilities.
proposals.trigger: The EP17 amendment is deferred or vetoed, or the board signals the line is over-programmed. A supervisor in a district with a pending request or a high-profile crash is the opening.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a parallel local money source with its own cap (about $700k per district over 5 years) and its own timing. A 5YPP revision in this route took 3-4 months, a much shorter lag than waiting for the next 5YPP. The money would fall between PW2 and 'general fund' in the path order.
proposals.already_in_model: No. PW2 falls back to the general fund, then HSIP. EP25 and EP26 do not appear in the pathways PW0-PW6 or in F-j. The ledger notes the Lincoln Way precedent, but only as evidence, not as a path.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: EP25 NTP is $700k per district over FY24-28; EP26 lists people with disabilities as a target ($47M); in 2024-11 a district supervisor used $500k of NTP to design two new signals with APS at Lincoln Way, and the 5YPP revision took 3-4 months (LW p.15-18).
proposals.parameter: sw_ntp_route (switch) with q_ntp
proposals.range: switch 0/1; q_ntp U(0, 0.4) probability per year that a sponsor emerges after an F-j failure; amount b_ntp U($100k, $500k) per success
proposals.rule_modified: PW2 fallback chain (D3.6): after F-j veto or deferral beyond theta_defer, try NTP/equity with q_ntp before the general-fund request; shortens the F-j recovery path.

proposals.behaviour: Strategic timing and withdrawal: staff holds the amendment back, or pulls it before the vote, until the controller backlog has been cleared by another allocation or until the item can ride the next 5YPP and strategic-plan cycle. This avoids a recorded veto and a longer lockout.
proposals.trigger: Vote-count or staff-recommendation signals are weak, or an outage has just made controllers the board's priority.
proposals.effect_in_model: Replaces part of the F-j veto probability with a controlled delay t_hold. A clean pre-vote withdrawal avoids a repeat-veto penalty. If it holds to the 2027 autumn 5YPP start, the amendment enters a full re-programming window, where EP17 capacity can be re-ranked.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j has t_defer after a veto and a fallback of 'next 5YPP (2027 autumn to 2028)'. A proponent-initiated hold before the vote is not written, nor the lock-out effect of a recorded veto (a vetoed item being harder to bring back). Keep only the proponent-initiated hold.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: the next strategic plan and 5YPP start in 2027 autumn and pass in 2028; the 'next 5-year period is not expected to be so far ahead' of pay-as-you-go. No document support for a withdrawal or a repeat-veto penalty.
proposals.parameter: p_hold
proposals.range: U(0, 0.5), probability that the amendment is held when the signal 'controller-outage claim pending' is on; t_hold U(3, 18) months
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (D3.5): with probability p_hold the draw of q_veto is skipped and a delay t_hold is applied instead; q_veto at the later date is multiplied by (1 - eps_hold) with eps_hold U(0, 0.3).

proposals.behaviour: Pre-submission scope intervention. Before the SG017 allocation request is finalized, the disability-office staffer sends a written inquiry or marked-up comment to SFMTA and SFCTA asking that the request text name a dollar share for new APS at C-type intersections with adequate poles and conduit. The aim is to change the content of the request, not to add general pressure. The model's pressure(t) only raises p_start for the whole task. PW6 treats the outcome as SFCTA scoping the grant to 'replace' (q_sg017_block). It has no actor who acts on the SFMTA draft itself.
proposals.trigger: The SG017 request is in PREPARING, and a staffer sees that the CIP scope text allows new APS while the last two allocations went to controllers. The staffer's capacity to act is limited, and they act only if a drafting window is visible (about 1 to 3 months before the request is filed).
proposals.effect_in_model: In PW6 and PW0, when an SG017 request instance is created, with probability p_scope_inject it carries a ring-fenced APS line of a_sg017_named dollars. That line cannot be bumped by controller/failure-priority projects, so it is exempt from q_sg017_block. The line is also only visible to the SFCTA stage once it is in the request text. If the intervention is absent or late, the request goes out controller-only, as in 2025.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in the model. pressure(t) in D3.1 is a diffuse input to p_start. D3.6 PW3 sets owner/specified/oversight, but not a named line item. PW6 and q_sg017_block (D10) describe a block at the SFCTA stage, not an insertion at the SFMTA drafting stage.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7 (l.283): the ODA staffer proposed a follow-up with MTA/DPW and then 'recommend and support letters'. 01 §2.7.1 (l.309): the 2026-09-18 agenda has no APS item and no letter, so the follow-up was not observed. 01 l.446-447: the CIP text allows new APS and past grants went to controllers. Whether anyone has ever sent a pre-draft request is no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_scope_inject (0 to 0.6, default 0.15, scenario scan {0, 0.15, 0.4}); optional a_sg017_named U($0, $250k), already bounded by a_sg017
proposals.range: p_scope_inject 0 to 0.6
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 start rule and D3.1 SUBMITTED instance creation; when it fires it overrides q_sg017_block (D10) for that instance

proposals.behaviour: Meeting-calendar gating of the Council channel. The Council meets in discrete sessions, and APS reaches the agenda only when staff schedule it. Staff can place an APS item, a resolution, or a support letter on a meeting agenda only at those dates. A request window that falls between meetings, or a draft deadline that arrives before the next meeting, means no Council-backed action happens in that cycle. Staff may also wait for a better window and hold an item for a more favourable agenda slot rather than raise it at once.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event is generated but the next agenda deadline is after the SG017 submission date, or the agenda is already full (curb ramps take the slot, as in 2025 and 2026).
proposals.effect_in_model: Council-channel pressure events (C2 via MDC) are not drawn continuously at λ_press. They are released only in meeting months, each with probability p_agenda. Events produced while the window is closed are deferred to the next meeting (delayed past the draft deadline), or dropped with probability q_slot_lost. This makes the Council channel structurally late relative to short SFMTA and SFCTA windows.
proposals.already_in_model: Only partly. D3.1 draws pressure events at an unknown rate with decay k. F-m interrupts pressure for t_quiet (interruption is not calendar gating). 01 §2.7.1 l.311 says the activation rule is an 'unknown parameter, test zero and non-zero scenarios', but 02 has no meeting-gated release.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7 (l.287-288): the 2026-07-17 item 7 had zero public speakers, and the next listed meeting was 2026-09-18. 01 l.307: APS reached the agenda only twice from 2018 to 2026. 01 l.309: the 2026-09-18 agenda had no APS item.
proposals.parameter: p_agenda (0 to 1, default 0.25) with q_slot_lost (0 to 0.5) and meeting interval t_meet (2 or 3 months)
proposals.range: p_agenda 0 to 1; q_slot_lost 0 to 0.5; t_meet in {2, 3}
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 generation of pressure events for the advocacy node C2; replaces the continuous Poisson release for the MDC channel only

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS as a curb-ramp or ADA transition item. Staff move the ask into the channel where the Council has actually written letters and where a federal time obligation exists. The ask becomes 'while you dig for the ramp, set the APS in the same work order' or 'include signal-side accessibility in the ramp scope'. They avoid asking for a separate APS item, which has no federal timetable and no letters on record.
proposals.trigger: A ramp support letter or ramp funding discussion is already scheduled, or the staffer judges a separate APS ask unlikely to be heard (no APS letter in the record).
proposals.effect_in_model: With probability p_reframe the APS request is attached to a curb-ramp parent project. The task takes the 'inclusion with parent' path (Fs) at a lower cost per installation (the pole and ramp costs are shared). It then inherits the parent delay t_parent and its cancel risk (F-g). The cost is that the intervention is delayed by the parent schedule.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.4 'inclusion with existing project' and PW4 'allocate by intersection' already include parent-project routes. Neither lets the advocacy side switch an intersection's route by reframing, and neither makes pressure efficiency depend on which channel it came through.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7 (l.279): two MDC letters (2025-04, 2026-04-16) both went to curb ramps, with no APS letter (0). 01 l.284: ramps have a 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) transition-plan obligation and APS has no federal retrofit timetable. 01 l.112: the senior engineer's argument for doing curb work together.
proposals.parameter: p_reframe (0 to 0.5, default 0.1) and gain_ramp_link (the multiplier on pressure efficiency when routed through the ramp channel, 1 to 3)
proposals.range: p_reframe 0 to 0.5; gain_ramp_link 1 to 3
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure(t) conversion plus D3.4 route assignment (moves a share of C-type intersections to the 'inclusion with parent' path)

proposals.behaviour: Cross-issue linkage as informal leverage. Staff make Council support for SFMTA items that the agency wants (for example a letter or a favourable resolution on other signal or capital items) implicitly conditional on a named APS line. No document records such a deal. It is an informal side bargain.
proposals.trigger: A moment when the agency needs a Council letter or hearing (a larger capital item, a Vision Zero update) and the SG017 request is still open.
proposals.effect_in_model: A one-off event: with probability p_link the agency commits to name an APS line in the SG017 request (the same effect as proposal 1's ring-fenced line). Otherwise the agency treats the offer as a mere request and the staffer's favour is spent (the 'linkage' budget goes to zero for t_link months).
proposals.already_in_model: Not in the model. Council support letters are a low-weight advocacy resource (C2), and PW3 'accountability' (D1 enforcement escalation) works by lawsuit, not by bargaining.
proposals.evidence: No document support for the existence of such a bargain. Related only: 01 §2.7 (l.279) the Council's tools are advisory, with 'letters to the CPC' as one tool, and l.290 'binding force 0; about one influence per year'.
proposals.parameter: p_link (0 to 0.3, default 0.05) with cooldown t_link (6 to 24 months)
proposals.range: p_link 0 to 0.3; t_link 6 to 24
proposals.rule_modified: Adds a new event type in D3.1 that sets the ring-fenced line of the SG017 request (same hook as p_scope_inject); P(Council-letter available) is used as an input

proposals.behaviour: Scope-line pre-clearance and letter-timing. MOD staff, anticipating that SFMTA drafts the SG017 allocation request, write a short joint technical note or staff-to-staff ask (and draft a Council support letter for the same item) that names APS explicitly as an eligible line in the request text, before the request is finalised. Letter content is aimed at the allocation memo wording, not at generic advocacy.
proposals.trigger: The month the SG017 request enters PREPARING (or a fixed lead before the SFCTA allocation deadline) AND the last allocation went to controllers (a visible blocking precedent). Also needs a Council meeting slot in that window.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers q_sg017_block in PW6 for that cycle, or raises the chance that the allocation scope text includes new APS. Costs MOD staff time and one Council letter slot per year, so it competes with the curb-ramp letter the Council already writes. If the window is missed, the effect is zero for that cycle.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 (D3.6) and q_sg017_block (D10) model SFCTA or SFMTA blocking APS in SG017, and C2 (O2) has generic advocacy pressure. But no rule lets an advisory-body actor act on the request-wording timing; pressure(t) is untimed and has no 'window-aligned' variant, and the Council letters in the evidence are curb-ramp only. Not dropped because the timing-aligned, text-specific lever is not written.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: tools are advisory only (resolutions, hearings, letters to CPC); both 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 letters were curb-ramp, 'no APS letter' is listed as a gap. 01 §2.7: ODA staff proposed after 2026-07-17 to follow up with MTA and DPW and then 'recommend/support letters'; follow-up not observed. 01 line 446-447: SG017 CIP scope text allows new APS, but FY24 and FY25-26 allocations went to controllers/cabinets/RRFB.
proposals.parameter: p_scope_letter (probability per SG017 request cycle that MOD/Council acts inside the preparation window), U(0, 0.6); effect: multiply q_sg017_block by (1 - eta_letter), eta_letter U(0, 0.5). Switch sw_scope_letter on/off.
proposals.range: p_scope_letter U(0,0.6); eta_letter U(0,0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 trigger (q_sg017_block draw) and the window-timing of pressure(t) into p_start for the SG017 task

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS as part of the existing ADA/curb-ramp transition-plan track. MOD staff, who already co-own the curb-ramp prioritisation with DPW, ask for APS at ramp sites to be scored or scoped inside the ramp/ADA-transition program or the 'City public facilities' site list, so APS rides on a track that has a federal timetable obligation instead of competing for SG017.
proposals.trigger: Repeated blocking in SG017 (controller priority, F-k-type no-slack) combined with the asymmetry that curb ramps have a 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) timetable and APS does not. Activates only after a PW6 block signal (q_sg017_block fires).
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a funding route: a share of C-type backlog intersections with a ramp job pending get APS added at the ramp work (marginal cost closer to u0 plus the shared ramp excavation), bypassing the SFMTA task state machine. Changes install timing and the cost_by_actor split (cost shifts to DPW/ramp budget). Also raises dependency on ramp project delay (t_parent analogue).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 'Fs/merged projects' and PW4 route by parent project and corridors, and the ramp cost ($200k) is a cost component (F-f, D3.3). But there is no 'merge into ramp program' route owned by a non-SFMTA actor, and no advisory actor can trigger it. Not dropped: the actor-initiated rebinding is not written.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: MOD co-funded and prioritised DPW curb ramps in 2008 and the plan entered the 10-year capital plan; ramp has a federal timetable duty, APS 'has no corresponding federal retrofit timetable' (inferred). 01 §2.1: 'opening the ground triggers ramp work' and senior engineer says not touching ramps is five times faster, showing the physical coupling. No document shows MOD actually requesting APS inside the ramp track.
proposals.parameter: sw_ramp_rebind (switch) and f_ramp_share U(0, 0.3): fraction of pending C intersections co-scheduled with a ramp job that are re-routed to the ramp track after a block signal; delay t_ramp U(6, 36) months.
proposals.range: f_ramp_share U(0,0.3); t_ramp U(6,36) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 fallback step and PW4 route allocation; adds a new delivery path in D3.4 (joins the 'merged into existing project' row)

proposals.behaviour: Information forcing: MOD/Council requests the SG017 allocation request and the prior allocation scope as a public record or places an APS line-item report on the Council agenda, so SFMTA must state in writing whether APS is in the request. This raises the cost of silent omission without any binding power.
proposals.trigger: The Council's annual or semiannual agenda cycle (about one effective chance per year, 01 §2.7 influence channel) following a year with no APS action; does not need any external legal event.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the oversight(t) level, a one-time bump decaying over k months, specific to the SG017 task; it also raises the chance that deflection (p_deflect) gets documented, which makes the later D1 escalation to negotiation or litigation easier (a write-on-record effect). Strength depends on whether SFMTA responds with 'selected based on funding' as in 2026.
proposals.already_in_model: No explicit equivalent. oversight appears as a beta term (β_ov) in p_start and PW3 sets oversight high as an intervention, but there is no endogenous, actor-triggered oversight event produced by an advisory body, and no 'paper trail' variable that feeds the escalation ladder. Kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7 line 287: the 2026-07-17 APS agenda item had no public comment; line 283: staff proposed follow-up and support-letter recommendation, not observed afterwards. 01 §2.1 line 131: oversight 'does not actually work' and parties push responsibility to each other. No document shows a records request.
proposals.parameter: p_record_req (probability per year that the advisory body forces a written APS statement) U(0, 0.5), and oversight bump delta_ov U(0, 0.3) with decay k_ov U(6, 18) months; optional counter 'paper_trail' that adds to the escalation signal for D1.
proposals.range: p_record_req U(0,0.5); delta_ov U(0,0.3); k_ov U(6,18) months
proposals.rule_modified: oversight(t) input to p_start (D3.1) and the D1 escalation trigger (PW3 theta_idle path)

proposals.behaviour: Strategic restraint, waiting for a better window. Because past SG017 allocations went to controllers (firewall patch priority), MOD staff may judge that pushing APS now would lose and could cost them the single yearly Council letter slot or credibility with SFMTA, and instead hold the APS ask until the controller backlog is cleared or a new Prop L cycle opens.
proposals.trigger: A visible competing safety/security priority consuming SG017 (controllers or firewall) and an estimate that the block probability is high. Resolves when the competing priority ends or 5YPP is reopened.
proposals.effect_in_model: Advocacy-side pressure is suppressed in the SG017 window, which lowers pressure(t) and the p_start for the SG017 task. This is an endogenous quiet period that depends on SFMTA's competing priority, not a random one. Total effect is a delay that may avoid a failure (a rejected ask counts as precedent) but extends time to first funding.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-m (D3.5) models advocacy pressure going quiet with an exogenous rate λ_quiet and duration t_quiet. It is not conditional on a visible competing priority, so the endogenous, strategic version is absent. Kept as an extension of F-m only if the condition is written.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 447: FY25-26 SG017 funds went to controller replacement for the firewall vulnerability, a priority outranking APS. 01 §2.7 line 290: MDC channel about one letter or resolution a year, so a wasted slot has an opportunity cost. No document states MOD decided to hold back; this is an inference from the one-slot constraint.
proposals.parameter: sw_strategic_wait with threshold theta_block: lambda_quiet is replaced by lambda_quiet_endog = 1 if q_sg017_block_estimate > theta_block, theta_block U(0.4, 0.8), reset when the blocking priority ends or on the next cycle.
proposals.range: theta_block U(0.4,0.8)
proposals.rule_modified: F-m (quiet-period rule) trigger and the pressure(t) feed into p_start

proposals.behaviour: Timed intervention at the allocation-request drafting stage. MOD staff target the narrow SFMTA SG017 request-drafting window (before the allocation request goes to SFCTA), by sending a staff-to-staff ask or a short MDC support letter that names APS in the request scope. The model treats MDC only as a diffuse, rare, unscheduled pressure source; it has no mechanism where advocacy is aimed at a specific, observable drafting event and is much more effective there.
proposals.trigger: A visible signpost: SG017 FY27/FY28 allocation request enters preparation (PREPARING task for the Prop L EP17 field), or a CIP/5YPP document lists SG017 scope that includes new APS. The actor wants to act only when the window is open and the scope is still editable.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a pressure pulse that is targeted rather than spread. While the SG017 request is PREPARING, a targeted nudge raises the probability that the submitted instance carries an APS component (lowers the effective q_sg017_block) and adds a small boost to p_start for that field only. Outside the window the nudge is zero, so effort is not wasted. This differs from pressure(t), which is generic, decays with k, and feeds only p_start.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.1 has generic pressure(t) with decay k and lambda_press; 02 D3.6 PW3 raises owner/specified/oversight; PW6 and q_sg017_block (D10) cover the SG017 route. None of these ties an advocacy action to the drafting window of the specific request. Kept because the window-targeting is not written anywhere.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7 (MDC rows): the tool is only advisory, 'ODA staff proposed follow-up with MTA/DPW then a recommendation and support letter' (MDC26t), with no follow-up seen by the 2026-09-18 agenda (section 2.7.1); two letters existed but both for curb ramps, none for APS. So the support-letter tool exists and was used for another asset class, which supports the plausibility of re-aiming it. No document support that it is timed to a drafting window; that part is inference.
proposals.parameter: p_target (switch plus probability that MOD staff act inside the SG017 drafting window); effect size d_aps_scope
proposals.range: p_target U(0, 0.5) per request cycle (0 = status quo, matching the observed 0 APS letters); d_aps_scope = reduction in q_sg017_block of 0 to 0.3 (additive, floored at 0)
proposals.rule_modified: D10 q_sg017_block and a_sg017 (PW6 start rule); adds a field-specific term to p_start for the Prop L EP17 task in D3.1

proposals.behaviour: Reframing and borrowing the curb-ramp channel: MOD staff fold APS into the existing curb-ramp advocacy package (letters, DPW-MTA coordination ask, ADA transition-plan language) as a 'paired ramp plus signal at the same crossing' request, instead of pushing APS as a standalone item. Because MOD already co-funds and ranks DPW curb ramps and is the one office with a standing legal-obligation frame, it can piggyback APS on that frame.
proposals.trigger: A curb-ramp funding or coordination event (the 2026 ramp budget is said to rise sharply; ODA asked DPW and MTA to coordinate strategy), occurring while some crossings in the C/N pending list are scheduled for a ramp rebuild.
proposals.effect_in_model: Creates a new link between the ramp pipeline and the APS pending list: a crossing whose ramp is being rebuilt moves from the 'dig separately' cost class to the 'bundled with existing work' class, which lowers its unit cost and raises odds of joining the Fs (with signal works) or a joint-scoped path. This also increases the chance that a SG017-type request names that crossing. It works through cost and path assignment, not through generic pressure.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. 02 D3.4 and 'Fs' cover bundling with signal works. 01 section 2.12 notes DPW designs ramps leaving room for future APS but ramp work does not trigger APS ('APS is MTA's job'); the model has no ramp-event trigger. Kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7: MOD co-funded and ranked DPW curb ramps (ADA transition plan, 2008); ODA deputy asked DPW and MTA to coordinate; ramp budget 'will rise'. 01 line 127: the SFMTA senior engineer says skipping existing ramps would be 'five times faster' and cost over $500k otherwise, so ramp co-timing changes cost a lot. 01 line 376: DPW leaves provision for future APS but does not trigger it. Whether MOD actually uses this frame is no document support.
proposals.parameter: q_ramp_pair (probability per year that a ramp event at a pending crossing is converted into an APS-paired work item through MOD coordination)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.15) per pending crossing per year; paired crossings get the ramp share (about $200k) removed from c_full
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4/I-queue entry and the c_full draw; adds a new event type beside PW5's lambda_hw hardware-event generator

proposals.behaviour: Waiting for a better window rather than acting on each allocation: MOD staff and the Council hold advocacy capital for the Prop L 5YPP rewrite window (2027 autumn to 2028) and the HSIP C14 cycle, and explicitly accept letting the FY27/FY28 SG017 allocation pass if it is again used for controllers. This produces deliberate non-intervention in the current request, which looks the same as inactivity but is strategic and then followed by a large coordinated push.
proposals.trigger: A SG017 request is drafted with no APS line (seen as past allocations all went to controllers), plus a known later window (5YPP amendment/rewrite) within a horizon of a few months to two years.
proposals.effect_in_model: Replaces the memoryless pressure stream with a stock of 'saved' advocacy that is released as a burst when a window opens. Pressure during the SG017 cycle is lowered, and pressure at the 5YPP/C14 window is raised by the saved amount, with the net effect being fewer but larger pulses. It changes timing of PW2/PW6 transitions: a later but more likely Prop L amendment.
proposals.already_in_model: Not found. 02 F-m models random quiet periods (lambda_quiet, t_quiet) but as exogenous breaks, not as chosen waiting that is later released. D3.6 transitions wait for 'the next available window' for the actor who is deciding, not for the advocate's pressure. Kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.7.1: MDC treats APS as an information report, 'about 1 influence opportunity a year', and the activation rule in the absence of events is unknown (01 line 73). No document shows deliberate saving; no document support for the stockpiling itself.
proposals.parameter: sw_save (switch) with release multiplier g_burst
proposals.range: sw_save in {0,1}; g_burst U(1, 4) multiplier on lambda_press at the next 5YPP or HSIP window, with the lull before it multiplied by 0.5 to 1
proposals.rule_modified: lambda_press schedule and pressure(t) in D3.1 p_start; interacts with F-m (replaces the exogenous quiet period when sw_save = 1)

proposals.behaviour: Putting a name on the responsibility: MOD staff request a written, public answer from SFMTA on why the SG017 request does or does not include new APS where poles and conduit are adequate (a status question at the Council, or a records/information request), instead of asking for money. This makes buck-passing costly because the 'no funds / high cost' reply must now be given on the record against a CIP line that explicitly allows new APS.
proposals.trigger: The SG017 request is submitted or about to be submitted without APS scope, and the CIP text allowing new APS is public; the Council has a meeting agenda slot or a staff channel.
proposals.effect_in_model: Reduces p_deflect for that field for a period, since replying 'no funds' to a CIP scope that includes APS is a weaker excuse. It also adds the option that SFMTA staff respond by adding a small APS line (a_sg017 > 0) to avoid a documented refusal. The change acts only on the request actor's deflection response, not on advocacy volume.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.6 PW3 (accountability first: deadline, named owner, restored reporting) raises owner/specified/oversight as a policy path, and D3.1 has p_deflect. But in the model these are policy interventions applied by an outside analyst, not something MOD staff themselves do in the current situation; and PW3 is not tied to the SG017 CIP wording. Kept narrowly as an agent behaviour with its own trigger.
proposals.evidence: 01 line 83: the closed loop of 'no money' replies and 'no one applied', with the buck-passing claim as inference. 01 lines 446-447: the SG017 CIP scope text allowing new APS and past allocations that went to controllers. 01 section 2.7: ODA staff proposed follow-up and a support letter (not observed afterwards). The effect on deflection is no document support.
proposals.parameter: d_pdefl (reduction in p_deflect for the SG017 field after a documented accountability ask)
proposals.range: Applied with probability q_ask U(0, 0.4) per request cycle; p_deflect multiplied by U(0.5, 1) for r to 2r months afterwards
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (p_deflect, r) for the Prop L EP17 / SG017 task; also feeds `specified` in p_start

proposals.behaviour: Pre-submission scope-wording intervention. Before the SG017 allocation request is finalized, the MOD/MDC staff member asks SFMTA preparers and SFCTA programming staff to list 'new APS at intersections with adequate poles/conduit' explicitly as a deliverable (not just 'replace'), and offers a letter citing the CIP scope text. It targets the allocation wording, upstream of the SFCTA board decision.
proposals.trigger: SG017 request enters PREPARING and the staff member knows past allocations were controller-only. Needs a deadline-aware window; a late letter does nothing.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers q_sg017_block for that cycle and/or raises a_sg017, if the ask lands at least t_ask_lead months before the submission deadline. Acts on PW6 at the PREPARING-to-SUBMIT stage, not through the generic pressure(t) channel.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 and q_sg017_block exist (02 D3.6, D10 ~line 375); generic advocacy is pressure(t)/lambda_press (D3.1), with MDC an 'information channel' of unknown activation. No rule lets a targeted, deadline-timed wording ask reduce q_sg017_block. Kept as a narrow addition.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 line 279 (MDC letters 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 both curb ramps, 0 APS letters); line 283 (ODA staff said in 2026-07 they would return to recommend support letters; 2026-09-18 agenda shows nothing). 02 lines 446-447: CIP scope text allows new APS, past grants were controllers. No document support that such a wording request has ever been made.
proposals.parameter: p_scope_ask (per-cycle switch) with r_scope and t_ask_lead: q_sg017_block := q_sg017_block*(1 - r_scope) if ask is made at least t_ask_lead months before deadline.
proposals.range: p_scope_ask U(0, 0.5); r_scope U(0, 0.5); t_ask_lead U(1, 4) months (all inferred)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 transition (SFCTA restricts scope to 'replace'); D10 q_sg017_block; timing coupled to D3.1 PREPARING.

proposals.behaviour: Site-list supply. MOD hands SFMTA a ready, prioritised list of pole-and-conduit-adequate intersections (drawing on its 'city public project' site list and disability-use priorities), so the SG017 request can name concrete APS sites cheaply.
proposals.trigger: SG017 request is in PREPARING and SFMTA's constraint is staff time or site identification.
proposals.effect_in_model: Reduces D_prep (or delta_split) for the APS-bearing instance and raises the share of backlog C-type intersections that pass the 'existing poles and conduit adequate' filter. Moves PW6 from possible to cheap through the preparation-workload channel, not the pressure channel.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. D3.1 treats D_prep and delta_split as exogenous and strain(t) as internal to SFMTA; no rule lets an outside actor offload preparation work, and the MOD site list is not used as an action.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 line 280 (MOD supplies the city public project site list for APS scoring, TOOL p.8); s2.1 line 106 (one associate engineer scores all applications); s2.1 line ~119 (pole/conduit about $200k each, so site choice drives cost). No document support that MOD has offered a list for SG017.
proposals.parameter: p_list (activation) and d_prep_offset (months removed from D_prep when a list is supplied, floor 0.5*D_prep).
proposals.range: p_list U(0, 0.4); d_prep_offset U(0, 2) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 preparation time D_prep + (m-1)*delta_split; D10 D_prep.

proposals.behaviour: Window-gated advocacy and bundle-linking. The staff member holds a request in cycles likely to fail (SFMTA strained, controller priority announced) and concentrates a letter, hearing or ODA director item into a later SG017 cycle or the next 5YPP update, or attaches APS to a curb-ramp funding letter where MDC already has traction.
proposals.trigger: Signals that the current cycle is blocked: strain(t) high, a controller-priority project announced (as with the FY25-26 firewall controller replacement), or a curb-ramp letter cycle open.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure events are lumpy: drawn at a higher rate in 'open' windows and lower in blocked ones, and a share ride on a ramp letter. Less pressure is wasted on cycles with high q_sg017_block.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. lambda_press and F-m (random quiet periods) exist (02 D10 line 340, D3.5 F-m) but are unlinked to window state. PW4 and PW2 reroute funding sources, not advocacy timing.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 line 279 and summary: both letters went to curb ramps (a funded vehicle with a federal timeline, line 284), while APS appeared only twice on 2018-2026 agendas as information items. No document support for deliberate cycle-skipping.
proposals.parameter: g(state) multiplier on lambda_press: g_hi in open windows, g_lo in blocked ones; plus p_attach (APS clause added to a ramp letter, coupling into pressure(t)).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure(t) accumulation; D10 lambda_press; F-m.

proposals.behaviour: Redirecting deflected pressure to the funder. When SFMTA answers with 'cost / no funding', the staff member does not accept the answer but re-issues the request to the SFCTA board, the Mayor's budget staff or CPC, asking for an explicit APS line inside SG017. The advocate, not SFMTA, passes the task on.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event ends in DEFLECTED and the staff member has a channel to the funder or budget office. Fires after a deflection, not at random.
proposals.effect_in_model: A share of deflected events become a second-stage event that raises funder-side specified/oversight for k_f months, which can then push q_sg017_block down or open the PW2 path, instead of the event being lost.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 has SFMTA deflect to SFCTA/budget/Caltrans and PW3 raises oversight system-wide. There is no rule where an advocate recycles a deflected event as pressure on the funder. Drop if the team treats the PW3 uplift as equivalent.
proposals.evidence: 01 s1.2 line 83 (the 'no money / not applied' loop; advocates lack resources to force applications); s2.1 line 131 (oversight inactive; parties blame each other); s2.7 line 283 (ODA staff proposed following up with MTA and DPW, no follow-up seen). No document support that anyone has redirected deflected pressure to the funder.
proposals.parameter: p_redirect (share of DEFLECTED events re-issued to the funder), beta_fund (uplift to funder-side specified) lasting k_f months.
proposals.range: p_redirect U(0, 0.4); beta_fund U(0, 0.5)*beta_spec; k_f U(3, 12) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch; D3.6 PW3 specified/oversight inputs.

proposals.behaviour: Solution-bearing ask. Instead of generic pressure ('fund APS'), the advocate hands the agency a ready, HSIP-shaped ask: 'add a new countdown signal (SI18PB) and APS to the SG015/SG142 package, here is the carrier and the draft intersection list'. The ask comes with a funding path, so it is harder to answer with 'cost / no funding'.
proposals.trigger: Application window open and deadline near (here, one week out), SG142 known to be APS-only and ineligible, and the advocate knows the carrier/eligibility rule (QA13 Q3).
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers p_deflect for events that carry a specific ask (so more pressure ends up in pressure(t) instead of DEFLECTED). Also adds the pressure only inside the open window, rather than as a flat scalar. Net effect: higher p_start for that window.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. Pressure events, p_deflect and pressure(t) exist (02 D3.1). PW3 raises specified/owner/oversight (02 D3.6). But p_deflect is one constant per event and does not depend on whether the ask is eligible-shaped, and pressure is not window-gated. Not a duplicate of PW3, which is a structural lever, not an advocate-side reframing choice.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1 line 130: SFMTA answers advocacy with cost and 'selected based on funding'. 01 §2.4: 'APS-only is ineligible in any category; APS must be part of a broader safety project' (QA13 Q3). 01 §3 (lines 420, 442): SG142 is APS-only and fails in C13 while SG015 is the SI02 carrier in the same cycle. No document shows an advocate making such a framed ask (no document support for the behaviour itself).
proposals.parameter: delta_ask (multiplier on p_deflect for a carrier-framed ask) and w_pulse (window gate: pressure counts toward p_start only if the event falls within W months before the deadline)
proposals.range: delta_ask U(0.3, 1.0), where 1.0 = no effect; w_pulse W in {0 (off), 2, 4} months; switch sw_ask in {0,1}
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_deflect branch and the pressure(t) term in p_start

proposals.behaviour: In-kind drafting help and nomination. The advocacy organisation supplies the agency with the pieces that make the BCR package cheaper to prepare (priority-intersection nominations from members, local near-miss and complaint locations, user letters) and asks that nominated intersections be put in the package.
proposals.trigger: Short window before the deadline; the advocate sees preparation time (D_prep) as the binding constraint, not will. Also triggered when the request list (76 items) is ordered by points, not by blind-user need.
proposals.effect_in_model: (a) Reduces D_prep and delta_split for the open window, so more instances are ready by the deadline (fewer MISSED). (b) Forces k nominated C-type intersections to the front of the packing order. If their crash counts are low, the package BCR can fall under 5.0 and trigger F-a (cost of the behaviour).
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 treats D_prep as fixed (U(1,6)); D3.3 step 2 sorts strictly by BCR; pressure is only a rate on p_start. Nothing lets an outside actor change preparation workload or the package order.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8 lines 319-321 (SA07 IV.J.2: plaintiffs to participate 'meaningfully' in funding applications; semiannual meetings must report 'funding applied for and efforts with Caltrans'). 01 §2.9 line 337: list order is by points, with other items 'selected based on funding'. 01 §2.4 line 215: support letters do not score, so nomination is the only influence that survives. No document shows the advocate offering this help.
proposals.parameter: adv_assist (days of preparation saved, as fraction of D_prep) and k_nom (number of forced nominations)
proposals.range: adv_assist U(0, 0.4); k_nom in {0, 1, 2, 3}; sw_assist in {0,1}
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 preparation time formula and D3.3 packing algorithm step 2 (sort order) and step 3 (skip/stop rule)

proposals.behaviour: Ally mode. The advocate stops pressuring and supports the agency's own funding requests: appears at the SFCTA board for the Prop L amendment, supports a top-up request after an overrun, writes to the mayor/board for the general fund request, and backs the agency in delivery fights.
proposals.trigger: After the agency has visibly acted (submitted a package, won an award, or filed an amendment), or when pressure has been answered with cost talk repeatedly and the advocate switches tactic.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers q_veto (F-j), raises q_topup (F-e, F-f), shortens t_defer, and raises the general-fund and PW2/PW6 success odds. Pressure events change sign: they stop feeding p_deflect and instead feed the downstream approval odds.
proposals.already_in_model: No. The model has only adversarial advocacy: lambda_press, p_deflect, lambda_quiet (F-m), and escalation to negotiation/lawsuit (PW3, D1). q_veto, q_topup and t_defer are independent constants with no actor input.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8 line 320: SA07 IV.J.2 and V: plaintiffs support SFMTA requests to the mayor and council. 01 §2.8 line 324: CCB describes the 2007 deal as a 'successful advocacy campaign'. 01 §2.7 line 283: ODA proposed support letters (not yet seen). 01 §2.3 / 02 F-j: Prop L amendment precedents of 3-4 months with no advocate input recorded (no direct document support for ally behaviour in 2024-26).
proposals.parameter: ally_gain (relative reduction of q_veto and relative increase of q_topup) and p_ally (probability the advocate is in ally mode in a given year)
proposals.range: ally_gain U(0, 0.5); p_ally U(0, 0.6); switch sw_ally in {0,1}
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (q_veto, t_defer) and F-e/F-f (q_topup); D3.1 pressure event handling

proposals.behaviour: Post-award watchdog. After a package is approved, the advocate shifts pressure from 'start' to 'deliver': tracking the E-76 dates, PE 9 / CON 36-month flags, partner-project (SG015) slippage and the PIF step, and using the semiannual report to name the agency's own plan dates (SG142 start 2027-07 vs C13 award 2027-03/04) when they slip.
proposals.trigger: A package is APPROVED or a milestone date is missed; the report cycle (twice a year) shows a slipped date.
proposals.effect_in_model: Shortens t_partner and t_pif/t_con tails and lowers the chance of TERMINATED via 5-year check or partner cancel, because slipping is made visible. Costs the advocate effort, so it competes with start-side pressure for the same lambda_press budget.
proposals.already_in_model: No. Pressure only enters p_start (D3.1); D3.4 delivery and F-d, F-g have no advocate-side term; semiannual reports appear only as an owner/oversight setting.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8 lines 321-323: reports must include 'funding applied for and status'; the series lapsed and LightHouse says it restored it in 2022-07 (shows the advocate does act on reporting). 01 §3 lines 421, 636 (C3): SG142 start date 2027-07 is inconsistent with the 15-28 month empirical award-to-construction time. No document shows watchdog behaviour on delivery.
proposals.parameter: watch_effect (proportional cut to t_partner and the t_con right tail while watching) and a budget split s_watch between start-side and delivery-side pressure
proposals.range: watch_effect U(0, 0.3); s_watch U(0, 1) of lambda_press; sw_watch in {0,1}
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 HSIP delivery (t_partner, t_con) and D3.5 F-d / F-g; D10 lambda_press allocation

proposals.behaviour: Package-content lobbying: the advocacy organisation asks SFMTA, in the week before the deadline, to attach APS as a cost line to the SG015 visibility-upgrade application (or to any other BCR instance already being built) instead of arguing for the APS-only SG142 line. It reframes the request from 'fund APS' to 'APS rides on a carrier that already scores'.
proposals.trigger: A window is open and the task is in PREPARING (deadline within roughly 1-2 months); the advocate knows (or learns from SFMTA staff) that an APS-only line is ineligible and that a partner project SG015 exists in the same cycle.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the probability that the packaged instance for the partner corridor includes APS cost and APS-eligible intersections, which changes what the packing step selects. It does not change whether the task starts. It also adds extra prep load on the Signal Shop (small increase in D_prep or delta_split), so there is a trade-off with strain.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW1 (HSIP first) is a policy pathway where SG015 and APS are bundled by design (D3.6), and F-g covers partner delay. But nothing makes bundling an outcome of an actor's request. In D3.1 pressure(t) only enters p_start; it never changes package content. Not dropped, because the lever (who asks, and when) is not in D3.1/D3.2.
proposals.evidence: 01 s3.1 'hard facts': SG142 pure APS $488,144 ineligible and over the $360k cap, 'only if changed to a carrier-based BCR application could it qualify'. 01 s2.8: 2007 agreement SA07 s.IV.A.1 obliges SFMTA to seek extra funds from federal/state/local sources, and s.IV.J.2 gives plaintiffs a role in funding applications (a contractual hook for such a request). No document shows advocates actually making this kind of ask; support is for the hook only.
proposals.parameter: p_bundle_ask (0-1; plus lead time t_ask_lead U(0,3) months before deadline)
proposals.range: p_bundle_ask in {0, 0.1-0.6}, default 0 as the control. If the ask is made and the task is PREPARING, the packaging step is forced to include the SG015-corridor C-type intersections with APS (PW1 start rule) even in pathways PW0/PW2/PW4. If the ask is made too late (t_ask_lead < D_prep + delta_split), it has no effect.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 packing algorithm step 1 (candidate set) and D3.1 PREPARING duration; bypasses the PW1-only restriction of the candidate set.

proposals.behaviour: Deadline-synchronised pressure: the advocacy organisation does not apply pressure as a steady background rate. It saves its letters, board and committee testimony, and MDC agenda items for the weeks around the application deadline and the 5YPP/budget windows, because that is when a decision is still open.
proposals.trigger: A funding window is within about 3 months of its deadline, or a Prop L 5YPP amendment or two-year budget decision is scheduled.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes the timing of pressure events. The same annual total of pressure events is concentrated into windows, which raises pressure(t) exactly when p_start is drawn and lowers it elsewhere.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 uses pressure(t) from a Poisson rate lambda_press that is not tied to the window calendar; F-m adds random silent periods (lambda_quiet, t_quiet) but not synchronisation. If pressure arrives after the p_start draw for that window, it decays (k months) and is wasted. So the model could understate the effect of timing and overstate that of volume.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8 'parameters': advocacy activation rate with no event is unknown, test 0 and nonzero (0.1-0.5 effective pressures per year); LightHouse got the semiannual report re-established in 2022-07, an example of targeted action. 01 s2.8 board minutes: ~0/39 public comments on APS in Aug-Oct 2026, which suggests the unsynchronised baseline is near zero. No document says advocates deliberately time pressure to deadlines.
proposals.parameter: press_sync (fraction of annual pressure events moved into pre-deadline windows)
proposals.range: 0 (current, uniform Poisson) to 1 (all events inside the 90 days before a window deadline or budget decision); sweep {0, 0.5, 1} at constant annual total lambda_press.
proposals.rule_modified: Arrival process of pressure events feeding pressure(t) in D3.1 (the logistic p_start), and the F-m quiet-period generator.

proposals.behaviour: Local-match and top-up advocacy: because HSIP needs a 10% local match and the F-e/F-f overrun gaps are covered only if SFMTA/SFCTA approves a top-up, the advocacy organisation lobbies the Board and the transportation authority (CAC) to commit the match or a top-up reserve to the APS component, rather than lobbying Caltrans.
proposals.trigger: A top-up or match request is pending (F-e q_topup, F-f overrun beyond contingency), or the Prop L / general-fund agenda touches street safety.
proposals.effect_in_model: Increases the probability that a funding gap is covered (q_topup) and reduces termination of the project, so APS instances that clear the BCR threshold are more likely to reach delivery. It also lowers the chance that a project is TERMINATED and its intersections go back to the pool.
