proposals.already_in_model: No. q_topup in F-e/F-f is a fixed probability. Advocacy pressure(t) acts only through p_start in D3.1, not through gap financing. F-k (the director's 10% redirection) and F-j (Prop L veto) are not influenced by advocacy either.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: SA07 s.IV.J.2, plaintiffs 'support SFMTA requests to the mayor and Board'. 01 s2.3/s2.2 on SFCTA precedent for top-up requests (F-f cites an SFCTA precedent). No document shows advocates doing this for APS specifically.
proposals.parameter: adv_topup_lift (additive increase in q_topup and decrease in q_veto when pressure(t) > threshold)
proposals.range: 0 to 0.3, gated by pressure(t) >= theta_press; 0 as control.
proposals.rule_modified: F-e / F-f q_topup, F-j q_veto, evaluated at the gap-decision event.

proposals.behaviour: Goodwill-triggered restraint: when SFMTA visibly acts (submits an application with APS, or a project is awarded), the advocacy organisation scales back public pressure and shifts to cooperation (partnering on outreach, staying quiet at hearings), to protect its working relationship with staff. If the application then fails or slips, it escalates.
proposals.trigger: A SUBMITTED instance containing APS exists, or an award is announced; then a miss, rejection or delay beyond a tolerance.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes pressure endogenous: it falls after a visible action and rises after a visible failure. This creates a risk of a self-inflicted 'quiet' period exactly when slippage risk is highest (pre-CON), which would be a feedback loop that the current random F-m quiet period does not produce.
proposals.already_in_model: Partially. F-m generates exogenous quiet periods at random (lambda_quiet, t_quiet), and PW3 escalates D1 after theta_idle months of nothing. But no rule links quiet to SFMTA's visible actions, and the escalation in PW3 only starts from inactivity, not from a failed or slipped submission.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: board minutes 2026-08 to 10, ~39 public comments, none on APS; no public statements found from LightHouse/CCB/NFB-CA/ILRC on SF APS funding in 2024-26; the 2007 agreement was reached by structured negotiation, not suit (a cooperative style). This supports 'quiet is a possible stable state'; there is no document on why.
proposals.parameter: adv_trust_decay (months for pressure to recover after a visible SFMTA action) and adv_escalate_on_fail (0/1)
proposals.range: adv_trust: pressure multiplier 0.2-1.0 for 6-24 months after SUBMIT/APPROVED; adv_escalate_on_fail in {0,1}, switching pressure to the high level on REJECTED/MISSED/delay > theta_parent.
proposals.rule_modified: Pressure source rate lambda_press (D3.1 pressure(t)) and the F-m quiet generator.

proposals.behaviour: Deadline-aligned pressure. The advocacy lead times its contact (letter, a request at the semiannual APS status meeting, a call to the SFMTA project lead) to the weeks before the known application deadline, and uses the days left to ask for a concrete bundled application. It does not apply pressure at an even background rate.
proposals.trigger: A public Caltrans calendar (C13 call 2026-07-01, deadline 2026-11-02) combined with the capital plan showing SG142 as a pure-APS line that is ineligible.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure arrives clustered in a pre-deadline window, so it raises p_start at the moment PREPARING can still start. Today lambda_press is a time-uniform event rate and pressure(t) decays over k months. A pressure event after the PREPARING lead time has already run out cannot produce a SUBMIT, so the same pressure volume has much less effect.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D10 has lambda_press and F-m has lambda_quiet. Neither is tied to the window calendar in D3.1. No section makes the pressure schedule a function of deadlines, so it is kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8 'Resources' rows: SA07 IV.J.2 requires 'meaningful participation' in SFMTA funding applications, and the semiannual meeting reports must cover 'funds applied for and status'. These are application-stage hooks. 01 s2.8 'Tunable parameter' row: activation rate unknown, test 0 and non-zero. No document support for deadline timing itself.
proposals.parameter: sync_press (window_sync): multiplier on lambda_press in the m_lead months before each known deadline, while lambda_press is cut proportionally elsewhere so the annual total stays the same.
proposals.range: sync_press in {1 (off), 2, 4}; m_lead U(1, 4) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start via pressure(t), and the D10 lambda_press schedule

proposals.behaviour: Pressure that carries a concrete ask. The advocate arrives with a ready answer to the 'cost / no funding' reply: bundle APS with the SG015 visibility carrier or with new countdown signal heads. Only the SG142 dollar figure and the 22 intersections need to be re-labelled. This makes it harder to deflect the pressure without a stated reason.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event that falls in the same window as an ineligible SG142 and a planned SG015 in the same cycle. The advocate has read the capital plan, the Caltrans Q&A (APS can ride on a new countdown head, SI18PB), and the MDC 2026 cost presentation.
proposals.effect_in_model: Cuts the deflection probability for that pressure event: p_deflect becomes p_deflect * (1 - delta_ask). It also cuts the preparation time D_prep for the bundled instance. The advocate writes the narrative and crash framing, and SFMTA only has to confirm the engineering.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 treats pressure as a scalar, and p_deflect is a constant on the task. PW1 is a path chosen by the model, not a lever an outside actor pulls. PW3 raises 'specified' but only after owner idle time. So it is kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.2 decision-rule row: SFMTA answers with 3 pages of 'Technical Challenges and Cost' ($40k to $1.5M) instead of an application. 01 s5 parameter table: SG142 about $22k per intersection against 'at least $40k' in the MDC presentation, unresolved conflict C4. 01 s3 bundling: the QA13 rule that APS may go with a new countdown. No document support that any advocate has done this.
proposals.parameter: delta_ask: relative drop in p_deflect, and a reduction in D_prep, when an ask-type pressure event happens.
proposals.range: delta_ask U(0, 0.6) for p_deflect; dD_prep U(0, 1.5) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (p_deflect), and D_prep in PREPARING

proposals.behaviour: Venue switching by signpost. Once HSIP is known to be closed to APS-only requests, the advocacy organisation moves its limited effort to the local funding window that is open now (Prop L five-year plan amendment, general-fund request) and does not spend more on HSIP. Failing that, it spends its effort on whichever venue shows the most recent sign of movement.
proposals.trigger: SG142 judged ineligible for C13; a Prop L amendment window or a budget cycle coming up; the advocate's own record showing no spoken support from SFMTA staff at HSIP.
proposals.effect_in_model: The pressure stream is divided across fields (HSIP, Prop L, general fund) by weights that update on signposts. The model's pressure(t) is divided across fields at fixed shares, so HSIP pressure is overestimated after ineligibility is known, and local-field pressure underestimated.
proposals.already_in_model: No. PW2 and PW6 move the model-level path across fields. No actor in C2 chooses where its pressure goes. D3.6 signposts switch A2's route, not the advocate's venue.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: 'Tunable parameter' row (activation rate unknown, test 0 and non-zero), and the 'Constraints' row that the advocate holds no enforcement tool after 2010. No document support for venue choice by advocates.
proposals.parameter: w_venue(t): share of lambda_press going to the venue on the open window; updated by a rule, w_HSIP = w0 * exp(-gamma * months since ineligibility signal).
proposals.range: gamma U(0, 0.5) per month; w0 in {0.33, 0.6, 0.9}; switch off with gamma = 0
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure(t) allocation across fields X, and the D3.6 signpost rules for PW2 and PW6

proposals.behaviour: Borrowed voice through the MDC / ODA channel. The advocacy lead asks the disability office to turn its stated 2026-07 intention (follow up with MTA and DPW, then advise and write a support letter) into an actual letter that names APS. The letter targets the SFMTA / SFCTA decision-makers, not Caltrans.
proposals.trigger: ODA staff said in July that they would come back with a letter recommendation, and nothing appeared on the September agenda. The advocate takes over the agenda follow-up.
proposals.effect_in_model: Converts MDC from a mere information channel into an occasional pressure source. A letter event adds a one-off bump to oversight(t) and pressure(t), but explicitly not to the Caltrans BCR score. This matters only if a Caltrans letter has zero score weight.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. O2 lists MDC as part of C2 (advocacy and its channel). D10 has 'MDC activation unknown' as an open parameter. D3.3 states support letters have no weight with Caltrans. The effect on SFMTA / SFCTA as an internal letter recipient is not written, so the proposal is limited to that.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7 incentive row: ODA staff proposed 'follow up with MTA, DPW ... then recommend and support letters' after 2026-07-17. 01 s2.7 timeline 2026-09-18: agenda, ODA report and LightHouse briefing had no APS and no support letter. 01 s2.7 'Constraints': letters on file are curb ramps only (2025-04, 2026-04-16). 01 s2.4 Caltrans: 'support letters not scored'.
proposals.parameter: p_letter: probability per year that advocacy converts the MDC channel into an APS letter, and its size.
proposals.range: p_letter U(0, 0.8) per year; bump size in oversight(t) U(0, 0.3)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 oversight and pressure terms in p_start (the MDC pressure source); D10 MDC activation parameter

proposals.behaviour: Vacancy-contingent escalation (or restraint) by the advocate. The advocacy organisation learns of the vacancy through the semiannual APS status report, staff contacts or an unanswered request. It then treats 'no named owner plus freeze' as a signpost. It raises pressure early: a written demand, a request for an off-cycle meeting, and a citation of the funding-seeking duty in the expired 2007 agreement. A cautious variant holds fire until a hire is made, so as not to burn goodwill with a counterpart who has just left.
proposals.trigger: owner is in the vacant state (F-h) and the freeze is on (F-i). Awareness is delayed until the next semiannual report or contact, up to 6 months.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes the pressure term for the duration of the vacancy: lambda_press is multiplied by m_vac after a notice lag t_notice. The factor is above 1 for escalation and below 1 for restraint. A secondary effect is to raise the daily chance that the D1 enforcement tier steps up (epsilon_enf). This lets pressure(t) in p_start and the deflection loop respond to the vacancy state. Under the written rules, vacancy affects only owner, and pressure is exogenous.
proposals.already_in_model: No. Pressure events arrive at an exogenous lambda_press (D10). F-m only adds random quiet periods that are independent of the A2 state. PW3 escalates only on the signpost 'no application for theta_idle months', which is a policy-path rule and not advocate behaviour. Nothing makes advocacy depend on the vacancy.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8 table: 'Every half-year the group receives the APS report'; 'LightHouse says it re-established the report, restored 2022-07' (an advocate that reacts to a lapse in information). 01 s2.8 parameter row: 'activation rate with no event unknown; test 0 and non-zero'. 01 s5 line 624 uses the same unknown. No document shows advocates reacting to a vacancy. Mark 'no document support' for the direction of the response.
proposals.parameter: m_vac (multiplier on lambda_press while owner is vacant) and t_notice (months from vacancy to advocate awareness)
proposals.range: m_vac in {0.3, 1, 2, 4}, with 1 as the current model. t_notice U(0, 6) months, from the semiannual cycle.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure(t) update and lambda_press in D10. It also adds a link between F-h and the epsilon_enf step in D1.

proposals.behaviour: Venue shifting: with the engineer gone and the A2 task hard to start, advocates stop addressing SFMTA staff. They take the request to the funder and the elected layer. This means asking SFCTA or a supervisor's office to propose a Prop L EP17 amendment, asking the board for a budget line, or seeking a legislative earmark. The ask changes from 'apply' to 'fund it'.
proposals.trigger: owner vacant and p_start low for a stretch (for example, no PREPARING task for theta_adv months), or an earlier pressure event that ended in DEFLECTED.
proposals.effect_in_model: Creates an advocate-initiated, exogenous trigger for the Prop L amendment event (F-j / PW2) and for a general-fund request. It also lowers q_veto, because the amendment arrives with a sponsor. It bypasses A2's task state machine for that route, so A2 vacancy no longer blocks it.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW2 and F-j model the amendment, but only as a policy path the designer chooses to start. The pressure-to-DEFLECTED branch (D3.1) points the deflection toward SFCTA and budget, but the advocate never follows it there. The advocate-initiated version of this behaviour is not in the model, so it is kept as a proposal.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 line 177: the D4 supervisor funded two APS-bearing signals through an NTP of $500k and a 3-4 month 5YPP amendment. 01 s2.3 line 188: the CAC has advice-only power. 01 s2.3 line 189: no CAC question about missing APS was found (inferred absence). 01 s2.8 line 320: the 2007 agreement SA07 s.IV.J.2 and s.V says plaintiffs support SFMTA's requests to the mayor and council. No document shows advocates currently lobbying the funder.
proposals.parameter: p_venue (probability per quarter, once the signpost holds, that advocacy launches a direct funder request)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.3) per quarter; 0 reproduces the current model. When fired, q_veto is multiplied by 0.5 to 1.0 and t_defer is unchanged.
proposals.rule_modified: F-j and PW2 start conditions. This adds a second start condition to the Prop L amendment event that does not pass through A2.

proposals.behaviour: Freeze-waiver campaign: advocates reframe the request from 'apply for APS funds' to 'exempt the vacant position from the freeze because it is essential and tied to a legal duty'. They aim at the hiring authority or the board, not at funding.
proposals.trigger: vacancy plus freeze (F-h with F-i), after a short mobilisation delay.
proposals.effect_in_model: Shortens the vacancy duration t_vac with probability p_waiver per quarter, so owner returns to its original tier sooner. It also ends the strain term from the freeze earlier for this one post. It leaves strain(t) for the wider Signal Shop unchanged.
proposals.already_in_model: No. t_vac is an exogenous U(3, 18) and strain_end is an exogenous date. Nothing in F-h or F-i lets an outside actor change the vacancy length.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 line 105: the DHR eligible list of 41 people in 2025-05, so a filled post is feasible once released. 01 s5 line 584: the freeze applies to 'non-essential' hiring in 2024-10, which implies an essential-post exception category exists. 01 s5 line 583: 6-9 months to fill an approved vacancy. No document shows advocates ever requesting such a waiver, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_waiver (probability per quarter that a vacant post is released from the freeze)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.25) per quarter; 0 is the current model. When it fires, the remaining t_vac becomes the 6-9 month fill time from 01 s5.
proposals.rule_modified: F-h recovery path (t_vac) and F-i, through a hazard on the vacancy state.

proposals.behaviour: Advocate-supplied preparation: while the engineer post is empty, the organisation (and its legal partners) hands the capital-budget team a ready package. The package holds a ranked intersection list, community requests, crash and user statements, and letters of support. The aim is to shorten the work needed to start an HSIP or local application, since there is nobody to draw it up.
proposals.trigger: vacancy plus an active pressure(t) above a threshold, and an open application window.
proposals.effect_in_model: Reduces D_prep (and so the chance of finishing before the deadline) by a fraction f_aid while the task is in PREPARING during the vacancy. It could also reduce the q_drop abort chance. It is a supply of capacity from outside the agency, which the model has nowhere to put.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D_prep and delta_split are fixed U() draws per window; only the actor's own state changes them. The agency is the sole behavioural actor (O2 table).
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8 line 320: SA07 s.IV.J.2 'meaningful participation' of plaintiffs in funding applications (so a past channel for joint preparation). 01 s2.7 line 283: ODA offered to 'follow up with MTA, DPW and then suggest support letters'. 01 s2.7 line 281: MOD co-funded and ranked DPW curb ramps. These show the form of assistance, but none shows advocates preparing APS applications. Otherwise 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: f_aid (fractional reduction of D_prep during vacancy) with an activation chance p_aid
proposals.range: f_aid in {0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.4}; p_aid U(0, 0.5) per window. 0 is the current model.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING duration D_prep + (m-1)*delta_split, and q_drop in F-h.

proposals.behaviour: Vacancy-triggered re-aiming of pressure. The advocacy lead sees the informal owner has gone and that pressure aimed at the vacant desk will hit nothing. They redirect pressure from the engineering group to a decision node that still has authority: the funding-body board (SFCTA, for a Prop L EP17 amendment), the budget/capital-planning office, or the elected level. The model's pressure event only targets task X in A2 and is answered by deflect-or-absorb.
proposals.trigger: Owner vacancy (F-h) with hiring freeze (F-i) active, plus no action on the task for more than a set number of months, and a funding window or amendment calendar visible ahead (EP17 amendment, 2027-autumn 5YPP, annual budget).
proposals.effect_in_model: While the vacancy lasts, a share of pressure events bypass A2. They raise the chance that the PW2 amendment path (or general-fund request) is put on a decision calendar, or lower the veto/defer probability there. They do not raise p_start via pressure(t) in the normal way. Pressure on A2 drops correspondingly, so the model shows a trade-off rather than a pure gain.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 / lambda_press gives one undirected stream of pressure into pressure(t); PW3 doubles it; F-j has q_veto and t_defer as fixed random draws. Nothing makes the target of pressure depend on vacancy, and nothing lets pressure act on q_veto/t_defer. Not covered by any 02 section, so kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: 'Agreement IV.J.2 requires SFMTA to let plaintiffs participate meaningfully in its Prop K funding applications; plaintiffs support SFMTA requests to mayor and council' (SA07 IV.J.2, V). 01 s2.8 also records advocates getting the semiannual report restored in 2022. 01 s2.3 notes the amendment precedent of 3-4 months. Redirecting during a vacancy has no document support; it is an inference from these standing channels.
proposals.parameter: phi_redirect: share of pressure events routed to funder-level targets while owner is vacant.
proposals.range: U(0, 0.8). Effect on F-j: q_veto multiplied by (1 - gamma_redirect*phi), gamma_redirect U(0, 0.5); t_defer shortened by the same factor. Reverts to 0 when the post is filled.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure branch (split of the 1-p_deflect arm); F-j (q_veto, t_defer); D10 lambda_press target field.

proposals.behaviour: Advocate fills the vacant coordination role: the organisation itself assembles the application inputs (a ranked list of intersections, crash and complaint evidence, endorsement letters) and hands them to the capital-budget staff, cutting preparation time. This is a substitute for the missing owner, not pressure.
proposals.trigger: Owner vacancy plus a published deadline (C13 on 2026-11-02, or the next window) and the advocate judging that a missed window costs two years.
proposals.effect_in_model: Reduces D_prep (and the delta_split cost of splitting) for a PREPARING task while the vacancy lasts, and lifts the abandon chance q_drop from F-h downward. The effect has a cost: advocate capacity is limited, so it applies to at most one field at a time and decays if the advocate also runs other campaigns.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 treats D_prep as exogenous U(1,6) and F-h only lowers owner and applies q_drop; the advocate (C2) only emits pressure events (O2 actor table). Not covered, kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: advocates have, from the agreement, rights to the semiannual report that includes 'funds applied for and status' and 'efforts to obtain Caltrans funds'. This shows they hold the information. No document shows an advocate drafting application material, so: no document support for the drafting itself.
proposals.parameter: sigma_assist: fractional cut in D_prep, and in the PREPARING abort chance q_drop, while vacant and while an advocate-assist switch is on.
proposals.range: sigma_assist U(0, 0.5); switch on/off; max one concurrent field.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING duration and the q_drop clause of F-h.

proposals.behaviour: Window-timed escalation: the advocate holds back pressure until just before a decision window or hearing, then concentrates it, instead of a steady Poisson stream. Possibly also saves the formal escalation (legal threat) for the moment when a hiring freeze removes the 'we are staffing up' excuse.
proposals.trigger: Knowledge of the funding calendar (HSIP deadline, 5YPP cycle, budget hearings, semiannual meeting) and a belief that early pressure is absorbed by the vacancy (the deflect reply 'no staff').
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure arrivals move from rate lambda_press to bursts in the m months before each window opens. Within the burst the pressure counts are higher and p_deflect is lower, because a refusal right at a deadline is more costly to the receiving office. Outside bursts the rate falls. Net annual pressure is held constant, so the test is only whether timing matters.
proposals.already_in_model: No. lambda_press is a constant-rate process (D10), with decay k; F-m only switches it off for a stretch. Windows are exogenous (O2) but pressure is not tied to them. Kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7.1: the 2026-07-17 and 2026-09-18 meetings show APS on the agenda only as an information item, with zero public comment, and no support letter after the official said they would come back. This shows pressure is not timed to windows in the record. No document support for deliberate timing; it is a counterfactual for the model.
proposals.parameter: sw_timed: switch for window-locked pressure; burst length m_burst; share of annual pressure placed in bursts f_burst.
proposals.range: sw_timed in {0,1}; m_burst U(1, 4) months; f_burst U(0.5, 1.0). p_deflect inside burst = p_deflect * (1 - d_burst), d_burst U(0, 0.4).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure arrival process and the p_deflect draw; D10 lambda_press.

proposals.behaviour: Reframing and bundling with a different ADA claim: the advocate joins the disability-access coalition and ties APS to the curb-ramp / PROWAG / transition-plan agenda, where a federal schedule obligation exists, so that APS rides on a funding stream that has a time limit and a stronger legal footing.
proposals.trigger: The vacancy plus the evidence that curb ramps get letters and budget increases while APS gets none; a window in which ramp funding is rising.
proposals.effect_in_model: Opens a new carrier for some intersections: APS added as a scope item to curb-ramp work orders (an external actor, DPW, supplies the schedule). Adds a probability that a C-type intersection is served without A2 preparing anything. It also makes pressure double-count against both topics, so it competes for advocate effort with direct APS pressure.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW5 (design standard) and PW6 (existing SG017) bundle APS into hardware work, and 'merged into existing projects' is a route. But those are owned by SFMTA staff. A coalition-driven link to ramps via an outside actor is not there. Kept, narrower than a new pathway.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: curb ramps have a federal transition-plan time obligation (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)), 'APS has no corresponding federal schedule obligation'; both 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 MDC letters were about ramps, none about APS. Also ODA asked DPW and MTA to coordinate (MDC26t). So the gap is documented; the advocate acting on it has no document support.
proposals.parameter: lambda_ramp: yearly chance per C-type intersection that a ramp job is allowed to carry an APS add-on, set by coalition effort; coalition share c_coal of advocate effort.
proposals.range: lambda_ramp U(0, 0.05)/yr per intersection scaled by c_coal U(0, 0.5); a total yearly cap on add-on cost b_ramp U($0, $200k).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 delivery routes (new row beside PW5/PW6 generation); D3.6 PW5 event generation; D10 effort split with lambda_press.

proposals.behaviour: Accepting a lower-ambition substitute: given the freeze, the advocate settles for a procedural commitment (named owner, a reporting date, a pre-funding deadline) instead of money, and may withdraw the stronger demand to keep the relationship, or the reverse, trading silence for a verbal promise that is never enforced.
proposals.trigger: Hiring freeze makes new money or new posts look impossible, and the agency offers a verbal assurance, a meeting or a report.
proposals.effect_in_model: The advocate's pressure is converted into a one-off bump to oversight and specified, then pressure is damped for a quiet period. If the promise is not kept, the advocate's trust falls and the next escalation step is quicker, which links to the D1 ladder.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW3 raises owner/specified/oversight by policy design and F-m turns pressure off at random. Neither makes the advocate's own concession and later trust loss depend on whether the promise is kept. Kept, but a weaker proposal.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: after 2010 plaintiffs are only consulted and cannot set deadlines (MDC23 slide 10); the semiannual report restart in 2022 was achieved through advocacy and is the only recorded procedural win. 2024-26: no public statements from advocacy groups on APS funding found. No direct document support for settling for promises.
proposals.parameter: q_accept: probability that an agency procedural offer pauses pressure; trust state tau_trust that raises eps_enf when a promise lapses.
proposals.range: q_accept U(0, 0.7); pause t_quiet reused U(6, 36) months; eps_enf multiplier after lapse m_lapse U(1, 3).
proposals.rule_modified: F-m (quiet period becomes conditional and not random); D1 enforcement escalation rate eps_enf; oversight/specified draws.

proposals.behaviour: District-supervisor earmark route. Advocates ask a district supervisor to put APS into the Neighborhood Transportation Program (EP25) recommendation, instead of waiting for the HSIP line or a Prop L amendment.
proposals.trigger: A deflection (DEFLECTED), or a signal that SG142 is ineligible in C13 (F-a or F-b). Advocates need a quick local source before the deadline passes.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a funding source outside PW0-PW6 and F-j/F-k. A small local grant ($0.5M-scale) for C-type intersections in one district goes through a short 5YPP amendment (3-4 months). That bypasses the BCR gate, the PIF requirement and the HSIP deadline, and it is limited to the district's intersections.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in 02. A search for NTP, EP25 and supervisor in 02 found nothing. PW2 covers only the Prop L EP17 amendment, and F-k covers only the director's 10% reallocation and the SG000 reserve.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: EP25 NTP, each district $700k over FY24-28 (NTP5 p.7-8). A district supervisor used $500k of NTP to design two new signals with APS in 3-4 months, after the 2024-11 Prop K item (LW p.15-18). 01 section 2.6 says the mayor and council move money indirectly through supervisors on the SFCTA board and through NTP recommendations.
proposals.parameter: sw_ntp (0/1) and q_ntp, the probability per year that a district earmark is granted when advocacy pressure is active. Add t_ntp, the lag, and b_ntp, the grant size.
proposals.range: q_ntp U(0, 0.3) per year; b_ntp U($200k, $500k); t_ntp U(3, 6) months; sw_ntp in {0,1}
proposals.rule_modified: Adds a new branch to the D3.6 pathway table, between PW2 and the general-fund step, and a new local-fund source in D3.2. It bypasses the p_start gate for the covered intersections.

proposals.behaviour: Pre-deadline scope lobbying on the carrier. Advocates ask SFMTA, before the C13 submission, to widen SG015's named-corridor scope, or to pair SG142 intersections with SG015 intersections, so that more pending C-type intersections can be carried by a visibility project that is itself HSIP-eligible.
proposals.trigger: The C13 deadline is next week, SG142 is APS-only and ineligible, and SG015 is in the same cycle. The only cheap fix is to attach the pending intersections to the eligible package.
proposals.effect_in_model: Widens the PW1 candidate set in C13, not C14. Today PW1 allows only intersections on the five named corridors, about 1 intersection. With scope lobbying, a share of other C-type intersections becomes eligible in C13, which changes the PW1 BCR and the F-a pass rate. The cost is that SFMTA's design-prep time D_prep grows.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW1 widens to other corridors in C14 after a C13 failure. The C13 widening by pre-deadline lobbying is not modelled. The task state machine has no way for advocates to change the package contents.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 3 note: the SG015 scope is limited to five named corridors, with priority on arterials with existing poles (line 444). SG142 and SG015 are listed in the same cycle (line 442). SG142 is ineligible as written (line 420). 01 section 2.4: support letters carry no score (QA13 Q32, Q68), so the lever is package scope, not letters.
proposals.parameter: p_scope_widen, the probability that the pre-deadline ask succeeds; f_widen, the share of non-corridor C-type intersections added to the PW1 candidate set. Only active if the ask comes at least one preparation period before the deadline.
proposals.range: p_scope_widen U(0, 0.4); f_widen U(0, 0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.3 packaging step 1 (candidate selection) and D3.6 PW1 start condition. It also changes m, the number of instances, in D3.1.

proposals.behaviour: Window-focused pressure. Advocates know the HSIP submission window and the Prop L allocation calendar, so they concentrate their contact in the few weeks before the deadline instead of spreading it at a steady rate.
proposals.trigger: A known external deadline within a short horizon. Here the C13 deadline is next week, so the PREPARING decision has to be made now.
proposals.effect_in_model: pressure(t) rises sharply just before each window and is near zero between windows. The effect on p_start is then largest at the one moment when U < p_start matters. A given annual pressure budget has more effect than a uniform rate gives. Quiet spells (F-m) are mostly harmless when they fall between windows.
proposals.already_in_model: No. lambda_press is a constant rate (D10) and pressure(t) decays with k. Neither depends on the calendar. F-m creates quiet spells at random, not by calendar.
proposals.evidence: no document support for timing behaviour. Related: 01 section 2.8 records that LightHouse got the semiannual report re-established (2022-07), which shows event-driven action. 01 section 5 treats the no-event activation rate as unknown, with no data for 2024-26.
proposals.parameter: omega_window: multiplier on lambda_press in the w months before a window deadline, with the annual total held fixed. omega = 1 gives the current model.
proposals.range: omega U(1, 5); w U(1, 3) months
proposals.rule_modified: The lambda_press event generator and pressure(t) in D3.1 and D3.2 (the p_start formula).

proposals.behaviour: Forum shopping after a deflection. When SFMTA staff reply 'cost, no funding' and point at SFCTA, the budget office or Caltrans, advocates take the same ask to the point named, for example the SFCTA board and its citizens advisory committee, rather than letting the pressure fade.
proposals.trigger: The task enters DEFLECTED (p_deflect). The deflection letter itself names the next place to go.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure on a deflected task is not lost. With probability p_escalate it becomes a pressure event on the Prop L amendment path: q_veto falls and t_defer shortens for the next amendment. It also adds a small boost to oversight(t). The effect is to convert the deflection into a start of PW2 earlier than the current trigger (rejection or deferral past theta_defer).
proposals.already_in_model: No. In D3.1 a deflected task goes to IDLE after r months and 'this pressure leaves no effect'. PW2 starts only by scenario, not by an advocate reaction to a deflection.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: a supervisor on the SFCTA board turned a request into a 5YPP amendment in 3-4 months (D4 precedent, LW p.15-18). 02 D3.1 itself says the staff reply points to SFCTA, the budget office or Caltrans. 01 section 2.1 evidence on mutual blame (MDC26 p.4-6, p.8). No document shows advocates actually doing this in 2024-26 (01 section 7 row 7: no data on advocate behaviour).
proposals.parameter: p_escalate: the probability that a deflected pressure event is passed on to SFCTA. delta_veto: reduction of q_veto, applied for k months.
proposals.range: p_escalate U(0, 0.6); delta_veto U(0, 0.3)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (the 'leaves no effect' clause), and F-j (q_veto, t_defer) plus the PW2 start condition in D3.6.

proposals.behaviour: External shadow steward. With the informal owner gone, the advocacy org's policy lead keeps its own tracker of the ~76 pending requests, drafts location lists, crash/site data and scoring arguments, and hands a near-ready package to whoever covers the desk (or to the Signal Shop on a call). The org supplies preparation labour and continuity instead of only pressure.
proposals.trigger: Owner vacancy (F-h) plus hiring freeze (F-i) with no response to pressure within some months; the org judges that waiting for a hire costs more than donating effort.
proposals.effect_in_model: While vacant, PREPARING can still start at a reduced but non-zero rate: owner is raised from weak to an intermediate tier (via an external-steward term) and D_prep is shortened by a fraction. It partly offsets the F-h drop in owner and the q_drop abort. It acts on A2's task state machine, not on the advocate's pressure channel.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.1/D3.2 give advocates only pressure(t) (events, decay k, deflect p_deflect); owner is a property of A2 and falls under F-h. PW3 raises oversight/owner only as a policy path, not as an endogenous advocate response. Not in D3.5 F-a..F-m.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: SA07 IV.J.2 'meaningful participation' in the funding applications; semiannual reports must list funds applied for; LightHouse claims it re-established the report in 2022-07 (lighthouse-aps-are-they-working-43407). 01 s2.9 Portland: 11 community-originated requests. No document shows an advocate doing application prep in SF, so the support is indirect.
proposals.parameter: p_steward (per prep window, probability the org supplies a prep package) with companion rho_ext (fraction of D_prep removed)
proposals.range: p_steward U(0, 0.5), 0 = off; rho_ext U(0.1, 0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start (adds beta_ext*steward term; owner floor while vacant) and the D_prep formula; softens F-h's owner drop and q_drop

proposals.behaviour: Pressure redirected from the vacant desk to the funders. Because nobody at A2 can act, the policy lead lobbies the funder-side nodes directly: SFCTA / its citizens advisory committee on the next 5-year plan, the Board of Supervisors / Mayor budget process, and the SFMTA director, asking for an APS line or earmark that does not depend on an A2 application.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus a prior deflection (DEFLECTED state) pointing the org to SFCTA / budget / Caltrans: the org takes the pointer literally and follows the buck-passing arrow.
proposals.effect_in_model: A share phi of pressure events is routed to funder nodes instead of the A2 task. It lowers q_veto and t_defer (F-j), raises q_dir (F-k, director 10% / SG000 use for APS) and may create a funding line without any application. Pressure aimed at A2 shrinks accordingly.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly no. 02 D3.1 DEFLECTED only sends the pressure away, and pressure(t) enters only p_start at A2. F-j and F-k are independent random events not driven by advocates. Advocates never act on the funder nodes.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: SA07 IV.J.2 and V (plaintiffs support SFMTA's requests to the Mayor and Board). 01 s2.2 and s2.3 (director adjustment, Prop L amendment precedents, 5YPP cycle). 01 s1.2 closed loop 'no funding -> no application' is exactly what this behaviour tries to break from outside. No SF record of this being done in 2024-26 (s2.8: zero public statements found).
proposals.parameter: phi_redirect, fraction of pressure events sent to funder nodes
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6), 0 = current model
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure branching (third outcome after p_deflect); F-j (q_veto, t_defer) and F-k (q_dir) become functions of redirected pressure

proposals.behaviour: Vacancy-triggered early escalation. The org treats a vacant, unfilled owner post as a visible breach of accountability (no named contact, no scoring) and sends a demand letter or a notice invoking the 2007 settlement's duty to seek funds and ADA meaningful access, earlier than it would otherwise.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy duration exceeds a tolerance threshold, especially when the semiannual report is skipped or no named contact exists.
proposals.effect_in_model: The annual rate of raising the external-enforcement tier (D1) is multiplied while owner = vacant and no reply. Raises enforce(t) in p_start once the tier moves, and may switch on the pathway-style negotiation step in the baseline.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly no. eps_enf (D10) is a constant yearly rate U(0, 0.1); D1 escalation to negotiation/suit occurs conditionally only inside PW3 (D3.6). In the baseline path it is not conditional on vacancy.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.10: NYC 2024 amended order 'full effort to secure funds'; SF 2007 agreement expired 2010-06-30 with no later enforcement record (lflegal index). 01 s2.1: senior engineer cites the litigation environment as a reason to coordinate with curb ramps. No document shows SF advocates escalating after a staffing gap, so the support is only a plausible trigger.
proposals.parameter: m_vac_enf, multiplier on eps_enf while owner vacant for longer than tau_tol months
proposals.range: m_vac_enf U(1, 5); tau_tol U(3, 9) months
proposals.rule_modified: eps_enf in D10 / D1 tier update; F-h now couples to the enforce(t) term

proposals.behaviour: Strategic waiting, then a timed push. The org deliberately holds back during the vacancy, to avoid burning bridges with a successor and to avoid pressuring a desk that cannot answer, then concentrates its pressure shortly after the post is filled or just before the preparation window opens (window timing, such as the 1 January local-field window or HSIP deadline).
proposals.trigger: Hiring freeze with an unknown end date; knowledge that p_start only matters in open windows and that new hires are most receptive early.
proposals.effect_in_model: During vacancy lambda_press is scaled down; at refill, a pulse of pressure events is released (or a window-aligned pulse). Pressure is no longer a memoryless Poisson stream, it is timed so it falls in windows where p_start applies and the owner is present.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-m (02 D3.5) is an exogenous random quiet period with no refill pulse; lambda_press is constant (x2 only for PW3 start); k is a pure decay. Timing to windows or refill is not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: advocates' activation rate in quiet times unknown, tested at 0 and non-zero (0.1-0.5/yr); LightHouse restoring the semiannual report is the counter-example. No document on timing choices, so no document support for the timing itself.
proposals.parameter: pulse_mult, size of the post-refill pressure pulse, with hold_frac (share of lambda_press kept while vacant)
proposals.range: hold_frac U(0, 1); pulse_mult U(1, 4) events at refill; 1 and 1 = current model
proposals.rule_modified: lambda_press schedule in the monthly step 'owner leaves / refill, pressure' (O3 step 2); links F-h refill event to pressure(t)

proposals.behaviour: Venue shifting. When the engineering owner post is vacant, the advocacy policy lead stops sending pressure to the SFMTA engineering node (which cannot act) and routes it upstream to the SFCTA board and Prop L amendment process, the budget/Capital Planning route, and MDC/ODA. The target is the funder that could write a dedicated APS line, not the vacant desk.
proposals.trigger: F-h owner vacancy (and F-i hiring freeze): the desk that normally receives a request is known to be empty, and the semiannual report or reply is overdue or answered only with 'cost / no funds'.
proposals.effect_in_model: Today every pressure event goes into pressure(t) and feeds only A2's p_start (D3.1), or is deflected back to SFCTA/budget/Caltrans (p_deflect). With this switch, during a vacancy a share v_shift of pressure events bypasses pressure(t). They instead (a) lower q_veto for the Prop L EP17 amendment (F-j) and shorten t_defer, and (b) raise the chance the general-fund annual request is entered (PW2 second step). Net effect: the vacancy makes upstream funding lines more likely at the same time as it makes A2 application starts less likely. This can produce a money-flows-without-an-owner path that the M-A deflection loop does not allow.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in model. F-m covers pressure going quiet, PW3 covers a one-time escalation to negotiation/suit, PW2 covers Prop L amendment as an exogenous intervention path. None of them has pressure re-targeting itself as an endogenous response to F-h. DROP check: I found no D3.2/D3.5 rule where an advocate's pressure changes q_veto or t_defer.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8: SA07 §IV.J.2 plaintiffs 'support SFMTA requests to the mayor and council' and take part in Prop K applications (so upstream venues are part of the advocate's historical repertoire); LightHouse pushed the semiannual report back in 2022-07 (counter-example to inactivity). 01 §2.3 / 02 F-j: Prop L amendment decided by the SFCTA board, with a 3-4 month precedent. No direct document of an advocate re-targeting during a vacancy: 'no document support' for the trigger itself.
proposals.parameter: v_shift
proposals.range: U(0, 0.7); default 0.3. Active only while owner is in the vacant state (F-h) or strain_end has not passed. Effect size when active: q_veto multiplied by (1 − 0.5·v_shift), t_defer multiplied by (1 − 0.3·v_shift).
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure(t) routing (split into pressure_A2 and pressure_upstream) and F-j (q_veto, t_defer); gated by F-h/F-i.

proposals.behaviour: Reframe the request as part of the curb-ramp / ADA transition-plan obligation, so APS rides on a funding stream that already has a legal timetable and recurring MDC support letters. The advocate joins the curb-ramp coalition and asks for 'APS wherever ramps are rebuilt' instead of asking for a separate APS line.
proposals.trigger: A stand-alone APS ask has been answered with cost/no-funds (deflection), and the ramp program is visibly funded (annual MDC letters) while APS is not.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a ramp-rider channel that does not need the vacant APS owner. With probability p_ramp_rider per ramp-program funding event, a C-class pending intersection whose ramp is rebuilt gets APS as a funded add-on. This bypasses A2's PREPARING task, uses a different money pool (ramp budget), and competes with it for Public Works/contractor capacity. It also increases per-intersection cost pressure (ramps are about $200k each), so the cost_by_actor output shifts toward the ramp program.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW4 'merge with parent project' and PW5 'design standard on hardware change' use SFMTA's own projects and maintenance budget. Neither models an advocate-driven riding of the ramp program or its legal timetable. DROP check: not found in D3.6 or D3.2 as an advocate action, so kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7 (line ~279): MDC letters of 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 both concern curb ramps, none concerns APS. 01 §2.7 (line ~284): ramps have a federal transition-plan timetable (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)); APS has no equivalent obligation. 01 §2.1: digging triggers ramp work and 'installing together is cheapest' (MDC23 p.6, MDC26 p.7).
proposals.parameter: p_ramp_rider
proposals.range: U(0, 0.4) per ramp-funding event per eligible C-class intersection; switch sw_ramp_rider ∈ {0,1}. Cost add-on uses existing u0.
proposals.rule_modified: New arrival path into D3.4 'concurrent project' delivery (Fs to I) plus a new row in the D3.2 mechanism-switch matrix; PW4 gets a fourth route.

proposals.behaviour: Informal substitute ownership. The advocacy organisation offers to act as the de facto owner of the request: it keeps the list of pending intersections, prepares crash/priority data and a draft packaging argument, and names a successor contact inside the agency, so the vacant desk only has to sign off.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy plus hiring freeze lasting longer than a threshold θ_vac months, with a funding window (HSIP call or Prop L cycle) approaching.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the penalty of the owner drop in F-h. owner falls by one tier less (or D_prep falls by a fraction), and q_drop for PREPARING tasks decreases. It does not change the capacity of the Signal Shop or the BCR rules. It also adds a cost to the advocate side (reported in cost_by_actor) and a possible conflict-of-interest route: applications prepared with outside help may be treated differently in the eligibility review. This tests whether an outside owner can substitute for an inside one, which the model currently cannot represent because owner is purely internal.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in model. F-h only lets the owner drop and later recover by hiring (t_vac); strain/K_crew are internal; advocates exist only as pressure and enforcement tier (D1). DROP check: no assistance rule found.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1: only one associate engineer scores all requests (single point of failure). 01 §2.8: SA07 §IV.J.1/J.2 gives the advocates semiannual meetings and 'meaningful participation' in funding applications, so a legal basis for assistance exists. No document shows advocates drafting an application: 'no document support' for the behaviour itself.
proposals.parameter: adv_assist
proposals.range: U(0, 0.5) fraction by which D_prep is cut and the F-h owner drop is softened; active when vacancy duration > θ_vac, θ_vac U(2, 9) months; switch sw_adv_assist ∈ {0,1}.
proposals.rule_modified: F-h (owner drop size, q_drop) and D3.1 PREPARING duration D_prep.

proposals.behaviour: Calendar-timed pressure. The advocate holds back the ask until a decision window is open and then concentrates it: before the HSIP call or the Prop L / budget cycle, instead of at a constant rate. During a vacancy it may deliberately wait until the post is filled so that the pressure lands on a named person who can act.
proposals.trigger: Vacancy with a visible expected fill date, or an approaching window in the §O3 event table. The advocate judges that pressure now would only be deflected (p_deflect high) and is wasted.
proposals.effect_in_model: λ_press is currently a constant Poisson rate (U(0, 0.5)/yr, doubled by PW3). Replace it with a time-varying rate: the same total, but a share w_sync of events is moved to the k months before each window opens, and a share w_wait is withheld while the owner is vacant and released on fill. This changes how often a pressure event meets a state in which p_start can use it (window open, owner present) versus a state in which it is deflected or decays (k-month decay). Predicted: the same annual pressure produces more starts when synchronised, fewer when withheld.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in model. F-m (quiet periods) and PW3 (escalation after θ_idle) are exogenous or follow an idle trigger; pressure decay over k months exists but pressure is not timed to windows. DROP check: no window-synchronised rule found in D3.1/D3.5.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7.1: ODA said it would come back with a support-letter recommendation after 2026-07; the next agenda (2026-09-18) had no APS item, so timing relative to meetings matters. 01 §2.8: 'activation rate unknown; test 0 and non-zero'. No document of calendar-timed or withheld pressure: 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: w_sync (and w_wait)
proposals.range: w_sync U(0, 0.8) share of annual pressure events moved into the 1-6 months before a window opens; w_wait ∈ {0, 1} switch, which withholds events while the owner is vacant, with release lag U(0, 3) months after fill.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure(t) arrival process (λ_press) and its interaction with the §O3 window schedule; interacts with F-h and F-m.

proposals.behaviour: Venue shifting: instead of pressing the A2 (SFMTA) task owner, advocates take the same complaint to the funder or elected venue (SFCTA board and CAC, a district supervisor, SFMTA board) and ask for a specific earmark. Examples are a New Tenant Program-type (NTP) design grant or a 5YPP amendment that names APS.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event is answered with the cost / no-money line (the DEFLECTED branch), or SFMTA says it is not the applicant for that fund. The advocate then concludes that the staff-level route is closed. Strength rises when a window is near (5YPP round 2027 autumn to 2028).
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure no longer only feeds p_start through pressure(t). A fraction of pressure events bypasses the A2 task machine and raises the chance that a Prop L amendment or local dedicated line is opened. In effect it lowers the F-j trigger, shortens t_defer, or injects a funded local batch that SFMTA then has to accept and deliver. It also makes SFMTA's deflection a cause of venue shifting rather than a dead end.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW2 'local first' (D3.6) starts with an EP17 amendment, but it is a policy pathway chosen by the experimenter, not a behaviour that advocates trigger after a deflection. F-j (D3.5) covers veto and delay of the amendment but not who starts it. D3.1 routes all pressure through p_start. So the mechanism of advocate-initiated bypass is not captured.
proposals.evidence: 01 sec 2.3 (about l.177): a district supervisor used an NTP grant of $500k to design two signals with APS in Lincoln Way, and the 5YPP amendment took 3-4 months. 01 l.83: the 'no money and no application' loop, where advocates 'have no resource to force an application'. 01 sec 2.8 l.320: the 2007 agreement already gave plaintiffs a role in SFMTA's funding applications. No document shows APS advocates doing this in 2024-26 (01 l.331: no public statements found), so the trigger is inferred.
proposals.parameter: p_venue (probability that a deflected pressure event is re-routed to a funder or elected venue)
proposals.range: U(0, 0.4) per deflected event, 0 as the control. If it fires, then with probability (1 - q_veto) a local APS earmark of $0.25-0.5M is created after t_defer months and the PW2 route opens without the experimenter starting it.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (add a third exit); links to F-j and PW2 start conditions.

proposals.behaviour: Window-timed pressure: advocates concentrate their asks in the months before a fund window opens or a deadline falls (HSIP cycle deadline, FY budget cycle, 5YPP round), and stay quiet or low in between.
proposals.trigger: A published calendar event: HSIP call, SFMTA budget hearing, SFCTA 5YPP update, or an SFMTA disability council agenda item that references funding.
proposals.effect_in_model: The number of effective pressure events per year stays the same, but their timing aligns with the months in which p_start is evaluated (task machine starts only when the window is open). With a pressure(t) decay constant k of 1-12 months, a uniformly random Poisson stream mostly decays before the window. Aligned pressure can raise p_start much more at the same cost to advocates. It also makes the effect of a quiet spell (F-m) depend on whether it overlaps a window.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 / D10 have lambda_press as a Poisson rate with exponential decay k, independent of the window schedule (O3 event table). F-m only turns pressure off at random.
proposals.evidence: No document support for advocates' timing. Support for the mechanism exists only on the window side: 01 sec 2.3 and 3 (5YPP next round 2027 autumn to 2028; HSIP C13 deadline and C14 2028-07); 01 l.177 (3-4 month amendment).
proposals.parameter: w_sync (share of pressure events whose timing is moved to the m_lead months before the next open window)
proposals.range: w_sync in {0, 0.5, 1}; m_lead U(1, 6) months. Holds the annual event total fixed (lambda_press unchanged).
proposals.rule_modified: O3 pressure event generation (step 2 of the monthly loop) and its interaction with the window check in D3.1.

proposals.behaviour: Deflection ratchet and cost rebuttal: advocates keep a written record of each 'costly / no funds' reply and answer the next one with peer unit-cost benchmarks (packaged HSIP projects at $10k-76k per intersection) and a request for a named application and a date. Repeated deflection then becomes harder for SFMTA to use.
proposals.trigger: A second or later DEFLECTED event within a short period (e.g. 24 months). Triggered more strongly when peer cost data are available and when the semiannual report or the 60-day notice rules give a venue for the reply.
proposals.effect_in_model: p_deflect falls with the number of recent deflections instead of staying fixed, and a deflected event leaves some residual pressure instead of none. Over several years this changes the shape of the outcome: early pressure looks wasted, later pressure converts. It also lets the experimenter test whether a documented-record strategy beats volume.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 says a DEFLECTED event 'leaves no effect' after r months and p_deflect is one fixed parameter. PW3 (D3.6) sets owner, specified and oversight stronger by policy but does not model advocate learning.
proposals.evidence: 01 l.83 and sec 2.1 l.130: SFMTA answers with a cost presentation (min $40k, max $1.5M, pipes and ramps about $200k each) and 'selected based on funding'. 01 l.378 and l.609: packaged unit cost $10k-76k elsewhere in California. 01 sec 2.8: LightHouse says it got the semiannual report re-established (2022-07), an example of record-keeping working. 01 l.331 shows no current public replies, so the behaviour itself is unsupported.
proposals.parameter: rho_ratchet (fractional reduction in p_deflect per deflection in the last 24 months) with phi_resid (share of pressure retained after a deflection)
proposals.range: rho_ratchet U(0, 0.3) with floor p_deflect >= 0.2 x baseline; phi_resid U(0, 0.5); both 0 = current model.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch and the p_deflect draw; adds a state counter per field.

proposals.behaviour: Scope-add at parent-project design: advocates attend design outreach, CAC and board comment on funded signal or corridor projects and ask that pending-list intersections or APS hardware be added to the scope while design is still open.
proposals.trigger: A parent project (SS4A, corridor, new signal) is in design or in a 5YPP/grant action and contains or is near pending-list intersections whose APS inclusion is marked 'likely' or 'not verified'.
proposals.effect_in_model: The inclusion probability pi for 'bundled into existing project' intersections is not a fixed draw but can be raised during the design window (after that, change orders cost more). It can pull some of the 52 unidentified-parent and 'likely' intersections out of the never_served pool without any new application, and without using the A2 task machine.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.4 has pi as a static probability of staying in scope; PW4 (D3.6) adds corridor candidates 'added at design time' but as an SFMTA-side routing choice. No advocate action changes pi over time.
proposals.evidence: 01 sec 3 (about l.432-456, l.482): parent projects, 3 completed, several 'likely, not verified' such as Eddy/Fillmore (12 of 16 intersections say APS) and Golden Gate/Larkin. 01 l.206: APS is funded when attached to new countdown signals. Advocate role in such comment: no document support (l.331).
proposals.parameter: d_add (increase in pi for a parent project if an advocacy event lands during its design window)
proposals.range: d_add U(0, 0.3), capped at pi = 1; window = design months of the parent project (from t_dsg); 0 = current model.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 'already in project' row (pi becomes pi + d_add x 1{pressure event in design window}); PW4 start condition.

proposals.behaviour: Coalition support for SFMTA requests: advocates, as the agreement already contemplates, publicly back SFMTA's own request for APS money and bring in allied groups (Vision Zero, bike/ped, senior and disability groups). The pressure turns from 'you must' to 'we will help you win it'.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA agrees, or is pushed, to file a request (an amendment, a general-fund ask, an HSIP package) and the vote or review is contested or uncertain. It also fits after a deflection when SFMTA says the board 'would not approve'.
proposals.effect_in_model: It lowers the veto or delay risk at the second gate rather than the start risk at the first gate. q_veto, t_defer and q_topup, which are exogenous draws now, would depend on whether supporters exist. It also changes the experimenter's reading of pathways that hinge on a board vote (PW2, PW6).
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-j (D3.5) fixes q_veto U(0, 0.5), F-e and F-f fix q_topup, with no link to advocate activity. D3.1 pressure only goes to the task start.
proposals.evidence: 01 sec 2.8 l.320: agreement section IV.J.2 and V: plaintiffs 'support SFMTA's requests to the mayor and board' and must be allowed to take part in the Prop K application. 01 sec 2.3: the amendment precedent of 3-4 months. No evidence of current coalition behaviour.
proposals.parameter: omega_support (relative cut in q_veto, t_defer and the q_topup shortfall when advocates are active that year)
proposals.range: omega_support U(0, 0.5), applied as q_veto x (1 - omega_support x 1{active}); 0 = current model. 'active' reuses the existing lambda_press / lambda_quiet state, so no new random process.
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (q_veto, t_defer) and F-e/F-f (q_topup) draws.

proposals.behaviour: Follow-the-pointer re-aiming. When SFMTA answers 'costly, no money' and points to the budget or the county transportation authority, advocates take the same complaint to the funder (authority board, budget hearings, Board of Supervisors) instead of dropping it. The deflected pressure is converted into pressure on the funding-holder.
proposals.trigger: A pressure event ends in DEFLECTED, i.e. the exact meeting described in the situation, where the reply names a different body as holding the money.
proposals.effect_in_model: A share of deflected pressure is re-booked as pressure on the funder-side tasks (Prop L amendment, general-fund request, and SG017 grant wording) instead of being discarded. This raises p_start for local-fund windows and lowers the chance of F-j veto or delay (q_veto, t_defer), but leaves the SFMTA engineering task unchanged.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.1 states that a DEFLECTED task is 'this pressure leaves no effect', and only the 1 - p_deflect branch is added to pressure(t). F-m only covers advocates going quiet, not re-aiming. PW2 and PW3 are policy paths, not a reaction to deflection.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.8, pressure channels in the settlement: SA07 IV.J.2 requires 'meaningful participation' in the authority funding applications, and advocates support requests to the Mayor and Board. 01 section 2.8 also records ~39 board public comments with 0 on APS, so the funder route is unused today; no document shows it being used after a deflection. Treat the re-aim as 'no document support' for behaviour, only for the channel.
proposals.parameter: f_redirect: share of a deflected pressure event converted to funder-side pressure
proposals.range: U(0, 0.8); baseline 0 reproduces the current rule; test 0 vs 0.4 vs 0.8
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch; adds a second pressure stock pressure_funder(t) that enters p_start of the local-fund windows and reduces q_veto in F-j (decay k shared).

proposals.behaviour: Window-aligned pressure. Advocates concentrate their asks in the weeks before a decision deadline (HSIP application window, biennial city budget submission, 5-year plan revision) instead of at a constant rate, because a complaint outside a window decays before anyone can act on it.
proposals.trigger: A known external deadline within w months, or the advocates learning that an agency decision window is about to open or close.
proposals.effect_in_model: The Poisson timing of pressure events in the model is shifted toward the n months before each field window. With decay k only 1-12 months, a window-aligned event is still alive at the moment p_start is evaluated, while an unaligned event is mostly gone. The average rate lambda_press stays the same, so only timing changes.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D10 lines 340-341 give a homogeneous rate lambda_press and decay k; D3.6 pathways treat windows as exogenous to SFMTA only. F-m interrupts the rate but does not time it.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 3.1 gives the windows: HSIP C13 deadline 2026-11-02, budget deadline 5-01 in even years, 5-year plan revision autumn 2027 to 2028. 01 section 2.7.1 notes the staff promise to come back in 2026-07, with no follow-up in the 2026-09 agenda. No document shows advocates timing their asks, so behaviour is 'no document support'.
proposals.parameter: win_align: probability that a pressure event is drawn inside the w months before the next window instead of uniformly
proposals.range: U(0, 1); w = 3 months; baseline 0 = current uniform rule
proposals.rule_modified: O3 event generation for pressure events (inter-arrival timing), with lambda_press total held fixed.

proposals.behaviour: Cost rebuttal. Advocates answer 'costly' with unit-cost and carrier numbers (a cheap hardware swap on the signal head versus a full pole replacement) and the 90-day reply and 3-year likelihood rights in the request policy. This takes away the cost reply as an easy way out for the next meeting.
proposals.trigger: A deflection that cites cost, and the advocates having the cost and carrier figures (from the semiannual status report or their own public-records request).
proposals.effect_in_model: After a rebuttal event, the cost branch of p_deflect falls for a period, so more pressure stays in pressure(t) rather than being discarded. It does not change the true cost; it changes how often cost is accepted as a reason to stop.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 holds p_deflect fixed; costpress(t) (M-C) is a physical or budget effect on SFMTA, not a persuasion effect. The semiannual report is only the oversight state variable.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.8: SA07 IV.J.1 semiannual meetings with reports on 'applied funds and status' and efforts to Caltrans; LightHouse restored the report in 2022-07. 01 section 2.9 and 3.1: the 90-day reply and 3-year-possible duty; 01 section 3.1 mentions the SG015 FY24 unit cost around $14k per head. No document shows advocates actually running a cost rebuttal.
proposals.parameter: rho_rebut: relative reduction of p_deflect after an informed pressure event, lasting t_rebut months
proposals.range: rho_rebut U(0, 0.6); t_rebut U(3, 18); active only when oversight >= weak
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1: p_deflect becomes p_deflect * (1 - rho_rebut * informed(t)), where informed(t) is set by an oversight-level event.

proposals.behaviour: Scope nomination. Instead of general pressure, advocates name specific requested intersections that sit on, or near, an already scheduled parent project (a repaving, ramp, or signal job) and ask that APS be put into that scope at design time.
proposals.trigger: A parent project of the 'merged' (Fs), corridor-candidate, or unidentified-parent class reaches its design stage while some of the ~76 are within its footprint.
proposals.effect_in_model: For the nominated intersection, the probability pi that it stays in the parent project scope rises, and the attached partner delay t_parent is the only cost. It converts general pressure into intersection-level assignment without creating a new application instance.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW4 (assign by intersection) already routes them, but only as a policy lever that SFMTA applies; the baseline has no advocate behaviour that pushes the in-scope probability. Keep as a narrow add: an advocate-side trigger on the existing pi.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 3.2 and D3.4 table (merged row, pi for 'more likely/unverified'); 01 section 2.7: MDC staff offered to follow up with the transport agency and Public Works on coordination, 'no follow-up observed'. No document shows advocates naming intersections for scope.
proposals.parameter: adv_nominate: per-year chance that advocates push a given pending intersection into a parent project, raising pi to pi + delta_pi
proposals.range: adv_nominate U(0, 0.3) per year; delta_pi U(0, 0.4), capped at 1; baseline 0
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 'merged into existing project' row (pi) and PW4; one extra event type in O3.

proposals.behaviour: Funder-side venue shopping: advocates stop pressing SFMTA (who can only answer 'cost / no money') and take the same ask to the holders of money or the gate: the county transportation authority board and its advisory committee, district supervisors (each has a discretionary neighbourhood-project allocation), and the Prop L amendment vote. They ask an elected office to sponsor a named APS site or put APS in a grant line.
proposals.trigger: A deflection at the disability council. More observed deflections raise the chance of redirecting. Needs an open route (an unspent supervisor allocation, or a pending amendment).
proposals.effect_in_model: Creates a second pressure channel that does not pass through A2's IDLE->DEFLECTED draw. It lowers F-j q_veto and shortens t_defer, and opens a small externally sponsored funding event (a few sites) that A2 only submits or delivers. Today all pressure enters p_start through pressure(t) at A2, and deflection discards it.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: PW2 and F-j exist but are A2-initiated; no advocate-initiated pressure on the authority board or supervisors. NTP (EP25) appears in 01 but there is no NTP rule in 02. Kept, with the amendment piece overlapping PW2.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: EP25 NTP $700k per district over FY24-28; a district supervisor used NTP $500k for two signals with APS through a 5YPP amendment in 3-4 months (01 s2.3, about line 177). 01 s2.1 line 130: SFMTA answers with cost and 'selected based on funding'. 01 s1.2 line 83: the no-money <-> no-application loop. No document shows APS advocates doing this.
proposals.parameter: p_venue_shift
proposals.range: 0 to 0.6 per deflection event; sponsor lag U(2,9) months; success q_sponsor U(0.1,0.5); n_sp U(1,5) C-type sites; q_veto multiplied by (1 - 0.5*p_venue_shift)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (adds an outflow); D3.5 F-j; new NTP field in O2

proposals.behaviour: Cost-claim audit and ask narrowing: advocates stop restating 'fund all ~76' and instead challenge the cost framing with SFMTA's own presented range ($40k min vs $1.5M max) and peer-city unit costs, then table a small named cheap list (existing-pole sites or one corridor) with a date. This removes generic 'costly' as an available deflection.
proposals.trigger: At least one prior cost deflection; staff time and the per-site cost-class list. Stronger after a second deflection.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers p_deflect for the next pressure event in proportion to ask specificity, and wears down repeated deflection. The model's 'specified' variable covers ownership, not the ask.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. p_deflect is a fixed parameter (D3.1) and pressure(t) is an undifferentiated count. PW3 sets specified=1 as a package imposed on SFMTA, not an advocate tactic.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 line 130: three slides on 'Technical Challenges & Cost', $40k to $1.5M, rest 'selected based on funding'. 01 s2.12: NYC about $52-65k per site, Seattle $500k/yr, Portland 11 community requests. No document support for advocates narrowing the ask; the cost spread is supported.
proposals.parameter: sigma_ask (with ask_mode in {generic, named_list})
proposals.range: sigma_ask 0 to 0.7: p_deflect_eff = p_deflect*(1 - sigma_ask*s_ask), s_ask=1 if named_list; plus audit_wear U(0.7,1.0) multiplier on p_deflect per repeated deflection in 12 months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_deflect branch; D10 p_deflect

proposals.behaviour: Attention substitution across disability priorities: the advocate has a fixed yearly budget of pressure and spends it where a win looks likely (curb ramps have a federal timetable and ring-fenced general fund money; APS has neither), so APS pressure drops while a rival fight is live or after repeated deflection.
proposals.trigger: A competing ADA item with a deadline or fresh money; repeated deflection making APS look unwinnable.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes lambda_press time-varying and negatively tied to a rival-issue calendar. Quiet spells become a choice that ends when a window or trigger appears, not random noise.
proposals.already_in_model: F-m (D3.5) generates quiet spells randomly (lambda_quiet, t_quiet) with no cause; the cause and the reallocation are not modelled. Kept as a refinement of F-m's mechanism.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: council letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 both went to curb ramps, none to APS; ramps have a federal timetable (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)), APS none. 01 s2.6 line 257: general fund ADA right-of-way $125M/10 years goes to ramps. 01 s2.8: no public APS statements 2024-26 from the advocacy groups; 0 of ~39 board comments on APS.
proposals.parameter: rho_sub
proposals.range: 0 to 1: lambda_press_eff(t) = lambda_press*(1 - rho_sub*rival(t)), rival(t) in {0,1} from an exogenous calendar with duty cycle U(0.2,0.6); rho_sub=0 reproduces the current model
proposals.rule_modified: D10 lambda_press; D3.5 F-m

proposals.behaviour: Window-timed pressure with data hand-off: advocates concentrate pressure just before a known decision window (grant deadline, 5-year plan update, budget hearing) and hand SFMTA a ready site list with crash data, shortening preparation, because pressure outside a window only decays.
proposals.trigger: Public calendar of windows; a prior missed window that advocates recognise as a lost cycle.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure arrives as a burst before a window instead of a Poisson stream, and D_prep shrinks, so an instance that would be MISSED can be SUBMITTED. Matters because IDLE->PREPARING starts only when a window is open and pressure decays within k months (as short as 1).
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured: lambda_press is Poisson (D10 line 340) with decay k (line 341) and no calendar link. PW3 only doubles lambda_press at start.
proposals.evidence: No document support for advocates timing pressure. Related: a supervisor-sponsored site went through a 5YPP amendment in 3-4 months (01 s2.3); window structure in 02 O2 line 64; 01 s2.8 line 332 says activation rate unknown, test 0 and non-zero.
proposals.parameter: sw_timed (0/1) with lead time w and prep saving delta_data
proposals.range: sw_timed in {0,1}; w U(1,4) months before the next window; delta_data U(0,2) months off D_prep for the first instance; at 0 current Poisson timing
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure(t) generation and D_prep; D10 lambda_press, k

proposals.behaviour: Venue shifting: after SFMTA staff answer 'costly, no money', advocates stop pressing the SFMTA delivery team and instead lobby the gatekeepers of the money: SFCTA board and CAC (Prop L amendment), the Mayor/Board of Supervisors budget process (general fund line), and they write support letters for SFMTA's own funding requests, as 2007 settlement §IV.J.2/§V already contemplates. Advocates become allies of SFMTA staff against the budget holders instead of opponents.
proposals.trigger: A DEFLECTED response (D3.1) that names SFCTA/budget/Caltrans as the place the money sits. Advocates take the deflection literally and follow it. Stronger when pressure at SFMTA has already been deflected once.
proposals.effect_in_model: Pressure stops being a single scalar acting only on A2's p_start. A share of pressure events instead lowers the failure probability of the funding gates: it reduces q_veto and t_defer (F-j Prop L amendment), raises the chance a general-fund request is listed (PW2 second step), and raises q_dir (F-k, chief's 10% / SG000 reserve use). Under M-A/M-D this is the only advocate action that can reach the cause of the deflection.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.1 sends pressure only into pressure(t) -> p_start; D10 has lambda_press, k, q_veto, q_dir as independent draws. No rule links advocate pressure to q_veto/q_dir/general-fund listing. PW3 raises owner/specified/oversight, not gatekeeper outcomes. Nothing in 02 D3.1-D3.6 routes pressure to SFCTA or the budget process, so not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8: 'agreement §IV.J.2: SFMTA must let plaintiffs participate meaningfully in its Prop K funding applications; plaintiffs support SFMTA requests to mayor and council' (SA07 §IV.J.2, §V). 01 §2.3 (D4 precedent: Prop L amendment took 3-4 months). 01 §2.8: 2024-26 no public statements by the advocacy groups on SF APS funding were found (activation rate unknown). Whether this actually changes veto odds: no document support.
proposals.parameter: w_gate (share of each pressure event routed to funding gatekeepers instead of A2)
proposals.range: 0 to 0.6 (0 = current model). When routed: q_veto multiplied by (1 - g1*w_gate), q_dir and P(general-fund line listed) raised by g2*w_gate, with g1, g2 in U(0, 0.5), unobserved.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure branch (1 - p_deflect), and F-j / F-k / PW2 gate probabilities in D3.5 and D10

proposals.behaviour: Cheap escalation below litigation: written administrative complaint or formal rights letter (ADA transition-plan / PROWAG compliance, DOJ or federal funding-condition complaint, or a formal demand letter) instead of waiting for structured negotiation or a lawsuit. It is a low-cost, reversible signal that lifts enforce(t) a little without moving D1 a whole tier.
proposals.trigger: Repeated deflection, or a quiet period (F-m) lasting beyond a threshold; also after a meeting where the only answer is 'no money'. Advocates keep the lawsuit as a reserve and send a complaint first.
proposals.effect_in_model: enforce(t) gets a temporary additive bump that decays, and p_deflect falls for a while because refusing a rights letter in writing is riskier than refusing verbally. D1 tier is unchanged unless the complaint is ignored.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D1 has tiers none / credibility unknown / structured negotiation / lawsuit / decree, and eps_enf is an annual rate of moving up a whole tier; PW3 jumps to negotiation then lawsuit. No sub-tier action with its own decay exists. Not dropped.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: the ADA transition plan for curb ramps carries a federal timetable duty (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)) while 'APS has no matching federal retrofit timetable' (MDC26 p.10), so a complaint hook is weaker for APS. 01 §2.10 on NYC/Chicago/DC suits. No document shows a SF advocate sending a complaint in 2024-26: no document support for the behaviour itself.
proposals.parameter: p_complaint (annual rate of a complaint-type event) with strength b_complaint
proposals.range: p_complaint U(0, 0.3) per year; b_complaint adds U(0, 0.5) of one tier-step to enforce(t), decaying with time constant k; p_deflect multiplied by (1 - U(0, 0.3)) for 12 months after it
proposals.rule_modified: D1 enforce(t) and p_start term beta_enf*enforce(t); D3.1 p_deflect

proposals.behaviour: Making deflection costly: advocates take the 'costly / no money' answer, put it on the record (minutes, a written follow-up, a request for the cost estimate and the funding source), and bring it back at the next meeting. A repeated, recorded deflection leaves a residual of pressure, and each additional deflection of the same request is less likely to be accepted without an explanation.
proposals.trigger: A DEFLECTED event at a public body that keeps minutes (disability council, board). The reply 'no money' is recorded, then cited next time.
proposals.effect_in_model: After DEFLECTED the pressure is currently erased. Instead a fraction rho_resid of that pressure stays in pressure(t), and p_deflect declines with the count of earlier deflections to the same pressure source (memory).
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 states that after DEFLECTED returns to IDLE 'this pressure leaves no effect', and D design concepts say 'learning is not modelled'. Reporting and oversight appear only as the oversight variable in PW3. Not dropped. (It adds a small piece of memory against the 'no learning' choice; flag this to the author.)
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8: LightHouse says it was the group that re-established the semi-annual report, restored 2022-07 (S/sfmta-aps/lighthouse-aps-are-they-working-43407.html); 01 §2.7: ODA staff proposed to 'follow up with MTA and DPW then bring recommendations' (MDC26t), no later trace found by 2026-09-18. Direct evidence that recorded deflections raise later cost for the agency: no document support.
proposals.parameter: rho_resid (residual pressure kept after a deflection) and d_memory (reduction in p_deflect per prior recorded deflection)
proposals.range: rho_resid U(0, 0.5), 0 = current model; d_memory U(0, 0.2) per prior deflection, floor at 0.3 of the base p_deflect
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (the line that discards pressure) and the p_deflect draw

proposals.behaviour: Coalition and reframing: advocates attach the APS request to the curb-ramp / ADA-transition effort, which has a legal timetable, a dedicated funding stream and a letter-writing habit, rather than pressing APS as a stand-alone cost item. Concretely they ask the cross-disability bodies to add APS language to the ramp letters or to the ramp programme's scope.
