proposals.trigger: Disability council in which another access item (curb ramps) already has money and a deadline, while APS has none; SFMTA's cost argument is easier to resist when APS is priced as a small add-on to a ramp job.
proposals.effect_in_model: A new route to money for the C-type pending intersections that have a ramp job scheduled: APS cost is carried as an add-on in the ramp programme's budget, outside HSIP BCR and outside the Signal Shop-only local line; it also raises owner/specified weight for ramp-linked intersections.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly, not fully. PW4 has 'merge into parent project' and PW5 has an annual hardware/button-replacement add-on with a fixed budget b_hw, but both are SFMTA-initiated. No rule for a DPW/ADA ramp programme that the advocates themselves persuade to carry APS. Weak overlap with PW4, so keep but mark as variant of PW4.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.7: MDC letters of 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 both concern curb ramps, none on APS (0 APS letters); MOD co-funds and ranks DPW ramps, which entered the 10-year capital plan (2008 transition plan p.3); ODA raised the point that 'ramp budget will rise a lot'. Whether APS can be funded through the ramp budget: no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_ramp_bundle (switch) with q_ramp_carry (probability a ramp job takes an APS add-on) and share of pending C intersections coinciding with a scheduled ramp job (f_ramp_overlap)
proposals.range: sw_ramp_bundle in {0,1}; q_ramp_carry U(0, 0.4); f_ramp_overlap U(0.05, 0.3), inferred and unverified
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW4 (new route alongside 'merge') and D3.4 delivery table (new row: ramp-programme add-on, cost not counted in BCR, delivered by Public Works schedule)

proposals.behaviour: Target the top-up decision, not the general agenda. When the overrun is announced, the advocacy policy lead uses the existing semi-annual report meetings and the settlement-style 'meaningful participation' channel to lobby the funding board and the budget office specifically for the supplemental appropriation (public comment, letters, calls to board members) and frames the top-up as a legal-exposure issue.
proposals.trigger: Design completion reveals a gap above contingency (F-f), and the advocacy group is informed (60-day notice norm, semi-annual report). Fires only at the moment a q_topup request is pending, so it is event-timed rather than a background Poisson process.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the approval probability of the top-up request (and of the one re-request after t_pause) for the affected batch. Without it, q_topup is a fixed draw independent of whether anyone outside the agency is watching; with it, an active, informed advocate shifts q_topup up and shortens t_pause, while a silent advocate (the 2024-26 observed state) leaves it unchanged.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-m/lambda_press cover generic, time-random pressure that feeds p_start via pressure(t), and PW3 escalates enforcement tiers. Neither conditions the top-up probability (F-f/F-e q_topup) on advocacy attention at the overrun moment. Not a duplicate: kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: SA07 IV.J.2 (agency must let plaintiffs participate in funding applications; plaintiffs support the agency's requests to the mayor and council); semi-annual reports must include funding applied for and status; LightHouse credited with restoring the report (counter-example of effective pressure). 01 s2.11 / F-f: precedent of a 13th St top-up of $2.7M. 2024-26: no public advocacy found, so the effect size is undocumented ('no document support' for magnitude).
proposals.parameter: adv_topup_lift (additive logit shift to q_topup when advocate_active AND an overrun event is open); optionally adv_notice_lag (months between overrun and advocate learning of it)
proposals.range: adv_topup_lift in {0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0} logit units; adv_notice_lag U(0, 6) months; gated by a Bernoulli advocate_active = (lambda_press > 0 and not in a F-m quiet spell)
proposals.rule_modified: F-f and F-e top-up step (q_topup); couples D3.5 to the advocacy state in F-m

proposals.behaviour: Cost-source reframing: argue that the new conduit and curb ramps are ADA right-of-way work and belong on the citywide ADA curb-ramp line rather than on the APS budget, so the APS-specific gap shrinks to hardware. The advocate demands the ramp and conduit share be split off and paid from the ADA public right-of-way general fund or the public works curb-ramp program.
proposals.trigger: Overrun is dominated by conduit and ramp items (the situation stated) and an ADA curb-ramp programme with a standing general-fund line exists. Advocate raises it at the budget and board stage before a TERMINATE decision.
proposals.effect_in_model: Moves part of the excess cost (the ramp/conduit portion) out of the APS gap to an external pot, reducing the amount that needs q_topup and lowering termination risk. Also changes who pays (cost_by_actor shifts from the transport agency to the public works / citywide ADA line), and may add a coordination delay.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-f funds gaps only by contingency then q_topup from SFMTA/SFCTA; PW4 allocates sources by intersection but lists only parent project, corridor and local/SI02. No path draws on the citywide ADA general-fund ramp line. HSIP treats ramps as eligible cost but that is a different rule (D3.3 table). Kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.11 (line ~257): general fund ADA public right-of-way $55M FY26-30 and $71M FY31-35, flowing to curb ramps; mayor's budget lists priority curb ramps and barrier removal (line ~258); 01 s2.10: 2008 transition plan co-funds and ranks DPW curb ramps with a 10-year capital plan; 01 line 284: curb ramps carry a federal transition-plan timetable obligation but APS does not. Whether the ramp line can be applied to ramps at APS sites is not documented.
proposals.parameter: sw_ramp_offload (switch) with share f_ramp_offload of the ramp/conduit part of the overrun that is diverted, and delay t_offload
proposals.range: sw in {0,1}; f_ramp_offload U(0, 0.8) of the known ramp component (about $200k per site per 01 s2.1 MDC26 p.4-6); t_offload U(2, 12) months added to the design-complete to construction path; success Bernoulli q_offload U(0, 0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: F-f (funding source for the gap before q_topup) and PW4 (add a fourth route 'ramp line'); cost_by_actor output

proposals.behaviour: Triage-and-sequence instead of all-or-nothing: the advocate accepts deferring the highest-cost sites and presses the agency to keep the cheap sites moving (and to lock APS hardware into the batch) so overrun does not stall the whole batch. Possibly paired with accepting a smaller APS-only scope (no new ramp) at sites where the existing curb ramp is already compliant.
proposals.trigger: Batch-level shortfall after contingency is exhausted, with sites ranked by realised cost; the advocate would rather get most sites than hold out for all.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes which intersections are TERMINATED: instead of a random per-site termination when a gap is unfunded, the agency drops the costliest sites first and releases funds to the rest, producing more installs earlier and a longer tail of never-served expensive sites. Also lowers the pressure on the funding board because the ask shrinks.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-f terminates 'the project / the intersection' and D3.4 says a TERMINATED project returns intersections to the pool; D3.3 packing drops low-BCR sites for HSIP only. The model does not state a rule for ordering which sites are dropped inside a locally funded batch or for descoping a site's ramp component. Kept as a clarification switch.
proposals.evidence: No document support for the advocate acting this way. Indirect: 01 s2.8 NFB now supports installation in consultation with the blind community while ACB supports installing at every signalised crossing (PROWAG fn), so organisations differ on how much to concede; 01 s2.1 MDC26 p.4-6 gives the per-site cost range $40k to $1.5M, so cost ranking is feasible.
proposals.parameter: triage_rule (categorical: 0 = random site terminated, 1 = costliest first, 2 = costliest deferred to next window) and scope_cut_share
proposals.range: triage_rule in {0,1,2}; scope_cut_share U(0, 0.5) of a site's ramp cost removed where an existing ramp is compliant
proposals.rule_modified: F-f termination step (which sites are dropped) and the local batch sizing under costpress(t) in D3.2

proposals.behaviour: Escalate to a visible, dated demand with a litigation-readiness signal when the agency's response is a cost-based deflection. The policy lead stops using private channels and issues a public letter with a deadline, citing peer-city court orders, converting a one-off 'we have no money' reply into an enforcement-tier jump sooner than the background rate.
proposals.trigger: A top-up refusal or a public statement that sites are 'selected based on funding' (the deflection reply) landing on a batch that was already funded; or a second deflection within t months.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the external-enforcement tier (D1) conditionally on a deflection event rather than only at the exogenous epsilon_enf rate or after the PW3 idle threshold, and increases pressure(t) for k months. Creates a trigger-driven escalation ladder from deflection to demand to formal negotiation.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW3 escalates after theta_idle with no applications, and epsilon_enf is an exogenous annual rate; p_deflect only records the deflection and leaves 'no lasting effect'. There is no coupling from a deflection event, or from a refused top-up, to the advocate's escalation. Kept, but it overlaps PW3 so it should be a single switch.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 line 130: agency answers advocacy with cost and 'no funds' (MDC26 p.4-6, p.8); 01 s2.10: NYC order 281 added 'full effort to secure enough funding' and Chicago order named responsible persons; 01 s2.8: the 2007 structured negotiation was reached without suing; 01 line 367 and open item 5 admit the litigation rate is pure inference. 2024-26: no public advocacy recorded, so willingness to escalate is unobserved.
proposals.parameter: esc_on_deflect (probability that a deflection or top-up refusal moves the enforcement tier up one step) and esc_lag
proposals.range: esc_on_deflect U(0, 0.3) per event; esc_lag U(3, 12) months; 0 reproduces the current model
proposals.rule_modified: D1 enforcement tier transition and F-m / p_deflect branch in D3.1 (the deflected pressure no longer 'leaves no effect')

proposals.behaviour: Event-targeted top-up lobbying. When a locally funded batch is flagged as over contingency, the advocacy policy lead mobilises specifically for the supplemental appropriation: board testimony, support letters, calls to the board member of the affected district, and a reminder of the 2007 agreement duty to seek added funds. The model has advocacy pressure only as a background Poisson stream aimed at A2 starting tasks, never as a response to a named overrun.
proposals.trigger: Overrun discovered at design-complete node (F-f) with the gap exceeding κ_cont, so a top-up request (q_topup) is pending and a decision date is visible, for example a board calendar item.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the approval odds of the pending top-up request and shortens the pause before re-request, which lowers the chance of TERMINATED. Effect is conditional on advocate state being active (not in F-m quiet) and decays if the request is repeated.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. q_topup is a flat U(0,0.7) constant (02 D10, F-f, F-e) and does not depend on pressure(t) or advocate state. pressure(t) enters only p_start (D3.1). F-m switches advocacy off at random but never ties it to an overrun event. Not captured, so kept.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: SA07 IV.J.2 'plaintiffs support SFMTA requests to mayor and council' and IV.A.1 duty to seek added funds; 01 s2.8 reactivation example: LightHouse pushed the semi-annual report back in 2022-07 (advocate-claimed). 01 s2.11: SFCTA precedent of a $2.7M top-up on 13th St. No document support that advocates have testified on an APS top-up since 2024 (01 s2.8: 0 of ~39 public comments, 0 found statements).
proposals.parameter: beta_topup_adv (logit shift on q_topup when advocate_active and request pending)
proposals.range: 0 to 1.5 logit units; 0 = current model; also scan adv_active_prob at overrun 0.1 to 0.6 because activation rule is unknown
proposals.rule_modified: F-f and F-e top-up draw: q_topup_eff = logistic(logit(q_topup) + beta_topup_adv * advocate_active); advocate_active drawn from lambda_press state and F-m

proposals.behaviour: Accepting or resisting phased descoping. Faced with a cost jump, the agency can keep APS and push conduit or curb-ramp work to a later phase or other program. The policy lead decides whether to accept APS-only minimal scope at sites where existing poles and conduit are usable, or to resist because it fixes the unfinished sites in place. Their stance changes whether the agency goes for partial delivery or stalls the whole batch.
proposals.trigger: Shortfall beyond contingency and q_topup refused or uncertain, with the agency's notice to the advocate group (semi-annual report or ad hoc meeting).
proposals.effect_in_model: Instead of all-or-nothing TERMINATED per intersection, a share of over-budget sites is kept at a cheaper APS-only scope (cost drops by the pipe and ramp add-ons), the rest go back to the pool. If the advocate resists, the agency's deflection probability and delay rise while pressure rises.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. F-f says the gap is closed by contingency or top-up or TERMINATED. Pipe and ramp add-ons (q_pipe, q_ramp, $200k each) are drawn once at list entry and always charged. PW6 only chooses sites with usable existing poles at entry; it does not downscope a site after overrun. PW1/PW4 reassign funding source, not scope.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.1 (MDC26 p.4-6): cost from $40k minimum to $1.5M upper bound, pipe and ramp roughly $200k each, so minimal-scope APS exists. 01 s2.8: advocate groups differ historically (NFB 2001 against blanket APS, now supports consultation; ACB strongly supports everywhere). No document support for phased descoping in SF.
proposals.parameter: p_descope_keep (share of overrun sites retained at APS-only scope) and adv_descope_stance in {accept, resist}
proposals.range: p_descope_keep 0 to 0.6 when accept; resist sets it to 0 and adds +delta_pressure
proposals.rule_modified: F-f gap closure branch: add a third outcome between top-up and TERMINATED; recompute site cost = c_base only for kept sites

proposals.behaviour: Shifting the ramp component to the curb-ramp program through a coalition. The policy lead works with mobility-disability groups and the disability office so the new curb ramps are charged to the citywide curb-ramp funding stream, leaving only the APS and conduit to the APS budget.
proposals.trigger: Overrun is attributed mainly to curb ramps (q_ramp true on the site), and a curb-ramp funding stream and advisory-body channel exist.
proposals.effect_in_model: Removes some or all of the $200k ramp cost from the gap of those sites; the remaining gap goes through top-up or termination. Costs time (coordination lag) and may be refused, in which case the ramp competes with ramp-only projects for the same money.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. Costs are single-pool; there is no cross-charge to a ramp program. Funding fields are HSIP, Prop L, General Fund/CIP, SS4A, signal projects (02 O2); no ramp-fund node.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.x mayor/general fund row (line 72): General Fund ADA right-of-way earmark $125M/10 years flows to curb ramps; line 265: capital plan says accessibility capital is often in other departments' budgets; line 282: ODA deputy said ramp budget will rise sharply; line 279: advisory-body letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 were curb-ramp only, none for APS. Whether ramp money can be cost-shared into an APS project is not documented.
proposals.parameter: s_ramp_shift (probability that ramp cost is moved to the ramp program) with t_coord lag
proposals.range: s_ramp_shift 0 to 0.5; t_coord U(2,9) months; amount shifted 0 to 100% of the $200k ramp add-on
proposals.rule_modified: F-f gap computation and D3.4 cost bookkeeping: gap = max(0, actual - plan*(1+kappa_cont) - ramp_shifted)

proposals.behaviour: Termination-triggered escalation. If an overrun leads to TERMINATED sites that were already funded and designed, the advocate group treats it as broken delivery and escalates (public letter, press, formal demand citing the 2007 agreement and out-of-state court orders) without waiting for an idle period.
proposals.trigger: Count of TERMINATED funded sites in the last 12 months at or above theta_term, or a visibly cancelled batch.
proposals.effect_in_model: Immediate jump in enforce(t) and a one-off pressure pulse, which raises p_start, owner and q_topup next cycle and lifts litigation hazard. Also lets a high-profile failure end the quiet state (F-m).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW3 escalates to negotiation and then suit only after theta_idle months with no application; the annual suit rate is a flat 0 to 0.1 scenario value; F-m gives random quiet. None is triggered by a termination event. Kept as a trigger-based escalation.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.10: NYC and Chicago orders require 'all efforts to obtain funding'; DC complaint targets balancing against other priorities; line 367 annual suit rate is purely inferred. 01 s2.8: 2010-onward, plaintiffs are only consulted and cannot set deadlines, and no SF enforcement since 2010. No document support for a termination-triggered escalation in SF.
proposals.parameter: theta_term and p_escalate_on_term
proposals.range: theta_term 1 to 4 sites; p_escalate_on_term 0 to 0.3 per qualifying event; pressure pulse size 0 to 2 units of pressure(t)
proposals.rule_modified: Event rule on TERMINATED; sets enforce(t) and pressure(t) step and resets lambda_quiet timer (F-m)

proposals.behaviour: Ramp-cost shifting (reframing the overrun as an ADA curb-ramp problem). The advocacy lead argues that the new-ramp part of the overrun belongs to the citywide curb-ramp programme, and asks the curb-ramp funder or its disability committee to carry it, so the APS batch keeps only the signal and conduit share.
proposals.trigger: Overrun is discovered at design completion (F-f) and the new-ramp add-on (q_ramp, about $200k per site) is a large part of the gap. Advocates already have a working channel, and a funded ADA ramp line, to point at.
proposals.effect_in_model: Part of the funding gap in F-f is paid by a source outside the APS budget before q_topup is drawn. This reduces the gap that goes to top-up, lowers the TERMINATED rate, and shifts cost_by_actor toward the ramp programme. Ramp work then also becomes a gating dependency, because ramp delivery is slow (about 6-9.5 years for the large ramp contracts).
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.5 F-f says the cost is counted once and any gap needs a top-up (q_topup) or the site is TERMINATED. 02 D3.4 has no cross-programme cost transfer for ramps. 02 D3.6 PW4 assigns funding sources by site, but only among incorporated, corridor and local routes, not a ramp programme.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.6 line 72: general fund ADA right-of-way earmark of $125M over 10 years goes to curb ramps, and APS has no matching earmark (inferred). 01 s2.11 line 373: curb-ramp budget $4.0M in FY26, requests of $8.1M and $12.2M. 01 s2.7 lines 279 and 305: the disability committee tracks curb-ramp dollars, but there is no APS letter. 01 s2.11 line 376: public works treats APS as the transit agency's job and ramp work does not trigger APS. These show the channel and money exist; no document shows ramp cost actually being moved.
proposals.parameter: f_ramp_shift (with delay_ramp)
proposals.range: f_ramp_shift U(0, 0.8): share of the q_ramp add-on carried by the curb-ramp programme. delay_ramp U(0, 36) months added to the site's CON date when the shift is used.
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f: apply the shift to the gap before the contingency (kappa_cont) and q_topup test. Add delay_ramp to the D3.4 delivery chain.

proposals.behaviour: Targeted escalation of a cost overrun (venue shopping and a sunk-design argument). Once the overrun is known, advocacy turns from a generic push on the agency to a specific request to the funding bodies that decide the top-up: 'design is done, cancelling wastes it, and the 2007 duty to seek more funds still applies'. The lead also offers written support for the agency's own top-up request.
proposals.trigger: Overrun beyond contingency becomes known to advocates (see proposal 3 for how). The top-up decision is open and the site would otherwise be TERMINATED.
proposals.effect_in_model: q_topup rises for the affected batch for a limited window. The effect is on the funding decision, not on the agency's start probability, so it can change which sites get finished even when the general pressure rate is zero.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 D3.1 pressure(t) enters only p_start and is generic. 02 D3.5 F-f and F-e treat q_topup as a fixed draw U(0, 0.7) with no link to advocacy. F-m only switches general pressure off. PW3 escalates D1 tiers only on an idle trigger.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8 line 319: settlement s IV.J.2 requires the agency to let plaintiffs take part in its Prop K applications, and plaintiffs support the agency's requests to the mayor and council. Line 318: s IV.A.1 duty to seek extra funds. 01 s2.11: 13th St top-up of $2.7M shows top-ups are decided by funding bodies. No document shows advocates acting at a top-up decision, so the link itself is a hypothesis.
proposals.parameter: adv_topup_boost (with t_boost)
proposals.range: adv_topup_boost U(0, 1.5) added to logit(q_topup), applied only if advocacy is active (not in an F-m quiet spell) and the D1 tier is at least 'credibility unknown'. t_boost U(3, 12) months.
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-e and F-f: q_topup' = logistic(logit(q_topup) + adv_topup_boost * active(t)).

proposals.behaviour: Event-triggered, delayed advocacy response, including a choice to stay quiet. Advocacy rate is not a constant background rate. It reacts to a visible bad event (a site pulled, a batch stalled) after a lag set by what advocates can see, and the lead may deliberately hold back to protect the working relationship while a top-up is being negotiated.
proposals.trigger: A TERMINATED event, a paused project (t_pause), or an overrun report reaches the advocates. The only regular channel is the semiannual APS report, so detection lags by up to six months. The opposite case: a negotiation is under way and the lead judges that public pressure would hurt it.
proposals.effect_in_model: lambda_press becomes a function of observed bad events (a spike after a lag) rather than an exogenous draw, with a suppression option during open negotiations. This changes when pressure arrives relative to the overrun decision, which matters for proposal 2 (pressure after the top-up window closes has no effect).
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D10 line 340 has lambda_press as exogenous U(0, 0.5), doubled at PW3 start. F-m has random quiet spells. Neither reacts to project events or has a detection lag. So the reactive and the strategic-silence parts are not captured.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8 lines 321 and 323: advocates get a semiannual status report, and the advocates' own account is that the report was only re-established in 2022-07 after pushing. 01 s2.8 line 331 and line 624: no public statements 2024-26, while private channels are not recorded, consistent with either silence or off-record work. No direct document for strategic silence: no document support for that part.
proposals.parameter: press_react, t_detect, t_react, quiet_negotiate
proposals.range: press_react U(1, 5) spike multiplier on lambda_press; t_detect U(0, 6) months; t_react U(3, 12) months; quiet_negotiate 0/1 sets lambda_press to 0 while a top-up request is open.
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 pressure(t) generation, F-m, and the D10 row for lambda_press.

proposals.behaviour: Cost-phasing request: accept a smaller, ordered first tranche. When the batch is over budget, the lead pushes for a staged order that completes the cheaper sites (no new conduit or ramp) now and leaves the expensive ones for a later round, rather than fighting for all sites at once. The lead may also put forward its own site priority list for the order.
proposals.trigger: The gap exceeds contingency and advocates expect full top-up will not come soon. The alternative is losing the whole batch or having it silently shrink.
proposals.effect_in_model: Sites inside the batch are ordered by a priority rule instead of by the agency's order. Cheap sites are installed earlier, expensive sites join the leftover pool with a later date. Raises early installs and lowers batch-level termination, but may reduce long-run coverage of hard sites.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.5 F-f drops a site to TERMINATED when the gap is unfunded, and local batch size follows the budget. D3.3 packs HSIP bids by BCR rank. Nothing models advocate-driven ordering inside a local batch or a deliberate staged tranche.
proposals.evidence: No document support for advocates proposing phasing. Related facts only: 01 s2.1 line 130 (remaining sites 'selected based on funding'); 01 line 119 (unit costs $40k to $1.5M, conduit and ramp add-ons about $200k each, so sites differ a lot in cost).
proposals.parameter: sw_phase (with phase_share)
proposals.range: sw_phase 0/1; phase_share U(0.3, 0.8) = share of over-budget sites deferred instead of terminated, ordered cheapest first.
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f (what happens to the unfunded part) and local-batch ordering in D3.3/D3.4; deferred sites go to the pool and re-enter at the next local funding window.

proposals.behaviour: Outage-salience reframing plus APS-ready controller rider. The advocacy lead stops asking for a stand-alone 'APS line' and presents APS as part of the visible-failure category that wins money. Pitch: silent or dead signals during outages strand blind pedestrians; any controller replacement funded from EP17 must be APS-capable or APS-ready (a condition on the allocation, not a new line). This moves APS from competing with controller replacement to riding on it.
proposals.trigger: The amendment appears on the SFCTA board agenda while EP17 is over-programmed and controller replacements after an outage are the visibly prioritised item. The advocate expects a 'no room' answer and re-labels the ask.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers q_veto and q_sg017_block for the amendment/allocation, because the request no longer competes with the controller line. Adds a share of controller-replacement dollars that can carry APS hardware at the C-type intersections. The trade-off is that the amendment's coverage shrinks to intersections where controllers are replaced.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 (02 D3.6) uses the existing SG017 line and models only the blocking by outage-priority projects (q_sg017_block). PW5 covers an APS add-on at button or hardware replacement, but as a design standard, not as an allocation condition set by an advocate at the board. The outage-framing lever on q_veto and q_sg017_block is not in the model. Retained, scoped to the reframing lever and rider only.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1: 'EP17 hardware replacement $1M (FY25+FY26) went to about 98 controllers with firewall defects, and the 2023 PIF had listed APS replacement as an eligible use' (OCT25 p.7; EP17-5YPP p.70). 01 §2.3: 'outcomes are driven by visible failures; controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages'. 01 §2.6 line 353 notes Access Board deleted the controller/software-replacement APS trigger, so only a local rider could create it. No document shows an advocate making this framing; that part is no document support.
proposals.parameter: sw_frame_outage (0/1) with effect size d_frame in U(0, 0.5), a relative cut in q_veto and q_sg017_block when on. Optional second parameter f_ctrl_aps in U(0, 0.5), the share of controller replacements that carry APS-ready hardware.
proposals.range: sw_frame_outage in {0,1}; d_frame U(0,0.5); f_ctrl_aps U(0,0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (q_veto), PW6 trigger (q_sg017_block, a_sg017), and the PW2 entry condition

proposals.behaviour: Ask-shrinking and sunset: the advocate pre-negotiates a smaller or time-limited amendment (for example one fiscal year, or a non-dedicated 'eligible use' line with a cap) because a full dedicated line will be refused in an over-programmed EP17. The lever is the size and durability of the ask, chosen against its chance of passing.
proposals.trigger: Staff signal that the full-size ask will be deferred or voted down because of over-programming. Triggers when estimated pass probability for the full ask falls below a threshold.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes q_veto a decreasing function of ask size. Dollars flowing to APS equal ask size times pass probability, so a smaller ask can yield more expected money than a full ask. The line can lapse at sunset, which is a new termination condition for the local dedicated line. The amendment may also get an earlier slot, which shortens t_defer.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-j treats the amendment as a single binary event with fixed q_veto and no ask-size variable. The model's note on the SF SFCTA 3-4 month Lincoln Way precedent (01 §2.3) concerns speed, not size.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: Lincoln Way NTP of $500k led to a 5YPP revision in 3-4 months (LW p.15-18), and EP33 funded a one-off '19th Avenue APS' project of about $249k in FY2011/12 (AW 2019 5YPP p.7, p.37). Both show small, specific allocations passing. No document supports an advocate choosing the ask size; that part is no document support.
proposals.parameter: ask_scale in U(0.2, 1.0) as a fraction of the full dedicated line; q_veto = q_veto0 * ask_scale^gamma with gamma U(0.5, 2); line sunset length t_sunset in {12, 24, 60} months.
proposals.range: ask_scale U(0.2,1); gamma U(0.5,2); t_sunset {12,24,60}
proposals.rule_modified: F-j and PW2 (local-first), plus the D10 q_veto row

proposals.behaviour: Strategic withdrawal and re-timing: the advocate pulls or defers the amendment before the vote to avoid a recorded 'no', and repositions the same request into the 2027-autumn to 2028 5YPP development cycle, which is the window in which a line can be created without displacing an existing programmed project. During the wait the advocate builds board support and CAC familiarity.
proposals.trigger: A pre-vote count or staff briefing gives estimated pass probability below a threshold (theta_vote) and the next 5YPP window is near enough that waiting costs less than a failed vote.
proposals.effect_in_model: The local line opens later (at the start of the next 5YPP window) but with a higher pass probability, and the failure counter in F-j and the PW2 hand-off (to general fund) is not triggered. Interaction with pressure(t): the advocate may raise lambda_press while waiting.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j lists 'wait for the next 5YPP' as a recovery path after a veto or deferral by the board. The model does not have the advocate choosing to withdraw before the vote or choosing the timing. Retained, scoped to advocate-chosen withdrawal.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: next 5YPP window is 2027 autumn, adopted 2028, covering FY28/29-32/33 (SP p.8, p.10, p.46). 01 §2.3 also says allocations follow 'applications prepared and submitted by eligible applicants' (SP p.22), so a withdrawal costs little. No document shows advocate withdrawal; that part is no document support.
proposals.parameter: theta_vote in U(0.2, 0.6) (withdraw if estimated pass probability is below it) and q_pass_wait in U(0.4, 0.9) (pass probability in the next 5YPP window); sw_withdraw in {0,1}.
proposals.range: theta_vote U(0.2,0.6); q_pass_wait U(0.4,0.9); sw_withdraw {0,1}
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (veto/deferral branch) and PW2 entry and fallback

proposals.behaviour: Sponsor and coalition route: the advocate recruits a district supervisor who sits on the SFCTA board to carry an NTP (Neighborhood Transportation Program) or similar discretionary allocation for APS at named intersections, and allies with general pedestrian-safety and senior or disability groups so the ask is not seen as a single-constituency request competing with controllers.
proposals.trigger: The line amendment is stalled by over-programming, or a board member signals willingness to use discretionary money after a local incident or news event.
proposals.effect_in_model: Opens an extra funding source (a discretionary allocation per board district, small and fast) that bypasses the EP17 amendment, and adds a coalition effect on pressure(t): a larger multiplier on lambda_press and reduced chance that pressure is deflected (p_deflect falls).
proposals.already_in_model: No for the sponsor route: 02 has no NTP or district-sponsor path (grep of 02 finds no NTP). pressure(t) and lambda_press exist (D3.1, D10) but are exogenous and carry no coalition size.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: 'D4 supervisor in 2024-11 used NTP $500k to design two new signals with APS at Lincoln Way, 3-4 months through the 5YPP revision' (LW p.15-18). 01 §2.6: 'mayor and council can move money indirectly through supervisors who sit as SFCTA directors and NTP recommendations' (NTP5 p.7-8). Coalition size has no document support; 01 §2.8 notes no public statements by the advocacy groups in 2024-26 were found.
proposals.parameter: sw_ntp_route in {0,1}; a_ntp in U($0, $500k) per board district per cycle; p_sponsor in U(0, 0.3) per year; coalition multiplier m_coal in U(1, 2.5) on lambda_press with p_deflect scaled by 1/m_coal.
proposals.range: a_ntp U($0,500k); p_sponsor U(0,0.3)/yr; m_coal U(1,2.5)
proposals.rule_modified: New funding branch beside F-j/PW2 (the local-first path), and the pressure(t) inputs lambda_press and p_deflect in D3.1

proposals.behaviour: Cost-line unbundling: the advocacy policy lead argues that the curb-ramp and trench share of an over-budget site is an ADA curb-ramp obligation and should be paid from the Public Works / citywide ramp line (or the ADA right-of-way general-fund earmark), so only the APS hardware plus conduit stays on the APS batch. The overrun gap is partly moved to another budget instead of being met by a top-up or by termination.
proposals.trigger: Design completes and the cost discovery (F-f) shows an overrun beyond contingency, with the ramp or pipe add-on (q_ramp, q_pipe) being the driver; works best while the ramp line is growing (FY26 $4.0M to FY27 $8.1M).
proposals.effect_in_model: In F-f, before the top-up request (q_topup), a fraction of the gap attributed to the ramp add-on (about $200k per site) is removed from the APS gap and charged to the ramp program with probability q_ramp_shift. If it succeeds, the site waits t_ramp_wait months for the ramp contract (ramp designers are short) before APS install. If it fails, the old path (top-up, then TERMINATED) applies. This lowers the termination rate but raises delay.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. 02 D3.5 F-f says c_full and the pipe/ramp add-ons are 'already counted once' and any gap beyond contingency goes only to q_topup or TERMINATED. 02 O2 line 51 and D10 line 357 treat ramp cost as an APS cost with no other payer. Ramp program funding appears only as background (01 2.11), not as a payer for the overrun.
proposals.evidence: 01 2.6 line 72: general-fund ADA right-of-way earmark $125M/10 years 'flows to curb ramps'; 01 2.11 lines 373-376: ramp FY26 $4.0M, FY27/28 requests $8.1M/$12.2M, and 'DPW designs ramps with future APS in mind, but ramp work does not trigger APS, APS is an MTA matter'; 01 2.7 line 282: the disability office asked the two departments to coordinate strategy; 01 2.7 line 284: ramps have a federal transition-plan duty that APS lacks. No document shows this being done for an overrun, so support for the behaviour itself is weak.
proposals.parameter: q_ramp_shift (probability the ramp share is accepted by the ramp program); t_ramp_wait (months of added wait, e.g. U(6, 36), inferred from the Contract 35 delay of about 8 years)
proposals.range: q_ramp_shift U(0, 0.5), with 0 as the control; share moved = the ramp add-on only (0 or $200k per site); t_ramp_wait U(6, 36) months
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f funding-gap source order (insert a ramp-line step between contingency and q_topup); 02 D3.4 internal-delivery queue entry time

proposals.behaviour: Pressure aimed at the top-up decision. Instead of generic pressure, advocates (testimony, letters, meeting requests) concentrate on the specific allocation or top-up request that decides whether the overrun is funded. The effect is to raise the approval odds of that one request, not to start new applications.
proposals.trigger: An overrun top-up request is filed (F-f / F-e) and an allocation or board date is visible. The advocate is not in a quiet spell (F-m) and the group has a standing channel (the 2007 agreement's consultation clause, the twice-yearly status report).
proposals.effect_in_model: q_topup (and the second-attempt probability after t_pause) rises with the stock pressure(t) at the date of the request: q_topup_eff = logistic(logit(q_topup) + β_topup·pressure(t)). If the advocate is in a quiet spell the boost is 0. This couples the top-up outcome to advocacy activity, which today only affects p_start.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. 02 D3.1 puts pressure(t) only inside p_start (and p_deflect); 02 D3.5 F-f and D10 line 379 make q_topup a fixed prior U(0, 0.7) independent of pressure. F-m only gates whether pressure exists at all.
proposals.evidence: 01 2.8 lines (resources): 2007 agreement §IV.J.2 requires SFMTA to let the plaintiffs 'participate meaningfully' in its funding applications, and the plaintiffs back SFMTA's requests to the mayor and council; 01 2.3 line on D4: a supervisor got a 5YPP amendment through in 3-4 months once a visible failure occurred; 01 2.3: CAC gives support consistently to EP17/EP18. Counter-evidence in 01 2.8: no public advocate comments on SF APS funding found for 2024-26, so the baseline activation is near zero.
proposals.parameter: β_topup (coefficient of pressure(t) on the logit of q_topup)
proposals.range: U(0, 1.5); 0 = off (control)
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f and F-e top-up approval probability q_topup (and the retry after t_pause)

proposals.behaviour: Window-timed pressure: the advocacy group holds its effort until a budget window that can fund the shortfall (the next strategic plan / 5YPP cycle starting autumn 2027, the annual general-fund request, an allocation calendar slot) rather than applying it at a constant rate. The group reads an overrun as a reason to wait for the next plan and ask for a dedicated APS line then.
proposals.trigger: A funding shortfall exists and the next plan or budget window opens within a lead time L_sync; also triggered after a TERMINATED or pause event when the next window is known.
proposals.effect_in_model: The λ_press arrival process becomes non-homogeneous: pressure events bunch into the κ_win months before each external window (5YPP development 2027 autumn to 2028, annual budget cycle) and drop to a lower base rate otherwise. The mean number of events per year stays the same. A pressure event then lands in a window where the funder can act, so p_start and the PW2/PW6 routes see a higher effective boost; outside windows it is wasted or becomes p_deflect fodder.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. 02 D3.1 and D10 line 340 treat λ_press as a constant-rate event stream (U(0, 0.5)/yr, doubled only at PW3 start). The windows exist as an exogenous schedule (02 O3) but pressure is not aligned to them.
proposals.evidence: 01 2.3: next strategic plan plus 5YPP start autumn 2027, adopted 2028, covering FY28/29 to FY32/33 (SP p.8, p.10, p.46); 01 2.3: 5YPP score gives 'community support' 5 and 'disadvantaged' 5; 01 2.8: LightHouse revived the half-year report in 2022, showing the group acts on process hooks. No document shows timing pressure to a window, so mark as no document support for the timing itself.
proposals.parameter: κ_sync (share of annual pressure events placed in the κ_win months before an external window; 0 = uniform) and κ_win (months)
proposals.range: κ_sync U(0, 0.8) with 0 as control; κ_win U(3, 9) months
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 / D10 λ_press event-time generation (timing only, not total rate); interacts with 02 D3.6 PW2 and PW6 windows

proposals.behaviour: Site re-ranking inside a fixed batch: when the money cannot cover every site, advocates push to fund the cheap, conduit-ready sites now (and the sites with documented blind-user requests, near services or transit) and to hold the expensive new-conduit sites for a later source, instead of letting cost or order of design decide. They accept a phased batch rather than a stalled one.
proposals.trigger: The overrun means the batch is no longer fully fundable (gap beyond contingency) and the batch is still being ordered or allocated; the advocate has a seat in the consultation channel.
proposals.effect_in_model: The funding order within a local batch changes from the model's default order to a mix: with weight ω_adv sites are ranked by 'advocate priority' (request flag / community-support score) and with 1−ω_adv by lowest cost first. The result is more sites installed earlier in the high-ω case but the expensive sites move to the back of the pool (never_served risk), and TERMINATED events fall on expensive sites instead of random ones.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured in the written rules. 02 D3.2 only says the local batch is sized by planned cost x (1 + κ_cont) and F-f terminates the site that cannot be topped up; no ordering rule or advocate input to ordering is written down. HSIP ordering is by BCR (D3.3), which advocates cannot move.
proposals.evidence: 01 2.3: EP17 5YPP score weights (readiness 5, urgency 4, disadvantaged 5, community support 5, leverage 4, safety 4); 01 2.1 (cost rows, line 119/127): base $40k vs up to $1.5M per site, 'selected based on funding' for the rest of the request list (line 130); 01 2.9 (request list) shows requesters as an input. No document shows advocates reordering a funded batch, so mark partly as no document support.
proposals.parameter: ω_adv (weight of advocate priority in local-batch ordering, with cost-ascending ordering as the remainder)
proposals.range: U(0, 1); 0 = pure cost order (control), 1 = pure advocate priority order
proposals.rule_modified: 02 D3.2 / D3.4 local batch selection order and F-f choice of which site is TERMINATED when the gap is not covered

proposals.behaviour: Reframe the outage/controller problem as an accessibility failure and ask that APS be a rider on the controller line (APS-ready controller replacement), instead of competing against it. The advocate stops presenting APS as a rival to controller money and presents it as a safety-of-function issue: when a controller goes down after an outage, the APS goes silent and blind pedestrians lose the only non-visual crossing cue. This turns the visible-failure channel that currently favours controllers into one that also favours APS.
proposals.trigger: An outage or controller-failure event occurs (or is on the board's agenda) while the amendment is pending. EP17 is over-programmed, so the board already accepts failure-driven reprioritisation.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the chance that the existing SG017 line is absorbed entirely by controllers, and lowers q_veto for the amendment. It also lets a fraction of each controller replacement carry APS-ready wiring or hardware, which feeds the PW5 or PW6 install stream. The advocate's pressure is converted from a generic scalar into a targeted claim on the contested pool.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 and q_sg017_block (02 D3.6, D10) cover APS written into SG017 and the money being used up by controllers. PW5 covers APS attached to hardware replacement. Neither has an actor who changes q_sg017_block or q_veto by reframing; both are exogenous draws. Only that conditional, advocate-driven shift is new.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'visible-failure-driven: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages'. 01 section 2.1: the 2023 PIF had listed APS replacement as an eligible use of the $1M that went to about 98 controllers. No document support for advocates actually making this framing; it is an inference from those two lines.
proposals.parameter: r_frame in U(0, 0.6): the share by which q_sg017_block and q_veto are reduced when a failure event occurs inside the amendment window. A second switch, sw_aps_rider in {0, 1}, sets whether a fraction f_rider U(0, 0.3) of controller replacements carry APS-ready wiring.
proposals.range: r_frame U(0, 0.6); sw_aps_rider in {0, 1}; f_rider U(0, 0.3)
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (q_veto), D10 q_sg017_block, and the PW5/PW6 generation rule (adds a conditional reduction tied to failure events).

proposals.behaviour: Offer a scaled-down or conditional ask to make approval easier in an over-programmed plan. Examples: a smaller dedicated line, a sunset-dated line that falls away after 2 to 3 years, or an amendment funded by an explicit offset from a named lower-scoring line. The advocate trades ask size for approval probability and supplies the funding source that an over-programmed plan lacks.
proposals.trigger: A staff or board signal that EP17 has no headroom (FY26 to FY28 uncommitted balance is about $0 to $0.5M per year) and that some members are reluctant to take money from controllers.
proposals.effect_in_model: Replaces a fixed-size line with an ask whose size and veto probability move together. A smaller ask raises approval chance but covers fewer of the pending intersections per year. This changes the dollars per year available to the local-dedicated route and therefore the number of C-type intersections served.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-j has q_veto U(0, 0.5) and t_defer as exogenous draws. a_sg017 is the only dollar amount tied to this channel, and it covers SG017, not a negotiated amendment. There is no link between the size of the ask and the probability of approval, and no offset-source rule.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: 'EP17 FY26 to FY28 uncommitted headroom $0 to 0.5M per year' and 'only changing the hardware replacement rows or revising the 5YPP is possible' (the 5YPP table at 01 line 613). The 5YPP also states that the next five years are not expected to be as over-advanced. No document support for advocates offering this concession.
proposals.parameter: a_ask (dollars per year, amendment size) with a rule q_veto = q_veto0 + e_ask * (a_ask - a_ref) / a_ref, where e_ask is the elasticity. Add sw_sunset in {0, 1}, which ends the line after T_sunset years.
proposals.range: a_ask in $0.25M to $1.0M per year; e_ask U(0, 0.6); T_sunset in {2, 3, 5} years
proposals.rule_modified: F-j: q_veto becomes a function of the ask size; D3.6 PW2 gets a dollar size and a sunset switch.

proposals.behaviour: Strategic timing: withhold or withdraw the amendment when its veto risk is high, and put effort into the next 5YPP and strategic plan cycle (autumn 2027 to 2028), where APS can be scored and programmed as a line from the start. A recorded 'no' on the amendment is a worse state than not asking, because it creates a precedent and a stated reason that staff can cite later.
proposals.trigger: The advocate's estimate of the board vote is below a threshold, or the 5YPP calendar opens within a few months so that waiting costs little.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes the PW2 sequence. Instead of amendment then veto then general fund then HSIP, the advocate can skip the visible failure and go directly to the 5YPP window, with a better chance of approval because the line is in the baseline. The cost is a delay of about 12 to 24 months and the loss of the SG017 window.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D3.6 PW2 and F-j list 'or wait for the next 5YPP round (autumn 2027 to 2028)' as a recovery path after a veto or deferral. What is not modelled is the advocate choosing to wait before the vote, and a different success rate for an amendment pushed through versus a line entered at the 5YPP.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.3: next 5YPP window autumn 2027 to 2028; a 3 to 4 month amendment precedent (Lincoln Way). 5YPP scoring includes 'community support 5' and 'disadvantaged populations 5', so organised comment has a scoring channel there. No document support for advocates choosing to withdraw.
proposals.parameter: sw_wait in {0, 1} and theta_veto_estimate U(0.2, 0.6): withdraw if the perceived q_veto exceeds this threshold, then enter the 5YPP window with approval chance q_5ypp U(0.4, 0.9).
proposals.range: sw_wait in {0, 1}; theta_veto_estimate U(0.2, 0.6); q_5ypp U(0.4, 0.9)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2 (adds a pre-vote branch) and F-j (adds a withdrawal action that avoids the veto state).

proposals.behaviour: Mobilise supporting voices in a burst before the vote (a joint letter, a bloc of public commenters, borrowed support from disability and senior or pedestrian-safety groups) and press for a written commitment with a reporting duty, rather than a one-off ask. The pressure is concentrated in a short window and carries information about who is behind it.
proposals.trigger: The amendment is placed on the board or committee agenda (a fixed date, with a CAC step before it).
proposals.effect_in_model: Instead of a Poisson stream of pressure with rate lambda_press, a single pulse arrives before the vote and raises approval chance, with the size of the pulse depending on how many allied groups join. After the vote, a reporting condition raises oversight for a period. Today the model has no link between advocacy and the specific vote.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. lambda_press and pressure(t) with decay k, and F-m (pressure interruption), are generic and continuous. PW3 sets oversight and specified at higher levels. The vote-linked pulse and the coalition-size dependence are not modelled.
proposals.evidence: 01 section 2.8: 'no public statement on SF APS funding by LightHouse, CCB, NFB-CA or ILRC in 2024 to 26'; 'board minutes: 0 of about 39 public comments concerned APS'; the unobserved activation rate is flagged as uncalibrated. 01 section 2.3: CAC is advisory and has not raised the APS gap; 5YPP scores 'community support 5'. The 2007 agreement (section IV.J.2) says plaintiffs support SFMTA requests for funding, which is document support for a coalition role with the agency.
proposals.parameter: pulse_size P U(0, 1) as a one-time addition to pressure(t) at the vote date, scaled by n_allies in {0, 1, 2, 3}; reduction of q_veto = b_pulse * P.
proposals.range: P U(0, 1); n_allies in {0 to 3}; b_pulse U(0, 0.5)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure(t) and F-j q_veto: adds a dated pulse at the amendment vote, and a post-approval oversight increase.

proposals.behaviour: Targeted dollar-ask / earmark drafting. The advocacy lead pre-negotiates a small, time-limited APS line sized to fit inside the existing EP17 slack, with a ring-fence clause (protected from drawdown by outage-driven controller replacements).
proposals.trigger: Amendment is calendared at the SFCTA board; EP17 is over-programmed so any APS line is a visible zero-sum trade against controllers; strongest right after an outage.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes the content of the PW2 amendment, not just whether it passes: a smaller, ring-fenced ask lowers q_veto and shortens t_defer, and the ring-fence lowers later leakage of the line to controllers (q_sg017_block-type). An oversized ask without ring-fence raises deferral or trimming.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-j has q_veto/t_defer as exogenous; PW6 has q_sg017_block. Neither is driven by the advocate's drafting choice, and ask size is not modelled. Behaviour not covered; only outcome variables exist.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: EP17 FY26-28 uncommitted headroom $0-0.5M/yr and 5YPP 202% ahead (EP17-5YPP p.10-11, p.14); controllers got EP17 hardware money after 2022 and 2025 outages (OCT25 p.7, inference). Funding table row 'Prop L restore APS line'. No document shows an advocate drafting an earmark: no document support for the behaviour itself.
proposals.parameter: ask_fit (requested annual APS line / uncommitted EP17 headroom) and ringfence (0/1). q_veto = q_veto_base*(1 + a*max(0, ask_fit-1))*(1 - r*ringfence); t_defer scales alike; ringfence also multiplies q_sg017_block by (1 - r).
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (q_veto, t_defer) in D3.5; PW2 start and PW6 q_sg017_block in D3.6; D10 q_veto, t_defer.

proposals.behaviour: Reframing APS as a safety / liability / 'same-cabinet' item so it competes with controller replacement on the controllers' own terms (pedestrian-injury hot spots, peer-city litigation exposure, adding APS while the cabinet is already being replaced).
proposals.trigger: Board is choosing between APS and post-outage controller replacement; the advocate sees the contest as one of salience.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises APS priority in the SFCTA/SFMTA ranking and converts some controller-replacement events into APS-bundled events. Without it, 'visible failure' is a fixed advantage for controllers.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. lambda_press/pressure(t) and D1 enforcement tiers model generic pressure and litigation; PW5 models a design standard. Nothing models reframing that changes how the request competes, and no incident-driven priority parameter exists.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3 (visible-failure-driven, OCT25 p.7, inference; PIF 2023 listed APS replacement as eligible use of the controller $1M, OCT25 p.7 / EP17-5YPP p.70; scoring weights urgency 4, equity 5, safety 4, EP17-5YPP p.12-13); peer-city litigation s2.11. No document says an SF advocate reframed: behaviour inferred, mechanism partly supported.
proposals.parameter: frame_boost: additive term to the APS priority score; attach_rate: probability a controller replacement is widened to include APS at that intersection.
proposals.range: frame_boost 0-0.3 of the 31-point scale (default 0); attach_rate 0-0.3
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 (raises chance APS is written into SG017 requests, lowers q_sg017_block); PW5 trigger widened to controller outage events; SFCTA priority comparison.

proposals.behaviour: Coalition building with equity/disability groups and district supervisors before the hearing: cosponsors, a supervisor offering a district NTP bridge, and organised public-comment turnout at the amendment hearing.
proposals.trigger: Advocate learns the amendment is calendared and knows a single voice cannot beat controllers for scarce money.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises approval odds at the board (pressure on SFCTA, not SFMTA) and can open a small alternative money source (NTP bridge) usable before the amendment lands.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. lambda_press/pressure(t) are generic pressure on SFMTA; the Lincoln Way NTP precedent is in the evidence but is not a modelled path. No board-directed pressure variable and no supervisor bridge path.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: a district supervisor used NTP $500k to design two new signals with APS in 2024-11, 3-4 month 5YPP amendment (LW p.15-18); EP25 NTP $700k per district per 5 years (NTP5 p.7-8). s2.8: zero APS public comments in 2026 board minutes (sets baseline of no coalition); LightHouse credited with restoring semiannual reports in 2022. The coalition behaviour itself: no document support.
proposals.parameter: coalition_strength C in [0,1] scaling q_veto by (1 - c1*C) and t_defer by (1 - c2*C); bridge_prob: per-amendment probability of a supervisor NTP bridge of size b.
proposals.rule_modified: F-j (q_veto, t_defer) in D3.5; PW2 start; add NTP bridge as a source in the D3.3 local-money path.

proposals.behaviour: Accepting a downgraded outcome and turning it into a monitoring lever: if a dedicated line will not pass, trade it for a soft commitment (report-back, named staff owner, 'consider APS at controller replacements' condition, placeholder in the next 5YPP) and then wait for the 2027-28 window while using the semiannual report as an audit trail.
proposals.trigger: Amendment looks likely to be deferred or rejected because EP17 is over-programmed; a visible loss would waste the campaign.
proposals.effect_in_model: F-j gets a middle outcome: no money, but owner, specified and oversight rise for the APS task (PW3-like effect), and the advocate lowers pressure until the next 5YPP window instead of escalating at once.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW3 has owner/specified/oversight, but only as a chosen starting path, not a fallback after a failed PW2. F-j sends rejection straight to general fund or the next 5YPP.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: 2007 agreement had semiannual reports and 'meaningful participation' in funding applications (SA07 s IV.J.1-2); reports lapsed, restored 2022 after LightHouse pushed; activation rate unknown. s2.3: 'the next five years are not expected to be this far ahead' (EP17-5YPP p.11), next window 2027 autumn-2028. The downgrade-then-monitor tactic: no document support.
proposals.parameter: p_soft: share of would-be vetoes/deferrals that end as a soft commitment; on trigger owner, specified, oversight each +1 level, and lambda_press multiplied by w for t_wait months.
proposals.range: p_soft 0.1-0.6; w 0.3-0.8; t_wait 6-24 months
proposals.rule_modified: F-j outcome branch (add third state 'soft commitment'); D3.1 p_start inputs owner/specified/oversight; lambda_press timing (F-m).

proposals.behaviour: Scope-lock at the allocation-request stage. Advocates use their standing right to 'meaningful participation' in funding applications to get a written APS line (or minimum-dollar earmark, or a named list of C-type sites) into the SG017 allocation request before it is sent to the county transportation authority. They do not wait for the grant to be spent. This lowers the chance the money is diverted to controllers.
proposals.trigger: Advocates learn (via the semi-annual report meeting or the CIP) that an SG017 allocation request is being prepared (task in PREPARING for the SG017 field), and the CIP text allows new APS but the last two allocations went to controllers.
proposals.effect_in_model: Reduces q_sg017_block (probability the SG017 grant excludes new APS or is consumed by failure-driven projects) and raises a_sg017 (dollars of SG017 that can go to APS) for the allocation in question. It acts at the point of drafting, so it adds an advocacy action on the A2 request instance, not on the generic pressure scalar.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. PW6 and D10 have q_sg017_block and a_sg017 but treat them as exogenous draws, not responsive to advocate action. Generic pressure(t) feeds only p_start (D3.1), not the content or scope of an SG017 request. Not captured: advocate-conditioned scope content. The 'blocked' outcome itself is captured, so only the advocate counter-move is proposed.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8: SA07 §IV.J.2 requires SFMTA to let plaintiffs 'meaningfully participate' in funding applications; 'plaintiffs support SFMTA's requests to the mayor and council'; semi-annual meetings must report 'funds applied for and status'. 01 §3.2 (l.446-447): CIP scope text allows new APS where conduits and poles are satisfactory; FY24 and FY25-26 SG017 grants went to cabinets/detectors/RRFB and ~98 controllers. Whether the 2007 agreement's participation clause still binds after its 2010-06-30 term is not documented (02 D3.5/01 §2.8 'constraint' rows say only consultation remains), so the strength of this lever is inference.
proposals.parameter: e_lock
proposals.range: U(0, 0.6): fractional reduction of q_sg017_block when advocate_active = 1 and the SG017 task is in PREPARING (q_eff = q_sg017_block × (1 − e_lock)). Also optional switch sw_lock in {0,1}. Gate: advocate_active requires a draw from lambda_press, so F-m quiet periods turn it off.
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 transition 'SFCTA limits scope to replace or money used by failure-priority projects (q_sg017_block)'; D10 q_sg017_block / a_sg017; interacts with F-m.

proposals.behaviour: Advocate-supplied site nomination and pre-verification (reframing the request from 'the whole 76-site list' to a short C-type list with confirmed adequate poles/conduit). Advocates (or their members) do the legwork the agency says it lacks: ranked list of nearby crossings used by blind pedestrians, with a pole/conduit check, so the SG017 line can pick low-cost installs near the $40k end, not face the $1.5M ceiling the agency cited.
proposals.trigger: The agency answers pressure with 'cost / no funding' (the deflection loop, 01 §1.2, §2.1) and advocates choose to lower the stated barrier instead of repeating the demand; or the SG017 request is being drafted and the C-site list is stale.
proposals.effect_in_model: Shifts the cost/eligibility distribution of candidates used in the SG017 request: raises the share of C-type sites flagged 'existing poles OK', lowers D_prep for the SG017 instance, and lowers p_deflect for that field (the 'cost' excuse is weakened). Turns pressure from pure demand into a supply of preparation work.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 only has pressure as a scalar that raises p_start or triggers deflection; D_prep and m_C/costpress are not advocate-dependent. PW6 restricts SG017 to 'C sites with usable poles' but takes that set from the ledger, with no advocate input.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.1 (l.130): the agency presented 3 pages on 'Technical Challenges & Cost' ($40k to $1.5M, conduit and ramps ~$200k each), and said other sites are 'selected based on funding'. 01 §1.2 buck-passing loop: advocates 'have no resource to force an application'. 01 §2.8 shows no document of advocates doing site work in 2024-26 (searched, none found), so there is no direct document support for the behaviour itself. The $40k floor and C/N split are documented; advocates exploiting them is inference.
proposals.parameter: nominate_gain (nom)
proposals.range: U(0, 1) as the share of pending C-type sites pre-verified by advocates; effects: D_prep_SG017 × (1 − 0.5·nom) and p_deflect × (1 − 0.5·nom), active only when advocate_active = 1. Switch sw_nominate in {0,1}.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 preparation time D_prep and p_deflect; PW6 eligible-site set.

proposals.behaviour: Venue/timing-aimed pressure: advocates save public comment, letters and board testimony for the few moments where the SG017 decision can change (the SFMTA capital budget stage and the county transportation authority allocation hearing and its citizen advisory committee), rather than spreading it evenly in time. They also hold fire when no SG017 request is open.
proposals.trigger: A window opens: an SG017 allocation request is in PREPARING or submitted and awaiting a board hearing (allocation calendar ~8-13 weeks from submission, no August meeting).
proposals.effect_in_model: Replaces constant-rate pressure with pressure whose effect is concentrated inside a window. Same total pressure events per year, but a larger weight on beta_pr when a window is open and ~0 weight when not. It changes p_start and p_deflect only for the field whose window is open.
proposals.already_in_model: No. pressure(t) is a single exponential-decay sum of events at rate lambda_press (D10) with no link to which field's window is open; window timing is exogenous and only affects p_start through the state machine. F-m only models quiet periods.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: allocation request lead time 8-13 weeks, 'no CAC question on APS found in reviewed memos', CAC has advisory power only; 2026 board minutes: 0 of ~39 public comments touched APS (01 §2.8). 01 §2.3 also shows a quick route exists: a district supervisor changed a 5YPP in 3-4 months after one event, so a timed push can work. No document shows advocates timing their pressure; this is inference.
proposals.parameter: w_focus
proposals.range: U(1, 5): multiplier on beta_pr·pressure when any SG017/EP17 request window is open; outside windows multiplier = 1/w_focus (events total conserved). Switch sw_focus in {0,1}.
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start formula term β_pr·pressure(t); D10 lambda_press and k.

proposals.behaviour: Venue shift to a district-supervisor route (NTP/EP25 or a supervisor-sponsored 5YPP amendment) when SG017 looks closed, with advocates coalition-building with a supervisor's office, using the precedent that a supervisor funded two new signals with APS. This is a parallel local funding line, separate from the SG017 line and from the Prop L amendment of PW2.
proposals.trigger: Advocates see SG017 FY27/28 allocation excluding new APS (the q_sg017_block branch fires) or the request is delayed beyond a threshold, and a district office is receptive.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a side branch inside PW6's failure path: instead of going straight to 'Prop L amendment', a probability q_nTP that a supervisor-sponsored amendment of limited size (≈ $500k, 1-3 C-type sites in one district) is approved in 3-4 months, bypassing F-j veto risk for that slice. Shortens time-to-first-install for a few sites.
proposals.already_in_model: No. 02 has no NTP/EP25 or supervisor-sponsored path (grep: no 'NTP' hit in 02; PW2 uses the full EP17 amendment, F-j treats the board veto). The district precedent is only in 01.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: EP25 NTP $700k per district over FY24-28; D4 supervisor used $500k NTP in 2024-11 to design two new signals with APS at Lincoln Way, 3-4 months for the 5YPP revision (LW p.15-18). 01 §2.3 EP26 equity line names people with disabilities. No document shows blind-advocacy groups using this route.
proposals.parameter: q_ntp
proposals.range: U(0, 0.4) probability per year of a successful supervisor-sponsored side line once SG017 is blocked; size $ntp_size U($200k, $500k); latency U(3, 6) months. Switch sw_ntp in {0,1}.
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 failure branch (add a node before 'Prop L amendment'); D10 new parameters; interacts with F-j and F-k.

proposals.behaviour: Shopping for a different pot (district-supervisor NTP / EP25 or EP26 equity money). Instead of fighting for the EP17 amendment, the advocate asks district supervisors to recommend a one-off APS project from the Neighborhood Transportation Program, or asks for an equity-priority line, which sidesteps the over-programmed EP17 and the controller-outage competition. Reframes the request from 'restore a signal line' to 'a district disability-access project'.
proposals.trigger: EP17 over-programmed (about 202% ahead); amendment deferred or rejected (F-j), or board staff signal that EP17 has no room; also the NTP recommendation cycle opening.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a funding route outside EP17 and outside SFMTA general funds. Money comes from a different board-level decision (a district supervisor recommends, SFCTA allocates) with its own approval probability and amount. It could fund a small batch of C-type intersections before the 2027-28 5YPP window. It also lets SFMTA submit an application under another line, which matters because the task state machine requires SFMTA to start the application.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in 02. A grep for NTP, EP25, EP26, EP18 and supervisor in 02 returns nothing. F-j's recovery list names only a re-hearing, the next 5YPP, or the general fund. PW1-PW6 do not include it.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3 resources: 'EP25 NTP: each district supervisor recommends projects, $700k per district over FY24-28' and 'EP26 equity priority projects explicitly name disabled people, $47M'. 01 §2.3 also records the Prop K precedent of a dedicated '19th Avenue APS' project (about $249k). No document shows an advocate actually using this route, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: `sw_alt_pot` (0/1) and `a_ntp` U($0, $700k per 5 years) with `p_ntp` U(0, 0.3). Triggered when F-j fires or when `q_veto` is drawn as a veto. Success creates an extra local-funding batch of size a_ntp and gives SFMTA a pre-filled application for the task state machine.
proposals.range: sw_alt_pot in {0,1}; a_ntp U($0, $700k); p_ntp U(0, 0.3)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j recovery path and D3.6 PW2 fallback chain. Adds a branch before 'general fund'.

proposals.behaviour: Shrinking or ring-fencing the ask so the board can say yes. The advocate does not ask for a large dedicated line. It asks for a small, explicitly protected sum such as $250k per year, with proviso language that the sum cannot be redirected to controller replacements or other outage fixes. It may also accept funding by reducing another EP17 line.
proposals.trigger: Board staff or commissioners point out that EP17 is over-programmed; a controller outage makes replacement funding salient just before the hearing.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers the veto and deferral probability of the amendment and lowers the share of funds later diverted by outage-driven projects. The price is a smaller amount per year and a longer time to clear the roughly 76-intersection backlog.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. `q_veto` is a flat U(0, 0.5) in D10 and does not depend on the size of the ask. `q_sg017_block` (PW6) covers SG017 money being used on controllers, but there is no ring-fence option and no link between ask size and approval. Not captured.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: EP17 5YPP committed $27.49M against $8.52M pay-go, 'about 202% ahead'; FY26-28 funds go to TSP, hardware replacement and others with 'no APS installation line'. 01 §2.1: the EP17 hardware money went to about 98 controllers with firewall defects, although the 2023 PIF had listed APS replacement as eligible. 01 §2.3 inference: 'driven by visible failures, controllers got EP17 money after outages in 2022 and 2025'. No document shows the advocate asking for a ring-fence, so that part has no document support.
proposals.parameter: `ask_size` U($100k, $1M per year) and `ringfence` (0/1). Rule: `q_veto = q_veto0 + γ_size·(ask_size / EP17 headroom)` and `q_sg017_block × (1 − ρ_rf·ringfence)`, with ρ_rf U(0.3, 0.9).
proposals.range: ask_size U($100k, $1M); ringfence in {0,1}; γ_size U(0, 0.4); ρ_rf U(0.3, 0.9)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (`q_veto`, `t_defer`) and PW6 `q_sg017_block`, `a_sg017`.

proposals.behaviour: Event-timed pressure instead of a constant rate. The advocate concentrates testimony and letters on moments that give leverage: right after a signal outage or controller failure makes accessibility visible, just before the amendment hearing, or during the 5YPP and strategic-plan cycle. It stays quiet between those moments.
proposals.trigger: A controller or power outage event; the amendment appearing on the SFCTA board or CAC agenda; the 2027 autumn start of the next 5YPP.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes `λ_press` state-dependent, so pressure is high when the outage competes with APS and when the vote happens, and low otherwise. This changes how often pressure lands on the board versus on SFMTA, and whether a pressure spike coincides with the veto decision.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. 02 D10 has `λ_press` U(0, 0.5) per year as a constant Poisson rate, doubled at PW3 start, and F-m switches it off for `t_quiet`. A trigger-based multiplier is not there.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: 'controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (inference). 01 §2.8: LightHouse pushing for the semi-annual report to be restored in 2022-07 is the one observed activation; 'no public statement found for 2024-26'; board minutes show 0 of about 39 public comments about APS. Whether this is event-timed is not documented.
proposals.parameter: `k_trig` multiplier on `λ_press` during `w_trig` months after (a) an outage event, (b) an amendment hearing being calendared.
proposals.range: k_trig U(1, 8); w_trig U(1, 4) months
proposals.rule_modified: D10 `λ_press`, and the pressure(t) input to `p_start` and to the board decision in F-j.

proposals.behaviour: Demobilisation after a soft concession. If the amendment is deferred but SFMTA or SFCTA promises a report, a staff review, or 'consider it in the next 5YPP', the advocate accepts the promise and stops pushing until the next window. Its leverage decays because the promise looks like progress.
proposals.trigger: F-j ends in deferral rather than rejection, with an informal promise of reporting or review; semi-annual meetings continue to supply reports.
proposals.effect_in_model: Turns an endogenous drop in `λ_press` into a consequence of deferral. This lengthens the deflection loop (no application, no money, 'no funds' reply). The existing F-m only has random quiet periods unrelated to the decision outcome.
proposals.already_in_model: Not in 02. F-m generates quiet at random annual rate `λ_quiet`; PW3 escalates but only on idle time (`θ_idle`). Nothing couples quiet to a deferral or a concession.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8: since 2010 the plaintiffs are only 'consulted, cannot set deadlines' (inference); reports are still received twice a year (MDC23 slide 10; MDC26 p.11); 2018 board committee hearing had only public comment, 'no action'. The loop in 01 §1.2 ('no resources to force an application, so still nobody applies') is the same closed loop. No document shows demobilisation after a concession itself.
proposals.parameter: `q_coopt` and `t_coopt`: after F-j deferral, with probability q_coopt set `λ_press` = λ_press × (1 − d_coopt) for t_coopt months.
proposals.range: q_coopt U(0, 0.7); d_coopt U(0.5, 1.0); t_coopt U(6, 30) months
proposals.rule_modified: F-m (adds an endogenous trigger) and PW2/PW3 transition thresholds `θ_defer`, `θ_idle`.

proposals.behaviour: Coalition and endorsement stacking before the vote. The advocate lines up the disability commission, the citizens advisory committee, other disability groups and district offices so that the amendment arrives with visible community support, which raises the support score and lowers the chance of deferral. This uses up organisational attention, so less pressure goes to other targets.
proposals.trigger: Amendment date set; the 5YPP scoring criteria reward community support and vulnerable groups.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers `q_veto` and `t_defer` for the amendment (and possibly raises the priority of an APS line against controller replacements). Costs: pressure on SFMTA (`λ_press` for the application path) falls for that period because of limited staff.
proposals.already_in_model: Not captured. D1 only has escalation levels (negotiation, lawsuit); the actors are independent ('no direct social network between actors' is listed under 'not built' in D). CAC appears in the evidence but not in a rule.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.3: the 5YPP scoring gives community support 5 and vulnerable groups 5 (max 31); CAC has advisory power only, and 'EP17/EP18 5YPP and the 2025-10 allocation were all unanimously supported'. 01 §2.8: 2007 agreement §IV.J.2 has plaintiffs supporting SFMTA's requests to the mayor and board, which is a precedent for supportive coalition behaviour. No document shows the coalition being built for this amendment.
proposals.parameter: `coal` (0/1) with `coal_cost`: `q_veto × (1 − ρ_coal·coal)` and `λ_press × (1 − c_coal·coal)` on SFMTA targets for `w_coal` months.
proposals.range: ρ_coal U(0, 0.4); c_coal U(0, 0.5); w_coal U(2, 8) months
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (`q_veto`) and D10 `λ_press`.

proposals.behaviour: Gate-targeted lobbying. The advocacy organisation stops treating SFMTA's task as the only target and concentrates written and oral comment on the SFCTA allocation step (CAC, board, allocation memo), asking that the SG017 allocation scope say 'replace and install new APS where poles and conduit are adequate' instead of 'replace'. It times the push to the weeks before the allocation request is drafted and the memo is calendared, not at random.
proposals.trigger: A SG017 allocation request is being prepared (FY27/FY28 $500k each), and the organisation reads the memo history showing earlier allocations went to controllers or cabinets. This is the PW6 situation.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers q_sg017_block directly. In the model the blocker is a pure random draw, and pressure(t) only enters A2's p_start. Pressure aimed at the SFCTA gate does not currently reach the step that decides whether APS stays in the SG017 scope. It also lets an advocacy action change PW6's outcome without changing A2's task start.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.6 PW6 has q_sg017_block (U(0.2, 0.9)) as an exogenous random draw, and D3.1 has pressure(t) feeding only p_start. Neither lets an actor choose the venue. Kept because the venue choice and its effect on the blocker are not written down.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8: the 2007 agreement SA07 §IV.J.2 requires SFMTA to let plaintiffs 'participate meaningfully' in its funding applications, and the 2026-08 to 10 board minutes show 0 of about 39 public comments on APS. 01 line 447: SG017 allocations FY24 and FY25-26 never went to APS. 01 line 446: the CIP scope text allows new APS. There is no document showing the organisation has commented at the SFCTA gate, so the behaviour itself has no document support.
proposals.parameter: gate_lobby (switch) with gate_intensity g in [0, 1] and a timing window t_lobby_lead of 1-6 months. When on, q_sg017_block_eff = q_sg017_block * (1 - g * 1[lobby active in the allocation-drafting window]). Lobby activity is a Bernoulli event per cycle with probability p_lobby U(0, 0.6) (inferred); the baseline value is 0.
proposals.range: g U(0, 0.6); p_lobby U(0, 0.6); t_lobby_lead U(1, 6) months; off = baseline
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 trigger (q_sg017_block); D10 q_sg017_block

proposals.behaviour: Pacification after a small win. Once any SG017 allocation or other source names new APS, even a token one, the organisation reads that as progress, reverts to the cooperative semi-annual-report mode, and cuts its own pressure for a period. It does not escalate to structured negotiation or a lawsuit while it sees money moving.
proposals.trigger: The first APS-labelled funding event, for example an SG017 allocation that includes a new-APS line, or a HSIP award. Alternatively, a visible SFMTA commitment such as a report promise.
proposals.effect_in_model: Endogenous demobilisation. After a trigger, lambda_press is multiplied by (1 - d) for t_demob months, and eps_enf, the escalation rate, drops. The result is that a small early win can lower the total money reaching the 76 pending intersections, because follow-on pressure disappears. A funded-then-stalled path (a token $250k) can then be worse than no win.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-m (D3.5) makes pressure interruption exogenous (lambda_quiet, t_quiet), not triggered by a win. D3.6 PW3 raises pressure only after an idle spell. Nothing makes pressure fall after funding.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8: after the 2007 agreement (expired 2010-06-30) plaintiffs were only consulted. lflegal shows no SF extension, amendment or enforcement record after 2010. 2018: the board committee heard 'only public comment, no action'. 2024-26: no public statement by LightHouse, CCB, NFB-CA or ILRC found. This fits the pattern of going quiet while a relationship appears to work. The causal link to wins is no document support, a design inference.
