proposals.parameter: demob_after_win (switch) with demob strength d in [0, 1] and duration t_demob. When on, the first APS funding event sets lambda_press *= (1 - d) and eps_enf *= (1 - d) for t_demob months.
proposals.range: d U(0, 0.8); t_demob U(6, 36) months; off = baseline
proposals.rule_modified: D3.5 F-m (replaces the random lambda_quiet draw with a conditional one); D3.1 pressure(t); D10 lambda_press, eps_enf

proposals.behaviour: Negotiated set-aside or floor. Instead of pushing the generic request, the organisation uses the semi-annual meeting and its consultation right to bargain for a written minimum share of SG017 (or a listed intersection set from the 76 pending, restricted to those where poles and conduit are adequate), in exchange for dropping or delaying demands for a firm deadline or escalation. This is an informal side deal, not a formal rule change.
proposals.trigger: The organisation has its bi-annual meeting or a status-report moment close to the allocation request, and SFMTA signals that it will not commit to dates (the existing deflection pattern, 'cost' and 'no funds').
proposals.effect_in_model: Sets a floor on a_sg017, the SG017 money available to APS, which is now a random U(0, 250k) with no bargaining. The cost is a concession: PW3's specified and oversight upgrades (a written time limit and a named owner) are not obtained, and sit at their current values. This creates a trade-off between money now and accountability later, which the paths do not currently contain.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. D3.6 PW3 has structured negotiation, but only as an escalation step after idleness and for the whole accountability package (owner, specified, oversight). A scoped money-for-pressure bargain on one fund is not modelled. a_sg017 is only a draw.
proposals.evidence: 01 §2.8: SA07 §IV.A.1 'SFMTA will seek additional funding from federal, state and local sources' and the bi-annual meeting with report on 'funding applied for and status'. 2007 structured negotiation is the precedent for deal-making outside court. 01 §2.1: the senior engineer cites the litigation environment as a reason to keep curb-ramp work together. There is no document showing a set-aside has been asked for, so the specific behaviour has no document support.
proposals.parameter: setaside_deal (switch) with floor share f_floor of the SG017 per-year funds and concession c in [0, 1]. When on, a_sg017 = max(a_sg017_draw, f_floor * 500k) and specified and oversight gains are scaled by (1 - c), i.e. the deal replaces the accountability package in PW3.
proposals.range: f_floor U(0, 0.5); c U(0, 1); p_deal (chance the deal is reached per cycle) U(0, 0.5); off = baseline
proposals.rule_modified: D10 a_sg017; D3.6 PW6 and PW3 (links them); D3.1 specified, oversight

proposals.behaviour: Gate-targeted pressure: the advocate times and aims comment letters / public comment at the SFCTA allocation request for SG017 (and the board memo), asking that the scope explicitly list new APS, rather than pressuring SFMTA's APS team in general.
proposals.trigger: Public posting of the SG017 allocation request or SFCTA board/committee agenda; advocate sees draft scope limited to 'replace' or controllers.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers q_sg017_block (the chance SG017 money is not used for new APS) and raises a_sg017 for that cycle only. It does not feed pressure(t) or p_start. It acts at the approval gate, not the task state machine.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. Pressure (lambda_press, beta_pr, pressure(t)) exists in D3.1, but it is undifferentiated and acts only on A2's p_start. q_sg017_block (D10, PW6) is exogenous with no advocate input. So the gate-targeting is NOT captured.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8 gives the advocate a right to participate in SFMTA's Prop K funding requests (SA07 IV.J.2) and 'supports SFMTA requests to mayor and council'. 01 l.447: SG017 past allocations went to controllers (FY24 control cabinets/detectors/RRFB, FY25-26 about 98 controllers). 01 s2.8: no 2024-26 public comment found. No document shows gate-targeted lobbying; labelled no direct document support beyond the participation right.
proposals.parameter: theta_gate (advocate gate-targeting intensity)
proposals.range: 0 to 0.6, as a multiplicative reduction of q_sg017_block: q_eff = q_sg017_block * (1 - theta_gate * I[advocate_active]). Test 0, 0.3, 0.6. Needs the F-m quiet state as a precondition.
proposals.rule_modified: PW6 trigger and D10 q_sg017_block; couples to F-m (no effect while lambda_press = 0).

proposals.behaviour: Supply-side scoping help: the advocate hands SFMTA/SFCTA a ranked list of intersections it wants, filtered to ones its members believe already have adequate poles and conduit, so the 'existing poles/conduit usable' condition is easier to meet and the first batch is chosen by community priority.
proposals.trigger: A funding window is open and the CIP wording limits new APS to sites with adequate poles and conduit; the advocate has member knowledge of where it is cheap.
proposals.effect_in_model: Changes batch selection among C-class intersections. A fraction of the advocate-nominated sites move earlier in the queue, and the batch's mean unit cost falls (fewer sites hit the +$200k pipe/ramp add-ons). It also lowers the chance that 'not ready' is used as a reason to deflect.
proposals.already_in_model: No. D3.1 and D3.4 pick sites without an advocate input. The cost add-ons q_pipe and q_ramp are drawn per site, independent of any advocate action. Nothing in 02 gives the advocate a selection role.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: the 2007 agreement gave the advocate 'meaningful participation'. 01 s2.8 and l.308 show LightHouse and SFMTA did joint survey work in 2008 (a joint LightHouse/MOD survey). 01 l.570: unit cost depends on pipe/ramp add-ons that are conditional ('may'). No document says the advocate keeps a pole-readiness list; labelled no document support for that part.
proposals.parameter: phi_nominate (share of each batch drawn from advocate-nominated sites) and rho_ready (extra probability a nominated site has q_pipe = q_ramp = 0)
proposals.range: phi_nominate 0 to 0.5; rho_ready 0 to 0.4
proposals.rule_modified: D3.4 batch selection order and the per-site draw of q_pipe/q_ramp at list entry.

proposals.behaviour: Sequencing concession (informal side deal): the advocate accepts 'controllers first this cycle' in return for a dated, named commitment to new APS in the next allocation, and holds back pressure in the meantime.
proposals.trigger: The advocate sees a firm controller-first plan (firewall-vulnerability work) that it cannot defeat, and an SFMTA/SFCTA staffer offers a future-cycle promise.
proposals.effect_in_model: Sets lambda_press to a low level for t_concede months (like F-m, but chosen, not random). It also sets a one-time 'promise' that raises specified and owner for the next window. If the promise is not kept, a rebound pressure jump and a higher epsilon_enf follow.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. F-m (quiet periods) gives silence, but it is random and carries no promise or rebound. PW3 gives the commitment, but as a policy lever the city chooses, not a bargain the advocate trades into. A voluntary trade-off with a rebound is NOT captured.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8 and SA07: the 2007 agreement was reached by negotiation, not suit ('structured negotiation', no litigation). 01 s2.8: since 2010 plaintiffs are only consulted and cannot set deadlines (inferred). 01 s2.8: LightHouse pushed for the semi-annual report to return in 2022. No document describes a controllers-first trade; labelled no document support for the trade itself.
proposals.parameter: c_concede (probability the advocate concedes when a controller-first plan is posted); t_concede; r_rebound (pressure multiplier if the promise fails)
proposals.range: c_concede 0 to 0.7; t_concede 6 to 24 months; r_rebound 1 to 3
proposals.rule_modified: F-m and the D1 enforcement tiers: adds an endogenous quiet state, and links the promise to specified and owner in p_start.

proposals.behaviour: Cheap documentation threat: the advocate records unmet obligations (the duty to seek extra funds, the semi-annual report contents, the missing APS applications) and cites them as a credible ADA/PROWAG complaint risk, without filing. The threat is raised only when the report or list shows no funding action.
proposals.trigger: The semi-annual APS report or the pending-request list shows no application for outside funds; peer-city cases (NYC, Chicago, DC) are visible.
proposals.effect_in_model: Raises the 'ADA suit threat' share of pressure events. The probability that deflection (p_deflect) is chosen over starting falls when the threat is credible, with no change to the external-enforcement tier unless it is actually filed.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly. C2 lists 'ADA suit threat' as a resource (02 s O2), and PW3 / epsilon_enf model the suit itself (escalation by one tier). A documented, unfiled threat that changes p_deflect, and rises with a visible gap in reports, is NOT captured.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.8: SA07 IV.A.1 obliges SFMTA to seek outside funding; IV.J.1 requires the report to list 'funds applied for and status'. 01 s2.10 and l.386: NYC, Chicago and DC suits give peer precedent. 01 l.83: the 'say no money / did not apply' loop. 01 s2.8: no filings after 2010, so threat intensity is unknown.
proposals.parameter: kappa_threat (reduction in p_deflect per unit of documented gap)
proposals.range: 0 to 0.5 as p_deflect_eff = p_deflect * (1 - kappa_threat * gap_flag), where gap_flag = 1 if no application has been submitted for 12+ months and the report is being sent
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (p_deflect) and the pressure(t) accumulation.

proposals.behaviour: Allocation-stage intervention: the advocacy policy lead shows up at the SFCTA allocation step for the SG017 request (staff review, CAC, board) and asks that the grant scope explicitly name new APS at sites with adequate poles/conduit, or asks for a reporting condition. Advocacy effort is aimed at the narrow decision point where scope gets limited to 'replace', not at SFMTA's start decision.
proposals.trigger: SFMTA files or announces an SG017 allocation request (FY27/FY28) whose draft scope or past pattern is controller-only; a public agenda item or memo draft becomes visible 8-10 weeks before the grant.
proposals.effect_in_model: Lowers q_sg017_block (and raises the share of the $500k usable for APS, a_sg017) in PW6 for that allocation event only. Pressure currently acts only on p_start (SFMTA's decision to prepare an application); this adds an effect on the SFCTA gate, a different node.
proposals.already_in_model: Partly: PW6 and q_sg017_block exist (02 D3.6 PW6, D10 q_sg017_block) but q_sg017_block is a fixed prior U(0.2,0.9) and is not influenced by any actor. lambda_press/pressure(t) (D3.1) only feeds p_start. So the targeted version is not captured.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: allocation 'based on applications prepared and submitted', staff review -> CAC -> board; 'CAC has advisory power only'; 'no CAC question about APS absence in memos reviewed' (absence). 01 s2.8: SA07 IV.J.2 required SFMTA to let plaintiffs participate 'meaningfully' in Prop K applications (historical channel, expired 2010); 2026 board 0/~39 comments on APS (absence of such a move). No direct document showing advocates doing this now.
proposals.parameter: p_adv_alloc (probability advocates engage at a given SG017 allocation event) U(0, 0.6); delta_block (relative cut in q_sg017_block when engaged) U(0, 0.5); optional switch sw_adv_alloc in {0,1}. Engagement suppressed during F-m quiet periods.
proposals.range: p_adv_alloc U(0,0.6); delta_block U(0,0.5); sw in {0,1}
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 trigger (q_sg017_block) and D10 q_sg017_block / a_sg017; interacts with F-m (quiet periods).

proposals.behaviour: Supervisor sponsorship route: the advocacy organisation asks a district supervisor to fund new APS through the district Neighborhood Transportation Program (EP25) or a similar district allocation, as a parallel local money source when SG017 goes to controllers.
proposals.trigger: SG017 allocation for the year is spent on controllers or excludes APS (q_sg017_block fires), or a visible APS failure/complaint occurs; supervisors have discretion over $700k per district per 5 years.
proposals.effect_in_model: Adds a new fund channel with its own yearly probability and dollar amount that pays for a small batch of C-type sites (internal-installable), entering the same Signal Shop queue and K_crew limits. It is a bypass that does not pass through SFMTA's p_start decision (SFMTA still must install, so strain applies).
proposals.already_in_model: No. Grep of 02 finds no NTP/EP25/supervisor channel. Local routes in 02 are Prop L amendment (PW2), General Fund request, SG017 (PW6), and director 10% reallocation (F-k).
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: EP25 NTP 'each district supervisor recommends projects, $700k per district FY24-28' (NTP5 p.7-8); precedent: D4 supervisor used NTP $500k in 2024-11 to design two new signals with APS at Lincoln Way, 3-4 months through 5YPP amendment (LW p.15-18). 01 s2.3 'outcome is driven by visible failure'. No document that advocates have used this route for APS.
proposals.parameter: lambda_ntp (annual rate at which advocacy converts into a district sponsorship) U(0, 0.3), a_ntp (dollars per event) U($0, $300k), t_ntp lag in months U(3, 12). Enabled only after q_sg017_block fires.
proposals.range: lambda_ntp U(0,0.3); a_ntp U($0,$300k); t_ntp U(3,12)
proposals.rule_modified: New branch after the PW6 trigger and in F-j/F-k recovery paths; D4 outputs (installed_5y) via Signal Shop queue.

proposals.behaviour: Logrolling/concession: the advocate accepts that FY27 SG017 goes to controllers (safety-of-infrastructure framing) in exchange for a written commitment that part of FY28 SG017 goes to new APS at pole-adequate sites. Pressure is deliberately withheld in the trade year.
proposals.trigger: A controller or hardware failure is publicly visible (as in the 2022 and 2025 outages) so contesting the FY27 allocation looks costly, and SFMTA signals willingness to earmark later.
proposals.effect_in_model: Makes q_sg017_block year-dependent: raises it in year 1 and lowers it in year 2 by an earmark fraction; temporarily sets lambda_press to 0 in the trade window (self-chosen quiet, unlike random F-m). Risk branch: the promised earmark is not kept (probability q_renege), which converts to PW2 start with a delay.
proposals.already_in_model: No. F-m has random quiet periods but not strategic withdrawal or a deal; SG017 block probability is a single static prior.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.3: controllers got EP17 hardware money after 2022 and 2025 outages; FY25-26 $1M for ~98 controllers (01 s3.2 end). No document support for the advocate side of the deal; no document support for any earmark promise.
proposals.parameter: sw_trade in {0,1}; s_earmark (share of FY28 $500k committed to APS) U(0, 0.5); q_renege U(0.2, 0.7); t_trade_quiet U(6, 18) months of zero lambda_press.
proposals.range: s_earmark U(0,0.5); q_renege U(0.2,0.7); t_trade_quiet U(6,18)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.6 PW6 and D10 q_sg017_block/a_sg017 (year-dependent), D10 lambda_press and F-m.

proposals.behaviour: Site-list pre-screening: the advocate (with the city disability office's site list used for APS scoring) hands SFMTA a ranked list of requested intersections tagged by likely adequate poles/conduit and by user demand, so that the allocation scope can be written at once and the 'adequacy' determination is pushed to site checks that the advocate can later audit.
proposals.trigger: The SG017 CIP scope makes 'where poles and conduit are adequate' the gate and SFMTA has not stated which sites pass.
proposals.effect_in_model: Shortens D_prep (and removes some of the delta_split cost) for the SG017 request, and shifts the share of C-type sites classified as pole-adequate toward the advocate's list; may also raise the chance a contested 'not adequate' ruling is reopened (re-inspection).
proposals.already_in_model: Not as an actor action. D_prep is a fixed prior and site adequacy is drawn once by Bernoulli (q_pipe, s_* in D3.3); no actor supplies information.
proposals.evidence: 01 s2.7: MOD supplies the 'city public projects' site list for APS scoring (TOOL p.8). 01 s2.1 (decision rule): 'other intersections on the request list are selected based on funding', adequacy treated as SFMTA-internal. No document that advocates have prepared such a list.
proposals.parameter: adv_prescreen in {0,1}; dD_prep_adv (months saved) U(0, 2); d_adequate (shift in share of C sites accepted as adequate) U(0, 0.15).
proposals.range: dD_prep_adv U(0,2); d_adequate U(0,0.15)
proposals.rule_modified: D3.1 D_prep and the preparation-time rule; D3.3 site-eligibility draws for the SG017 route.
